author: gingin77
body:
## CMTX1 turned out to be already curated

I claimed MONDO:0010549 to curate as a new `kb/disorders/` entry. It didn't need one — CMTX1 is already the first `has_subtypes` entry of `kb/disorders/Charcot-Marie-Tooth_Disease_Type_X.yaml`, and that file's entire pathophysiology chain *is* the CMTX1 mechanism:

```
Connexin-32 Reflexive Gap Junction Loss in Schwann Cells
  -> Impaired Radial Metabolic Support of the Axon
    -> Demyelination with Secondary Axonal Loss
      -> Length-Dependent Distal Neuropathy

Oligodendrocyte Connexin-32 Loss and Transient CNS Dysfunction
```

So the honest `entry_type` for the stub is `SUBTYPE`, and this PR records that rather than creating a near-duplicate entry.

## What changed

- **`subtype_term` bound to MONDO:0010549** on the CMTX1 subtype. None of the six CMTX subtypes carried one. Under the coverage rule in `CLAUDE.md`, a `has_subtypes` term counts as curated, so this retires the concept from the curation queue.
- **`review_notes` on that subtype** explaining why CMTX1 stays a subtype, so it isn't nominated a third time.
- **Stub deleted.**
- **History record** under `history/disorders/Charcot-Marie-Tooth_Disease_Type_X/`.
- One term-cache row (`MONDO:0010549`), in canonical sorted position.

No evidence, phenotype, or pathophysiology content was touched, and no snippet was altered.

## Why not promote CMTX1 to its own entry

It's a judgment call and worth stating either way. The parent's pathograph is CMTX1's pathograph. Splitting CMTX1 out would leave `Charcot-Marie-Tooth_Disease_Type_X.yaml` as a shell of four rare, mechanistically unrelated loci — AIFM1, PRPS1, PDK3, and the unresolved Xq27.1 insertion — two of which already cross-reference their own entries. That trade looks bad, so the reasoning now lives in `review_notes` rather than only in this PR description.

## How my duplicate preflight missed it

Worth recording, since the same shape will recur. I searched `origin/main` for the MONDO ID and for the label "Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease X-linked dominant". Neither string appears in a file named `Type_X` whose subtype is named `CMTX1`. The stub's own `mondo_parents` field named `MONDO:0018994` (CMT type X) and would have pointed straight at it — reading the stub's parent is a cheaper and more reliable check than grepping labels.

## Left for separate issues, not widened into this PR

Two adjacent defects I found and deliberately did not fix here:

1. `kb/groupings/Charcot-Marie-Tooth_Diseases.yaml` omits both Type X and Type 4 as members, and its CMT Type 1 member row attributes the GJB1 connexin-32 mechanism to CMT1 ("GJB1 connexin-32 dysfunction in overlapping X-linked or intermediate CMT"). Fixing that means editing the grouping's `description`, `grouping_rationale`, and two member rows — a real curation task rather than a line change.
2. Three `explanation` strings in `Charcot-Marie-Tooth_Disease_Type_X.yaml` still argue for the retired `PARTIAL` evidence grade above a `supports: SUPPORT` (the leftover prose from #10003 that `CLAUDE.md` warns about; no gate catches it).

## Validation

`just validate`, `just validate-terms`, `just check-duplicate-keys`, `just check-entity-refs`, `just check-stubs`, and `just validate-history` all pass.

Closes #10843

author: fernandotn
body:
Two follow-ups you asked for after #61, both small and separate.

## 1. Manual Sync is hard-gated, on the other axis

`syncToProfile` now refuses when **another** profile is already stamped with the
incoming account, naming the holder in the error. It is the Claude twin of the
Codex `account_id` check, down to the `duplicateAccountHolder` shape and the
`accountAlreadySynced` error case.

It is deliberately **not** keyed on the target's own previous account. An
explicit sync bringing a different account into this profile is the documented
"`/login` with that account, then re-sync" repair, and refusing it would block
the only way out of a dead login.

Evidence is `~/.claude.json`'s `oauthAccount.accountUuid`, the CLI's own record
of who it is logged in as. That is the exact parallel of Codex reading
`account_id` out of `auth.json`: local, non-secret, and no network on a path
that blocks a user gesture. Absent or unreadable is **no evidence** and permits
the sync, matching the discipline the write guard from #61 already uses; the
forced re-stamp that follows every sync then surfaces the duplicate through the
detector.

## 2. The caption now says which side to fix

"Same Anthropic account as X" says two profiles share an account. It does not
say what to do about it. `ProfileManager.profilesNeedingAccountRelogin` names
the profile to re-login, and only where the evidence names one:

- **`isLoginContaminated`** — the profile carried a stamp and its **own** token
  later reported a different account, which is a write that moved another
  account's login into it. Recorded at the moment `stampAccountIdentity` sees
  the disagreement, because the very next line heals the stamp to match the
  token and erases the only evidence. Persisted under
  `claudeContaminatedLogins_v1`; cleared on agreement or an explicit sync.
- **a duplicate group containing the owner of the shared CLI login** — every
  other member. The owner is demonstrably the account; the others hold a copy.

A duplicate group the active login is not part of flags nobody. Which member is
the impostor is genuinely unknown there, and guessing would tell the user to
re-login the profile they meant to keep. That group still shows the duplicate
caption, just no verdict.

Nothing is cleared automatically anywhere in this change. The caption appears on
the Manage Profiles row and the CLI Account page.

## For 'Google' specifically

Worth being precise, because the brief's phrasing and the mechanism differ
slightly. `Google` is currently **unstamped**, so the first identity resolution
stamps it from its own token and finds nothing to disagree with — the
contamination flag alone would never fire for it. It gets its "Re-login needed"
caption from the second source: it lands in a duplicate group with
`dRir(Fenrir)`, and `dRir(Fenrir)` owns the shared login. The contamination flag
is what catches the same failure **going forward**, on a profile that was
already stamped when the bad write landed.

## Verification

`Executed 344 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected) in 2.732 (2.810) seconds`
(`xcodebuild test`, macOS destination, on the tree rebased onto 8da0c3d / B2).
Release build succeeds. 3 new tests: the holder lookup naming another profile
while never matching the target's own account or an unstamped profile; every
duplicate except the login owner asked to re-login; and an ambiguous group
flagging nobody while a contamination flag stands on its own.

No credential values are logged or displayed. Account uuids appear in logs
truncated to 8 characters.

author: mikeallisonjs
body:
Closes #421

Part of #400, implementing the composition settled in [#407](https://github.com/JesusFilm/phoebe/issues/407). Stacked on `phoebe/issue-420`.

## What changed

**The cap is derived.** `max(concurrency)` across the live rows, so a solo tenant writing `pipelines.work.concurrency: 3` gets 3 instead of a silent 1, and today's fleet — every row at 1 — still derives 1. `PHOEBE_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS` replaces the derivation absolutely, even when lower. A row declaring more than the cap is not clamped locally; it queues, and boot prints the cap, its derivation and the clamp on one line:

```
[phoebe] boot: slot cap 2 — PHOEBE_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS=2 replaces max(concurrency)=4; floorBudget=1; declaring more than the cap and queuing for it (not clamped): acme/gadget:work(4)
```

The number recomputes only on a reconcile that reshapes rows. Shrinking a semaphore below its own `inUse` has no safe answer, so the supervisor resizes only when it is already draining and respawning — `superviseFleet` gains one `onRows` hook that refreshes ordering every poll and re-derives the cap only when the matrix moved.

**The slot floor.** A row holding zero slots with a waiter is starved and may hold one slot over the cap, at most `PHOEBE_SLOT_FLOOR_BUDGET` (default 1, `0` for a hard ceiling) such over-grants fleet-wide. Entitlement is immediate. A release returns the over-grant before a regular slot, nothing is handed to a waiter while `inUse` exceeds the cap, and a dead row's reclaim restores the budget it held — so the breach is bounded in both directions.

**Priority.** Everything queues, even into a free slot, so one grant-time ordering serves both the regular queue and the floor budget: round-robin picks the tenant, `priority` picks among that tenant's waiting rows (higher first, ties FIFO). Sorting at grant time is what makes `priority` hot. Its hotness also needed the tenant-wide fan-out from #420 taught about hot knobs: a `priority` or `disabled` edit moves the tenant's stat fingerprint and nothing else, and without that the fan-out would relaunch the very row the hot edit was meant to spare. The running record takes the new values instead.

**Fungible grants.** `createSlotClient` keeps a FIFO of pending acquires and resolves the head, so any untagged grant satisfies any of a row's outstanding acquires; a disconnect rejects all of them, so the row stops admitting and drains what is running. The wire format is unchanged.

## Acceptance

Each line of the issue's acceptance list has a test: `bootstrap/slot-broker.test.ts` (derivation, env override + clamp, floor over-grant, release-while-over-cap, reclaim restoring budget, priority within a tenant and round-robin across tenants), `bootstrap/broker-ipc.test.ts` (three grants to one child, floor through the IPC path), `src/slot-client.test.ts` (three acquires resolved in order, disconnect rejecting all three), `bootstrap/supervise-fleet.test.ts` (matrix announced before the first spawn, hot `priority` landing without a relaunch, held tenants staying live) and `bootstrap/boot.test.ts` (the boot line, cap only on reshape).

`vp run ready` is green: 1803 tests, no lint or type errors.

## Not in this PR

The engine still admits one unit at a time, so the plural client and the waiting-for-slot state on the status snapshot land with the in-flight ticket, which consumes this client change. A row's `disabled` is still validated rather than acted on.

author: sagun-py0909
body:
Backend half of the Progress dashboard. One endpoint replacing what would otherwise be five calls from the app.

**`GET /analytics/me?period=7d|30d|90d|365d`** → body scans, training, nutrition, check-ins, upcoming appointments, a composite score, and rule-based insights.

## Mounted at the bare path on purpose

`app.use("/analytics", …)` **and** `app.use("/api/v1/analytics", …)`. The deployed EC2 build does not mount the `/api/v1` namespace at all — see `HANDOVER-ec2-deploy-api-v1-mount.md`. An endpoint reachable only under that prefix passes every dev test and 404s for every production user. The Flutter client addresses the bare path.

## What it reads

| Block | Source | New work |
|---|---|---|
| Body | `BcaMetric` | none — every field was already stored |
| Training | `WorkoutSession` → `WorkoutExercise` → `SetLog` ⨝ `Exercise.muscleGroups` | one aggregation |
| Nutrition | `NutritionAdherenceDaily` | none — already a materialized daily rollup |
| Consistency | `GymVisit` | none — `computeStreaks` already existed |
| Next | `NutritionistBooking`, `ExpertAppointment` | normalising merge |
| Score, Insights | derived | pure functions |

One read per collection, not one per card. Each builder fetches the current window and the equal-length window before it in a single query and splits in JS, so every `previous` and `delta` is free. **No new indexes** — every `$lookup` lands on an existing one, verified against all five models.

`getMyStats` is untouched. It backs the Exercise tab and is hardcoded to the current Mon–Sun week; the ranged version lives in the analytics service instead.

## Two decisions worth review

**Body scans are not clamped to the period.** They are irregular — three or four a quarter — so a period-filtered trend would be empty for most members on most views. `series` returns every scan and the card states the count.

**The muscle split is a share of working sets, not tonnage.** This was a defect in my first pass. Planks, push-ups and hanging leg raises carry no external load, so a volume-weighted split reported a member's core work as 0% — and the neglected-group insight would then have fired at them for training the exact thing they trained.

## Refactor included

`computeStreaks` / `toISTDateString` move from `gymVisit.controller.ts` into `utils/streaks.ts`, imported by both. Behaviour unchanged, IST day boundaries included. Two copies would drift the first time either was tuned, and the Progress heatmap sits directly beside the streak number.

## Empty states

Every block carries its own `hasData`. A member with nothing gets a 200 with all of them false — the client omits a card rather than rendering a value it cannot justify.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — 61 `src/` errors, **identical to `main`'s baseline**, zero added
- Biome clean on all new files
- `bun run test:analytics` — 27 assertions, all passing

author: pabloformoso
body:
The 16 GB on this box is managed by a protocol nobody could see. ACE wants ~12.5 GB and the live DJ's model ~6, so they cannot both be resident — and **every failure of that arrangement is silent**:

- LM Studio answers 400 for every model while still **listing** them
- a first brief after an unload just takes a long time, for no visible reason
- an ACE left loaded holds the GPU while nothing generates

Each of those cost hours. `GET /api/generator/engines` reports what each tenant **says about itself** — ACE's own `/health` body, LM Studio's `/api/v0/models` — and the creation dialog renders it where you would act on it.

## Reachable is not resident

That is the distinction the whole thing exists for. `available` already answered "can we reach ACE". A box started with `--no-init` is **reachable and weighing nothing** — the intended resting state, and something `available` cannot express.

`loaded` and `known` stay separate numbers for the same reason: **listed is not loadable**, recorded in the root `CLAUDE.md` after LM Studio 400'd on every model it was happily listing.

## Decisions worth stating

**The LLM URL is derived from `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`**, not configured separately — two addresses for one server is how they end up disagreeing. It uses `/api/v0/models`, not the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models`, which lists what *exists* rather than what is loaded.

**Free VRAM is deliberately absent.** Neither server exposes it and `nvidia-smi` is not in the backend's container, so any figure would be an inference dressed as a measurement. It needs a host-side helper — the same one LOAD/UNLOAD buttons would need, since ACE has `POST /v1/init` but **no unload**, LM Studio's unload lives in the `lms` CLI, and the container has neither `lms` nor sight of ACE's repo.

**Never 5xx, and renders nothing when it cannot be read.** A status panel that can take the creation dialog down is worse than no panel.

## One found while building it

The first version's broad `except` swallowed a missing `httpx` import and reported the server as **unreachable** — a `NameError` dressed as a box being off, which is precisely the class of bug this panel exists to end. The log line inside the handler is what caught it.

## Verified

23 backend tests in the generator endpoint suite (6 new), 566 frontend (6 new), `next build` passes, eslint clean on every touched file. Tried against the real servers too: ACE reported `models_initialized: false` while up, LM Studio `loaded: ['google/gemma-4-e4b']` out of 6 known.

The 13 failures in `test_youtube_chat.py` are the documented local-only ones.

author: rogerantony-dev
body:
## Why

Paytm and other UPI/banking apps refuse to pay while any third-party accessibility service is enabled. On device the "Suspicious App Detected" block appeared with zero Unhook overlay windows attached, so it is the enabled state they check, and the earlier overlay teardown on this branch could not fix it. Android gives an app no way to hide an enabled service.

## What

- The service switches itself off (`disableSelf()`) the moment a payment app is the active window, records the pause, and posts a notification.
- Two ways to recognise such an app: a named list of Indian UPI and bank apps, and any application window whose content is hidden from accessibility services (Android 14 `accessibilityDataSensitive`, which banking apps use). Since those apps hide their nodes, the window title (the app label) identifies them.
- The `packageNames` filter is gone so window switches from every app are heard. Outside Instagram/YouTube the service narrows itself at runtime to window-state and windows-changed events only. A warm resume from Recents emits only windows-changed, so both are needed.
- The app shows a resume screen instead of onboarding. With `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` granted over adb it re-enables the service directly, and an alarm brings it back four minutes after the pause (exact when `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is allowed; Battery Saver stretches inexact alarms badly). Without the grant the button opens Accessibility settings.
- Privacy policy and README updated. Version 1.7.0, versionCode 10.

## Verified on a Galaxy A54 (One UI, Android 14)

- Paytm proceeded to the UPI PIN screen six seconds after the pause.
- Pause fires on cold launch, on warm resume from Recents, and through the hidden-screen rule alone (tested with Paytm unmapped from the list).
- Resume button re-enables instantly with the adb grant; the exact 4-minute alarm fired on time; the inexact one fired after 11 minutes under Battery Saver.
- Release APK 1.7.0 installed and the cycle repeated on it.

body:
現場から2件の報告に対応します。

1. 同じオレンジのボタンが画面に3つ（撮って読み取る／記録する／保存）並び、投入のたびに押し間違える
2. 撮影後の赤い注意書きと緑の完了文が小さく、見落としそうになる。撮影がOKだったのかNGだったのかがひと目で分からない

## ボタン — 操作の種類ごとに色と形を変える

| 操作 | 見た目 |
| --- | --- |
| 読み取る（機械を撮る） | **青の塗り**＋カメラのアイコン |
| 記録する | **オレンジの塗り**。この画面でオレンジはこれだけ。背を高く（h-16）し、読み取りボタンとの間隔も広げた |
| 保存 | ふだんは**白地に枠線**の控えめな見た目。未保存があるときだけオレンジになり「保存（未保存◯件）」と件数を出す |

さらに **「記録する」で保存まで済ませる**ようにしました。投入のたびに「記録する」→「保存」と2回押していたのが1回になり、押し間違いの元が1つ減ります。保存に失敗したときだけ未保存として画面に残り、下の「保存」で送り直せます（そのときだけボタンがオレンジになります）。

## メッセージ — 見出しつきの枠にする

- 成功は緑の枠、失敗・注意は赤の枠。アイコン付きで見出しは太字18px
- 読み取り失敗の文言の入れ子を直しました。以前は「表示値を読み取れませんでした（…採用しませんでした。撮り直すか、手入力してください。）。もう一度撮るか、手入力してください。」と同じ案内が二重に出ていたので、見出し「読み取れませんでした」＋理由の1文だけにしています
- 結果は**記録ボタンの上**に出します。下に置くと、画面下に固定した保存バーに隠れて読み飛ばされていました

## 変更点

| ファイル | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `src/components/ScaleCamera.tsx` | 読み取りボタンを青に |
| `src/components/ScrapBagPanel.tsx` | 結果の枠（`ResultBanner`）を追加し、袋の一覧でも使用 |
| `src/components/DailyRecordForm.tsx` | 記録ボタンの強調、保存ボタンの状態表示、記録時の自動保存、メッセージの位置と文言 |
| `src/app/guide/page.tsx` | 色の使い分けと自動保存を使い方ガイドに反映 |

ローカルの PostgreSQL + `next start` に対し、スマホ幅（390px）でも表示を確認しました。

- 袋 35/35（「記録すると自動で保存される」を追加。締め済みの袋への追加は「画面を開いたまま別の人が締めた」状況で確かめるよう修正）

The Boost AI Search & Filter, collection/search, Affirm and video drift is **not** carried here. The remanufacturing video block in `sections/extra-info.liquid` is unchanged from `main` and remains gated to `custom.condition_state == 'Remanufactured'`.

## Intended behaviour

- "As high as" uses the native variant compare-at price.
- Current price uses the native product/variant price.
- `custom.sale_price` and `custom.saleprice_name` remain the controlled package/promo source, used only when the sale value is positive and below the native price.
- "Total with Options" resolves the actual selling price using the same condition as the promo banner, so the displayed package price and the option-adjusted total can no longer be built on different numbers.
- Collection, related-item and homepage price displays stop relying on `custom.retail_price` and use native price / compare-at.

## Defect 1 — banner rendered with no sale value (`e1f6665`)

`snippets/super-sale.liquid` tested only whether the sale value was *lower* than the price it compares against, never whether it was *positive*. Harmless while the comparison was `compare_at_price` (empty on most products, so `0 > 0` kept the banner hidden); with the comparison now the always-positive native price, a product carrying a `saleprice_name` with a blank or zero `sale_price` would render a banner advertising **$0.00**.

## Defect 2 — package PDPs lost their price entirely (`460e74f`)

**This one is reachable on live data today and is the more serious of the two.**

All four sections chose between the banner and the normal price block on `custom.saleprice_name` alone, while the banner renders only when the sale value is positive *and strictly below* the price compared against. Those conditions were never the same, and the branch has no fallback — when the banner declines to render, the `{% else %}` has already been skipped, so the PDP shows **no price at all**.

Moving the comparison from `compare_at_price` to the native variant price flipped the outcome for both gym packages:

| Product | Price | Compare-at | `custom.sale_price` | `custom.saleprice_name` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 Sq Ft Gym (Set B) | $242,528.80 | $285,328.00 | 242,528.80 | Package Price |
| 1,500 Sq Ft Gym (Set B) | $110,060.55 | $129,483.00 | 110,060.55 | Package Price |

Both carry a `saleprice_name` with a `sale_price` **equal to** the regular price. Against `compare_at_price` the banner rendered, because the compare-at is higher. Against the native price the comparison is equal-to rather than greater-than, so the banner drops out — and with the `{% else %}` skipped, both package PDPs lose their price display.

Fixed at all 8 call sites: each now computes the sale value and enters the banner branch only when the banner would actually render. A sale name alone is not a sale. This is the same condition the Total with Options resolver already uses, so the branch, the banner's own guard and the option total now agree on one definition of "there is a package price".

Found by the Codex review on this PR, which flagged the missing fallback. The underlying mismatch is older than defect 1's guard and was already live-reachable on both packages.

## Drift revert (`fd43fbb`)

`shopify[bot]` commit `52cfe65` re-applied the Boost AI Search & Filter drift to `config/settings_data.json`, `templates/collection.json` and `templates/search.json`. Merging it would have disabled Boost AI Search & Filter on collection and search pages store-wide. Those three files are byte-identical between `main` and `460e74f`, and the bot is their only author on this branch, so they were restored to their `main` state. The pricing diff is untouched by this revert.

## Verification performed

- **Scope**: `git diff --name-only main..HEAD` returns exactly the 13 files above; all five excluded paths confirmed absent.
- **Liquid integrity**: tag-balance check across all 12 changed `.liquid` files — all balanced. This also clears the relocated `{% endif %}` tags in the original diff.
- **Behaviour matrix**: the two live package states plus the blank, zero, equal-to and above-price cases. No case yields a blank price, and Total with Options always resolves to the figure the page displays.
- **Preview matched source**: MD5 manifest of all 13 changed files compared between preview theme `188142584124` and the branch — 13/13 match as of `460e74f`. The pricing files are unchanged by `fd43fbb`, so the preview's pricing behaviour is current; re-confirm the manifest at merge time along with the head SHA.
- **Preview is unpublished**; the `main` theme, products, metafields, prices, discounts and inventory were not modified.

## Known limitation — variant switching does not refresh the price block

Raised by the Codex review and confirmed in code. `handleUpdateProductInfo` in `assets/product-info.js` swaps only `#price-{{ section.id }}` and a fixed list of auxiliary IDs. The `.product__prices` block sits outside that region, so a variant change does not re-render it via the section swap.

Partly mitigated, and mostly pre-existing:

- `main-product-comb.liquid` and `main-product-variants.liquid` carry an inline `__pmMin` script whose `paint()` rewrites "As high as" and "You save" on form change, so those track variant changes on `product.combined-listings`, `product.variants` and `product.variants-pulley`.
- `paint()` does not know about `.price-banner`, in any section — but the banner was already variant-dependent before this PR (`current_price: compare_at_price`), so that staleness exists on `main` today and is not introduced here.
- Genuinely new: "As high as" moves from the product-level `custom.retail_price` to a variant-level value, and the banner-vs-price branch becomes variant-level. T

author: valdepeace
body:
Fixes #23044

Adds `@mastra/azure-ai-search`, a vector store provider backed by Azure AI Search. Supports create/upsert/query/update/delete on indexes, metadata filtering, hybrid (vector + text) search, and semantic ranking.

```ts
import { AzureAISearchVector } from '@mastra/azure-ai-search'

const store = new AzureAISearchVector({
  id: 'azure-search-vectors',
  endpoint: process.env.AZURE_AI_SEARCH_ENDPOINT!,
  credential: process.env.AZURE_AI_SEARCH_CREDENTIAL!,
})

await store.createIndex({ indexName: 'my-collection', dimension: 1536 })
await store.upsert({ indexName: 'my-collection', vectors, metadata })
```

Also fixes a handful of filter/semantic-search/hybrid-query bugs found while testing, and adds the store to the vector databases guide and reference docs.

 Supersedes #10146 — same feature, rebased on current main and with the blocking review feedback from that PR addressed.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## ELI5

This PR adds a Mastra connector for Azure AI Search. It lets applications store, find, update, and delete vectors in Azure with metadata filters, text search, semantic search, and hybrid search.

## Changes

- Adds the `@mastra/azure-ai-search` package.
- Adds index management, vector upsert, query, update, and deletion.
- Adds OData and Mastra metadata filtering.
- Adds semantic, hybrid, multi-vector, exact, and exhaustive search support.
- Adds Mastra Memory integration.
- Adds configurable schemas, vector fields, metadata indexes, semantic settings, HNSW settings, and compression.
- Adds credential, API key, connection-string, retry, custom-header, and HTTPS proxy configuration.
- Validates dimensions, index names, filter operators, and filter values.
- Fixes empty filters so empty arrays and `$in` filters match no documents.
- Prevents unsupported operators from producing unfiltered queries.
- Improves retry proxy handling, upload batching, deletion after upload, pagination, vector retrieval, metadata handling, and error reporting.
- Adds unit, integration, and cross-store conformance tests.
- Adds package documentation, API reference documentation, setup examples, and vector database guide coverage.
- Adds release changesets for the package and filter behavior fixes.

author: linuxdynasty
body:
Extracts the observability-coverage **materialization** intent family out of the
`internal/projector` root into `internal/projector/observabilitycoveragematerialization`,
continuing #6057 under epic #6053.

## Why a new package rather than a second builder in the sibling

The **correlation** family already lives in `internal/projector/observabilitycoverage`.
Its scoped `AGENTS.md` states the rule directly: do not widen that package's export
surface past its one `BuildObservabilityCoverageCorrelationReducerIntent`, because
every family in this series exports exactly one builder. Correlation and
materialization are different families that share a subject, not one family split
across two files.

## The builder now takes the neutral seam

It previously took root's `*reducerIntentFactIndex` and called
`index.firstOfKindMatching`. That method is a thin delegate to
`FirstOfKindMatching` on `projectorintent.FactLookup` — the same seam the sibling
correlation builder already consumes — so the child takes the lookup and makes the
identical call. Same index, same closed `observabilityResourceTypes` set, no
dependency on a root type.

## Two root files leave, not one

The child carries its own `factschema_decode_aws.go` rather than importing root's
`decodeAWSResource`: root imports this package to dispatch, so importing root back
would cycle — the same reason `internal/projector/ec2` and the sibling carry their
own. The filename is load-bearing, since the payload-usage gate globs
`factschema_decode*.go` recursively and AST-scans each body for a
`factschema.FactKindXxx` reference.

That move took the last caller of root's `decodeAWSResource`, and `go-lint` flagged
the orphan at commit time. Root's `factschema_decode_aws.go` contained only that
function, so it is deleted. Before removing it I checked what it would strand: its
two helpers, `newProjectorDecodeError` and `factschemaEnvelope`, each have many
other root callers, and the payload-usage gate stays satisfied because
`iaminstanceprofile`, `observabilitycoverage`, and this new package all carry their
own decode with the fact-kind reference.

`observabilityResourceTypes` moves with the family and remains one leg of the
documented three-way mirror with the sibling package and the reducer's
`observabilityResourceSignals`; the doc-trio records that in each place a reader
might look.

## Ledger

`internal/projector` ratchets **49 -> 47** — two files leave root. The digest was
recomputed from the final tree after the rebase rather than carried forward, the Go
mirror was regenerated from the TSV, no grandfather row was added for the child, and
only the `internal/projector` row differs from `main`.

## Verification

Exit codes captured directly, after the final edit, on the rebased head.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./...` | 0 |
| `go vet ./internal/projector/...` | 0 |
| `go test ./internal/projector/... -count=1` | 0 (32 packages) |
| `precommit-go.sh lint-all` | 0 issues |
| `precommit-go.sh dirgate-all` | 0 |
| `verify-package-docs.sh` | 0 |
| `verify-markdown-line-cap.sh --all` | 0 |
| `verify-telemetry-coverage.sh` | 0 |
| `verify-performance-evidence.sh` | 0 |
| local promotion gate | all gates passed, stamped `67c6ac0f9c86` |

`TestReducerIntentProbeCountMatchesDocumentedCount` parses
`scope_generation_intents.go` with `go/ast`, which is the shape that can pass
vacuously, so I mutation-tested it rather than trusting a green run: deleting one
probe block fails it (exit 1) and restoring returns it to green. The probe count is
unchanged by this move.

## One note on the gate history

An earlier run of this branch failed the path-triggered live lane at
`bootstrap-index` with `ping postgres: [::1]:15432 (localhost): tls`. That was
infrastructure, not the diff: the change touches only projector Go files, two docs
and the two ledger mirrors — no postgres, docker, compose, port or storage surface —
and a stale `eshu-6401-postgres-red` container from another worktree had been up two
days contending for the live gate's fixed port. The identical tree passed on a quiet
re-run.

**No-Regression Evidence** and **No-Observability-Change** markers for this change
live in the new package's `README.md`, per the hot-path evidence gate.

author: revarbat
body:
Consolidates the three throwaway scripts behind the recent parity work into one documented tool: `scripts/compare_docs_images.py`.

It exists because neither obvious approach works at library scale — eyeballing 2576 BOSL2 images is hopeless, and a pixel diff flags **every single one**, since the two renderers light and label things differently.

## The metric

IoU of each image's foreground mask, averaged over 4×4 blocks and thresholded at half coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| lighting | **drops out completely** — a shaded pixel is still foreground, so shading changes colour but never the mask |
| axes, ticks, label strokes | **mostly drop out** — a pixel or two wide, so the block average erases them while a solid body survives |
| missing / moved / wrongly-scaled model | **does not drop out** — the point |

Without the block-average step the thin features dominated the score: there are hundreds and they never land in quite the same place.

## Two subcommands

- `compare REF NEW [--json out.json]` — ranks, and calls out any image only one side produced (the loudest signal: either we failed, or the reference did — OpenSCAD crashes on BOSL2's `cuboid_10`, we render it).
- `delta BEFORE.json AFTER.json` — what a change moved, and **exits non-zero if anything moved backwards**, so a fix that quietly breaks another image cannot pass unnoticed.

That is what the evaluator 0.55.5 run was checked with: **6 improved, 0 regressed**.

## Honest about its limits

Documented in the module docstring and `docs/docsgen.md`: a thin 2D line drawing of a few hundred blocks scores badly for a 2–3 pixel offset, so a low score there means "look at this", not "this is broken" — sort by `ref_px` when triaging.

## Tests

Build tiny images rather than rendering anything, so they run in milliseconds while pinning exactly the claimed properties: a shade change scores 1.0, a 1px rule across the frame scores 1.0, a moved body below 0.4, a missing body 0.0, and `delta` fails on a regression.

**1281 tests pass.**

## Summary
Resolves #735 (9 USD / 123 coins bounty) by replacing source-text lifecycle assertions with behavioral tests proving activation resumes across claimable, claimed, submitted, and verifying states without duplicate contract creation or redundant planner runs.

## Key Changes
1. **Behavioral Lifecycle Reconciliation Engine (`scripts/lifecycle_activation_reconciliation.py`):**

## Summary

- Adds `pillars/design/src/screens/finance/settings.tsx`, a design-playground screen for the institutions + currencies settings page (fixture-backed, no backend wiring), plus supporting kit components (`settings-row`, `settings-delete-dialog`, `institutions-settings`, `currencies-settings`).
- Decision: institutions and currencies stay on **one page** — both are short, related reference lists minted inline from the account form (POPS-2810) and only ever edited/retired, never browsed at volume. Splitting into tabs or separate screens would cost a click for no payoff at this size.
- Decision: replace the plain `DataTable` + `AlertDialog` combo PR #4372 shipped (no design spec existed yet) with a `CRUDManagementSection` + row-list shell. No screen in `pillars/design` uses `DataTable` anywhere — the pillar's small managed lists (accounts) use card/row treatments instead — and `CRUDManagementSection` is the shared `@pops/ui` component already used in production for this exact shape of screen (media's `SourceManagementSection`/`DimensionManager`). Edit stays a modal `Dialog` (matches `account-form.tsx`'s precedent for entity edit) and delete keeps the themed `AlertDialog` (better than the `window.confirm` media's own consumer falls back to).
- Promotes the decision into `pillars/finance/app/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`: replaces `DataTable` columns (`institution-columns.tsx`/`currency-columns.tsx`, deleted) with a shared `SettingsRow` + `CRUDManagementSection`. `useInstitutionsSettings`/`useCurrenciesSettings` and the edit/delete dialogs are untouched — this is a UI-layer restyle only, behavior preserved.

body:
## What this builds

Adds a functional `nxyz-cloud/` implementation alongside cloudcomplyXUNIA:

- Go control-plane API with durable state
- worker registration + heartbeat agents
- capacity-aware CPU/RAM scheduler
- stale-node detection
- workload create/list/delete endpoints
- live operator dashboard
- Prometheus-compatible `/metrics`
- Docker Compose topology with two worker nodes
- smoke test + Make targets
- dedicated GitHub Actions CI gate
- beginner-oriented architecture README and Mermaid topology

## Validation already performed locally

- `go test ./...` ✅
- `go vet ./...` ✅
- controller build ✅
- agent build ✅
- end-to-end controller/agent registration ✅
- workload scheduling and resource accounting ✅
- `/healthz`, `/api/v1/system`, `/api/v1/nodes`, `/api/v1/workloads`, `/metrics` ✅

## Security boundary

This v0.1 schedules workload intent but deliberately does **not** grant remote agents arbitrary host/container execution. OCI execution should land only with authenticated node enrollment, mTLS, signed workload specs, image policy, and sandboxing.

## Reference note

The supplied `projectsecio/projects-cloud-lab` URL currently resolves unavailable/404, so no unverified code was copied from it. The architecture is original and uses this repository's existing cloudcomplyXUNIA layer as the planned NIST/AWS compliance plane.

# What does this implement/fix?

_dbopen() raises dbopen_cnt at the very end, once everything has succeeded, but the two failure paths after the open give the connection back through dbclose(), which lowers it unconditionally. a connection refused for being read-only, or one whose busy handler could not be set, takes the counter down without ever having raised it, so dbopen_cnt walks towards negative numbers for as long as ftl runs

the increment moves up to just after sqlite3_open_v2() returns success. that is the moment there is something to count, and the point from which dbclose() is the way back out

sqlite3_open_v2() also hands back a handle when it fails, and the sqlite documentation is explicit that resources are associated with it whether or not an error occurs. that path returned NULL and dropped it, so every failed open leaked an sqlite3 object. it closes the handle now, with a plain sqlite3_close() rather than dbclose(), because the connection was never counted and dbclose() would take a decrement with it

low impact. the counter feeds one line, the DEBUG_DATABASE "Database busy - waiting %d ms (dbopen: %d)" message, and a failed open is not the common case. but that line exists to say how many connections are open while the database is contended, which is exactly when someone reads it

## How to test the change during review

nothing user visible changes, it is by inspection: the counter is raised and lowered on the same paths now, and the failed-open path releases what sqlite handed it. full suite in the container is 194 bats, 151 pytest, 12, 25, 9

author: soliforte
body:
## Summary

**Drone tracker.** Kismet's UAV PHY attaches DJI DroneID (Wi-Fi and ANTSDR RF) and fingerprint records to devices. Kestrel now:
- draws any drone that reports its own position at that position, outside the device cluster, as a per-drone coloured disc with a heading nose;
- builds its track from Kismet's 128-point telemetry history, sorted by telemetry timestamp because the threaded packet chain does not keep the vector in order, and places the drone at the newest point;
- shows home point and operator position with a dashed link when broadcast, and fades a drone that stops reporting after a minute;
- optionally jumps to a drone the first time it is seen (setting, default on) with a Drones toggle in the controls and settings;
- keeps a normal marker with a drone glyph for fingerprinted drones without telemetry, and names model/serial in its popup.

In Kismet 2025.09 the Wi-Fi DroneID parser only decodes serial and position; altitude, speed, heading, home and operator only arrive via the RF path, and the popup shows them when present.

**Faster, cheaper sync.**
- New devices are pushed over the eventbus `NEW_DEVICE` topic with field simplification and appear before the next poll (handler accepts simplified or full records).
- Default refresh interval is 2 s (Kismet's own device table polls every second). Polling backs off up to 30 s when an incremental poll takes longer than half the interval and the status line reports it.
- Kismet's `devices/views/all/monitor.ws` was evaluated and rejected: its change detection captures a stack-local timestamp by reference into a timer that outlives it, and on a live capture it delivered 4 updates in 15 s while REST showed 63 modified devices.

**Fixes.** Drone markers no longer fetch Leaflet's default marker images (404s); tab activation plus map start can no longer run two parallel polling chains.

Adds `kestrel.getStats()` for poll/push counters and documents the feed design in the README.

## Test plan

- [x] Synthetic DJI DroneID beacon replay on live Kismet 2025.09: Kismet decodes serial, position and 40-point history; map jumps to the drone; track is a clean arc ending at the marker; popup correct; AP record gets the drone glyph.
- [x] Fresh-AP pcap replay: three new devices reach the map ~0.5 s after the source opens via `NEW_DEVICE`, ahead of the poll; live capture pushed further real devices.
- [x] 20 s window shows exactly one poll chain at the 2 s cadence, ~30 ms per poll on ~530 devices, no backoff, no marker-image 404s.
- [ ] Real DroneID traffic (Wi-Fi or ANTSDR) to confirm heading, altitude, home and operator rendering.

author: nishant803
body:
Title: feat: apply Summarization suggestions directly to AEM page content

Summary
- Adds POST /sites/:siteId/opportunities/:opportunityId/suggestions/aem-apply, a new endpoint that writes a suggestion's content directly into an AEM CS page's own content tree — editing the human-facing page. This is distinct from the existing edge-deploy endpoint, which only ever writes a bot-targeted overlay at the Tokowaka CDN edge and never touches AEM itself.
- For each suggestion: resolves data.url to an AEM pageId via the existing determineAEMCSPageId resolver (@adobe/spacecat-shared-utils, same one resolveDocumentPath already uses for other opportunity types), fetches the page's content tree + ETag, resolves transformRules.selector against it, and applies transformRules.action (insertAfter / insertBefore / appendChild / replace) as a JSON Patch.
- Handles two shapes of transformRules: a direct target (selector names the existing node to act on — today's Summarization case) and an anchor + tag (selector names an existing anchor, tag names a new heading element to create relative to it — e.g. a "missing heading" fix), so the same endpoint isn't limited to one suggestion archetype.
- Auth: forwards the caller's own bearer token to AEM, the same pattern the existing content-api-access autofix-check probe already uses against this API — no new credential/auth path introduced.
- Scoped to aem_cs delivery-type sites only; returns a 400 otherwise.
- Selector matching is intentionally narrow today (bare tag or tag#id, against title/heading components only) and fails closed — an unresolvable selector or unsupported action returns a per-suggestion 404/422 in the 207 response rather than guessing a placement.

author: aiagencyos
body:
## A charge nobody wrote down — G-207 (audit QM-20)

G-178 got the important half right. `whoPays` is an enum because whose bill it is
causes the argument, and there is no numeric price field because *"a figure printed
inside a fixed-price quotation becomes a commitment the agency cannot keep and did
not make."*

What it left was `charge` — **free text the model writes** — printed verbatim into a
client-facing document:

> Razorpay — payment collection. Billed to you directly by the provider, and not
> part of this price. **2% per transaction**

That two per cent came from a language model. Not from the client, not from
Razorpay, not from anybody at this agency. **It was the one number in the whole
quotation with no row behind it** — in a system whose central rule is that every
price belongs to somebody who wrote it down. `crm.refuse_unread_price` refuses
exactly this at the row for a WhatsApp message; the quotation had no equivalent.

## The shape is ADM-12's

§5.3 solved this once, for samples and demos: *"only from a list the Admin
maintains… the list is empty until the Admin fills it."* The same answer fits, for
the same reason — an agent may repeat what a person recorded and may not invent the
thing itself.

`crm.third_party_charges` holds the service, the Admin's own words (**text, not a
number**: real charges are *"2% + ₹3 per transaction"* and *"₹8,300 a year, billed by
Apple"*), a **source**, and **`checked_on`** — which is what QM-20 actually asked
for, since it says *current and reliable*, not merely *recorded*.

A confirmation date in the future is refused as its own outcome: it is the one input
that would make the staleness warning lie. Six-month staleness **warns and blocks
nothing** — refusing a draft because nobody revisited a fee page trades a real deal
for a tidy record, which is the trade G-168 and G-177 both declined.

**Empty list means no figures at all**, which is not a degraded mode: G-178 already
calls it *"the honest answer and the common one"*.

## The control is the resolver, not the prompt

The model is shown service, words and an eight-hex ref, and cites one with
`chargeRef` — a field whose regex refuses anything shaped like money, so a bad ref
**fails the whole draft** rather than being quietly tidied up.

`resolveIntegrationCharges` then reads the words back out of the table, org-scoped
and active-only, and **deletes anything the model wrote in `charge` for itself** — a
figure left there is indistinguishable downstream from one an Admin recorded. The
ref is deleted too, so nothing can look the charge up a second time and get a
different answer. It runs at all three drafting doors.

## Live — `verify-quotation-scope` §I, 60/60

**The existing section had to be corrected first, and that is the finding in
miniature.** An assertion read `typeof i?.charge === 'string'` and **passed** — on a
charge the stub itself wrote: *"2% per transaction on the client's own account."*
QM-20 reproduced in a fixture and asserted as correct. It now asserts the opposite.

§I proves the other half, because "dropped" is otherwise indistinguishable from a
feature that never worked: the Admin records a charge, a future date is refused, a
direct row write is refused (HTTP 400), and a quotation drafted **through the
agent's own door** carries the Admin's words and not the model's — then after
withdrawal, a later draft names the service with no figure.

**Red-proved twice**, against the rebuilt app:

| control removed | result |
| --- | --- |
| `delete item.charge` | the model's own 2% is back in the document — 58/60 |
| the active-only filter | a **withdrawn** charge goes on being cited — 59/60 |

## Two measurement findings

**The guard test asked the wrong schema.** It used `quotationDocumentSchema` — the
stored jsonb, deliberately `.loose()` with `.catch(null)` so one malformed entry
cannot take the understanding and the exclusions down with it. Every bad ref sailed
through it. The refusal belongs on `quotationScopeSchema`, where the model's words
arrive; asserting it on the stored schema was asserting it of the one schema whose
job is *not* to refuse.

**Then the positive twin failed on an invalid fixture** — five unrelated required
fields missing. Which meant every *"bad ref is refused"* case had been passing for
the wrong reason: **a negative assertion over an invalid fixture refuses everything,
including the thing it is supposed to permit.**

## Two deliberate edits, and one stale docblock

`the-quotation-says-what-it-is-made-of.test.ts` pinned *"you may NOT invent a
figure"* and `integrations: validated.data.integrations ?? null`. Both are replaced
by stronger claims — the absolute prompt rule, and the resolver at all three doors.

And `app/(internal)/portfolio/actions.ts` still said *"nothing in the repository
sends from this list yet"*, which stopped being true when G-197 landed. Corrected —
a docblock describing a system as it was is the defect class PR #359 was opened for.

**Full chain from a clean `db reset`: 69/69 verifiers, 0 failures.** `npm run check`
green: 3,128 tests.

**Stacked on [#375](https://github.com/AiAgencyOs/AgencyOs/pull/375) → … → [#362](https://github.com/AiAgencyOs/AgencyOs/pull/362)** — merge in order and each diff reduces to its own change.

## Not verified

The `/settings` section is not visually checked in this PR. The write path is
verified live through the same RPC the form calls, including the Admin-only refusal
and the direct-write refusal.

body: PR **1 of 3** in the cash-request revamp. Schema and backend for the budget ledger; the worksheet and the documents follow in PR 2 and PR 3. Decisions this implements are recorded in `doc/CASH_REQUEST_PROGRAMME_QUESTIONNAIRE.md` §10. ## What changed Every cash-request line now names the **budget line it spends** (`costing_line_id`), so a costing becomes the operations file's fulfilment budget and the cash request draws it down, line by line: | | Meaning | | --- | --- | | **Budget** | the costing line, TTC | | **Committed** | claims against it from APPROVED requests | | **Disbursed** | apportioned from the instalments actually paid | | **Remaining** | Budget − Committed, **which may go negative** | Import defaults each line to what is **left**: claim 100 000 of a 150 000 Port Charges line today, and the next request opens showing 50 000. New: `GET /costings/:id/budget`, `GET /cash-requests/kpis`, `POST /cash-requests/:id/close-balance`, `POST /cash-requests/:id/payments/:paymentId/receipt`. Migration `12771` + seed `9099`. ## Why `cash_request_line` carried a label and an amount and **nothing that said which budget line the money came from**. `importCostingLines` read the approved costing, copied the label and `qty × unit_cost`, and threw the provenance away — so selecting the same costing twice produced the same lines at full value, twice, with nothing anywhere objecting. The legacy had the identical hole. It is why its own reconciliation module made `costing_line_id` **mandatory** on `ocr_line` and then had a human *re-type* the actuals: the one system that knew what had been disbursed against a budget line could not say so. ``` $ grep -in "cash|disburs|advance" admin/costing-module.php 380: Cash Request ``` One hit — a sidebar link. Same for the reconciliation screen. Budget → cash → actual was three manual re-typings and the three modules could not see each other. ### The gates, per the owner's decisions - An **OPS request needs an `APPROVED_LOCKED` costing** to be submitted at all (Q5). - **Every line must name a budget line** — there is no off-budget spend. An unbudgeted charge is amended into the costing and re-approved (Q4). - A claim over the balance may be **submitted with a written reason** — carrying `costing_id` and `doc_number` so the screen can offer the unlock in one click — and may **not be approved** (Q3). - **Remaining may go negative.** A line amended below what is already committed shows over-consumed rather than clamping at zero; the clamp would hide the one case somebody has to act on (Q6). ### A costing-side change that was not optional `costing.replaceLines` deleted every line and re-inserted, so **every `costing_line_id` changed on every DRAFT save**. A budget link to a uuid regenerated on every amendment breaks at exactly the moment it matters. It upserts in place now, keyed on the logical identity `diffLines` has always used, and the FK is `RESTRICT` — the service names the requests holding a line rather than letting a raw `23503` surface. ### Four defects fixed along the way Two were found only by standing up a real Postgres and driving the flows. Both are in paths the pure tests exercise correctly — the arithmetic was never wrong; the SQL feeding it was. - **A settled request's disbursed share was discounted twice.** `CLOSE_BALANCE` rewrites the claim to `settled_amount`, which is *already* that line's share of the cash that moved; scaling it again by the paid ratio meant a request settled at 1 000 000 reported 377 358 disbursed. - **An approved request was measured against a budget it was already inside.** Its own claim is committed, so `committed_elsewhere` counted the request itself and every approved request read as a breach of the budget it had just been approved against. `budgetForCosting` now takes `excludeCashRequestId`, which every read *on behalf of* a request passes; the registry read still counts everything, because there the question is "how much is left now" rather than "how much was available to me". - **`justify` went through `replaceLines`**, and its payload carries no line ids — so once a line carried `costing_line_id`, every justification would have deleted the originals and silently lost the budget link, and the file would appear to regain headroom it had already spent. It records spend **in place** now, which is also the right model: by then the lines are frozen facts. - **`action-authz.filterAllowed` swallowed every error** while filtering the AI catalogue, so a database outage inside the grant lookup produced an empty catalogue — indistinguishable from a correct "you may run nothing". It re-raises anything that is not a denial, and burns down a silent-catch baseline entry. ### Also in - `currency` + `exchange_rate_to_xaf` + `amount_xaf`, inherited from the costing for an OPS request. Without them a EUR costing imported as bare numbers and the request, the régie advance and the ledger posting were all wrong *together*. - `qty × unit_cost × VAT` back on the line — the legacy shape, and the one the voucher template has been printing `qty: 1` into — plus `line_no` so lines stop reshuffling on every save. - `CLOSE_BALANCE` settles a part-paid request at what actually moved and releases the rest of the commitment. Without it a request holds budget for ever against cash that will never move. - `REJECTED` is no longer terminal: it reopens to `DRAFT` keeping its reference, and a rejection now demands a reason. The legacy allowed both and we did not. - `received_by` / `received_at` / `received_ack_kind`, **per instalment** — the legacy's single `disbursed_time` on the header cannot say who took the second tranche. - `permission` gains `can_export`, `can_validate`, `can_disburse`, backfilled from what gated them yesterday so **no role loses access on deploy**. The AI action map moves with `rbac.js` so an assistant is never gated more loosely than a person at a screen. ### One deliberate non-change, and one recorded gap `/disburse` keeps `requireCapability("APPROVER")` **on top of** its new `can_disburse` grant. Dropping it would have *widened* the gate, because `can_disburse` is backfilled from `can_approve` — a tenant that had used the authority overlay to take disbursement away from some approvers would silently have got it back. With both gates, `can_disburse` can only ever narrow disbursement below approval, which is the direction that matters. A cashier without approval rights is still expressible: APPROVER is an overlay, not a grant. Separately: the AI path checks the module grant but **not** the authority overlay, so an assistant can run an action a person would be refused. That is pre-existing and is not widened here; closing it needs a column on `ai_action_catalogue`, which does not belong in a change about budgets. Recorded in `action-authz.js`, the file that would host the fix. ## How it was verified - **45 new unit tests** (`tests/unit/cash-request-budget.test.js`), all pure: the budget arithmetic, the over-consumed case, breaches totalled per budget line, the settlement split summing to the franc, line identity across an amendment (including two container sizes of one item, and a genuinely repeated key), the migration's shape, and both gates on the disburse route. - **15 integration tests** across two new suites, against a provisioned tenant — the owner's own worked example and the full gate flow. Both suites exist because writing them found the two SQL defects above. Self-skip without `DATABASE_URL`, like every other suite there. - Four existing suites updated where the change was deliberate: `REJECTED` is no longer terminal; `export` maps to `can_export`; the grant cache key carries a shape version; the AI verb allow-list gained `validate`/`disburse`. - **`npm run ci` — 32/32 gates green.** Plus, locally against a scratch Postgres: platform migrated, tenant provisioned from nothing, the tenant set replayed as a no-op, th

author: alex-dev-neo
body:
Fixes osmandapp/OsmAnd#25778.

### Problem

With the weather plugin enabled and no weather data downloaded, the OpenGL renderer crashes with a native `SIGSEGV` on a Qt thread-pool thread within about a minute of panning the map:

```
Cause: null pointer dereference (fault addr 0x8)
#00 OsmAnd::TileSqliteDatabase::isOpened() const+0
#01 OsmAnd::WeatherTileResourceProvider_P::obtainGeoTile(...)+1632
#02 OsmAnd::WeatherTileResourceProvider_P::ObtainTileTask::run()+1060
...
#07 OsmAnd::GeoTileObjectsProvider_P::obtainData(...)+2420
```

`getGeoTilesDatabase()` can return `nullptr`, but `obtainGeoTile()` and `obtainGeoTileTime()` called `isOpened()` on the result unguarded. All other call sites — `importTileData()`, `calculateTilesSize()`, `removeTileDataBefore()`, `removeTileData()`, `closeProvider()`, and every `getRasterTilesDatabase()` use — already check for null.

This is a regression from 55f5799 ("Use separate weather_tiffs.db"), which replaced the always-non-null `_geoTilesDb` member with a `QHash<WeatherSource, ...>` lookup and added null checks to the other call sites, but not to these two.

There are two ways the lookup comes back empty:

1. The constructor fills the map eagerly and inserts only on a successful `open()`, with no later retry. A single failed open — cache directory removed between manager creation and lazy provider construction, read-only filesystem, no free space — leaves the source without a database for the rest of the session, and every subsequent `obtainGeoTile()` crashes. Raster databases are unaffected because `getRasterTilesDatabase()` creates them on demand.
2. `WeatherSource::Undefined` is part of the public enum and is handled explicitly elsewhere (`WeatherRasterLayerProvider.cpp:53`). `getWeatherSourcePrefix()` maps unknown sources to `gfs_`, but the map lookup used the raw enum value, which was never inserted.

### Changes

* Guard both dereferences with `if (geoDb && geoDb->isOpened())`. `obtainGeoTile()` already falls through to `unlockGeoTile()` and returns `-1` for empty data, so lock bookkeeping and the caller contract are unchanged.
* Create geo databases lazily in `getGeoTilesDatabase()`, using the same read-lock / write-lock / double-check shape as `getRasterTilesDatabase()`, so a failed open can recover. No call site holds `_geoDbLock` while calling it — all of them acquire it afterwards — so the read-to-write upgrade introduces no deadlock. The eager creation in the constructor is kept, it is just no longer the only chance.
* Add `getStorageWeatherSource()`, which resolves anything other than GFS/ECMWF to GFS, and use it for the geo and raster database map keys and in `isEmpty()`. Without it, lazy creation would open a second `TileSqliteDatabase` over the same `gfs_*.db` file for `Undefined`.

### Testing

`WeatherTileResourceProvider_P.cpp` compiles cleanly for `aarch64-none-linux-android21` with the project's own flags; only the two warnings that were already present in the file remain.

author: sommmen
body:
## Summary

Found while live-retesting un_query's Roslyn engine against OPG Platform's CommerceDbContext (which derives from IdentityDbContext<TUser, TRole, TKey>), right after PR #24 merged. It broke **every single query** against any target DbContext whose base class or public surface reaches an assembly in SharedFrameworkAssemblyNames — not just queries that reference that assembly's types directly.

## Root cause

QueryCompiler.GetReferences only added MetadataReferences for:
- a small hardcoded BuiltInReferenceAssemblyNames allowlist (BCL types only),
- the target's own AssemblyPath + LoadedAssemblyPaths,
- the server's own QueryExecutionException/DbContext assemblies,
- options.AdditionalReferenceAssemblyNames (opt-in config).

It never referenced assemblies in SharedFrameworkAssemblyNames — these are deliberately excluded from 	arget.LoadedAssemblyPaths (they resolve via the default AssemblyLoadContext instead, per TargetAssemblyLoadContext.LoadedAssemblyPaths's own doc comment). Since CommerceDbContext : IdentityDbContext<...> and IdentityDbContext lives in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore (a shared assembly), the Roslyn compiler had zero reference to it, so compiling *any* UserQuery : CommerceDbContext subclass failed with 'IdentityDbContext<>' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced....

## Fix

GetReferences now also iterates AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies() and adds a reference for any assembly whose simple name is in SharedFrameworkAssemblyNames.Value — these are guaranteed already loaded into the default ALC by the time a query compiles, mirroring the same allowlist TargetAssemblyLoadContext.Load already treats as shared.

## Testing

- Added 	ests/Fixtures/IdentityApp (a minimal IdentityDbContext<IdentityUser>-derived fixture reproducing the exact shape) and a new QueryCompilerTests.CompileAsync_TargetDbContextDerivesFromIdentityDbContext_CompilesSuccessfully regression test. Verified it reproduces the original bug's exact error message when the fix is reverted, and passes with the fix restored.
- Full suite: `dotnet test dotnet-efcore-mcp.slnx` — **168/168 passed** (167 pre-existing + 1 new).
- Live-verified via the real MCP stdio protocol against a live SQL Server `CommerceDbContext` (OPG Platform, 177 entities, `IdentityDbContext`-derived) with the Roslyn engine enabled:
  - Anonymous-type projection (`Select(c => new { c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName })`) now compiles and executes, returning real rows — previously failed to compile for every query regardless of shape.
  - Explicit `Join` across two DbSets (`Orders.Join(Customers, ...)`) also compiles and executes end-to-end.
  - `Customers.Count()` still returns the same result (15483) as the DynamicLinq engine, confirming no behavior change for the existing engine.

author: sgort
body:
Renders a swimlane process diagram for **all twelve RIP phases**, derived from the BPMN Operaton actually has deployed, and deletes the hand-maintained R2.1-only model it replaces.

## Why

The Infra-board drew one phase, R2.1, from constants in `rip-model.ts`. Those constants had gone stale against the deployed BPMN, which is what produced the wrong diagram that started this work. A hand-kept copy of something the engine already knows will drift again, so this removes the category rather than extending it.

## How

```
Operaton --/process-definition/key/{key}/xml--> operaton.service (phaseBpmnCache)
                                                        |
                          packages/backend/src/rip-swimlane/bpmn-swimlane.ts
                                          parseSwimlane(xml, phaseCode)   <- pure, no I/O
                                                        |
                                GET /v1/rip/phases/:code/model
                                                        |
                        usePhaseSwimlane(code) --> <PhaseSwimlane model=... />
```

Fetched **by process-definition key, not definition id**, so a phase with no running instance still resolves and mock portfolio rows get a diagram too. The parser is pure, so it is tested directly against the twelve real `.bpmn` files.

## Deliberate, agreed changes to what R2.1 looks like

- Its 7 curated lanes become the BPMN's 9; the merged "Intake-overleg / Accordering" lane disappears
- Fewer document badges — only `ronl:documentRef`-tagged tasks get one, so a badge now means what the BPMN asserts rather than what someone typed
- Rework lines move into a reserved band below the lanes; canvas grows 616→654px

## Defects this found that a green suite could not

Verified in the browser by the reviewer after the automated work was complete:

- **38 nodes were invisible across the twelve phases** (R5.2 alone lost 12). Nodes sharing a lane and column drew at identical coordinates. R2.1 is the only phase with zero collisions — the one phase with a hand-authored predecessor to compare against, and the only one where the bug cannot occur. The suite passed because it asserted that nodes rendered, never that they rendered anywhere distinct.
- **Finished phases drew entirely uncoloured.** History came from the *current* instance while the diagram came from the *selected* phase. A past phase's own history lives on a different, completed instance, now resolved via `businessKey`.
- **The failure panel flashed on every project open** while the fetch was in flight.
- **A fake-success render** — `{ data: <empty model>, loading: false, error: false }` — introduced by the fix for an earlier error-flash, and worse than what it replaced.
- **Rework loops drew coincident lines**, then drew *through* nodes once that was first "fixed".

## Testing

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Backend | 1998 passed / 3 skipped (86 suites) |
| Frontend | 1095 passed (109 files) |
| `bpmn-swimlane.ts` | 100% branch |
| `doc-label.ts` | 100% branch |
| `PhaseSwimlane.tsx` | 98.3% branch |
| `rip-model.ts` | 100% branch |
| `ProjectDetail.tsx` | 83.45% → 88.05% branch |

Every file touched clears the repo's 80% per-file branch floor.

## Known and accepted

- `getWipStepInfo` stays R2.1-only, so the WIP tab still shows "—" for Huidige stap/Rol/Dagen on R2.2–R6.1. Out of scope by design: generalising it needs an answer for R5.2's parallel weekly cycle and R6.1's three labelled streams.
- `FASE1_NODE_ROLE` (19 entries) and `FASE1_DOCS` remain hand-maintained, because `stepRole` cannot be derived without giving `getWipStepInfo` the phase model. Both are guarded from two ends — a backend test against the parsed BPMN, a frontend test against the real tables — since nothing may import across the package boundary. Neither guard alone is sufficient, and both say so in their own comments.
- The twelve `.bpmn` files are **parser fixtures**, not a runtime source. Nobody has verified they still match ACC; a drifted fixture would make the known-answer tests check the wrong reality.
- The backend jest config has no `coverageThreshold`, so the branch floor is convention rather than CI-gated.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-rip-phase-swimlane-derivation-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-rip-phase-swimlane-derivation.md`

author: take-cheeze
body:
## Summary

This module's existing gated-FFN (SwiGLU/GeGLU-style) support only recognized the two-separate-producer shape (`Mul(gate_proj(x), up_proj(x))`). It did not recognize the equally common single-fused-producer-then-split shape used by real, currently-shipped models — Microsoft's own Phi-3/Phi-3.5 family (`onnxruntime-genai`-exported):

```python
# real HF transformers Phi3MLP.forward
up_states = self.gate_up_proj(hidden_states)   # ONE Linear, out_features = 2*intermediate_size
gate, up_states = up_states.chunk(2, dim=-1)    # traces to a Split node
up_states = up_states * self.activation_fn(gate)
```

**The core correctness challenge**: `gate` and `up` are two halves of the *same* physical weight tensor — column `i` and column `H+i` represent one physical neuron and must always be kept/dropped together, a single-tensor co-selection constraint rather than the "two independent tensors, same index set" rule the existing two-producer case uses.

## Empirically confirmed facts

- Live schema (`Split`, since_version 18): `num_outputs`/`axis` attributes, optional `split` sizes input — confirmed independently in this review too.
- Native `SwiGLU` (opset 28+) support already existed in this module from an earlier round; this PR is a second, independent reuse of that existing infrastructure, not something newly introduced here.
- Verified the matcher's core topology guard directly: `if split_a is not split_b or half_a == half_b: continue` — both operands of the combining `Mul`/`SwiGLU` must trace back (via `_trace_split_half_backward`) to the *same* `Split` node object identity and *different* halves, ruling out two coincidentally-similar-but-distinct tensors.
- Verified the co-selection logic directly: `_plain_branch_importance` (reused unchanged) computes a genuinely *joint* root-sum-square (or L1) importance per row index across `[gate_half_nk, up_half_nk]` — not two independent rankings — then `keep` is chosen once and applied at both offsets via `global_keep = concatenate([keep, keep + h])`.
- The adversarial test constructs per-neuron gate/up magnitude pairs where ranking by either half alone would pick a different keep-set than the correct combined ranking (`correct_keep=[0,1,2]` vs. `gate_only_keep=[0,2,3]` vs. `up_only_keep=[1,2,4]`), and asserts the real code picks the combined-ranking set — independently reviewed and confirmed to actually prove the property it claims to.
- Correctness confirmed end-to-end: the pruned model's output matches an independently hand-pruned reference model to 0.0 max abs diff via a real `InferenceSession` run.

## What's added / scope

New `_SplitGatedChain` family (dataclass, `_find_split_gated_chains` matcher, `_apply_split_gated_chains` slicer), reusing `_match_producer`, `_UNARY_PASS_THROUGH`, `_walk_to_consumer`, and `_plain_branch_importance` unchanged. Wired into `apply_structured_pruning` (full) and `apply_structured_wanda_pruning` (plain weight-magnitude fallback only). Reuses the existing `_iter_subgraphs` loop — works inside nested subgraphs automatically.

**Supported**: last-axis `Split` (auto or explicit `[H,H]` sizes, rewritten to `[keep_count,keep_count]` post-prune, with a guard against double-rewriting a shared split-sizes initializer with conflicting values), combine via plain `Mul` (either operand order) or native `SwiGLU`.

**Declined** (documented, not silently mishandled): Conv, quantized producer/consumer, dynamic split-size input, unequal/3-way split, decomposed SiLU, a bias-Add between producer and Split, `global_sparsity` mode. `analyze_pruning_sensitivity`'s dry-run mirror raises `NotImplementedError` for this family, mirroring the existing `Concat`-merged-chain precedent.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_pruning.py -q` — 766 → 781 passed, zero regressions (15 new tests)
- [x] `ruff format --check` / `ruff check` — clean
- [x] `mypy onnxsim/pruning.py` — 0 errors, unchanged from master's baseline
- [x] Core correctness against an independently reconstructed already-pruned reference, via real `InferenceSession` execution (0.0 max abs diff)
- [x] Adversarial paired-importance test (see above)
- [x] Declined/out-of-scope topology cases left byte-unchanged
- [x] Subgraph-nested (`If` branch) case

I independently re-verified the `Split` schema, confirmed `SwiGLU` support was genuinely pre-existing infrastructure (not newly introduced here), read the matcher's same-Split-node/different-half identity guard in full, confirmed `_plain_branch_importance` computes genuinely joint per-neuron importance across both halves, read and confirmed the adversarial test actually proves the paired-co-selection property, and ran the entire test/ruff/mypy suite myself in a clean environment before pushing.

body:
Adds .github/dependabot.yml.

- All security fixes per ecosystem arrive in **one grouped PR** instead of one per package.
- Weekly (Mon 06:00 IST) version updates, grouped: one PR for dev dependencies, one for minor/patch bumps of runtime deps. Majors stay individual.
- Docker base images and GitHub Actions kept current the same way.
- Max 5 open Dependabot PRs per ecosystem.

Ecosystems: npm

Part of the Sprinto vulnerability-SLA cleanup.

# What does this implement/fix?

follow-up to #3053, where DL6ER suggested this

the assets are generated into the build tree since #3053, but docs.h includes them with quotes, and a quoted include is searched next to the including file before the include path is consulted. a hex/ directory left in src/api/docs/ by a build from before that change is found first and goes on being found, with nothing left that could ever overwrite it. removing that directory at configure time was the guard against exactly this

angle brackets do not search next to the including file, so a leftover cannot shadow anything: api_docs carries CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR on its include path, and PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR/src next to it, where a stale src/api/docs/hex is not reachable as hex/... either. the guard goes with the quotes

low impact, it removes a workaround rather than fixing a live bug. the guard does its job today, this makes it unnecessary rather than makes something work that did not

## How to test the change during review

the mechanism on its own: two files in one directory including the same name, one quoted and one angled, with a second copy of the header on the -I path. gcc -H shows the quoted one reading the header beside it and the angled one reading the header from -I

in the tree: build, then plant a src/api/docs/hex/index_html.h containing an #error and rebuild without reconfiguring, with cmake --build cmake_ci rather than build.sh, since build.sh reruns cmake and on development the guard would sweep the file first. on development the build stops with that #error, on this branch it is ignored. full suite is 194 bats, 151 pytest, 12, 25, 9

author: suresh2692
body:
## Problem

The desk kept rendering **unstyled** after deploys — `/assets/**` 404 — on both stacks (`a2c-backend.oanstaging.com` staging_aws and `a2c-backend-development.oanstaging.com` develop). #73 and #75 both attempted a fix and both failed: the served asset manifest ended up **exactly one build behind** every deploy (develop-29 rendered develop-28's hashes; staging-aws-6 rendered staging-aws-5's).

## Root cause (confirmed on the box)

- Frappe caches `assets.json` in the **cache Redis** under a **shared (site-independent) key**.
- `redis-cache` is **not** recreated on deploy, so the **previous build's manifest survives** the image bump. New workers find it already cached (a HIT) and never re-read the new on-disk manifest → every hashed `/assets` URL points at the old file → 404 → unstyled desk.
- Two traps defeated the earlier "robust" fix:
  - **`bench clear-cache` is per-site and does not evict the shared `assets_json` key** (only `flushall` does).
  - **Restarting only the backend** lets a still-running `queue-*`/`scheduler` worker re-write the stale manifest back into Redis right after the flush.

Verified live: on-disk manifest was correct (`RFVWNJN6`), Redis held 372 keys with the stale (`MBDI7OJ7`) manifest; `flushall` + restart made it render correctly.

## Fix

Deterministic **stop → flush → start**: take every frappe process down, flush the cache Redis while nothing can write to it, then start them so each boots and reads the current on-disk manifest. `redis-cache`/`redis-queue`/`db` stay up; only cache contents are dropped.

Plus a **variable-free post-deploy verification** (curl the served `login.bundle` hash vs the on-disk asset, `cmp` on files — no shell vars/`$`/backslash so nothing needs escaping through the heredoc) that **fails the deploy** on a stale-manifest regression.

Applied to:
- `ci/deploy-ec2.sh` — develop deploy (`:8080`)
- `Jenkinsfile` staging_aws stage — staging_aws deploy (`:8090`)
