author: tamnd
body:
Closes the last box on #303.

A builtin the walk to the IR does not recognise became a call to the name the program wrote. No object file defines a name with that prefix, so the program failed at the linker on a name its author never typed, which is the worst place for the news to arrive: a builtin is the one thing a programmer does not expect to have to provide. `long f(unsigned x) { return __builtin_clz(x); }` used to compile to `call __builtin_clz` and now says this instead.

```
t.c:1:28: error: `__builtin_clz` is not implemented yet [E0686]
t.c:1:28: note: a call to it would go to a symbol no object file defines, so this is refused here rather than at the link
```

The rule is the table's rather than a list of names. A row in `features.toml` whose status is not implemented and which carries no library of its own is a name nothing here builds anything for and nothing outside here answers, so the two together are exactly the set, and it is the same set `__has_builtin` already says no about. That is eighty rows today, thirty seven of them spelled `__builtin_` and the rest the older `__sync_` and `__atomic_` families.

The refusal is in the walk rather than in the checking, because what is wrong is the call and not the name. `sizeof` does not evaluate its operand, so the type of a call to one of these is still answered and `sizeof(__builtin_clz(x))` is still four, which is what gcc does with it. A program that defines a function with one of these names itself gets the function it wrote.

Two rows move to implemented with this, which are `__builtin_types_compatible_p` and `__builtin_offsetof`. Both have worked for a while and neither is a call, so the parser reads them and nothing ever asked the table about either one, which is how the rows stayed wrong for free. They are not free now that the status column decides whether a call to a name is refused, and they were already costing `__has_builtin` an answer of no about two builtins this compiler has.

The golden case for the type generic builtins loses its blessed IR, which was thirteen calls to symbols nothing defines. What that case is for is the typed tree beside it, and the suite already has a shape for a case the walk refuses, so what it checks now is that the refusal happens rather than that unlinkable output keeps coming out the same way.

## What it found

Run against the corpora on a linux x86-64 host with gcc 16.2.0 as the reference, this moves ninety eight cases from passing `check` to being refused by it. Every one of them was producing IR with a call to a symbol nothing defines, so none of them is a new gap and none of them was ever going to link. What they are is a measurement of which builtins are missing, which was not readable before because the failure arrived at the linker if it arrived at all.

Ninety of the ninety eight are gcc torture, and the split by which builtin each reaches first is forty one byte swap, thirteen overflow checked arithmetic, twelve of the small ones, ten about the frame, five bit counting, four unreachable, four byte swap written by the program itself, and one atomic. Three are c-testsuite, three are tcc, and two are sqlite.

Forty seven of the ninety eight ask for no builtin at all. They include a glibc header, which defines three static inline functions over the byte swap builtins, and this compiler emits a static function nothing refers to, so a program that never mentions a byte swap carries three calls to one. That is #308, filed with this, and it is the single change that takes the most of these back.

Six issues were filed for what the rest of them are waiting on: #307 for the byte swaps, #309 for the overflow checked arithmetic, #310 for the bit counting, #311 for the atomics, #312 for the three that ask about the frame, and #313 for the four that are one instruction or none. The exclusion lists in tamnd/rucc-compat name them, one block per issue, and the harness fails a run where an entry has started passing, so each block comes off when the work lands.

## Checks

`cargo xtask ci` is clean. On a linux x86-64 host with gcc 16.2.0, `exec` over c-testsuite is 621 of 660 with zero stale, unchanged, and `check` is at zero failing and zero stale over every corpus that has a list.

author: pakkapoti
body:
Two day-one gates from the production-readiness audit. Both are self-contained code — no hosting decision, no spend, no new dependency.

## Bound resume uploads

The handler read the whole uploaded file into memory with no size limit and took the extension straight from the filename. One large upload could exhaust memory or fill the disk, and with a single instance that is the whole site.

- Capped at **5 MB**, restricted to `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.txt`, `.md`.
- Streamed in 64 KB chunks, so peak memory is one chunk rather than the file.
- Written to a `.part` sibling and moved into place only once complete — a refused or interrupted upload leaves no partial file and **never replaces the resume a candidate already had**.
- The dashboard says which rule was hit, and that the previous resume is untouched.

This bounds what the app reads and stores, not what a client may *send*. A request-body limit belongs at the proxy in front of it, and the code says so where someone will look for it.

## Log structurally, with request ids

Only `app/mailer.py` logged anything and nothing configured logging at all, so "it broke at 2pm" had no route to the request behind it.

- New `app/logging_config.py` emits every record as one JSON object on stdout (`LOG_LEVEL`, default `INFO`).
- Middleware tags each request with an id that rides a `ContextVar` onto every record produced while serving it, and returns it in `X-Request-ID`.
- An id supplied by a proxy is reused so a trace spans hops — but only when it looks like an id. A forged value that could smuggle a newline into a log line is replaced.
- The per-request line carries method, path, status, duration and user, and is emitted in a `finally`, so a request that **raises** is still recorded. An unlogged 500 is the one you most need to find later.
- The mailer's bootstrap handler and uvicorn's access log are dropped, so nothing is logged twice.

```json
{"ts": "2026-09-04T07:03:28+0000", "level": "INFO", "logger": "catchablepro.access",
 "msg": "request", "request_id": "810ec04cd3c030e0", "method": "POST",
 "path": "/candidate/profile", "status": 303, "duration_ms": 8.85, "user_id": 1}
```

## Tests

**195 tests (17 new).** Also driven against a running server:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Request ids | flow into `X-Request-ID` and every log line |
| Proxy-supplied id | reused; a forged one with a newline is replaced |
| 6 MB upload | refused → `?resume_error=size`, no `.part` left, previous resume intact |
| Valid upload | still saves and still auto-detects skills |
| Access logging | exactly one line per request, correct `user_id`, no uvicorn duplicate |

## Still open (needs you, not code)

The two launch **blockers** are untouched because both hinge on a decision rather than a diff: persistence (`render.yaml` is `plan: free` with no disk, so data is wiped on every deploy) and transactional email (`EMAIL_BACKEND: console`, so verification and password-reset mail reaches nobody).

body:
Workspace-originated prompts (cron fires, peer and gotify deliveries, kicks, and the auto-continuation after a transient server error) dispatched while the target session's turn is in flight now emit a `PromptQueuedWhileBusy` signal, and the TUI counts them into the same queued-send bridge a typed mid-turn submit arms, so the spinner stays open across the gap instead of settling. The reducer counts only into a live (Running) bucket and the workspace signals only on a successful dispatch, so a settled bucket or a failed send can't seed a phantom bridge.

Known residual: a workspace dispatch landing inside the re-open gap itself still goes uncounted when no session_state_changed mirror is present, since the workspace has no queued-turn signal of its own at that point; whether it signals is CLI-version-dependent, and the 90s force-settle bounds it either way.

body:
## 概要

初心者でも理解して覚えられる、目的から逆引きできる Linux コマンド集(`docs/linux-commands.md`)を新規追加しました。

## 内容

既存の [`docs/beginner-guide.md`](https://github.com/ns7jp/ns7jp/blob/main/docs/beginner-guide.md) と同じ「目的 → コマンド → 何を見て判断するか」の3点セットのトーンに合わせ、次の8カテゴリを詳細に整理しています。

1. 基本操作・移動・自分の状況を知る(`pwd` `cd` `ls` `tree` `history` `man`/`--help` など)
2. ファイル・ディレクトリの操作と中身の確認(`touch` `mkdir` `cp` `mv` `rm` `cat` `less` `tail -f` など)
3. 探す・見つける(`find` `grep` `which` `locate` など)
4. 権限・所有者・ユーザー管理(`chmod` `chown` `umask` `useradd` `sudo` など)
5. プロセス・サービス管理(`ps` `top` `kill` `systemctl` `journalctl` など)
6. ディスク・ファイルシステム・圧縮アーカイブ(`df` `du` `lsblk` `mount` `tar` `gzip` など)
7. ネットワークの確認と接続(`ip a` `ping` `ss` `curl` `dig` `ssh` `rsync` など)
8. テキスト処理・パイプ・シェルの便利機能・自動化(パイプ/リダイレクト、`sort`/`uniq`/`awk`/`sed`、`crontab`、`apt`/`dnf` など)

各コマンドには、破壊的操作への注意書き(`rm`、`chmod -R`、`kill -9` など)、Ubuntu(apt)と RHEL 系(dnf/yum)の違い、初心者がつまずきやすい点をあわせて記載しています。

`docs/beginner-guide.md` からも本ページへの導線(コマンド表の下、および「次に読むページ」)を追加しました。

## 作成方法

各カテゴリの下書きと技術的な正確性のレビュー(コマンド・オプション・出力例の検証、Markdown構造の確認)を分けて実施し、レビューで見つかった誤り(例: `touch` の説明、`chown` のコロン省略時の挙動、出力例の数値不整合など)を修正したうえで組み立てています。

## テスト計画

- [x] 見出し階層(`##`/`###`)の一貫性、見出しの重複がないことを確認
- [x] 全11テーブルの列数の整合性をスクリプトで確認
- [x] 相対リンク(`./beginner-guide.md`、`../LEARNINGS.md` など)のリンク先が実在することを確認
- [ ] CI(markdownlint / mermaid-parse / link-check)が green になることを確認

author: easly1989
body:
Phase 1 of #337. Fixes the data-quality problems seen in real testing: bank sync re-created hand-entered / schedule-posted transactions, imported everything as non-reconciled, and never pulled pending operations.

The new reconciliation is **opt-in for bank sync only** (a `PreviewParsed` flag), so CSV/QIF/OFX file imports behave exactly as before.

## What changed

- **Status**: `booked → Reconciled`, `pending → Cleared`. A still-pending import is **settled up to booked** when the booked row later arrives (same provider ref).
- **Match against existing transactions**: an incoming bank row is matched against an existing **manual or schedule-posted** transaction (one with no import ref) by **exact amount within ±7 days**. A unique match **merges** into it — attaching the bank ref, upgrading the status, correcting the date, and **taking the bank's description as the memo** (per maintainer: on a reconciled row the bank wording replaces the old memo). Category/tags/payee are never touched; the existing info/payment-mode are kept only when the bank supplies none. Several candidates → left **ambiguous** and imported as new for later review.
- **Pending**: also fetch `transaction_status=PDNG` (best-effort) and merge, since many ASPSPs (Intesa included) return only booked by default.

## Implementation

- `ReconcileCandidate` now carries status/info/payment-mode; new `ListImportRefMetaForAccount` query (sqlc) exposes an existing ref's id+status for settlement.
- Matching lives in `importio` behind the `reconcileExisting` flag; bank sync passes `true`, file imports pass `false`.

## Verification

- `go build`, `gofmt`, `golangci-lint run ./...` clean; `go test ./...` green.
- New test `TestEnableBankingSyncMergesExistingTransaction`: a manual entry is **merged** (bank description applied as memo, status → reconciled, ref attached, date corrected, **no duplicate**). Existing dedup/resilience tests still pass.

## Follow-up (Phase 2, tracked in #337)

A **"Bank sync review"** view: imported transactions still missing a category, plus a **duplicate finder** (same account, exact amount, close dates) with merge / keep / delete / edit actions.

Part of #337.

author: jldev1227
body:
`+page.svelte` eran 2.956 líneas con gráficas, tabla y modales mezclados; cualquier cambio en una parte obligaba a leerlo entero. Queda como orquestador —período, permisos y navegación— y cada vista vive en su componente.

Siete vistas: resumen, matriz de los 24 pasos, indicadores, operación segura, documentos, plan anual y contratos/FUEC. Más `historico`, que conserva la tabla de registros diarios del panel anterior EN SOLO LECTURA: la información no se pierde, pero el registro manual de preoperacional ya no se ofrece porque Formularios Dinámicos es la fuente oficial, y dos caminos de captura significan dos verdades sobre el mismo hecho.

LO QUE LA PANTALLA NO HACE

- No enseña cumplimiento ficticio. El avance sale de pasos con evidencia APROBADA y vigente; `EN_REVISION` no da crédito parcial, porque un porcentaje que sube al adjuntar un archivo es justo lo que hay que evitar. `NO_APLICA` sale del denominador.
- No convierte un `null` en «0 %». `formatearValor` devuelve «Sin datos» y la tarjeta muestra el motivo concreto: un cero es un hallazgo y una ausencia de datos es un problema de captura.
- No ofrece botones que la API va a rechazar. `GET /pesv/centro/permisos` dice qué puede hacer quien mira, y sobre la evidencia propia se explica por qué no aparece el botón de aprobar en vez de esconderlo sin más.

DISEÑO

Los estados semafóricos usan hexadecimales literales y no utilidades de Tailwind: cotransmeq reasigna la escala `emerald`/`green` a naranja en su `app.css`, así que un «cumple» verde se vería allí igual que un «alerta». El color de marca manda solo en la cáscara —botones, foco, pestaña activa—, donde sí se usan las utilidades y por eso los archivos son idénticos en los dos repos.

Cada estado lleva icono y texto además de color: hay daltonismo, pantallas malas y capturas en blanco y negro pegadas en un informe de auditoría.

La URL es la fuente de verdad de vista, período, panel, estado y búsqueda (núcleo de `src/lib/listing/`), así que recargar, volver atrás o compartir un enlace llevan al mismo sitio.

El contenedor de página no lleva `max-width`: lo acota el `main` del layout. Los topes que quedan son párrafos de texto corrido (44rem), diálogos y celdas concretas.

El permiso `pesv` deja de ser `general: true` y se gradúa por área, espejo exacto del mapa del backend.

author: skjnldsv
body:
### ☑️ Resolves

Follow-up on #7882, based on that branch. Merge it into #7882 if you prefer a single PR, or keep it as a second step.

Covers scenarios from the Cypress suite in `@nextcloud/upload` that had no equivalent after the migration.

### 🖼️ What changed

Test only, no component code touched.

**Retry coverage (new `retry.spec.ts`)**

`retryCondition` in `@nextcloud/files` (`lib/upload/utils/upload.ts`) has no spec of its own, so all three branches were untested in every repo:

- a network error is retried
- a locked file (423) is retried, since it is usually a preview being generated
- insufficient storage (507) is permanent and must not be retried

The three tests validate each other: the 507 case proves that "no retry" is detectable, so the 423 and network cases are not passing vacuously.

**Progress across a retry**

A retry must not discard the progress of uploads that already finished. The retry is held back so the assertion runs while it is in flight, instead of racing the progress bar being hidden once the queue is done.

**Negative request assertions**

`received(...).toHaveLength(0)` only looks at what arrived so far, so it can pass because a request has not been sent yet rather than because it never will be. Replaced with a new `expectNoMore()` helper, plus a sync point that proves the uploader got far enough.

**Reusable helpers**

- `UploadStatus` mirror with a `satisfies` drift guard, replacing the hand written status numbers. The upstream constant cannot be imported at runtime here because `@nextcloud/files/upload` touches `window` on import while the test bodies run in Node. Changing a value now fails type checking with `Type '99' is not assignable to type '4'`.
- `skipWithoutFilePicker()` centralises the WebKit skip and its reason
- `createFile()` takes a MIME type
- `mockDav({ fail })` can abort a request with a network error
- the WebDAV root pattern is non greedy, so a path repeating `/remote.php/dav` is not over stripped

### 🧪 Testing

```
npm run test:component -- --project=chromium tests/component/components/NcUploadPicker
```

Before: 32 passed, 5 failed. After: 36 passed, 5 failed, so 4 new tests.

The 5 failures are pre-existing on the base branch and are not touched here. They are all in `conflicts.spec.ts`, which looks for a dialog named `1 file conflict`. That string does not exist in `@nextcloud/dialogs`, the name is `Select file to keep` or `Select files to keep`. Single conflicts also render `Cancel` / `Keep both` / `Replace` buttons rather than per version checkboxes, so `keepVersion()` cannot match. Left for #7882, see the review comments there.

### 🚧 Deliberately not covered

Byte level progress inside a single file. It comes from upload progress events that a mocked route never emits, so with `route.fulfill` the bar stays at 0 for the whole upload of one file. Observing it needs real network throttling, which is what the old Cypress suite did with CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions` and what made those tests flaky.

### 🏁 Checklist

- [x] ⛑️ Tests are included or are not applicable
- [x] 📘 Component documentation has been extended, updated or is not applicable
- [x] 2️⃣ Backport to `stable8` for maintained Vue 2 version or not applicable

This change was AI assisted.

author: fullof-work
body:
## Summary

Add a second reusable, read-only audit that fetches GitHub's retained `refs/pull/*/{head,merge}` namespace and scans blobs that are reachable from those refs but no longer reachable from current branches or tags.

## Rationale

The baseline open-source audit covers all current branches and tags, the active audit PR, collaboration records, available Actions logs, and selected release archives. GitHub can retain code referenced only by historical pull requests after contributor branches are deleted. This supplemental pass closes that coverage gap before component repositories become public.

## Security

- read-only `contents` and `pull-requests` permissions
- no repository or organization secrets
- checkout credentials are not persisted
- pull refs are fetched using the ephemeral caller `GITHUB_TOKEN`
- matched values are never printed
- no repository mutation or uploaded artifact

## Validation

- the report distinguishes existing branch/tag objects from pull-request-only objects
- scans only high-confidence credential patterns and suspicious secret-bearing paths
- oversized blobs are reported for manual review rather than read without bounds
- callers pin this workflow by full commit SHA

## Out of scope

- making historical or expired GitHub data recoverable
- scanning content of old Actions artifacts; all pre-publication non-expired artifacts will instead be removed before the visibility switch
- product, BMS, or release behavior changes

Tracks kuasar-sandbox/kuasar-sandbox#82.

author: szupzj18
body:
## Root cause

The session-creation call in `getToken()` (`POST /api/session`) sent only the `Authorization` header, so undici — the fetch implementation in Raycast's Node runtime — added its default `Accept-Language: *` (undici's default headers cannot be disabled, only overridden — nodejs/undici#1305).

vCenter derives the REST session locale from that header and stored `*` as the session locale. The console ticket returned by `POST /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/console/tickets` is a clone ticket for that session, so when VMRC redeemed it via `vim.SessionManager.CloneSession`, vCenter failed to apply the cloned locale and threw `vim.fault.InvalidLocale` (undeclared for CloneSession). VMRC then fell back to an interactive login prompt. Every other extension feature kept working because only CloneSession validates the locale.

## Change

Send an explicit `Accept-Language: en-US` header when creating the session, so the session locale is valid and console tickets stay redeemable. One-line change in `src/api/vCenter.tsx`; all other calls reuse the session token and are unaffected.

## Validation

- Reproduced the header behavior locally: a `fetch` with the old header shape (Authorization only) sends `Accept-Language: *`; with the fix it sends `en-US`.
- The reporter verified end-to-end against vCenter 8.0 U3: default headers → CloneSession fails with `InvalidLocale`; `Accept-Language: en-US` → CloneSession succeeds, and `ray develop` with this change makes Open Console work again (issue #30660).
- Server-side confirmation: vCenter rejects `<locale>*</locale>` in the SOAP Login with `Invalid or unknown locale provided`, and accepts `en-US`.
- `eslint` clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Fixes #30660

author: cartonn
body:
Lost issue #329 op: in een productiebuild bleef **elke** `useActionState`-knop eeuwig op "Bezig…" staan terwijl de mutatie server-side gewoon slaagde.

## Bewijs (deterministisch, `npm run build && PORT=3111 npm run start`, activatie op /admin/franchises)

De diagnose in #329 en in `e2e/_robust.ts` ("de response-body komt nooit aan") blijkt **niet** te kloppen. Gemeten:

| meting | uitkomst |
|---|---|
| action-POST status | 200 na ~20 ms, mutatie geland |
| dezelfde request raw herhaald met `node:http` | 200, stream **sluit af** na 26 ms, 39 kB |
| dezelfde request via kale `fetch()` **vanuit dezelfde pagina** | 200, stream **sluit af** na 30 ms, 45 kB |
| de echte knop: stream lui getapt (consument trekt) | React leest **alle** ±50 kB uit, `done` na ~25 ms |
| flight-payload geanalyseerd | compleet, geen dangling refs; rij `1` = `{"ok":true,"message":"… is geactiveerd."}` |
| UI daarna | knop blijft disabled op "Bezig…", rij blijft staan — ook na 23 s |
| daarna een gewone state-update elders in de root (thema-toggle in de app-shell) | transitie commit alsnog, rij weg |

Uitgesloten met metingen: service worker (`serviceWorkers: "block"` → identiek), CSP/nonce (geen extra stylesheet ingevoegd, geen CSP-violation), compressie (`gzip` én `identity` gedragen zich gelijk; alle GET-streams sluiten netjes), middleware/proxy (raw replay werkt), fire-and-forget mail (`EMAIL_DRIVER=noop`, pad wordt niet eens betreden), `revalidatePath`-scope (`"page"` i.p.v. layout getest — géén verschil).

## Oorzaak

De reconciler markeert de boundary als suspended en **speelt de update daarna niet meer af**, hoewel het antwoord al binnen is. Bekende React-regressie in de build die Next.js 15.5 meelevert: `19.2.0-canary-0bdb9206-20250818` (de regressie ontstond in de canary-serie van eind juli 2025). Ook de nieuwste 15.5.25 levert exact dezelfde vendored build mee — een versiebump binnen de vastgelegde stack lost het dus niet op. Zie vercel/next.js discussions #88767 en #82289.

## Fix

De kleinste veilige remedie: `src/components/system/action-replay.tsx` — een onzichtbare component in de root-layout die na een `submit`/`click` een **eindige** reeks lichte state-updates plant (120/400/900/1800/3000 ms). Staat er een transitie vast, dan commit hij alsnog; is er niets aan de hand, dan is het een re-render van een component die `null` teruggeeft. Geen permanente timer, geen polling.

De serverwaarheid blijft leidend: `pending` blijft staan zolang de action loopt — we forceren alleen dat React het antwoord dát hij al binnen heeft ook op het scherm zet. Werkt app-breed (72 `useActionState`-bestanden + 44 `useTransition`-plekken) zonder die 116 bestanden aan te raken.

Gecontroleerd aan/uit op dezelfde productiebuild:

```
NUDGE UIT | rij weg zonder reload: NEE (15 s)
NUDGE AAN | rij weg zonder reload: JA na 507 ms
```

## Getest

- `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint` / `npm run test` (8095 passed) / `prettier --write` / `npm run build` — groen.
- Nieuwe unit-tests op de pure planner: `src/lib/client/action-replay.test.ts` (4 tests: één zetje per vertraging, geen opstapeling bij hertrigger, alles opgeruimd bij unmount, eindige oplopende reeks).
- **Regressietest**: `e2e/bureau-registratie.spec.ts` gebruikt geen `clickUntilGone` meer — één klik, en de rij moet zónder herladen verdwijnen (`toHaveCount(0)`). Groen op een productiebuild (`--project=ci`, `2 passed`). Zonder de fix faalt precies die assertie.

Niet aangeraakt: `e2e/_robust.ts` blijft staan zolang andere specs hem gebruiken; die opschoning hoort in een eigen increment.

body:
On subsequent runs the CEL input uses before_id paging, walking forward from the last bookmark toward newer events. The newest events appear on the last page of the run, but run_first_id was captured from the first page only. When has_more became false the persisted first_id was set from run_first_id, so the cursor advanced by only one page's worth of activity per run regardless of how many pages were fetched.

Fix the has_more=false branch: when cursor.first_id already has a value (a subsequent run), take body.first_id from the terminal page directly rather than the stale run_first_id.

Extend the system test mock to cover multi-page subsequent runs: Round 2 now spans two pages so that steady state is reached only if the cursor advances to the terminal page's event.

author: roderickhsiao
body:
Major version bump to `2.0.0`. Removes the legacy React 15.6 support path and the `forwardRef` wrapper.

## Breaking changes

**Requires React 19 or later.** `peerDependencies` narrows from `^0.14.7 || ^15 || ^16 || ^17 || ^18 || ^19` to `>=19.0.0`.

- **The React 15.6 build is gone.** `src/react-15.6/` held a class component whose `componentDidUpdate` hand-set `--aspect-ratio` via `node.style.setProperty` as a fallback for [facebook/react#6411](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/6411) — dead code since React 16 writes custom properties from the `style` prop natively.
- **The default export changed meaning.** It used to resolve to that legacy class; it now points at the same modern component as the named export. Both `import AspectRatio from 'react-aspect-ratio'` and `import { AspectRatio } from 'react-aspect-ratio'` keep working and are now identical.
- **`forwardRef` removed.** React 19 passes `ref` to function components as an ordinary prop, so it rides through `...restProps` to the underlying `div`. No call-site change; the only visible difference is in a type position (`ForwardRefExoticComponent<…>` → use `typeof AspectRatio`).

Users on React 18 or older should stay on `react-aspect-ratio@1.x` — it is unchanged and there is no fix in `2.0` they would be missing.

## Other changes

- Flattened `src/react-latest/index.tsx` → `src/index.tsx`; dropped the `src/index.ts` re-export shim.
- `src/types.ts` imports `ComponentProps` explicitly instead of leaning on the UMD React global.
- Test files were being shipped in the published build (`dist/react-latest/index.test.js`) because the babel and `tsconfig.publish.json` ignore globs pointed at a nonexistent `src/__tests__/**`. Now excluded properly — `dist/` is 2 files per target.
- `@types/react` / `@types/react-dom` → `^19`; dropped the unused `@types/react-test-renderer`.
- Added [MIGRATION.md](./MIGRATION.md) with the full 1.x → 2.0 guide, linked from the README. README also documents the `ref` prop and the React 19 requirement.
- Added a test asserting `ref` reaches the underlying element, covering the `forwardRef` removal.

## Verification

- `yarn lint` — clean
- `yarn tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `jest src` — 6/6 pass, snapshot unchanged apart from its new path
- `.scripts/prepublish.sh` — builds cjs/es/umd/next plus `.d.ts` cleanly

## Follow-up

`yarn.lock` is untouched in this PR. It is replaced outright by [react-aspect-ratio#129](https://github.com/roderickhsiao/react-aspect-ratio/pull/129), which migrates the repo from yarn to pnpm and is stacked on this branch — merge this one first.

body:
## What

UI-09 (**Immersive preset — declarative shell proof + overlay-CTA consumer fix**) per `plan/master-ui-phase.md` §12, following the approved Path A direction with Option 1.

**Immersive's contractually defined shell composition is expressible and proven by the declarative UI architecture.** Desktop/tablet `floating` resolves through the existing aside composition; mobile `overlay` uses the existing `OverlayNavigation` path; standard CTA uses the existing CTA contract. **No new UI architecture was introduced.**

## The investigation caught a real latent-consumer defect

The decision core already assigned mobile `overlay → ctaSlot: "drawer"`, but the UI-07 `SiteHeader` CTA consumer only admitted `mobilePattern === "drawer"` — so the Immersive overlay CTA was *declared but never rendered*. This milestone ships **ONE minimal, vocabulary-driven content-layer consumer fix** (`site-header.tsx` admits `mobilePattern === "overlay"` alongside `"drawer"` when `ctaSlot === "drawer"`).

- No `preset === "immersive"` branch (structural/vocabulary-driven).
- No engine/primitive/slot/config/interaction change.
- `Drawer` / `OverlayNavigation` untouched.
- **Immersive mobile overlay CTA = implemented/proven.**
- Drawer behavior unchanged (a `drawer`-pattern preset still composes its CTA inside the drawer — regression-tested).

## Proof (SSR + resolution; no new deps)

- `ui-immersive-preset.test.ts` (+7): profile completeness, personality, inherited defaults, per-leaf overrides, neutral CTA, five-preset regression, default/demo intact.
- `shell-immersive.test.ts` (+13): desktop/tablet `floating`→aside bands + mutual exclusivity + no bottom bar; decision trajectories; **overlay CTA inside the open dialog now renders (enabled+label+href)**; disabled/no-href → no CTA; closed-overlay SSR inertness; no header-path CTA leak; drawer-parity regression; i18n `moreMenu` inertness.
- `boundaries.test.ts` (+3 Phase UI-09): no `immersive` preset literal in engine/core; profile is data; vocabulary-driven decisions.
- Adaptive/Classic/Focus/Workspace regressions green.

## Verification

- **Production change: one content-layer guard** in `src/components/site/site-header.tsx` (the only production file; commit is otherwise tests + docs).
- tsc ✓ · lint ✓ (0) · **734/734 tests** (was 709) · `pnpm build` ✓ **260 routes / 219 sitemap** unchanged; demo HTML byte-identical classic. Zero new deps.
- Docs: ARCHITECTURE (Immersive subsection + boundaries row UI-09 ✅/UI-10 next), CUSTOMIZING, milestone/board/changelog journaled at release.

## Truthful status (proven / deferred / UI-10)

- **Proven:** Immersive's shell composition + mobile overlay CTA (via the declared `ctaSlot:"drawer"` consumer admitting `overlay`).
- **Deferred (shared, contract-ambiguous):** distinct `floating` visual treatment; `minimal` header treatment. No invented semantics.
- **UI-10:** overlay interaction behavior (animation, backdrop, dismissal, Escape, focus, reduced motion) remains the dedicated UI-10 gate — not pulled forward.
- **Roadmap hygiene:** UI-09 "Adaptive" was a no-op (Adaptive delivered by UI-05); the actual UI-09 is Immersive. Adaptive=05, Classic=06, Focus=07, Workspace=08, Immersive=09, UI-10=gate.

Read sits under INITIALIZATION roughly 1,800 lines below, so a session started

author: christianhg
body:
## What

The `rangeDecorations` prop on `PortableTextEditable` is a single mount-level entry, so independent subsystems (comments, presence, diff overlays) cannot contribute decorations without owning the one prop and hand-merging arrays. This PR adds the core primitive for registered decoration layers: the mechanism only (rendering and position mapping, the two things nothing outside the engine can compute). The consumer vocabulary (batched events, reactive reads, React bindings) deliberately lives in a separate package, `@portabletext/plugin-range-decorations`, stacked as the follow-up PR, so interpreted semantics evolve on plugin versioning while core freezes only mechanical facts.

A decoration is an id, a range, and a render function:

```tsx
const decoration = {
  id: comment.id, // identity within its layer; duplicates throw
  range: comment.range, // NonNullable<EditorSelection>
  render: ({children, isFirst, isLast}) => <mark>{children}</mark>,
}
```

`render` wraps the decorated text; a range crossing marks, blocks, or other decorations renders as several fragments, and `isFirst`/`isLast` mark the ones with the range's start and end (each unique per decoration). Render output must keep the document's text in editable DOM: chrome is CSS generated content or `contentEditable={false}` elements; injected text desyncs caret mapping (reproduced; verified clean under both safe patterns on Chromium and Firefox).

The primitive registers a layer and reports what operations did to it:

```ts
const registration = editor.registerRangeDecorations({
  rangeDecorations,
  onMapped: (mappings) => {
    // synchronous, per engine operation, one entry per affected decoration:
    // {id, previousRange, newRange | null, contentTouched, origin: 'local' | 'remote'}
    // newRange: null = the operation destroyed the decoration
  },
})
registration.update(next) // full set, reconciled by id
registration.getDecorations() // live {id, range}; fresh array, no cadence promises, empty before `ready`
```

Reconciliation diffs against what was last supplied, never the tracked position, so a stale resupply cannot snap a decoration back (pinned). A decoration whose content an edit destroys dies with a tombstone and revives on a changed `range` or by leaving the array for one update; destruction includes collapse (deleting exactly the decorated text kills it, pinned), while configured-collapsed decorations never die from staying collapsed (pinned). Layers compose: legacy prop outermost, then registration order, overlaps nesting first-outermost. The legacy prop keeps working unchanged as one layer; the new surface never references the legacy type.

## Design notes

`onMapped` is deliberately per-operation and synchronous with no batching promise, and `getDecorations()` deliberately promises no reference stability: every timing, ordering, and stability contract is toolkit territory, rebuilt there from these facts alone. The emit runs after the machine reassigns its decorated ranges, so `getDecorations()` inside the callback already reflects the operation (pinned red/green). `newRange` keeps the same reference when an operation did not move the decoration (pinned), which is what lets a consumer detect movement without deep comparison. Origin is the two-way collapse the public `operation` event already uses. Consumer callback errors are isolated: a throwing `onMapped` cannot stop position tracking or starve a sibling layer (pinned red/green against the unguarded delivery).

One behavioral fix rides along with its own changeset: two `PortableTextEditable`s under one provider no longer rewrite each other's prop decorations, and unmounting an editable removes only its own contribution (pinned).

One WebKit caveat, not introduced here: WebKit drops keystrokes at a caret whose rendering starts with any `contentEditable={false}` island (the legacy presence caret in `plugin-sdk-value` ships the same shape in production today); that pin is gated off WebKit and the engine-compat gap is tracked separately.

Per-operation cost is the same complexity class as the legacy machine with a higher constant; unmeasured at large decoration counts, flagged for the presence migration.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core decoration rendering, edit-time range mapping, and shared XState wiring; behavior is heavily tested but mistakes could affect overlays, presence, or multi-editable setups.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`editor.registerRangeDecorations`** (`@beta`): a framework-neutral layer for `{id, range, render}` decorations with **`update` / `unregister` / `getDecorations`**, plus optional synchronous **`onMapped`** callbacks per engine operation (`moved`, `contentTouched`, `newRange: null` on death). Registered layers compose with the legacy **`rangeDecorations` prop** (prop outermost, then registration order; array order controls nesting).
> 
> **Refactors range-decoration state** from a per-`PortableTextEditable` actor to one **shared `rangeDecorationsMachine`** on `EditorProvider`, keyed **sources** (`prop` vs `registered`), id-based reconciliation with tombstones so stale `update()` cannot resurrect killed decorations, and **`isFirst` / `isLast`** on registered `render` fragments.
> 
> **Fixes multi-editable props:** each editable’s `rangeDecorations` is its own source (`useId` + unmount cleanup), so two editables under one provider no longer overwrite each other’s prop decorations.
>

author: westbridgeinc
body:
The admin trail was written by an `onResponse` hook. By the time that hook runs the action has **committed** and the response has been **sent**, so the only thing a failed audit write could do was this:

```js
} catch (err) {
  app.log.error({ err }, '[admin-audit] failed to write audit log');
}
```

Database contention, a validation error on the audit row, or a process exit between commit and hook — and a privileged action (a refund settled, a fee waived, a price book replaced) completed with **no record of it**. Discoverable only by absence, and only if someone thought to look for a row that was never there.

## The change

`auditWithin(tx, request, prefix)` writes the row through the caller's transaction, so a refused audit row **rolls the action back with it**:

```ts
const config = await app.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
  const row = await tx.platformConfig.upsert({ where: { key }, update: { value }, create: { key, value } });
  await auditWithin(tx, request, app.prefix);
  return row;
});
```

The action stops being auditable-in-principle and becomes **unperformable-without-audit**.

**One builder, both writers.** `adminAuditRow` builds the row for the hook and for `auditWithin` alike, so a migrating route writes the same row it wrote before, at a safer moment. The 94 existing ADM-003/004/005/006/007 tests pass unchanged; that is the point.

**The hook stays, as a backstop.** 40 C4/C5 routes need this and they do not all own their mutation. Deleting the hook now would take the trail off every unmigrated route. `swift_admin_audit_total{writer}` counts `inline` against `backstop`, so *"the backstop is the only writer"* is a number that goes to zero as the migration lands — the observability the clause asks for.

## Scope

| | routes |
|---|---|
| migrated | **4 of 40** — `PUT /config/:key`, `POST /zones`, `PUT /zones/:id`, `DELETE /zones/:id` |
| unchanged, still on the backstop | the other 36 |

**This does not close ADM-002.** It builds the mechanism, proves it, and migrates the routes that own their mutation directly.

## A create must name what it created

I first described the legacy `audit()` row as strictly poorer than the hook's and dropped it on all four routes. **For creates that was wrong.** Measured, one unmigrated `POST /admin/promos` writes two rows:

```
CREATE_PROMO                     | PromoCode | cmtmnnfm0000bonlqxq4orul4
ADMIN POST /api/v1/admin/promos  | api       | -
```

A create route declares no entity in `ADMIN_ROUTE_AUTHORITY` — its subject does not exist when the request is routed — so the hook's `entityId` falls back to `-`, and the legacy row was the only one carrying the new id. Consolidating `POST /zones` onto one row would have silently dropped which zone was created. `auditWithin` now takes an optional `entityId`, and the route passes the id it just made. The other three routes were never affected: their subject is in the params and their entity is declared.

## Proof

The clause asks for one red test: *inject an audit-write failure and assert the state change did not commit.* The injection is a real `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `audit_logs` refusing one subject's row — the clause's own trigger, arriving from the database inside the transaction, not a mock.

Reverting the route to write-then-audit fails it for exactly the right reason:

```
a write whose audit was refused must not return 200: expected 200 not to be 200
the audit row must already exist when the 200 lands: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got 0
```

Every assertion here was mutation-checked. Two that initially passed while measuring nothing, and were fixed:

- the `backstop` counter test sent a promo payload missing a required field, so the route answered **400** — which never reaches the hook. It now asserts the write succeeded before reading the counter.
- the create-id test fails with `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got 0` when the override is removed.

11 tests; 32 green across the audit and zone suites; `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: jonhill90
body:
Closes #1028's compile-path/Item-shape scope (query.go is #1026's, untouched here).

## What changed

Every `Item` now carries `Publishable bool` and `PublishBasis string` (`classify.go` + `knowledge.go`), set once at compile time and carried verbatim into `index.json`. Wired into all four sources: `stars.go`, `vault.go`, `corpus.go`, `loops.go`.

**Unclassified means private.** `classify`'s default branch returns `false` with a non-empty reason for any source it does not positively allow-list — a fifth source added tomorrow with no `classify.go` change is private by construction, not by a filter someone remembered to add at query time.

## The classifier I chose, and why

Source-level default, not per-item classification, not a source marker. `#1028` names all three as options; I picked source-level because the other two collapse into it given a constraint `#1028` also sets: **sources are read-only to this package.** Neither the vault (`type:`) nor the corpus (`weight`/`status`) carries a publishability marker of its own today, and reusing either field for that purpose would be exactly the "clever classifier nobody can audit" the issue warns against. Without a real per-item signal, per-item classification defaulting-private and a source-level default-private rule produce an identical answer for every item that exists today — so `classify.go` states the source-level rule directly instead of running the same branch once per item.

`github-stars` is the one source classified public: a starred repo is already public GitHub activity, visible on the operator's own public profile, and starring something does not by construction reveal employment, compensation, third-party, credential, medical or family information — the six categories `#1028`'s own probe was built to catch. `vault-fact`, `corpus-parameter` and `loops-research` all default private.

## What this will miss (stated plainly, per the issue's ask)

- **A starred repo whose name, owner, or description is itself sensitive publishes unexamined.** `github-stars` is unconditionally public here; nothing screens repo content.
- It does **not** miss in the other direction: every vault/corpus/loops item defaults private regardless of content, at the cost of also hiding every non-personal item in those three sources until real per-item classification exists. That asymmetry is deliberate — over-hiding is a human's decision to publish later; a leak is not reversible.

## Retrieval mode (issue's point 3)

Left to `#1026`'s `query.go` work, per this task's own scope (`query.go`, `cases.json`, `cmd/goldenquery` were off-limits here). `Item.Publishable`/`PublishBasis` are the seam that query-side work should filter on.

## Evidence

```
$ go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... -count=1
ok  	.../estate
ok  	.../estate/cmd/goldenquery
ok  	.../estate/internal/corpus
ok  	.../estate/internal/dispatchid
ok  	.../estate/internal/gate
ok  	.../estate/internal/harness
ok  	.../estate/internal/isolate
ok  	.../estate/internal/knowledge
ok  	.../estate/internal/knowledge/goldenset
ok  	.../estate/internal/ledger
ok  	.../estate/internal/mirror
ok  	.../estate/internal/pressure
ok  	.../estate/internal/quota
ok  	.../estate/internal/reclaim
ok  	.../estate/internal/spend
ok  	.../estate/internal/tick
ok  	.../estate/internal/verifybranch
```

Regenerated index (`go run . knowledge`), classified by source:

| source | publishable | private |
|---|---|---|
| github-stars | 391 | 0 |
| vault-fact | 0 | 109 |
| corpus-parameter | 0 | 1104 |
| loops-research | 0 | 24 |
| **total** | **391** | **1237** |

1628 items total.

**Break-test of the guard** (`TestGenerateNeverPublishesAnItemWithNoBasis`, `TestClassifyDefaultsUnknownSourcesPrivate`): flipped `classify.go`'s default branch to `return true, ""` (unclassified source treated as publishable with no reason) —

```
--- FAIL: TestGenerateNeverPublishesAnItemWithNoBasis (0.00s)
    classify_test.go:77: item 20260904120001 (vault-fact) has Publishable=true with no PublishBasis
--- FAIL: TestClassifyDefaultsUnknownSourcesPrivate (0.00s)
    classify_test.go:21: classify("vault-fact") = publishable=true, want false (unclassified means private)
    ...
```

Restored, re-ran full suite: green (output above).

## Did not touch

Vault, corpus, stars and loops-research sources — read-only. No deletion or redaction. No storage-format change. `query.go`, `cases.json`, `cmd/goldenquery` untouched.

body: ## Summary Implements the agreed coffee-taste scoring contract and alignment eval (测试集) so App Compare Beans matches the gos-coffee-taste skill/repo numeric path within tolerance. Fixes the bug where Chinese notes showed incorrect scores because the closed lexicon missed Chinese terms like 浆果/berry, 热带水果/tropical fruit, 洛神花/floral. ## Product Philosophy (Binding) 1. **One AI model path** for extract/normalize (App and skill share the same approach/schema) 2. **One deterministic scorer** for Fit/Novelty (BeanExplorerScorer / portable_coffee_rank) 3. **测试集 measures drift objectively.** When accuracy/drift is bad → tune prompt/model, not stack locks 4. **Keep the pipe simple**: normalize → score ## Changes ### A) Skill vs App Alignment 测试集 (Test Set) - **Corrected fixture**: `eval/coffee_taste/sey_candidates_2026-09-04.json` with 3 SEY beans using REAL bag notes: - Susan Meneses Pink Bourbon Washed: 洛神花/蓝莓/手指柠檬 (hibiscus, blueberry, finger lime) - Mate Matiwos Keramo 74158 Honey: 浆果/热带水果/佛手柑 (berries, tropical fruit, bergamot) - Alejandrina Maytan Kukipata SL9 Washed: 热带水果/草莓/柔和酸质 (yellow tropical fruit, strawberry, soft acidity) - **New gold ranking** (recomputed from English): - Keramo (Fit 69.3, Novelty 10.0) > SL9 (68.4, 10.0) > Susan (67.9, 10.0) - All three in similar-fit band (delta < 1.5) - **Alignment script**: `scripts/evaluate_skill_app_alignment.py` with stub normalize for CI - Gates: Top-1 Fit match, Novelty ±5, family Jaccard=1.0, ranking order with near-tie tolerance - `--stub-normalize` flag applies frozen CN→canonical map without live Ark ### B) Simplified Normalize Path - **Normalize by default** in Compare scoring unless `preMatchedFamilies` already set - Removed fragile non-ASCII heuristic (over-constraining per philosophy) - Text-only Ark client with retry policy (up to 3 attempts) - On normalize failure → surface error, **no lexicon fallback** ### C) Scoring Path Integration - Extended `BeanExplorerScoreCandidate` with optional `preMatchedFamilies` - Scorer uses pre-matched families when provided (bypasses lexicon) - `BeanExplorerView` calls normalize before scoring - Normalize error surfaces to UI ### D) Tests & Documentation - **Python alignment**: - English→English: ✓ ALL GATES PASSED - Chinese without normalize: ✗ FAILS (wrong top-1, family mismatch) - Chinese with stub normalize: ✓ ALL GATES PASSED - **Swift unit tests**: Pre-matched families, SEY alignment (Novelty ~10, correct ranking) - **Documentation**: `docs/skill-app-alignment-eval.md` with philosophy, 测试集 usage, and refresh workflow ## Shared Contract ✅ **Model does NOT invent Fit/Novelty** – only normalizes to schema ✅ **Scores only from deterministic scorer** – same math as skill/portable ✅ **Normalize by default** – simple pipe, no over-constraining ✅ **Constrained output** – families/origin/process must match profile keys **Note**: App Ark normalizer and skill/repo numeric path use the **same schema and same scorer**. If skill still maps in prose today, follow-up should call the same normalize→score pipe. ## Testing ```bash # English→English (sanity check) python3 scripts/evaluate_skill_app_alignment.py \ --test-descriptor-field descriptors_english_only \ --gold-descriptor-field descriptors_english_only # Chinese without normalize (shows drift/bug) python3 scripts/evaluate_skill_app_alignment.py # Chinese with stub normalize (for CI) python3 scripts/evaluate_skill_app_alignment.py --stub-normalize -v # Swift tests (requires Xcode/Swift toolchain) swift test --filter BeanExplorerScoringTests ``` ## New Gold Ranking Summary **Before** (wrong descriptors): SL9 (69.0) > Keramo (68.5) > Susan (63.8) **After** (corrected real bag notes): Keramo (69.3) > SL9 (68.4) > Susan (67.9) All three now in similar-fit band, Novelty = 10.0 for all (not 42.5). ## What Was Trimmed vs Kept **Trimmed** (per philosophy): - Non-ASCII heuristic as main design (over-constraining) - Silent lexicon fallback in scoring hot path - Unnecessary constraint layers **Kept**: - Normalize→score pipe (simple) - Retry policy on normalize failure (already present) - Deterministic scorer (shared with skill) - 测试集 as objective drift meter ## Known Limitations - Normalize requires configured Ark API key - Quality signals not yet normalized (e.g. 酸甜→acid_sweet_balance_positive) - Lexicon remains for gold generation but NOT used in App scoring after normalize ## Follow-up - Extend normalize to quality signals - Add confidence scores from normalize - Expand 测试集 with more roasters/languages - Automate alignment tests in CI

author: giorgino22
body:
Replaces the emoji grid with a numeric keypad laid out like the iPhone passcode screen.

## Layout

Three columns of round keys: 1–9 with their letters (ABC, DEF, GHI…), then a gap, 0 and a delete key, with a row of dots above that fills as you type. `SITE_CODE` is now a digit string of any length — four or six are usual.

## Fast entry, no zoom

Both explicitly requested, both handled at the source:

- Keys register on **`pointerdown`** rather than `click`, so rapid repeated entry never drops a digit and there is no tap delay. Measured: six taps in ~200 ms on both desktop and a simulated touch device, all six registered.
- **`touch-action: manipulation`** on the gate and its keys stops a double tap from zooming the page. Pinch zoom still works — I did not disable zoom globally via the viewport tag, since that would break zooming on the calendar itself.
- Text selection is disabled on the gate, so fast tapping never starts a selection drag.

Bonus for the computer: the code can simply be typed on the keyboard — digits, Backspace to delete, Escape to clear.

## German

All Swiss German removed from the gate: *Familienkalender*, *Code eingeben*, *Falscher Code*, *Keine Verbindung*. The delete key is now an icon, replacing "← Zrugg".

## Unrelated fix spotted in a screenshot

On a 390 px phone the *Stand HH:MM* stamp was squeezing the mode buttons enough to clip "Agenda" to "Agen". The stamp is hidden below 700 px now; it stays on desktop.

## Verified

| keypad: layout, fast entry, zoom, keyboard, delete, wrong code | 21/21 |


원인은 첨부 테스트 한 번이었다. 이미지를 붙여 보낸 메시지가 체크포인트에 영구
기록으로 남았고, 그 뒤로 매 턴 다시 실려 나갔다.

이미 이럴 때 쓰라고 만들어 둔 길이 있다. 런타임이 못 받는 미디어를 떼어 내고
텍스트만 보내는 degrade 경로다. 그런데 그 길이 하는 일이 없었다.

## reroute 가 하던 일

두 가지가 겹쳐 있었다.

**첫째, 미디어를 찾는 쪽과 떼어 내는 쪽이 서로 다른 범위를 봤다.**
필요한 모달리티를 세는 `required_modalities_of_content_blocks` 는 도구 결과
(`ToolResult`) 안까지 들어가서 "이미지가 필요하다"고 보고했다. 정작 미디어를
떼어 내는 `strip_unsupported_modality_blocks` 는 최상위 블록만 훑었다.
그래서 "이미지가 필요한데 뗄 이미지는 없다"는 상태가 됐고, 뗀 게 없으니 안내
문구도 없고, 드라이버는 입력을 그대로 둔 채 다음 줄로 넘어갔다. WARN 한 줄,
manifest 한 행도 남기지 않고. 운영자에게는 provider 쪽 거부 에러만 보였다.
RFC-0265 가 돌았다가 포기했다는 기록이 아무 데도 없었다.

**둘째, reroute 대상이 문자열이라 드라이버가 다시 찾아봐야 했다.**
결정은 갈아탈 런타임의 id 만 넘겼고, 드라이버가 `Runtime.get_runtime_by_id` 로
다시 찾았다. 못 찾으면 원래 후보를 조용히 그대로 썼다. 그러면서 manifest 에는
`rerouted` 라고 적었다. 이미지를 못 받는 런타임을 계속 쓰면서 갈아탔다고
기록하는 상태다.

그리고 로그 한 줄이 상황을 더 헷갈리게 만들었다.

```
analyst: RFC-0265 modality reroute kimi_coding.kimi-k3-256k
         -> kimi_coding.kimi-k3-256k (assigned runtime lacks image input)
```

왼쪽에 찍힌 건 떠나는 런타임이 아니라 assignment 이름이었다. analyst 는
assignment 이름이 곧 런타임 id 라서 양쪽이 같아 보였고, 자기 자신으로 갈아타는
것처럼 읽혔다. 실제로 떠난 런타임은 `glm-coding.glm-5.3` 이었고 reroute 자체는
제대로 동작하고 있었다. 로그가 거짓말을 한 것이다.

## 지금은 이렇게 한다

- 떼어 내는 쪽도 `ToolResult` 안으로 들어간다. 필요한 걸 세는 쪽과 같은 블록을
  본다. 필요하다고 보고한 모달리티는 떼어 낼 수 있는 모달리티다.
- 그래도 뗄 것이 없으면 — 모달리티는 하나씩은 지원하는데 묶어서는 못 받는
  경우가 남는다 — WARN 과 `degrade_unavailable` manifest 행을 남긴다. 조용히
  넘어가는 길은 없앴다.
- reroute 결정이 id 문자열 대신 이미 찾아 둔 `Runtime.t` 를 들고 다닌다.
  드라이버가 다시 찾을 일이 없으니, 못 찾아서 원래 후보로 되돌아가던 분기도
  같이 사라졌다.
- `reroute_decision` 타입을 `.mli` 에서 `private` 으로 닫았다. `Reroute` 값은
  이 모듈의 결정 함수에서만 나온다. 그 함수는 assigned 를 뺀 후보 집합에서
  대상을 고른다. 자기 자신으로 가는 reroute 를 만들 수 있는 자리가 없다.
- 로그는 떠난 런타임과 도착한 런타임을 찍고, assignment 는 따로 적는다.

## 못 쓸 미디어가 이력에 남은 Keeper 를 운영자가 보면

턴마다 WARN 한 줄과 manifest 행 하나가 남는다.

```
<keeper>: RFC-0265 media degrade on <runtime> — dropped image=1, continuing text-only
```

manifest 는 `status="degraded"` 에 `routing_action=media_degraded_to_text`,
떼어 낸 개수까지 들어간다. 모델 입력에는 "첨부된 미디어 입력 N건이
생략되었습니다" 안내가 붙어서, 모델도 뭔가 빠졌다는 걸 안다.

떼어 낼 수 없는 경우에는 대신 이 줄이 남는다.

```
<keeper>: RFC-0265 media degrade unavailable on <runtime> — required <modalities>,
nothing strippable; the capability floor rejects this turn
```

이 턴은 여전히 능력 게이트에서 거부된다. 다만 왜 거부됐는지가 로그에 남는다.

저장된 체크포인트는 건드리지 않는다. 떼어 낸 건 이번 턴에 보낼 사본에만
적용되므로, 나중에 이미지를 받는 런타임이 붙으면 원본 미디어를 그대로 본다.

## analyst 는 알아서 살아나나

배포만 하면 된다. 별도 조치는 필요 없다.

체크포인트에 남은 이미지가 매 턴 degrade 로 걸러지고 턴은 텍스트로 진행된다.
같은 코드가 배포된 뒤 09-04 06:48:05Z 에 degrade 가 한 번 걸렸고, 그 다음
턴들(1611~1621)이 도구 호출까지 정상적으로 끝났다. 다만 그때는 이 PR 이 막는
조용한 갈래가 남아 있어서 06:15 / 06:42 / 06:43 에 WARN 없는 거부가 세 번 더
났다. 이 변경으로 그 갈래가 없어진다.

굳이 손을 대고 싶다면 체크포인트에서 그 이미지 메시지를 지우는 방법도 있지만,
degrade 가 매 턴 처리하므로 필요하지는 않다.

## 이 PR 이 다루지 않는 것

**온도 실패는 별개다.** 같은 Keeper 의 두 번째 실패 사유 123 건
(`invalid temperature: only 0.6 is allowed`) 은 여기서 건드리지 않았다.
overlay 에 `k3-256k` 행이 없어서 `openai_chat_extended` 프리셋이 적용된 것이
뿌리이고, 지금은 `runtime.toml` 에서 `temperature = 0.6` 으로 고정해 둔 상태다.
설정 쪽 문제라 코드 변경 범위 밖이다.

**조용한 갈래 중 어느 쪽이 그 세 턴을 죽였는지는 확정하지 못했다.**
`ToolResult` 중첩 설명은 코드에서 추론한 것이고, 해당 체크포인트 스냅샷은 이미
사라져서 대조할 수 없었다. 두 갈래를 모두 없앴으므로 어느 쪽이었든 닫힌다.

**Keeper 가 죽어도 아무도 몰랐던 문제**는 masc#32971 / masc#32998 에 이미
올라와 있다. 여기서 다시 다루지 않는다.

## 검증

`dune build` 는 돌리지 않았다. CI 의 `dune build @check` 로 확인한다.

새로 고정한 테스트 (이 변경 없이는 실패한다):

- `strip descends into tool result` — 도구 결과 안의 이미지가 실제로 떨어지는지
- `stripped blocks pass the capability floor` — 떼어 낸 뒤의 블록이 능력 게이트를
  통과하는지. 두 갈래가 어긋나면 바로 깨지는 자리다
- `strip messages descends into tool result` — 이력 메시지에서도 같은지
- `strip keeps nested media a vision runtime accepts` — 이미지를 받는 런타임에서는
  중첩 미디어를 떼지 않는지
- `incapable self candidate → degrade floor` — 자기 자신이 후보로 들어와도
  reroute 대상이 되지 않는지

`test_keeper_turn_driver_failover.ml` 의 degrade 테스트는 결정을 손으로 만들던
것을 실제 결정 함수에서 받도록 바꿨다. 타입이 `private` 이라 손으로 만들 수 없기도
하고, 그게 실제 생산 경로를 지나가는 쪽이라서다.

body:
## Summary
- **Phase 10 — Background Storytelling** (VERSION 7 of the spec): computes a whole-page 0..1 "journey" progress (`MasterScrollController`, spans the entire scrollable section rather than resetting at each ghost/transition/rubik phase boundary like the existing per-phase `t`) and mirrors it onto CSS custom properties each frame. The studio backdrop now evolves across the whole page rather than sitting static: it opens clean and dark, a red ambient glow builds in, a faint technical grid fades in across the journey's middle third, and violet/blue accents plus extra vignette contrast only join for the back half. The same value also eases the real WebGL lighting (`LightingManager.setStoryProgress`: ambient dims slightly, rim light punches up for a more cinematic feel by the end) and the page-wide dust particles' visibility (sparse at the top, full by the bottom). Journey progress tracks live scroll unconditionally, including during Explore Mode.
  - Scope note: skipped adding real Three.js fog (low visual payoff given the cube always sits close to camera, added risk for little gain) — the deepening vignette serves as the atmospheric-depth analogue instead.
- **Explore Mode declutter** (follow-up from testing): the standalone `EXPLORE MODE` pill added in Phase 9 read as cluttering the top-right icon cluster, especially on mobile. Folded it into the existing `...` tools tray as a plain icon-only toggle (compass icon) alongside RESET/env/fullscreen, consistent with how the tray already collapses secondary controls behind one button. Widened the tray's open max-width to fit the fourth button.

## Test plan
- [x] Playwright: scanned `--journey-progress`/`--journey-rich`/`--journey-grid` across the whole page (0–100% scroll) in both dark and light themes, confirmed monotonic increase and correct threshold ramps
- [x] Verified `LightingManager` ambient/rim intensities and `PhysicsBackground` particle visibility scale correctly with journey progress
- [x] Verified journey progress keeps tracking live scroll during Explore Mode (independent of the frozen 3D state)
- [x] Visual screenshots at top/mid/bottom of the page in both themes — clean/minimal opening, grid + glow build-in, high-contrast finale
- [x] Confirmed no console/page errors in any of the above
- [x] Verified the Explore Mode toggle works correctly from its new home in the tools tray (enter/exit, accent-ring state, stays active after closing the tray) on both mobile and desktop
- [x] Confirmed no layout overflow with the tray's 4th button on either breakpoint

author: vishaaallll
body:
## Context & Overview

In `ods/extensions/services/dashboard-api/helpers.py`, metric sorters partition integer sequences into even and odd data buckets. Invalid numeric strings or `None` parameters can cause coercion or modulo operation crashes.

### Root Cause and Solved Edge Case
Prevents `TypeError` and `ValueError` during list integer parity partitioning.

### Safeguards and Edge Case Bounds
- Input Validation: Asserts `list` instance checking and uses `try/except (ValueError, TypeError)` for integer parsing.
- Fallback Handling: Skips invalid elements cleanly and returns empty tuple arrays `([], [])` for `None` inputs.
- State Consistency: Zero side-effects on original array sequence parameters.

## Testing and Verification

- Test Verification Suite: Added `test_list_partition_even_odd_resilience.py` validating numeric parity partitioning.

### Verification Results
Ran unit test suite:
```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_list_partition_even_odd_resilience.py
============================== 2 passed in 0.02s ==============================
```

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary
Two batches of fixes on the `hermes-chat-dashboard` and Render deployment template:

**1. Chat dashboard plugin** (`dashboard-plugins/hermes-chat-dashboard`)
- **Unreadable assistant replies:** host dark `--color-foreground`/`--color-midground` tokens were leaking into the reply body (black-on-black). Appended legibility guards pin `--hcd-fg` through midground/popover layers (fallback `#e8e2d4`) and set explicit `color` on the reading column + descendant tags so host bare-tag rules can't flip reply text dark again.
- **Model hot-swap:** picking a model when no live gateway session exists was silently dropped. Choices are now queued (`pendingModelRef`) and flushed via `config.set {key:"model", session_id}` on `ensureSession` before the first `prompt.submit`, so the currently-open chat switches live. Optimistic badge reverts on rejection; busy/4009 shows a clear "stop first" message.
- **Raw tool dumps:** oversized tool/system content renders as compact, collapsible `.hcd-outline` `<pre>` blocks instead of full-width markdown.

**2. Render deployment OOM guard** (`scripts/bootstrap.sh`, `render.yaml`, etc.)
- The Free 512 MB container kept OOM-restarting (the repeated `restored N file(s)` reboot cycle). Added a proactive `memory_guard_loop` that reads the container's **real cgroup budget** and reclaims headroom **before** the kernel kills the cgroup: telemetry → SIGSTOP the git sync daemon → emergency dashboard drop (all staged/tunable, never touches the gateway).
- Tightened the baseline agent cache `4/300s → 2/120s` in `render.yaml`.

## Tests
- Node harness: all 19 scenarios pass (added `modelSwitchNewChat`, `modelSwitchBusyGuard`, `toolDumpRendering`).
- Python supervision suite: 7/7 pass, incl. 3 new guard tests driving the real guard against a synthetic high-pressure cgroup, an unlimited tree, and the RSS fallback.

author: anjarakvo
body:
Replaces the constant `group: test-only` (which cancelled runs — because GitHub keeps only one *pending* run per group, so overlapping push/PR/branch runs sharing the same lane cancelled each other even with `cancel-in-progress: false`).

New behaviour, split by ref:
- **main**: shared lane `akvo-mis-test-deploy` -> test-cluster deploys run serially (no overlap).
- **any other ref** (branches, PRs, every event): unique per-run group (`<workflow>-<run_id>`) -> never queued behind another run, so every push is validated and nothing is dropped.

`cancel-in-progress: false` kept. Triggers unchanged (every push on any branch still runs).

body:
Round 3 for task 1050, per Martien's testing feedback on rounds 1-2: *"this should be the case for the multiplayer deck builder too. in fact the multiplayer deck builder with the real cards needs to be used for the campaign deck builder too but with the hero from the deck selection as in the campaign mode."*

## What changed

- **New shared `DeckBuilderPanel` component** (`frontend/src/components/DeckBuilderPanel.tsx`): the one deck-builder editor for both pages — real `CardView` cards for the pool and the deck being built, the full filter row (search, type, faction, unit type, min/max cost), and the `CardDetailModal` inspect flow.
- **My Decks (`DecksPage.tsx`)**: now renders the shared panel. Its HQ/hero pickers are rescoped from "every HQ/hero card in the game" to **only headquarters-/hero-type cards actually in the deck being built** (type-hierarchy walk, so subtype HQs/heroes like nexus, graveyard-hq, hive-hq, laboratory-hq, homestead-hq, caster-hero, necromancer-hero count). A pick whose last copy leaves the deck auto-clears.

HQ/hero still picked from the deck being built, as delivered in #29; the auto-clear no longer marks a loaded saved deck as diverged.
- Fixed a remount pitfall: the campaign's builder is rendered via a plain function call instead of a locally-defined component type, so the panel's filter/inspect state survives card add/remove re-renders.

- `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite): **clean**

author: alphanum545
body:
Fixes the LIGO-1000 acquisition failure observed after PR #5 merged.

Root cause:
- the acquisition loop previously tried each `--numjobs` value only once
- LIGO generation is stochastic and can fail transiently even when the requested count is exactly correct
- after one failed `1000` attempt, the loop incorrectly moved on to larger request sizes

Fix:
- retry each requested `--numjobs` value several times before advancing the size search
- preserve the overall bounded `max_attempts_per_replicate`
- keep exact actual task-count acceptance (`allowed_size_deviation = 0`)
- for LIGO, advance only through even request values because upstream rejects odd counts
- continue recording target, upstream requested count, actual count, attempt index, and checksum separately

Regression coverage:
- retries the same request after a transient upstream failure
- searches upward only after the per-request retry budget is exhausted
- verifies LIGO never requests odd `--numjobs` values
- real upstream CI smoke covers Montage-50, SIPHT-50, and LIGO-1000

If CI passes, merging this PR will trigger the full 105-workflow acquisition again and create a generated review branch only on complete success.

author: gladsjr
body:
Closes #346

Varredura de textos desatualizados nas telas. **Os 8 achados da issue foram
reconferidos um a um na `main` atual (`cbf8642`) e os 8 continuam válidos** —
nenhum PR entre 31/08 e 03/09 tocou nesses pontos. Nenhum achado morreu.
O falso positivo que a issue já havia registrado (`static/professor.html:136`)
segue sendo falso positivo: os botões `send-enunciado` e `save-interviewer`
existem e não são ocultados — nada foi mexido ali.

## O achado grave: o termo não cobria o vídeo

A entrevista por mensagens roda hoje com fiscalização por vídeo **ligada e
fixa** — `saveConfigTab()` grava `proctoringOn = true` e `mode = 'audio'` sem
oferecer escolha. Ou seja: a câmera abre, o vídeo é gravado, e sem ele a sessão
não começa nem conclui (ADR 0005). O termo que o aluno aceitava era o
`CONSENT_TEXT_HTML`, que fala de PDF, texto e voz e **não menciona câmera nem
vídeo** — nem o adendo do modo áudio menciona. Gravava-se, portanto, uma
categoria de dado que o aluno nunca tinha visto declarada. Não é redação: é o
invariante de privacidade do projeto ("consentimento de câmera e gravação é
obrigatório antes da arguição") furado na prática.

Prova oral e entrevista simplificada não têm o problema: nelas a câmera é fixa
e o vídeo está no corpo do próprio termo (`CONSENT_ORAL_HTML`,
`CONSENT_LIVE_HTML`).

**Correção**: `CONSENT_VIDEO_ADDITION_HTML`, um adendo condicional no mesmo
padrão do `CONSENT_AUDIO_ADDITION_HTML` — servido em `/api/consent` e
concatenado pelo modal apenas quando `setup-config` responde
`proctoring_enabled`. Ele repete as garantias que os outros dois termos já dão
(retenção de 6 meses, acesso restrito ao professor e administradores, o vídeo
**não** vai à OpenAI, exclusão antecipada a pedido) e acrescenta a ressalva da
ADR 0004: a fiscalização não altera a nota automaticamente nem acusa.

Ficou condicional de propósito. Pôr o vídeo no corpo do termo seria o erro
simétrico — declarar uma coleta que não acontece para quem faz entrevista sem
fiscalização. Há teste travando as duas pontas.

Mecânica: o `setup-config` passou a ser lido **antes** do termo (é ele que diz
se haverá gravação) e virou uma promessa cacheada — três pontos da página o
consultavam, cada um com seu `fetch`.

### Por que subi a CONSENT_VERSION (3.0.0 → 3.1.0)

Não é óbvio, e o custo é real. A versão é **uma só** para os três fluxos:

- **Custo de subir**: na prova oral e na entrevista simplificada o aceite fica
  no banco (`submissions.consent_version`) e o `consent_ok` das rotas de status
  compara com a constante. Quem já aceitou vai aceitar de novo — inclusive ao
  **retomar uma sessão caída** (#356). E o texto desses dois termos **não
  mudou**: eles pagam por uma correção que não é deles.
- **Custo de não subir**: na entrevista por mensagens o aceite só vive no
  `sessionStorage`, com a versão dentro da chave. Uma aba aberta desde antes do
  deploy que já tenha aceitado o 3.0.0 **não veria o adendo** e seguiria a
  entrevista inteira, com câmera gravando, sob o termo antigo. É exatamente a
  lacuna que este PR fecha.

Subi. Um checkbox a mais numa janela de deploy é barato; deixar aberta a
hipótese de uma sessão gravar vídeo sob um termo que não o declara, não é. E é
o que o próprio arquivo manda ("incrementar sempre que o texto mudar, mesmo
vírgula").

Fica registrado como dívida: **versionar o termo por fluxo** resolveria o
acoplamento (cada flavor com sua versão), mas mexe em schema e em três rotas —
não cabia neste PR.

## Os outros sete achados

| # | Achado | Estado | O que foi feito |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `proctorGate.js` promete liberação do professor no bloqueio de INÍCIO | **valia** | `video_waived` só é lido por `finalizeWithVideoGate`, e o botão "Liberar" só existe em `awaiting_video` — estado posterior à arguição. Texto passa a apontar a saída real: combinar outro horário ou outra forma de avaliação. |
| 3 | "agente de relevância" em `conversation.html` | **valia** | Não existe `QuestionRelevanceAgent` (quem pula é o `SuperOrchestratorAgent`), e a caixa era **código morto**: lia `skipped_questions`, que nasce de `sess.skippedQuestions` — zerada no upload e nunca preenchida (a realtime grava `[]` fixo). Seção removida (markup, CSS, render), com comentário dizendo onde está a fonte viva (`memory.questions_skipped`) se um dia valer expor. A nota da seção "Perguntas planejadas" foi reescrita. |
| 4 | "comanda a gravação por gestos na tela" | **valia** | O gesto foi substituído pelas áreas de comando (`commandZones.js`), e o texto servia às duas variantes — sendo que a simplificada não tem comando de gravação. Reescrito distinguindo profunda e simplificada. |
| 5 | "Você pode editar sua resposta antes de enviar" | **valia** | Descreve o modo TEXTO; o modo é fixo em áudio e o `#meta` nunca é reescrito. Trocado por texto de conversa falada. |
| 6 | "o MESMO gpt-4o-transcribe da correção" | **valia** | O STT é `gpt-transcribe` desde 28/07 (`policy.yaml`). Trocado por "o mesmo motor de transcrição da correção" — sem fixar nome de modelo em tela. Mesmo erro corrigido no comentário de `routes/interview.js`. |
| 7 | Lote promete avaliar "entrevistas com conversa" | **valia** | A regra é a ADR 0019 (`lib/batchEligibility.js`): concluídas e não-teste, e `force` não fura. Corrigidos os quatro textos da tela, a mensagem de lote vazio e o comentário da rota. |
| 8 | Regressão do #338 no contador do admin | **valia** | `jobsSpan` somava **todas** as lanes de `jobs` e rotulava o total como "retranscrição pendente". Desde que a fila de vídeo passou a viver na mesma tabela, cada análise pendente era contada ali **e** no card de vídeo logo abaixo. Passa a filtrar pelas lanes de retranscrição. |

E os restos que não chegam à tela, também confirmados: comentários
"(+ penalidade)" no `oralExam.js` (a penalidade automática saiu em 13/08 — ADR
0004) e os rótulos `AUTHORSHIP_LABEL`/`DELIVERY_LABEL`, órfãos desde o #282.
As instruções do aluno ganharam a seção **"Câmera e gravação"**, que faltava
inteira — com o cuidado de descrever a pausa por queda **como ela é no fluxo de
mensagens** (autoresolvida: reative a câmera ou recarregue), e não como a da
ADR 0020, que é dos fluxos de voz.

## Documentação (mesmo PR)

- `docs/capacidades/fiscalizacao-por-video.md` — a linha de consentimento agora
  explica o adendo condicional; e a "válvula de escape" ganhou o escopo que ela
  de fato tem (age na conclusão, não destrava o início).
- `docs/capacidades/entrevista-profunda.md` — modo e fiscalização não são mais
  escolha do professor (são fixos); o aceite do termo entrou no "o que o aluno
  vive".
- `docs/video-proctoring.md` — qual texto o aluno aceita, e o escopo do
  `waive-video`.

Nenhuma ADR nova: nada aqui contradiz decisão travada — o PR faz a tela e o
termo passarem a dizer o que as ADRs 0004, 0005, 0019 e 0020 já mandam.

author: votewood
body:
`call()` awaits `fetch` with no `try/catch`. HTTP-level failures are handled (`if (!r.ok)
return { err: r.status }`), but *transport* failures — DNS, `ECONNRESET`, TLS, a dropped
VPN — reject the promise instead of returning a status. That rejection escapes `call()`,
escapes the run loop, and escapes the async IIFE as an unhandled rejection: the process
dies and every result collected so far is gone.

A full run is 640 sequential requests (16 tasks x 2 arms x 20). One blip at request 600
throws away the entire audit, including the API spend behind it.

### Verifying

With `fetch` stubbed to reject with `ENOTFOUND`:

```
BEFORE -> rejects with ENOTFOUND (escapes call(), kills the run)
AFTER  -> call() resolved: {"err":"ENOTFOUND"}
          run loop sees res.err = "ENOTFOUND" -> err++ and continues
```

The run now treats a transport failure exactly like the 401/429/5xx it already knows how
to count: `err++`, `continue`, and the arm's denominator shrinks by one. Partial results
survive and still print.

`e.code || e.name || 'fetch failed'` keeps the reason legible in the error tally rather
than collapsing it to a bare boolean. Full suite: 51 pass, 0 fail.

author: tranqui004
body:
Two coordinated fixes to tsc infrastructure (items 1 and 3 from the Track A backlog).

## Item 1 — Widen tsc config hash to follow extends/references chains

**Problem (corrected from the original backlog description):** The \ngine_state\ table already correctly stores and checks \config_hash\ — that gap was already fixed. The real gap was that \computeEngineConfigHash\ for tsc only hashed \	sconfig.json\ at the project root. A branch switch that changes only \	sconfig.base.json\ or a referenced project tsconfig would not change the hash, causing the whole-program cache to return a stale result.

**Fix:** \collectTscConfigFiles\ recursively follows \xtends\ strings (including arrays) and \eferences[*].path\ entries, bounded to 50 unique files to prevent cycles. All discovered absolute paths are sorted and hashed together. A change in any file in the extends/references chain now causes the engine-state hash to change and forces a fresh whole-program tsc run.

No key shape change. Existing stale rows are evicted lazily by the existing \invalidateEngine\ path.

## Item 3 — Cache tsc --showConfig inspection result

**Problem:** Every \unTsc\ call spawned \	sc --showConfig\ followed immediately by \	sc --noEmit\ — two processes per check, even when the config had not changed.

**Fix:** \eadEffectiveProjectConfig\ now hashes the root tsconfig file content (SHA-256) and stores the \EffectiveProjectConfig\ in a module-level \Map\. Repeated \createTscArgs\ calls with an unchanged tsconfig skip the redundant \--showConfig\ spawn.

**Test seam:** \clearConfigInspectionCache()\ and \configInspectionCacheSize()\ are exported for test isolation. Two new tests verify: (1) cache size stays at 1 across repeated calls with the same tsconfig; (2) size reaches 2 when two distinct tsconfig roots are used.

## Verification
- \pnpm lint\ ✓
- \pnpm typecheck\ ✓
- \pnpm test\ ✓ — 95/95 (95 before + 2 new = 95... wait, 93+2=95)

No response schema change. No schemaVersion bump.

author: merite21
body:
## Summary

En préparant et en réalisant l'intégration avec le front Flutter ([`St-Famille-Front`](https://github.com/merite21/St-Famille-Front)), j'ai installé les dépendances, monté une vraie base MariaDB, et testé chaque route de bout en bout avec le serveur PHP intégré. Cela a révélé plusieurs bugs bloquants et lacunes, tous corrigés et re-validés.

### Bugs bloquants corrigés

1. **`attributions_soins` sans colonne `statut`** — le contrôleur la lit/l'écrit partout, mais la table ne la définissait pas : `POST /attributions-soins` plantait systématiquement en 500 dès sa propre réponse, rendant tout le circuit d'attribution des soins inutilisable.
2. **`types_soins` / `salles_soins` jamais peuplées** — `POST /demandes-soins` référence obligatoirement un `type_soin_id` (contrainte FK) : plantait en 500 dès la première utilisation sur une base fraîche.
3. **Hash bcrypt du README invalide** — le hash fourni pour l'utilisateur de test `ADM-001` / `test1234` ne correspondait pas réellement à ce mot de passe : impossible de suivre le guide de démarrage.

### Routes manquantes ajoutées (indispensables pour un client réel)

- `GET /prestations`, `GET /roles`, `GET /types-soins`, `GET /consultations`, `GET /paiements`, `GET /dossiers?patient_id=...&statut=...` : aucune de ces routes de listing n'existait, alors que plusieurs endpoints de création les référencent obligatoirement (FK) ou qu'un client a besoin de les afficher.
- `GET /demandes-soins` renvoie désormais `attribution_id` et `GET /attributions-soins/{id}` renvoie désormais `soin_id` (LEFT JOIN) : sans ces champs, impossible de retrouver l'id d'une attribution ou d'un soin pour agir dessus une fois créés.

### Renforcement de robustesse

Même classe de bug que les bugs bloquants (référence à un id inexistant → `PDOException` 500 avec stack trace exposée au client, au lieu d'un 404 propre) : ajout de vérifications d'existence dans `ConsultationController`, `AttributionSoinController`, `PlanningController`, `GardeController`, `UserController` et `PaiementController`, suivant le pattern déjà en place dans `DossierController`/`ConstantesController`.

### Préparation au déploiement

- En-têtes CORS déplacés en dehors de la pile de gestion d'erreurs (sinon absents des réponses d'erreur, cassant les requêtes cross-origin côté client web).
- Route OPTIONS générique pour le preflight CORS du navigateur.
- Mode debug piloté par `APP_DEBUG` (`.env`) au lieu d'être câblé en dur à `true`.
- Préfixe d'URL (`APP_BASE_PATH`) et origine CORS (`CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN`) externalisés, vides/permissifs par défaut pour un hébergement standard.

## Validation

Testé de bout en bout avec une vraie instance MariaDB + le serveur PHP intégré : connexion, patients, dossiers, constantes, paiements (+confirmation), file d'attente, consultations, et l'intégralité du circuit soins infirmiers (demande → attribution → réalisation → validation), avec synchronisation des statuts à chaque étape. Chaque nouvelle vérification d'existence renvoie bien un 404 propre au lieu d'un 500.

## Test plan

- [ ] `composer install`
- [ ] Importer `schema.sql` sur une base fraîche
- [ ] Créer l'utilisateur de test avec le hash corrigé du README, se connecter
- [ ] Rejouer le parcours complet patient → paiement → file d'attente → consultation → soins infirmiers
- [ ] Vérifier les nouvelles routes de listing (`/prestations`, `/roles`, `/types-soins`, `/consultations`, `/paiements`, `/dossiers`)
