author: vimalvijayakumar1983
body:
## Summary

This release implements the permanent, reusable voice-quality and knowledge-serving architecture agreed for VAV.

- publishes immutable, versioned knowledge serving revisions and speech lexicons
- pins browser, inbound SIP, and every native outbound provider (Sarvam, ElevenLabs, and Inworld) to one verified knowledge revision for the full call
- makes native sessions use the exact pinned knowledge-base/revision on every turn and prevents active-call deletion
- adds exact-fact retrieval, partial multi-intent fallback, caller-assertion protection, current-date grounding, and grounding-aware dispositions
- keeps PostgreSQL immutable-revision retrieval at feature parity by unioning bounded contact, broad-title, and ranked full-text candidates, with strong contact evidence protected from footer noise
- records truthful STT wire configuration, provider-reported transcript language when available, stage timings, percentile latency, usage, and pending provider-billing state
- adds bounded greeting prewarm/cache and a per-agent experimental native Inworld single-pass lane; the existing tool loop remains the production control
- adds deterministic Tier-1 knowledge quality tests plus allowlisted browser/SIP audio-replay canaries
- adds durable provider cleanup/quarantine, retry fencing, stale-repair sweeping, guarded knowledge deletion, and immutable release rollback
- secures native Twilio routing with tenant-owned credentials, live DID/webhook verification, rotation invalidation, per-call callback credential binding, replay protection, and monotonic callbacks
- atomically binds a callback-first Twilio CallSid with a one-time 256-bit capability, persists only its digest, rejects cross-call collisions, and redacts the capability from application/access logs
- revalidates inbound agent/profile/DID/credential/route state inside a deadlock-safe provider and admission lock order before returning media TwiML
- authenticates direct Twilio voice callbacks before contention, then revalidates the current credential and route under provider/runtime locks so credential rotation cannot leak stale media capability
- reserves and terminalizes LiveKit inbound calls durably before provider startup and accounts truthfully for billable prewarm attempts
- enforces a single atomic Twilio media-session owner so duplicate streams cannot overwrite or terminate the real call
- permits VAV-native agents to bind to an immutable retained live knowledge release while draft changes await approval; Smallest.ai remains approval/provider-index gated
- performs complete, bounded readiness probes for Sarvam and ElevenLabs dependency chains, failing closed on unreadable workspace credentials
- keeps dependency auditing fail-closed for real vulnerabilities while bounding and retrying transient npm registry failures

## Safety and rollout

The branch deliberately begins with staged-schema compatibility and then enables the full release at Alembic head `20260904_024`.

Production must follow `docs/REALTIME_QUALITY_ROLLOUT.md`: deploy the compatibility bridge, take a verified backup, drain native calls, run migrations in a dedicated job, backfill a canary tenant, repair every quarantine, backfill all tenants, verify immutable pointers, re-run Twilio DID readiness and explicit activation for affected native profiles, then deploy the same full-release SHA to API/Celery/frontend/LiveKit worker and run browser + SIP canaries.

Before direct Twilio traffic is enabled, complete `docs/TWILIO_CALLBACK_CLAIM_ROLLOUT.md` and verify callback-capability redaction at every Railway edge/proxy, WAF, APM, tracing, and log-drain boundary.

This PR must not be released through a blind auto-deploy.

Diagnostic recording remains fail-closed. The release adds governance scaffolding only; it does not capture audio until consent, storage, retention, and access controls are configured.

- Final changed-path callback/retrieval matrix: **109 passed, 8 skipped**
- Direct callback/claim/admission matrix: **56 passed, 7 skipped**
- Immutable retrieval/serving matrix: **53 passed, 1 skipped**

- TypeScript: passed with zero type errors

author: deer
body:
`TypeUsages` previously exposed two overlapping public methods: `isCompatible(requested, candidate)`, a generic-aware wildcard/argument check, and `isAssignable(from, to)`, a raw class/interface-hierarchy check. The two names did not clearly convey which was the full JLS check, and `isCompatible`'s argument comparison had a latent bug: it compared nested parameterized type arguments in only one direction, so `List<List<? extends Impl>>` was wrongly accepted against a requested `List<List<? extends Base>>` even though the outer `List<...>` argument is invariant per JLS 4.5.1.

This change collapses the API to one public method, `isAssignable(subtype, supertype)`, a JLS 4.10 subtype check that is covariant through the class/interface hierarchy at the top level and applies JLS 4.5.1 containment to a parameterized supertype's own type arguments. The old raw-hierarchy check becomes a private helper, `isErasedSubtype`. Type-argument containment now lives in a private `contains`, with the invariance of a non-wildcard argument enforced by `isSameArgument`, which requires mutual `argumentsContained` in both directions and so correctly rejects the nested-wildcard case above. The former `isBoundAssignable` special-casing of parameterized wildcard bounds is gone: `contains` recurses straight back into `isAssignable`, which is now itself generic-aware.

The DI resolver is the only consumer. `Dependency.resolve` now calls `TypeUsages.isAssignable(candidate.typeUsage(), requested.typeUsage(), codeModel)` in place of `isCompatible(requested.typeUsage(), candidate.typeUsage(), codeModel)` -- arguments swapped to the new `(subtype, supertype)` order, semantics unchanged. `docs/CODEBASE_MAP.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the surrounding Javadoc are updated to describe the single entry point and its private helpers.

author: bobzhang
body:
Four commits, each independently reviewable.

## 1. `prompt~` (`e9e1d83`)

The prompt was positional while everything around it was labelled, so
the argument carrying the actual work was the one the call site never
named. That is real README code, not a strawman:

```moonbit
wf.try_agent(
  kind="judge",
  "Judge the finding through lens=\{lens}: real?",   // ← unnamed
  label="verify:\{lens}",
)
```

`agent`, `agent_as` (and, at the time, the `try_` pair) now take
`prompt~`, matching `agent_call`, which was already fully labelled. 119
call sites move with it, punning `prompt~` where the variable already
carries the name.

## 2. `try_agent` / `try_agent_as` deleted (`1cf0a58`)

`attempt` folds the typed error channel around any raising step, so the
two `try_` methods were a second spelling of one idea — and only for the
explore shape, which is why `agent_call` never had twins. **Five call
entry points become three**, with one way to reach a `Result`:

```moonbit
@workflow.attempt(() => wf.agent(prompt=item, kind="scout"))
```

It costs a closure at the fan-out site. It buys a surface where the
shape a caller wants is always a combinator — `attempt`, `retry`, their
composition — never another method to find.

## 3. `moon ide analyze` sweep (`16e28a4`)

The tool annotates each exported item with how many dependents touch it.

**Surface no one could reach.** `shim/claude` and `shim/codex` are
executables — nothing can import them — yet both exported their observer
wholesale. Their interfaces are now a bare `type X`:

```diff
-pub struct Codex { mut steps : Int; mut thread_id : String?; … }
-pub fn Codex::new() -> Self
-pub fn Codex::observe(Self, String) -> Array[Json]
-pub fn Codex::report(Self, structured~ : Bool) -> Json?
+type Codex
```

`Codex` also gains a `Codex()` constructor in place of `new()` — the
same move `9f3c021` made on `Claude`.

**Over-wide annotations.** `AgentDisposition`, `JournalEntry` and
`WorkflowEvent` carried `pub(all)` where the report says
`(all) or (open) can be removed`. Matching from outside still works —
that is what events and journal entries are *for* — so `pub` is the
honest annotation.

**Deliberate exports get a home.** Three symbols the report calls unused
are public on purpose, because their caller lives outside this
repository. They move to `exports.mbt`, which the tool recognises and
annotates `in exports.mbt`:

| symbol | who calls it |
| --- | --- |
| `worth_retrying` | a caller narrowing the `retry` policy rather than rebuilding it |
| `Runner::invoke` | a composing runner delegating by kind without reaching for the private field |
| `ContractProgress` + ctor | a caller watching a run that ends by cancellation |

The report is now clean apart from `ContractTerminal::ContextYield` and
`TimedOut` — `contract_run` produces them, nothing here matches them,
and a variant cannot move.

## 4. `AGENTS.md` (`1d4ea42`)

Writes the convention down: a `pub` nothing uses is either surface to
drop, or public for a named outside caller and belongs in `exports.mbt`.
A symbol that cannot name its outside caller belongs private.

## Gates

`moon check` (native + wasm, `--deny-warn`), `moon fmt --check`, and
`moon test` on both targets: 91/91.

Examples still pin the published `0.4.1`, so they cannot compile until a
release catches up — the pre-release state #12 already documents.

author: jideokus
body:
Main was red after two waves that changed rendered output on purpose. This re-points the tests at what shipped, and fixes one real regression they caught.

## Result

```
backend   80 failed, 1087 passed   →   0 failed, 1167 passed
web       93 failed,   51 passed   →   0 failed,   59 passed
```

Web blast radius: 4,134 passed, 2 failures in `BillingSettings.dom.test.tsx` (a date off-by-one) confirmed pre-existing on the untouched base. `next build` succeeds; no new typecheck errors.

## The regression it caught — mine

The heading of the ruled-out ledger was changed from `len(shown)` to `len(ledger)` so it would report the true total rather than a truncated one. Half right: by the time the heading is built, `shown` has already had the aggregate bookkeeping rows filtered out, and the same change had already removed the truncation. `len(shown)` was already correct, and `len(ledger)` put the overflow summary and the ungroupable row back in as two more rejections — so a hundred-rejection run read `(102)`.

That is precisely the defect `test_the_ledger_count_is_candidates_not_rows` exists for. The test was left red rather than adjusted, which was the right call, and the fix is `len(shown)`.

`_assert_the_ledger_adds_up` was also strengthened to check the same property across every corpus shape, so this is now guarded end-to-end rather than by one unit test.

## How the tests were re-pointed

Prose has moved twice in a night, so assertions that could be made structural were. Money statements are located **by the disclaimer they must carry** (`"not a projection"`, `"not what was agreed"`) rather than by their opening words. Tail arithmetic asserts `written_up + shown + beyond == total` against the constants, so changing a cap no longer needs a test edit. Section-ordering tests assert the property they were protecting — a qualifier appears before what it qualifies, nothing above the appendix names a set-aside theme — rather than hard-coded positions.

Where an exact string is the contract — an invariant disclosure, a caveat, a refusal — the literal is kept, because the wording is the point.

Two assertions were made **stronger** than before: the sanitizer test now asserts an exact round trip rather than a forbidden-substring list, so it catches a dropped tag the list never named; and the I3 check gained a per-row assertion over the tail's Worth column.

`test_a_finding_quotes_one_of_its_claims` became `test_a_finding_carries_a_summary_of_one_of_its_claims` — a finding no longer quotes anything, deliberately, and the old name encoded the behaviour that was removed.

## The web test file

`GoalAnalysisReport.dom.test.tsx` went from ~1,490 lines to ~190. The component no longer renders the document — it is chrome around a sandboxed iframe — so all 82 failures asserted a renderer that no longer exists, and the ten that "passed" passed vacuously. The new file maps every deleted concern by name to the Python test that now makes it, and asserts what this component is actually responsible for: the report arrives character-for-character, the sandbox is `allow-same-origin` without `allow-scripts`, whitespace counts as no report, and both irreversible document actions disable together.

## Also

Build-process vocabulary removed from nine docstrings across six files ("this ticket", "this PR"). Left alone: references to the client's own locked spec, and "gate 1"/"gate 2", which is product vocabulary.

Three functions are now unreachable and flagged rather than deleted, since removing them is a product change: `_further_findings_sentence`, `_findings_heading`, and `web/app/lib/goalRice.ts`.

author: testikun
body:
## Problem

OpenPI Web had no package-owned theme preference. A browser-local choice would create a second source of truth and drift from the canonical `/openpi-setup` contract. This implements the canonical theme slice of #350 without overlapping PR #359's language/localStorage work.

## Value

Users can choose `system`, `light`, or `dark` once through OpenPI setup, see that choice in no-argument setup status, and have every Web client render the same authoritative preference. The default follows the browser/OS color scheme.

## Approach

- Add `ui.webTheme` to `MyPiSetupConfig`, defaulting and failing closed to `system`.
- Extend the episode-scoped typed setup writer with `ui_web_theme`, update status/prompt/docs/defaults, and register the field in the config drift guard.
- Project the canonical preference in `WebSnapshot`; the browser resolves `system` with `prefers-color-scheme` and never persists a competing theme value.
- Refactor Web colors into semantic light/dark tokens so interactive, code, menu, dialog, and composer states remain coherent.

## Validation

- `bun run check` — passed, including the 15-field configuration contract.
- `bun run test` — passed: Node 1241 passed / 1 platform skip; Vitest 30 passed.
- Focused setup/config/Web suites — 95 passed.
- Runtime provenance: isolated `pi list` reported the single OpenPI source `/tmp/openpi-issue-350`, whose checkout was based on `72fbba52832841cfc78c2f7e7947eeb89efc73bc` plus this PR commit.
- Real local Workbench test: canonical `ui.webTheme=dark` produced `preferences.theme=dark` from `/api/snapshot` and rendered the final dark UI in an actual browser. No mock image was used. The 1280×720 screenshot is attached to the first #350 claim comment.

## Impact

- User-visible behavior: OpenPI Web gains canonical system/light/dark themes; default remains system-following.
- Model-visible context/tools: the existing setup tool gains one bounded enum field only during setup episodes; no ordinary-turn tool is added.
- Runtime/lifecycle: snapshots synchronously read the small canonical setup document; system mode reacts to browser color-scheme changes for the page lifetime.
- Persisted config/data: adds optional canonical `ui.webTheme`; old or invalid documents read safely as `system` and are normalized on the next setup write.
- Compatibility/risk: additive protocol field with protocol version unchanged; older clients ignore it, and the new client safely falls back to `system` if absent.

author: juanjux
body:
## Description

Python-managed forks inherit the native telemetry worker, but not a usable background runtime. Stopping that inherited worker in the child can run shutdown logic against parent-owned state.

This change uses the new libdatadog worker policy API to:

- disable child restart in the Python before-fork hook;
- restore native-fork restart in the parent hook; and
- drop the inherited worker without shutdown, then rebuild it lazily in the child.

## IMPORTANT 
This PR depends on the [companion libdatadog change](https://github.com/DataDog/libdatadog/pull/2464) and a release containing that API. It is temporarily pinned to the companion commit for validation and must be changed to the released version before merge.

## Testing

- `cargo check --manifest-path src/native/Cargo.toml --all-features`
- Telemetry regressions covering Python-managed and native fork sequences
- Full repository lint checks

## Risks

Fork-hook ordering is sensitive. Regression tests verify that the parent restores native-fork behavior and that the child does not emit lifecycle shutdown events for inherited state.

## Additional Notes

No release note is needed because this fixes behavior introduced by unreleased mainline changes.

author: ryanjamesmunden-rgb
body:
## The dead stop

Signing in re-rendered the join page with a Subscribe button where the sign-in prompt had been, and the visitor had to notice that and click again. A pause on the one screen where someone has already decided to pay is where they leave.

**Before:** see prompt → sign in → *notice the page changed* → find Subscribe → click → Stripe
**After:** press Subscribe → sign in → Stripe

Pressing Subscribe now carries the intent through the sign-in and continues by itself. The account is a step in buying, not a hurdle in front of it — while still being what lets checkout carry an account id, which is what makes the cancel button possible later.

**It only continues for someone who asked to subscribe.** Signing in to look around never throws anyone at a checkout they didn't request. And arriving at Stripe charges nobody — it's a page you fill in and confirm.

## It also stopped demanding an account for nothing

While Stripe is unconfigured the page falls back to the old payment link, and **that link cannot be tied to an account**. So the sign-in it was insisting on bought the visitor precisely nothing and cost a step.

That is the state the live site is in *right now*, so this is a real fix today, not just after the Stripe keys land. Signed-out visitors go straight to the payment link, exactly as they did before any of this work.

## The four states

| Visitor | Sees |
|---|---|
| Signed out, Stripe live | **Subscribe — £20/month** → sign in → Stripe |
| Signed in, not a member | **Subscribe** → Stripe |
| Already a member | "You're already a member — go to your account" |
| Stripe not configured | The existing payment link, no sign-in demanded |

## Testing

104 frontend files parse. Not clicked in a browser — the state worth checking after deploy is the middle of the new flow: press Subscribe signed out, and confirm Google's button appears rather than nothing.

author: tclose
body:
### Motivation

Two gaps surfaced while building a single-pass `group` over a mixed tree (dermoscopy
images + a Canfield Vectra export in one input dir):

- **`--ignore-path` conflated two things.** It only suppressed `FormatRecognitionError`
  for *unrecognised* leftovers, matched on basename only, and couldn't exclude a path
  that *is* a recognised datatype — so a vendor thumbnail that happens to be a valid
  `image/png`, three directories deep, could not be filtered out while keeping the real
  dermoscopy PNGs two deep.
- **`--on-resource-clash` was one global policy.** No way to say "PNG + JPEG views of a
  lesion may `merge`, but a PNG colliding with a directory format is a mistake — raise".

### `--ignore-path` → `--allow-unrecognised`

Renamed for clarity: the distinguishing behaviour is "applies **only** to paths nothing
recognised", not "matches a filename".

- CLI: `--ignore-path` → `--allow-unrecognised` (alias `--allow-unrecognized`);
  `XINGEST_IGNORE_PATH` → `XINGEST_ALLOW_UNRECOGNISED`.
- `group()` / `ImagingSession.from_paths` kwarg `ignore_paths` → `allow_unrecognised`.
- Behaviour unchanged: basename regex, delegated to fileformats' `from_paths(ignore=…)`,
  never touches a recognised fileset. `--allow-unrecognised '.*'` tolerates every stray
  file.

### New `--exclude-path <glob>`

Glob matched against each input path **relative to its input directory**, applied
*before* classification (`_drop_excluded_paths` in `from_paths`), so a match is dropped
even if a `--datatype` would claim it.

- `glob.translate` semantics: `*` does not cross `/`, `**` does; the whole relative
  path must match.
- Repeatable; `XINGEST_EXCLUDE_PATH`; `group()` / `from_paths` kwarg `exclude_paths`.
- e.g. `--exclude-path '*/*/*.png'` drops 3-deep vendor thumbnails while keeping 2-deep
  dermoscopy PNGs.

### Datatype-scoped `--on-resource-clash`

`--on-resource-clash` is now `<policy> <scope>` (`nargs=2`, repeatable, `default=()`),
backed by a new `ClashSpec(policy, scope)` arg type (`scope` = a MIME-like, a
`|`-union, or `all`).

- A clash between two filesets is resolved by the **first** `ClashSpec` whose `scope`
  covers **both** of them. The scope check is `SetOf`-aware (via `content_types`), so a
  re-merge into an existing `SetOf[Png, Jpeg]` is still covered by
  `image/png|image/jpeg`.
- `merge` folds both into `SetOf[<union of member content types>]`; `avoid` suffixes
  `__2`/`__3`; `overwrite` replaces.
- A clash **no** spec's scope covers raises `KeyError`, naming both datatypes — so a
  cross-type collision (e.g. `image/png` vs a directory format) is always surfaced
  rather than silently merged or overwritten, unless you deliberately give a scope that
  covers both.
- `ImagingSession.add_resource` still accepts a bare policy string, so `deidentify` /
  `associate` (which keep their scalar `--on-resource-clash`) are unchanged.

### Migration

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `--ignore-path <regex>` | `--allow-unrecognised <regex>` |
| `XINGEST_IGNORE_PATH` | `XINGEST_ALLOW_UNRECOGNISED` |
| `--on-resource-clash merge` | `--on-resource-clash merge all` |
| `group(ignore_paths=…)` / `from_paths(ignore_paths=…)` | `…allow_unrecognised=…` (+ new `exclude_paths=…`) |

`deidentify` / `associate` `--on-resource-clash` are untouched.

### Tests

- `ClashSpec` unit tests (single mime / union / `all` scope, bad-policy rejection, CLI
  `nargs=2` parsing).
- `add_resource` with `ClashSpec` list: union scope merges a Png+Jpeg into
  `SetOf[Png, Jpeg]`; two single-type specs don't jointly cover it → raise; a clash no
  scope covers → raise; `avoid` within scope; a 3rd fileset re-merged into an existing
  `SetOf`.
- `from_paths` with `--exclude-path '*/*/*.txt'` drops a 3-deep recognised file, keeps
  the 2-deep one.
- Renamed the `test_group_ignore_path*` CLI/API tests to `…_allow_unrecognised*`.

149 model / API / arg-types tests + 16 CLI `group`/`check_upload` tests pass;
`test_deidentify_cli_dicom_missing_transform` fails but is pre-existing on `main`.

### Docs

`how_to/pipeline.rst`: new subsections — *Recursing into nested directory formats*,
*Deciding what to skip* (`--exclude-path` / `--ignore-datatype` / `--allow-unrecognised`),
*Handling resource-name clashes*; fixed the stale "grouped by
StudyInstanceUID/SeriesNumber/ImageType" defaults paragraph. `cli.rst` auto-generates
from the updated option help. Sphinx builds clean.

author: pierre-warnier
body:
Closes #223. Follow-up promised in the review of #211.

## The inconsistency

`groupadd -K` was handled by hand-patching two variables inside `allocate_gid`:

```rust
for &(key, val) in overrides {
    match key {
        "GID_MIN" | "SYS_GID_MIN" => if let Ok(v) = val.parse::<u32>() { min = v; }
        "GID_MAX" | "SYS_GID_MAX" => if let Ok(v) = val.parse::<u32>() { max = v; }
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

So only four keys were understood, every other key was silently dropped, and the pair parser differed from `useradd`'s — `groupadd` accepted an empty key, `useradd` rejected it. The same flag behaved differently depending on which tool you ran.

## Changes

- **`shadow-core`** gains `login_defs::parse_override`, the one place that decides what a malformed `KEY=VALUE` is: missing `=` or empty key rejected, empty value allowed (it unsets the key for the run). Unit-tested.
- **`groupadd`** loads `login.defs` once, folds the overrides in with `LoginDefs::set` (from #211), and passes that to `determine_gid`. `allocate_gid` no longer reloads the file or carries a patch table — `gid_range` simply reads the overridden values. The `-K` help text, which I had narrowed in #162 to the four keys the old code honoured, is widened back to match.
- **`useradd`**'s parser becomes a thin wrapper over the shared one, so the duplication introduced in #211 is gone.

Behaviour change for `groupadd` only: a malformed pair now exits 3 (bad argument) as `useradd` already did, instead of being partly accepted.

## Tests

- Unit: `parse_override` accepts `K=V`, `K=` and `A=b=c`; rejects `K`, `=V` and `""`.
- Integration, as root: a `-K` GID range wins over the one in `login.defs` (regular and system ranges); a malformed pair exits 3 and writes nothing.
- `test_useradd` unchanged and still green (25/25), confirming the wrapper is behaviour-preserving.

## Verified

Full gate on Debian, rebased onto `main` after #235: `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` with and without `pam`, `cargo test --workspace` with and without `pam`, plus the root integration suites for `groupadd` (14/14) and `useradd` (25/25).

author: pleymor
body:
Two complaints, one deploy apart:

> si un jeu est déjà présent dans l'indexedDB, ne pas le copier à nouveau, c'est long

> bien ouvrir le salon VR automatiquement après. ne pas attendre un 2e clic, c'est hyper naze

Both were right, and **neither needed the compromise I had been defending.**

## "c'est long"

A kept game was never re-copied — the filter already excluded it. The waste was upstream: the folder was scanned and every cartridge hashed **before** anything checked whether there was work to do.

Listing what the device holds is one key query against IndexedDB. The order is now that way round, and a device with nothing missing does not even open its folder. A test asserts exactly that — that neither `scanFolder` nor `storedDirectory` is called.

## "hyper naze"

The second press is gone, and without betting on anything.

The transfer never needed a gesture. It needs the folder **permission**, which is already granted and requires no click — so it happens while the page sits there, before anybody presses. By the time they do, there is nothing left to do and the press walks straight into the session.

## And a claim I have been repeating without measuring it

Since #34 I have asserted that `requestSession` needs the transient activation the press carried, and that a native dialog or seconds of reading spends it. **I never measured that on this browser.** It was the whole justification for the second press, and being told to press again after sitting through a transfer is a miserable way to discover it was wrong.

So after a foreground transfer it now just opens the session. If the headset refuses, `VrShell` reports it and a second press still works — `needsPrepare` is false by then, so the button enters directly. This is labelled as the bet it is, and its failure locks nobody out.

The two "press again" messages are deleted from both locales; nothing asks any more.

## Verification

- 589 tests pass (+2), 0 failures
- `svelte-check`: 0 errors, 15 warnings across 9 files — the unchanged baseline
- `bun run build` succeeds
- **Proven to bite:** scanning before checking what is kept fails the suite, and so does re-copying what is already kept

author: artyomsv
body:
## What

**A claim I put in the repo yesterday is wrong, and this withdraws it.**

The comment added alongside `spire-ui`'s new `apk --no-cache upgrade` said its base carried **24 OS
vulnerabilities, four of them HIGH**. It did not.

That was measured against a **six-week-old local copy**. `docker run` and `docker build` resolve a
floating tag from the local store before the registry, so scanning `:1.30-alpine` reported on
whatever was pulled last, not on what the tag points at:

```
before docker pull:  sha256:44e36330…  created 2026-07-20   openssl 3.5.7-r0, libexpat 2.8.2-r0
after  docker pull:  sha256:9b87ad3d…  created 2026-09-02   openssl 3.5.8-r0, libexpat 2.8.4-r0
```

Re-measured after the pull, on current digests:

| Base | OS vulnerabilities |
|---|---|
| `nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine` | **0** |
| `nginx-unprivileged:1.31-alpine` | **0** |
| `eclipse-temurin:25-jre-alpine` | **34** |

**The tell was in the merge build and I did not read it.** `spire-ui`'s first CI run with the new
line upgraded nothing but `apk-tools`, while the three service images upgraded libcrypto3, libssl3,
libexpat and openssl. That is what sent me back to check.

## What changes, and what does not

- **Nothing about the service images.** `eclipse-temurin:25-jre-alpine` is genuinely stale on its
  *current* digest — 34 OS vulnerabilities, openssl 3.5.7-r0 and libexpat 2.8.3-r0, exactly the
  versions the 102 alerts named. Merge build `33847927972` logged
  `apk upgrade for build 33847927972` on all four images and the upgrades on the three services,
  where run `33810550375` had logged `CACHED`. That finding stands entirely.
- **`spire-ui` keeps the upgrade, on the honest argument.** The two nginx retags visible here are
  2026-07-20 and 2026-09-02 — six weeks apart — and the older carried the same openssl 3.5.7-r0 the
  service images were raising alerts on. So the line closes a *window*, not a present backlog, for
  about a second of build time. Removing it would trade that for nothing.
- **#97 stays declined on one reason instead of two.** The CVE argument is withdrawn. What stands is
  checked and independent: `stable-alpine` → 1.30.4, `mainline-alpine` → 1.31.5, so the bump is a
  **stable→mainline branch switch** that Dependabot cannot see. With both tags at 0 there is nothing
  on the other side of that trade.

## Also

Adds the general trap to `CLAUDE.md`'s gotchas, since it is not specific to this image:

> **Scanning a floating tag locally measures your last pull, not the tag.** `docker pull` first,
> then scan, and say which digest was measured.

Comments only plus two doc files — no production line changes. `testFast` green; `spire-ui` rebuilt
to confirm the Dockerfile still parses.

author: fred-labs
body:
AGENTS.md had grown into a second description of how the service, the cluster lane and the packaging work. A working agreement and a description of the system have different lifetimes: the copy drifts from the page that owns the fact, and a reader cannot tell which of the two is current.

**AGENTS.md now states only what a change must hold** — one lead of at most three lines per rule plus a single level of bullets — and links the page that describes each mechanism (206 lines to 89).

Four facts that lived only there move into the docs:

- **Add an interface operation** (developer guide): the contract, both transports, the route, every surface, and that a value the pod needs must travel the cluster path too.
- **A distribution's own verbs are not entry points** (developer guide), beside the rule about installed metadata it follows from.
- **Why a lane is not installable as an extra** (architecture), in the section on the dependency direction — which until now deferred to AGENTS.md for exactly that.
- **The auth gate is ASGI middleware resolving a principal** (HTTP API), which is what covers a new route and the mounted `/mcp` sub-app.

Two rules are added: a comment in a `.vast` is short and rare — ideally inline, at most two lines, and only where a value would otherwise read as arbitrary — and an addition to AGENTS.md follows the same rules it states.

**Second commit: the spelling dictionary.** `make checkspelling` fails on 165 occurrences across nineteen pages — technical terms, identifiers quoted in prose, and British spellings the documentation has picked up since the word list was last extended; none of them a typo. The drift is invisible because the docs workflow runs `make doc` and not the spelling target. With the words added, `make doc` and `make checkspelling` both pass.

author: oyren-ai-agent[bot]
body:
Minimal v1 of "prefer structured agent adapters over tmux typing". **Stacked on `comms/tmux-bridge-geometry`** (PR #61, itself on #56) — merge that chain first and this retargets cleanly. Orchestrator half is PR #106.

Scope held to detection + routing preference + tests. **No adapter protocol is defined here** — this routes to an endpoint a pane already advertises.

## Detection

A pane declares a structured transport by setting a tmux per-pane user option from inside itself:

```
tmux set-option -p @oyren_agent_endpoint http://127.0.0.1:<port>
```

The design note suggested "an env var or pane title". I used a **pane user option** instead: it is first-class tmux metadata that reads straight out of the existing list format (one more field, no extra call), and unlike the title it cannot collide with the human label agents already put there — every agent pane in this container has a ticket name in its title. An env var would need `/proc/<pane_pid>/environ` plus child-process walking, which is a bigger v1 than this ticket wants; it remains the natural v2.

Such panes report `mode: "structured"` and carry `endpoint`. Everything else stays `"tty"`, exactly as before.

## Routing

`POST /tmux/panes/:id/input` posts `{text, enter}` to the endpoint instead of running `send-keys`, and the response says which transport carried it. Typing into a terminal becomes the fallback for panes that have nothing better, rather than the default for everything.

## Three choices worth reviewing

**Only loopback http(s) endpoints are honoured.** Anything in the container can set a pane option, and this runtime holds the session token — an unrestricted value would turn it into an open proxy for whatever a pane names. Rejected values are not an error; the pane just stays `tty`. Tested against `evil.example`, `169.254.169.254`, RFC1918, `file://`, and the `127.0.0.1.evil.example` prefix trick.

**A failed structured send is a 502 naming the endpoint, not a silent fallback to typing.** If the endpoint *did* receive the text, retyping it would deliver the same message twice. The caller decides, with `transport: "tty"` — which also rescues a pane whose endpoint is wedged, so an advertisement can never strand a pane the caller can plainly see.

**The stale-pane guard applies to both paths.** A pane that changed since the caller observed it is not messaged over *any* transport.

## Verification

54/54 tests green (11 new: detection, endpoint validation table, routing both ways, the forced-tty override, both transport-failure modes, and the guard on the structured path).

Live on this container's real tmux server: a pane advertised `http://127.0.0.1:47701/msg` via the option, the bridge reported `mode=structured` for exactly that pane with every other pane still `tty`, and a send arrived at the HTTP endpoint as `{"text":"ROUTED-NOT-TYPED","enter":true}` with `via=structured` in the log — no keystrokes were sent. The option was unset afterwards.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

- 검색 기준 칩 문구를 `"[장소] 주변"`에서 `"[장소] 주변에서 검색"`으로 바꿨습니다(영문은 `Around X` → `Search around X`).
- 검색 기준 칩 아이콘을 `MapPin`에서 `MapPinned`로 바꿨습니다.
- 칩이 줄바꿈하지 않고, 한 줄에 들어가지 않는 이름만 칩 안에서 `…`로 잘리도록 했습니다.

## 변경 이유

두 칩은 배경색·크기·아이콘 색이 모두 같아서, 문구를 읽어야만 무엇이 출발지이고 무엇이 검색 기준인지 알 수 있었습니다. 특히 아무것도 정하지 않으면 검색 기준이 출발지로, 출발지도 없으면 현재 위치로 떨어지기 때문에 두 칩이 나란히 "현재 위치…"라고 말해 더 구분되지 않았습니다.

화살표는 둘의 관계("여기서 출발해 저기 주변을 찾는다")를 글자 대신 모양으로 보여줍니다. 문구를 "주변에서 검색"으로 바꾼 것은 출발지 칩만 동사를 갖고 있었기 때문입니다. 장소 이름만 있으면 그곳에서 무엇이 일어나는지 말하지 않아, 처음 보는 사람은 그 값이 검색 범위라는 것을 알기 어렵습니다.

아이콘은 이 칩이 "그 지점"이 아니라 "그 자리 주변"을 뒤진다는 뜻이라, 바닥 원이 깔린 핀이 뜻에 맞습니다. 도착지를 뜻하는 깃발류는 일부러 쓰지 않았습니다 — 이 값은 이동해서 가는 곳이 아니라 후보를 모으는 기준점이라, 옆의 화살표와 겹쳐 경로로 오해될 수 있습니다.

## 확인 방법

1. 위치 설정 화면을 엽니다. 두 칩 사이에 화살표가 보입니다.
2. 검색 결과에서 장소를 골라 검색 기준으로 지정하면 `"[장소] 주변에서 검색"`으로 표시됩니다.
3. 이름이 긴 장소(예: 국립현대미술관 서울관 앞 광장)를 지정하면 칩 안에서 `…`로 잘리고, 칩이 아래로 내려가지 않습니다.

실제 브라우저(Chrome, 420px 폭)에서 값이 없을 때·둘 다 있을 때·이름이 길 때 세 가지를 확인했습니다.

## 테스트 결과

- `npx vitest run` — 64개 파일 524개 테스트 통과
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — 통과
- `npx eslint .` — 통과 (경고 1건은 이 PR과 무관한 기존 `DeveloperChatPage.tsx`)
- develop(`db4a73b`) 병합 후 위 검사를 다시 돌려 통과를 확인했습니다.

칩 문구를 문장 그대로 유지했기 때문에 기존 테스트를 고치지 않았습니다. `LocationPage.test.tsx`는 이 PR에서 변경되지 않았습니다.

## Out of Scope

- 사이드바의 위치 표시. 이번에는 위치 설정 화면의 칩만 바꿨습니다.
- 출발지 칩의 아이콘·문구. `Navigation` 아이콘과 `"~에서 출발"`을 그대로 뒀습니다.

## 리뷰 참고사항

- **칩 폭을 반씩 나누지 않았습니다.** 처음에는 두 칩에 `flex-1`을 줬는데, `"현재 위치에서 출발"`처럼 짧은 쪽이 남는 자리를 붙들고 있어서 긴 이름 쪽이 자리가 있는데도 먼저 잘렸습니다. 실측으로 `"광화문광장"`(5자)부터 잘렸고, `flex-1`을 떼자 `"서울역사박물관 앞"`(9자)까지 잘리지 않았습니다. 그래서 칩이 제 내용만큼만 차지하고 한 줄에 정말 안 들어갈 때만 자르도록 했습니다.
- 줄바꿈(`flex-wrap`)을 없앤 것은 칩이 아래로 내려가면 화살표만 줄 끝에 홀로 남기 때문입니다.
- `MapPin`은 이 파일에서 검색 결과 줄과 즐겨찾기 목록에도 쓰이고 있어, 칩 하나만 바꿨습니다.

## 관련 작업

- 없습니다. 앞선 PR #371(즐겨찾기 개수·10개 제한)과 같은 화면이지만 서로 독립적인 변경입니다.

author: simplyjaytea
body: ## Summary Live QA hit `SIMPLYPF2E.Errors.BadJson` ("The AI response was not valid JSON. Try generating again.") on NPC Generate/Preview. This PR audits the JSON request/parse/retry path and fixes real defects that reject **complete** JSON, while staying fail-closed on truncated/incomplete output. ## Audit notes ### Root causes found 1. **`parseConceptJSON` used first `{` + last `}`.** A complete nested object with trailing prose that contains `}` (commentary, a second fence, "the closing } is required", etc.) slices past the real end and `JSON.parse` fails. The user then sees BadJson even though the model returned a complete object. Matching-brace scan with string/escape awareness stops at the object's own closer. 2. **Diagnostics hid the failure mode.** Parse failures dumped the raw payload via `console.error` with no `finish_reason`, content length, or reasoning size. Empty content with a populated reasoning channel used the generic EmptyResponse string, so a reasoning-only model looked like "not valid JSON" / empty rather than "JSON was not in the content field." `finish_reason: "max_tokens"` (common on OpenAI-compatible clones) was not treated as truncation, so a cut-off response could surface as BadJson instead of Truncated. 3. **Some complete payloads never reached the parser.** Chat Completions `message.content` as a text-part array would throw `TypeError` on `.trim()`, and SSE proxies that put the full message on `choice.message.content` (no `delta.content`) looked empty. ### Hypotheses checked and rejected - **Salvaging truncated JSON / nested-object rescue.** An unclosed root that contains a complete nested object still fails closed. Walking inward after an unmatched `{` would invent a partial concept. - **Accepting JSON from `reasoning` / `reasoning_content` / `thinking`.** No safe fail-closed path: that channel is a scratch trace, not the answer. Still rejected; if content is empty and reasoning ran, the UI now says so (`ReasoningWithoutJson`). - **`response_format: json_object` dropped incorrectly.** Compatibility retry still removes it only when a 400/422 body names that parameter (longest-first, so `stream` cannot steal `stream_options`). First and retry JSON attempts still send `json_object` unless the provider rejected it by name. - **Retry-once was dead.** It already fired for retryable BadJson/Empty/Truncated. This PR keeps that loop, asserts the `IMPORTANT RETRY` prompt, and attaches truncated diagnostics to the existing retry warning. ## What changed - String-aware first-complete-object extract; one unwrap of a JSON-encoded object string; text-part array join. - Truncation still rejected **before parse** for `finish_reason` `length` and `max_tokens`, including complete-looking prefixes. - Retry warning logs `finishReason`, `contentLength`, `reasoningChars`, and a 480-char preview (no request headers/keys). - New `ReasoningWithoutJson` string when the content channel is empty but reasoning tokens arrived. ## Verification (local) - `node --check` on touched `.mjs` - `lang/en.json` parses - `git diff --check` clean - All 59 `scripts/*.test.mjs` files pass ## Live QA for JT (not claimed here) - NPC Generate and Preview Plan on the same provider/model that produced BadJson. - Confirm either a parsed concept or a **specific** error: Truncated, ReasoningWithoutJson, BadStructure, or a provider error — not a false BadJson on complete JSON. - Optional: a reasoning-heavy local model should now name the reasoning-channel miss instead of Empty/BadJson. ## Out of scope - Feat-prerequisite evaluator / Rogue-Investigator widening - Hand-authored Rule Elements - Merge to `main` / release - Repairing truncated JSON into a partial concept

author: eugene999b
body:
## Fix
- Check the canonical School record and login directory separately before onboarding.
- Detect and remove stale orphan `SchoolLoginDirectory` rows instead of falsely blocking a new school.
- Return a precise school login-code conflict message when the code is genuinely reserved.
- Translate any remaining Prisma unique-constraint race into the same actionable error.

## Why
The generic P2002 handler could report a duplicate record even when the visible school record did not exist. `SchoolLoginDirectory.uniqueCode` is independently unique and is not relationally constrained to `School`, so a stale directory row can survive and block onboarding.

## Validation
CI should run schema/migrations, typecheck, lint, tests, and production build.

author: axvenlabs
body:
## Summary

RUST-115 composes the exact reviewed RUST-114 detached checkpoint-monitor verifier and rotates its three TEST-only monitors from M1/M2/M3 to M2/M3/M4 while preserving a 2-of-3 quorum.

- The predecessor set is the exact pinned RUST-114 monitor set.
- M1 is explicitly revoked; M2 and M3 continue; deterministic TEST-only M4 uses seed `0d ×32`.
- The rotation binds the exact predecessor RUST-114 monitor bundle SHA-256 and all 12 inherited RUST-113 checkpoint target fields.
- Rotation authorization is signed by the predecessor set under 2-of-3; all 3/3 valid two-monitor predecessor subsets are accepted.
- The successor bundle binds a new monitor-set epoch and all 3/3 valid two-monitor successor subsets are accepted.
- Revoked-monitor resurrection, quorum downgrade, duplicate/unsorted signers, payload/signature mutation, every target mutation, non-canonical successor evidence, old RUST-114 bundle replay, and signed same-parent fork substitution fail closed.
- Detached selftest fixes 50/50 expected rejection cases.
- Pins exact RUST-114 verifier blob `22b1bcad60b54ba2e4038ede6d4cb64a984dbfc7` and workflow blob `d8f3f090d9033d519b0cc787734e451eea79039e`.
- Producer private keys remain deterministic TEST fixture material only; verifier/selftest have no signing or network capability.
- Read-only CI uses chmod 0444 evidence, a fixed 225-path manifest, an 88-file verifier-only detached consumer, and isolated `env -i` + `/usr/bin/python3 -S`.
- 100+ checkpoint handling remains explicit through zero-padded numeric loops and `rust_*.py` / `RUST_*.md` triggers.

## Scope

Exactly six non-production files are added. No production monitor administration/signing, publication, key custody, HSM/TPM, OIDC, release/deployment authority, consensus change, or production Rust routing is introduced. Production consensus remains Python-authoritative.

author: hochhause
body:
Ein Commit, glatter Fast-Forward auf `main`.

## Kernbefund

**14 Abrollbehälter, 2 WLF.** Jeder AB hat `zug: [46]` — nur das WLF zieht ihn —
und seit D-85 zieht ein Zugfahrzeug nur einen. Von vierzehn konnten also zwei
gleichzeitig ausrücken; die anderen zwölf standen auf gekauften Stellplätzen.

**Leitgedanke:** wo es zu einer Last ein selbstfahrendes Gegenstück gibt, kommt
der Selbstfahrer in den Plan.

## Der Plan danach

| Topf | |
|---|---|
| **normal (23)** | HLF 20 ×6 · GW-L2-Wasser ×3 · DLK 23 ×2 · WLF ×2 · Dekon-P · ELW 2 · FwK · **GTLF** · **GW-A** · GW-Gefahrgut · **GW-Lüfter** · GW-Messtechnik · **SW 2000-Tr** · TLF 3000 |
| **ab (12 von 14 Plätzen)** | ×2: AB-Atemschutz, AB-Öl, AB-L, AB-Lüfter, AB-Schiene — ×1: AB-Gefahrgut, AB-Küche |
| **anh (5 von 5)** | NEA50 · Anh Lüfter · Anh Tierrettung · Anh Schlauch · **FKH** |
| **Rest (5)** | ELW2 Drohne · GW-Küche · GW-Verpflegung · HLF Schiene · GW-Tierrettung |

```
standard        44 → 45 Fahrzeuge   146 → 139 Sitze
standard-groß   56 → 57 Fahrzeuge   190 → 180 Sitze
```

Mehr Fahrzeuge, weniger Personal: Lasten kosten nie Besatzung, und
`GW-L2 (1/6)` wurde `GW-L2-Wasser (1/3)`.

Gestrichen: AB-Rüst, AB-Einsatzleitung, AB-Lösch, AB-Wasser/Schaum,
AB-Sonderlöschmittel, MTW. Ersetzt: AB-Schlauch → SW 2000-Tr, AB-Tank → GTLF,
GW-L2 → GW-L2-Wasser.

## Drei Funde

**PB war unvollständig.** Die im Spiel abgelesene Zugliste des `NEA50` hat drei
Einträge, die fehlten: `LF 10`, `GW-Werkfeuerwehr`, `WLF`. Nachgetragen im
Skript **und** im Auszug `daten/`, beide gegengeprüft. Das wirkt: `linkTrailers`
liest die echte Auswahl aus `/vehicles/<id>/edit` und beschneidet sie danach mit
`PB` — was dort fehlt, ist im Planer nicht kuppelbar, obwohl das Spiel es
erlaubt.

**Zwei Katalogeinträge waren übersehen worden**, beide weil sie abgekürzt
heißen: `SW 2000-Tr` (nicht „Schlauch") und `GW-A` (nicht „Atemschutz").

**Neue Prüfung in `pruefer.js`: „Wunschbild gegen Stellplätze".** Fängt zwei
stille Fehler — ein Profil, das mehr vorsieht als sein Topf trägt (der Kauflauf
vertagt dann ewig), und einen Topfnamen, den das Layout nicht kennt (der fällt
in `poolsOf` still in den ersten Topf und verbraucht fremde Plätze). Alle 18
Profile bestehen sie.

## Bestätigt, nicht geändert

Der Planer kauft schon heute keinen Anhänger ohne freien Spezialplatz, und
strenger als verlangt: `poolsOf` nimmt die Topfgröße aus `builtExtensions(b)`,
und das zählt nur **fertige und eingeschaltete** Ausbauten.

## Prüfungen

- `node --check` beide Userscripts
- `werkzeuge/pruefer.js` — nichts zu beanstanden, 18 Profile passen
- `werkzeuge/test-planung.js` — **248 Proben, 0 Fehlschläge**

## Vor dem Merge bedenken

`@updateURL` zeigt auf `main` — der Merge wird jeder Installation angeboten.
Diese Änderung ist **Daten**, keine Oberfläche: der nächste Kauflauf kauft die
neuen Selbstfahrer, und der Zerstören-Reiter meldet die gestrichenen ABs als
überzählig. Bei 23 Feuerwachen ist das viel Bewegung — mit „Nur Vorschau" an
ansehen, bevor es scharf läuft.

Offen und bewusst nicht gebaut: Lasten sollen frei hängen dürfen („zufälliges
Zugfahrzeug"). Drei Stellen, eine heikel — beschrieben in
`Notizen/NAECHSTER_SCHRITT.md`.

author: sushi-shi
body:
## Result

The five VOSTOK_NOVTABLE attributes merged through #557 cover every observable missing Vostok case. This follow-up does not invent a sixth attribute; it removes two stale commented-out hints that retail positively disproves.

## Evidence

- Compared the complete rich target/base instruction corpus: 2,352 target vtable references and 2,346 base references. All eight base-only vtable symbols are Scaleform types.
- Compared every paired Vostok constructor, destructor, and scalar deleting destructor. The only base-only own-vtable stores are three concrete generated destructors already classified as reviewed ICF/compiler behavior: functor_order, functor_response, and particle_action_gravity.
- Rechecked the five classes changed by #557. Their own abstract-base vtable references are absent on both target and base after the fix.
- Retail triangle_mesh_geometry::~triangle_mesh_geometry explicitly restores collision::geometry's vptr, so geometry must not be novtable.
- Retail sound_world::sound_world explicitly installs sound::world's vptr before the derived vptr, so world must not be novtable.

This establishes complete coverage of cases with an observable code-generation consequence. An attribute on a wholly unobserved or completely optimized-away source declaration is not recoverable from the PDB and executable and would be speculative.

## Verification

PDB statement/assembly audit and exhaustive rich-index vtable-reference scan. The patch removes comments only; no rebuild was run.

## Co i po co

Cztery szablony stron błędów pokazywały generyczny placeholder, który
gubił suchy ton serwisu dokładnie w momencie, gdy odwiedzający trafia w
ślepą uliczkę. Każda strona dostaje teraz tematyczny suchar po polsku i
przycisk powrotu na stronę główną.

| strona | suchar |
|---|---|
| 404 | „404 — ta strona wyparowała" / „Była tak sucha, że wyparowała…" |
| 403 | „403 — wstęp wzbroniony" / „Ochroniarz przeczytał ten suchar…" |
| 403 CSRF | „403 — formularz bez pieczątki" / „…Odśwież stronę i spróbuj ponownie." |
| 500 | „500 — coś chrupnęło" / „Serwer usłyszał suchar i się rozsypał…" |

## Jak

- Nowy `components/error-page.css` — jeden mały, wyłącznie klasowy, JS-free
  layout (wyśrodkowany blok, duży wygaszony numer, suchar, przycisk).
  Wpięty w globalny `{% compress css %}` w `base.html` (nie per-template,
  cf. #250): `500.html` renderuje `server_error` bez requestu i bez
  context processorów, a per-template `{% compress css %}` jest tam kruchy
  pod `COMPRESS_OFFLINE`. Rationale zapisane w nagłówku pliku CSS.
- Wszystkie teksty w `{% trans %}` z polskimi msgid (spójnie z podejściem
  z `base.html`, #285). Żaden msgid bez literalnego `%`.
- Usunięte bloki `{% if exception %}{{ exception }}{% endif %}` — strony
  serwują suchar, nie echo wyjątku Django.
- `tests/test_error_pages.py` — render każdego z 4 szablonów; test 500
  odwzorowuje dokładnie `get_template("500.html").render()` bez requestu.
  Oczekiwane stringi przez `gettext`, nie hardkodowane (CI nie kompiluje
  `.mo`).

- `pre-commit run --all-files` 2× — czysto
- `just test` — 576 passed
- `just coverage` — TOTAL 94% (gate: 90%)
- `mypy tests/test_error_pages.py` — czysto

Closes #286

body:
## Summary

Twenty commits, one per issue raised in the second post-merge review. All build, `go vet` clean, `go test -race` green, both fuzz targets pass, coverage 90.9% post-filter (above the new 85% floor).

Two commits touch public API:

- `revert(currency)!: remove PluralMajorUnit and PluralMinorUnit` walks back API surface added last round that only handled English plural rules. Consumers needing CLDR-correct pluralisation should use `golang.org/x/text/feature/plural` against the raw `MajorSingle` / `MajorPlural` / `MinorSingle` / `MinorPlural` fields, which stay exposed.
- `feat(arith): add Cmp panic-on-mismatch variant for sort adapters` adds a `Cmp(other) int` helper. `Compare(other) (int, error)` is unchanged.

Everything else is a correctness fix, ergonomic addition, doc improvement, test lock-in, or CI polish.

## Commits

| # | Commit | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fix(json): preserve underlying json error under ErrMalformedInput` | UnmarshalJSON was dropping the underlying parse error. Wrap with two %w verbs. |
| 2 | `revert(currency)!: remove PluralMajorUnit and PluralMinorUnit` | Helpers added last round were English-only and would mislead callers. Point at x/text/feature/plural instead. |
| 3 | `refactor(arith): return currency-preserving zero on Add and Sub overflow` | Brings Add and Sub into line with Mul's overflow shape. |
| 4 | `feat(arith): add Cmp panic-on-mismatch variant for sort adapters` | One-liner for callers that already know currencies match. |
| 5 | `feat(money): add Valid accessor` | Callers had to test `Currency() != ""` to check usability. |
| 6 | `fix(decimal): reject unknown RoundingMode instead of silently rounding` | Default arm quietly fell back to banker's rounding; now returns ErrInvalidRoundingMode. |
| 7 | `feat(format): add SymbolStyle option to LocalisedString` | Variadic SymbolStyle picks narrow, standard or ISO symbol. Old calls unchanged. |
| 8 | `perf(currency): validate scales at package init not per New call` | Moved the never-fires runtime check to init; drops work from the hot path. |
| 9 | `fix(money): require a currency for IsZero, IsPositive and IsNegative` | Zero-value Money no longer reports IsZero() = true. |
| 10 | `docs(format): document LocalisedString allocation cost` | Explicit warning that LocalisedString is not zero-allocation. |
| 11 | `test(json): assert error categories in TestUnmarshalJSON_Errors` | The table now asserts against ErrMalformedInput / ErrEmptyInput / ErrInvalidCurrency etc. |
| 12 | `test(decimal): cover FromDecimal on zero-decimal currencies` | JPY rounding path was untested. |
| 13 | `test(decimal): lock in the 1.005 float precision trap` | Documents the classic IEEE-754 gotcha as executable evidence. |
| 14 | `test(currency): assert HasISONum with a synthetic unknown case` | Synthetic Currency values exercise both sentinel arms regardless of dataset. |
| 15 | `test(errors): lock MoneyError.Error format string` | Format is now a test invariant. |
| 16 | `ci: cache staticcheck and govulncheck binaries between runs` | Skip re-install when cached, saves ~30s per PR. |
| 17 | `ci: exclude cmd generator from coverage floor and lift to 85%` | Filter cmd from coverage; raise floor. Post-filter total is 90.9%. |
| 18 | `ci: drop go 1.23 from matrix` | go.mod says `go 1.24.7`; 1.23 was never supported. |
| 19 | `refactor(currency): use distinct sentinels for ISONum and NumToBasic` | NumToBasicUnknown = -2 so accidental cross-comparison fails loudly. |
| 20 | `fix(parse): apply MaxStringLength after TrimSpace` | 65-space payload was ErrInputTooLong; now correctly ErrEmptyInput. |

## Verification

- `go vet ./...`: clean
- `go test ./...`: pass
- `go test -race ./...`: pass
- `go test -fuzz=FuzzNewFromString -fuzztime=5s`: pass
- `go test -fuzz=FuzzUnmarshalJSON -fuzztime=5s`: pass
- Coverage post-cmd-filter: 90.9%, above the new 85% floor

## Test plan

- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` pass
- [x] `go test -race ./...` pass
- [x] Both fuzz targets pass at 5s each
- [x] Coverage above the new floor

body:
## AIS-288: Teams files into the Vault — deep links, chat file scan, catalog defaults reach existing installs

Jira: AIS-288 (Epic AIS-73). Support case SUP-20260904-071240.

### Why
Session `20260904_090002_142f89`: the user pasted a Teams chat link and asked for the document from that chat. The agent read the chat twice as raw Graph JSON (16k chars, truncated) and gave up ("Dateizugriff war scheinbar nicht möglich"). Three causes:
1. **Frozen tool list.** Only 34 M365 tools were loaded. `m365_list_teams_message_attachments`, `m365_download_teams_message_attachment`, `m365_download_drive_file`, the mail-attachment tools, To Do and presence were missing although the manifest lists them in `default_enabled`: `mcp_servers.MSOffice365MCP.tools.include` is written once at install time and carried over verbatim on reinstall, so defaults added later never reach existing installs. This is independent of the client version.
2. No tool understands Teams deep links (`/l/chat/<chatId>`, `/l/message/<chatId>/<messageId>`); the agent has to extract and URL-decode the id itself.
3. No tool checks a chat for files and pulls them into the Vault; list messages → list attachments → download per file is too long a path for the model.

### What changes
- **Catalog defaults reach existing installs.** `tools/mcp_tool.py::_register_server_tools` unions a catalog server's `tools.include` with the manifest's current `default_enabled` (`_merge_catalog_default_tools`); an empty include (= all tools) and custom servers are untouched; the user's include still governs non-default tools. `hermes_cli/mcp_catalog.py::_apply_tool_selection` adds new manifest defaults to the prior selection on reinstall.
- **Teams deep links** are accepted wherever a chat id is expected: `m365_find_chat(query=<link>)` resolves directly (no ranking, `message_id` returned for message links), `m365_send_chat_message(chat_id|to=<link>)`, `m365_list_chat_messages`, `m365_get_chat_style`, `m365_list_teams_message_attachments`, `m365_download_teams_message_attachment`.
- **New tool `m365_download_chat_files(chat_id|to, last=5, include_images=False, save_dir=None)`** scans the last N messages for file references (SharePoint/OneDrive via the shares API, fallback "Microsoft Teams Chat Files") and optionally inline images, saves into the Vault under `documents/m365_attachments/<topic or person>/` (no overwrite; `(2)` suffix), returns `saved_path`, sender, time, message id per file, `errors` per failed download and a `hint` when nothing was found. A message link restricts the scan to that message.
- Prompt guidance (`build_teams_send_guidance`) gets a links-and-files paragraph when the download tool is present; skill `teams-message-draft` gets the "get the document from the chat" workflow and German triggers; `tool_search` learns `anhang/anhänge/herunterladen/datei` synonyms and `lade/laden/herunterladen/hol…` as download verbs; manifest `default_enabled` += `m365_download_chat_files`; docs updated.

### Tests
- `tests/optional_mcps/test_m365_server.py` (+11): link parser, link-aware tools, chat file download (vault path, images opt-in, duplicate names, message-link restriction, recipient by name, failure reporting), manifest.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_dynamic_discovery.py` (+4): include ∪ defaults, empty include untouched, custom server unchanged, real M365 catalog lookup.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_catalog.py`: reinstall adds new manifest defaults (existing test updated + new test).
- `tests/tools/test_tool_search.py`, `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py`: synonyms and guidance.

### Second commit: mail attachments and sending files
- **`m365_download_email_attachments(message_id, save_dir=None, include_inline=False)`** saves all file attachments of a mail under `documents/m365_attachments/mail/<subject>/` and returns the paths (inline images and attached mail items skipped by default; reference attachments via the shares API; per-file `errors`). Manifest `default_enabled` += it.
- **Sending files** already works through `attachments=[…]` on `m365_send_chat_message` (OneDrive upload + file card) and `m365_send_email` (inline, ≤ 3 MB), with Vault-relative path resolution. The prompt guidance, the `teams-message-draft` and `m365-mail-assistant` skills and the tool docstrings now state it and point at the paths the download tools return.
- Tests: `TestDownloadEmailAttachments` (+4), guidance test for mail/sending lines.

### Behaviour change
Existing catalog installs gain every manifest-default tool on the next MCP connect without reinstall. A user who deliberately unchecked a *default* tool gets it back; non-default choices are preserved.

### Manual check
Paste a Teams chat link and ask for "das Dokument aus dem Chat": the agent calls `m365_download_chat_files` with the link, names the Vault path, and works with the file. `hermes mcp status` after update shows the attachment tools for an old install.

## Summary

Adds a repository-local pre-commit guardrail system for Papyrus with no new hook framework dependency.

### Guardrails
- security invariant tests for government identity/browser defaults, exact runtime tool authorization, sandbox isolation, and credential-free command environments
- staged secret/key/material scanner
- generated SPDX 2.3 SBOM and repository-derived SSP under `/compliance`
- contract/schema drift manifest for shared contracts, ACP runtime, and agent tool schema exports
- workspace implementation boundary checks
- junk/debugging code scanner
- staged frontend accessibility + React AST checks
- Markdown/agent-output fixture validation
- filename/case/Unicode/path sanity checks

### Hook installation
`pnpm install` configures `core.hooksPath=.githooks` outside CI. The committed `.githooks/pre-commit` is executable and dispatches to the staged-aware Node runner.

### Compliance evidence
- `compliance/ssp.md` is tracked and fingerprints security-boundary Git blobs
- `compliance/contracts.manifest.json` is tracked and fails on contract drift
- `compliance/sbom.spdx.json` is regenerated and uploaded by CI rather than committed because its SPDX creation timestamp is intentionally dynamic

### CI
CI now verifies compliance evidence and contract drift before typecheck/test/build and uploads the generated SPDX SBOM on Linux.

No runtime production behavior is changed by this PR.

author: shawn-durrani
body:
Closes #334.

## Merge order

Built on #332 (Forget reaches membro), which is on main now, so this diff shows only this change.

## What this part does

The Voices page lists every voice crossband has learned. Forget deletes a person's stored audio here and unseats them from the room. Since #332 it also records the forget in the correction ledger, and the sync pass replays that into membro, which deletes its copy of the audio and sends that person's approved facts back to review.

## What changes for the owner

The pass that carries the forget ran only after a round, at most every two minutes, or at startup. Nothing ran it when Forget was pressed. So the explainer said the audio was deleted here and in memory, and for the next round or two it was deleted here only, with nothing on screen saying the rest was still on its way.

Now pressing Forget:

- deletes the audio here and unseats the person, as before;
- starts one forced sync pass on a worker thread straight away, and answers without waiting for it;
- leaves the forget in the ledger when membro cannot take it, so the next pass retries.

Move, delete and merge still travel with the round-end pass. They correct who said what; they do not remove a person.

## Risk

Acting: one extra pass per Forget, forced past the two-minute debounce. The lock in `sync_once` queues it behind a pass already running, so two never run at once. No token, or membro down, is the same logged no-op the round-end pass already is. A failure inside the kicked pass is logged on its own thread and never reaches the response. A Forget pressed during a turn now runs a pass during that turn, on a worker thread the turn does not wait on.

Leaving it: the both-apps promise is true eventually, not when the owner acted, and the gap is invisible.

## What prompted it

Reviewing #332, which makes Forget reach membro through the ledger. Fixes #334.

## Detail

- `backend/person_sync.py` `kick(memory_url)`, right after `sync_once` (~line 111): starts a daemon thread that runs `sync_once(memory_url, force=True)`, logs any exception, and returns the thread so a test can join it. `_replay_corrections` and `_run` are untouched; #335 edits the replay.
- `backend/routers/room.py` `forget_person()` (~line 382): gains `request: Request` and calls `person_sync.kick(request.app.state.settings.memory_url)` after the local forget and the roster unlink, just before returning. The 404 path kicks nothing.
- `docs/VOICE_ID.md`, "The durable home": the forget sentence now says Forget sends it the moment you press it and a later pass retries one membro could not take. `changelog.d/334-forget-kicks-sync.md` is the entry; #332's fragment is untouched.
- `tests/test_forget_kicks_sync.py`, a new file so it cannot conflict with #335's changes to `tests/test_person_sync.py`: `kick` runs a forced pass on its own thread and swallows an exception; the route end to end against `FakeMembro`, with the kicked pass held at a gate until the response has been asserted, then membro shows the person forgotten with no anchors after exactly one forced pass and one forget POST, with no round and no second sync call; and with membro at a closed port the route still answers ok and 404s, the kicked thread ends, and the forget stays pending.

Checks: backend `pytest -q tests` 1666 passed, 1 skipped (1662 + the 4 new here); `scripts/secret-scan.sh` clean on the diff, bare and with the local deny list. No frontend files change.

body:
`EphemeralSecret::from_bytes` takes `[u8; 32]` by value, and that type is `Copy`.
A production caller therefore has to materialise the scalar in a buffer of its
own, pass a copy in, and remember to clear what it kept. The experimental
rust-reality branch shows what happens when it does not:

```rust
let mut seed = [0_u8; 32];
getrandom::fill(&mut seed)?;
let inner = EphemeralSecret::from_bytes(seed);   // `seed` is never cleared
```

The incumbent this replaces has the opposite property. `aws-lc-rs` generates
inside its own key object, so the scalar never exists as bytes on the caller's
side, and rust-reality's call site documents that as deliberate:

> One ephemeral key per exchange, consumed by exactly one agreement. The private
> key never exists as raw bytes on this side […]

Losing that would have been a real cost of the migration, and it was not
necessary — `aws-lc-rs`'s `SecureRandom` is a sealed trait, so the incumbent
cannot be given a faster entropy source without importing raw bytes, but nothing
forces the same shape here.

## What changed

`EphemeralSecret::from_entropy(fill)` hands the filler the key's own storage.
No caller-side buffer exists to leak or to clear, and `getrandom::fill` already
has the signature. If the filler fails, the partially written key is dropped and
dropping zeroizes it.

The module still draws nothing from the operating system — the platform layer
supplies the filler — so `no_std`, determinism under test and direct
fuzzability are unaffected. That boundary was the reason `from_bytes` looked the
way it did, and it is preserved.

`from_bytes` stays, for tests, fuzzing and known-answer vectors where the input
has to be chosen rather than drawn, and its doc now says that is what it is for.

## What it does not claim

Rust does not promise a returned value is never moved, so this removes the
caller's copy rather than proving the bytes occupy one address for their whole
life. The doc comment says exactly that rather than implying more.

## Tests

- `from_entropy` and `from_bytes` produce the same public key and the same
  agreement for the same scalar;
- the filler's error is returned unchanged;
- the filler is handed the storage the public key is then derived from — the
  property the constructor exists for, rather than a scratch buffer copied
  afterwards.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`,
`cargo test --workspace --all-features` and
`cargo check -p fastcrypto --no-default-features` pass locally.

Refs #2, jacek4yang/rust-reality#232, jacek4yang/rust-reality#225.

author: lord-navy-crypto
body:
## Physical Lab dual-mode application architecture

This PR keeps the mathematical/numerical identity of the hybrid Labs while adding explicit, bounded physics applications.

### Hybrid mode design
- Numerical Error remains a standalone numerical-analysis tool and gains an optional **Quantum bound-state numerical verification** scene.
- Ising Monte Carlo retains sampling/convergence tooling and gains **Magnetic phase transition & criticality**.
- Random Walk / Monte Carlo retains estimator/scaling tooling and gains **Diffusion & stochastic transport**.
- Oscillation, Chaos, RADIA and Radiation remain physics-first and are not forced into an artificial hybrid selector.

### Numerical Error ↔ quantum relationship
The PR does not claim that numerical analysis and quantum mechanics are the same subject. The infinite square well is used as a controlled physical verification problem: finite-difference grid error becomes eigenenergy error, so refinement order, discretization error and analytic-reference comparison acquire a physical observable.

### Physics scenes
**Quantum verification**
- 1D infinite square well
- centered second-order finite-difference Hamiltonian
- analytic eigenenergy reference
- eigenenergy relative error
- grid-refinement convergence order
- probability density view
- SciPy tridiagonal eigensolver when available, NumPy dense fallback otherwise

**Ising criticality**
- zero-field nearest-neighbor 2D square lattice
- periodic boundaries, checkerboard Metropolis updates
- temperature sweep
- E, |M|, Cv, susceptibility, Binder cumulant
- exact infinite-square-lattice Tc reference
- finite-size peaks explicitly labeled pseudo-critical indicators

**Brownian transport**
- 2D Brownian diffusion with constant optional x drift
- centered MSD compared with 4Dt
- recovered diffusion coefficient and drift velocity
- representative trajectories and final radial distribution
- centered MSD prevents deterministic drift from being counted as diffusion

### Visualization contract
- physics quantities with different units are separated instead of compressed onto one arbitrary axis
- tight padded display ranges preserve small meaningful differences without changing stored values
- theory/reference traces stay on the same physical scale
- stochastic trajectory rendering is bounded; ensemble observables carry the result
- equal spatial scaling is used for 2D trajectories

### Dependencies
No new hard dependency is introduced. NumPy remains guaranteed. SciPy is optional for the tridiagonal quantum backend; Numba/Astropy/QuTiP remain future optional capabilities rather than forced install-time requirements.

### Validation
Adds deterministic CI checks for:
- tight numeric display range behavior
- quantum second-order grid convergence and analytic energy agreement
- bounded Ising observables and low-T/high-T magnetic-order separation
- Brownian recovery of D and drift

Scientific boundary: these are computational-physics verification/application studies, not experimental validation or certification.

author: nojukuramu
body:
Batch 2. The big ones:

**Song Roulette, in a Games tab.** Everyone throws songs in a pot; three or
more can go in the queue as a single entry, and when it reaches the stage the
room spins twice on the big screen — for who sings, then for what. The picked
song plays credited to the picked singer, gets scored like any other, and then
there is a three-second window to go again. A picked song leaves the pot; the
host can be excluded from the draw; nobody gets two rounds running where
anyone else is waiting. Starting a roulette needs three songs, carrying one on
needs one — refusing the second round of a three-song pot would end the game
two thirds of the way through it. The tab is built for more than it holds.

**The score counts up.** Under a drumroll, easing out so it races through the
seventies and agonises over the last three, which is where a room actually
makes noise. Then the leaderboard slides in underneath and *moves* the singer
to their new place rather than arriving already sorted. Every sound is
synthesised from an oscillator and a buffer of noise — a few hundred bytes of
code instead of a few hundred KB of WAV, and nothing to 404 mid-spin.

**Join approval, on by default.** A room code is six guessable characters
against a public broker, so an arrival now waits in a lobby: it can say who it
is and ask for a snapshot, and every other command is refused where it lands
rather than filtered out of a UI nobody is obliged to run. It is not sent the
room either — refusing a stranger's commands while handing them the queue to
read is a lock on a door with the window open. Admissions survive a host
reload, or a refresh would eject the whole room.

**Statistics**, outside a room: average and best, songs sung, time at the
microphone, sessions, winrate per game. Only your own songs — the score entry
carries the singer's client id, because names collide. Local storage, no
account, no server, said in as many words above the first number, with a
button to erase the lot.

**Search tells karaoke from music videos.** Title and uploader give a
confidence: above 0.9 the row is badged with a shifting purple-pink-orange
border, below 0.45 it is not shown at all. "Videoke" and "minus one" count,
because that is what the rooms this is built for actually search. A pasted
link bypasses all of it. Unchecked results are now hidden too — unless the
sweep ends with nothing, which is a blocked IFrame API and not thirty bad
videos. And a thin list provokes up to two more differently-worded searches.

Smaller, but asked for:

- Queue rows have a grab rail and drag with pointer events, so it works on the
  phone that most needs it. The drop sends the index it landed on, not a swap.
- "Up next" over the stage at 77%, gone after seven seconds, never during an
  advert.
- The fullscreen QR and room code are one compact badge in the top right.
- Adverts are labelled, not skipped: no page may skip, click or hide one, and
  saying so is the only honest thing left. Setup explains it.
- Tabs are icons with a caption; the theme button is a sun in light and a
  lamp-yellow moon in dark.
- Every animation is roughly half as fast again. A karaoke night is not an
  admin panel.
- The name gate always asks and arrives pre-filled and selected, instead of
  silently joining as whoever used the phone last.

New: js/sound.js, js/games.js, js/stats.js, tools/games-e2e.js. All ten
suites pass.

author: ishledo
body:
Three backend contracts changed under us — [ogen#134](https://github.com/ogen-app/ogen/pull/134), [#136](https://github.com/ogen-app/ogen/pull/136) and [#137](https://github.com/ogen-app/ogen/pull/137), all merged to `main` on 2026-09-03. Each is behaviour the front end was actively getting wrong rather than a new feature, so none of it is behind a flag.

## CON-165 — `published_url`, and the autosave that was clearing it

**This is the one to review first: it is a live data-loss bug, not a missing feature.** The post PUT is whole-resource and the handler assigns `published_url` from the request unconditionally. `postToPayload` omitted it, so every autosave sent no permalink and cleared the one the server had — a published post lost its link the moment anyone touched the editor. The field is written server-side, so no screen could put it back and nothing would have reported it.

- `published_url` is on `Post` and on `PostPayload`, and round-tripped, with a test that pins it there and explains why. The failure mode is silent, so the comment is what stands between the next reader and deleting a field "nothing uses".
- `duplicatePayload` deliberately does **not** carry it, alongside `published_at` and `publisher_post_id`: a draft copy holding the original's permalink would offer a *view post* link to somebody else's post.
- The link itself goes on the quick bar's scheduling line, in the slot that already holds *Add post link* — the same question in its two states, never both. A real anchor, not a button with a handler, so it middle-clicks and copy-links like any other link.

## CON-279 — the asset PUT is presence-aware

`alt_text` and `tag_ids` are pointers server-side now: omit one and the stored value is left alone; send it, including `""` or `[]`, and it is replaced.

- **`assetToPayload` is deleted**, with its test. It was not merely redundant afterwards — it made every title save carry the editor's copy of the tags, so saving a title would put back tags a bulk re-tag had just changed. The document editor now sends `{title, content}`; the image screen sends the four fields it shows.
- **Documents can be tagged, for the first time.** The Content Bank has always filtered by tag while nothing but the image screen could set one. `POST /api/content-bank/assets/tags` files a whole selection, so the selection bar gains a TAG action with `TagDocumentsDialog` behind it. Add is a search over every tag and can invent one; remove offers only the tags the selection carries, each with how many documents would lose it — a second search field would be offering no-ops.

## CON-156 — a campaign is archived or deleted, and has no status

`CampaignStatus` is gone from the client. `draft` and `active` both meant active, nothing ever showed either, and the server creates every campaign active now; `campaignToPayload` stops round-tripping it.

- `archived_at` on the DTO, `?archived=true` on the list, `archive`/`unarchive` endpoints and hooks. **The archived list is a sibling query key**, not a filter over the active one, so an archived campaign can never reach the sidebar or seed `useCampaign`.
- **An archive view on `/campaigns`**, behind a header toggle and held in the address so it can be linked and returned to.
- **An Archive card in campaign settings, above the Danger Zone rather than in it.** Archiving is the reversible option; filing it under a red heading beside a delete teaches people to avoid the safe one.
- **Archived campaigns render as rows, not cards.** The card scores a campaign for work in progress — posts due, gaps in setup, what needs attention — which is exactly what an archived campaign has none of.
- **Delete's copy is corrected.** The server soft-deletes now, but that row is our safety net and not an undo: there is no restore in the app or on the API. The copy says nothing that hints at one, and points at archiving instead.

## Notes for review

- New copy is catalogued in both languages (`campaigns.*`, `content.tagging.*`, `content.selection.*`, `posts.publishedLink.*`). The screens around it are still legacy hard-coded English — the existing state, not something this PR spreads.
- `CLAUDE.md` is corrected on both contracts, including a stale pointer to `campaignToPayload`'s file.
- **Not exercised against a running API.** The local container is down, so this is verified against the Go handlers by reading plus wire-level tests, not by a round trip. The archive endpoints and the bulk-tag call want a pass on staging before merge.
- Independent of #94 and #95; branched off `develop` and touches none of the same lines.

Checks: `tsc` clean, `eslint` 0 errors / 125 warnings, **928 tests across 80 files**, production build OK.

author: jumplink
body:
Found on the emulator while testing #77, not caused by it.

## The defect

The reader's save button is live from the first frame, whether or not anything
knows what the article is called.

Opened from a feed row that is fine: `openArticle` passes the title as a route
param. Opened by **URL alone** — a deep link, a shared address, an internal link
from another reader — there is nothing to write until `loadArticle` answers, and
`title ?? article?.title ?? ''` wrote the empty string. The error state offers the
button too, so a URL that 404s can be bookmarked.

What that leaves behind is worse than a failed action:

`/gespeichert` renders a blank line above `gespeichert 4. September`. Nothing says
which article it was, and it persists, so a restart does not clear it.

## The fix

`canSave` is `Boolean(title ?? article?.title)`. The bookmark is **dimmed and
inert** while that is false.

- **Dimmed, not absent.** The header is a fixed row of controls floating over the
  hero image. A button that appears when the article lands would shift the other
  two under the reader's thumb, mid-tap.
- **`accessibilityState={{ disabled }}`** as well, or the change says nothing to a
  screen reader — the buttons have no text.
- **Removing is never blocked** (`!saved && !canSave`). A saved article being
  re-read through a bare URL that then fails to load still has to be removable, or
  the entry cannot be reached from the only screen that lists it.

## Tests

Three added to `__tests__/artikel.test.tsx`:

- disabled while the load is pending with no title param, enabled the moment the
  article lands, and saving then writes the real headline
- **enabled immediately** when the route params carry a title — the ordinary path,
  and the negative control that keeps the first test from passing vacuously
- removal stays available after a failed load on an already-saved article

`npm run check` green, 222 tests.

Verified on the emulator against the original repro: `correctiv://artikel?url=…`
with a URL that 404s now reports `enabled=false, clickable=false` on the bookmark
instead of writing a blank row.
