author: pamirmundt
body:
## Summary

Fix C++ type collisions when generating A2L definitions from DWARF information.

DWARF type entries generally provide an unqualified `DW_AT_name`. Types with the same name in different C++ namespaces could therefore share an incorrect A2L typedef, causing instances to reference the wrong type definition.

## Changes

- Qualify colliding type names using their namespace or enclosing type.
- Preserve existing short type names when they are unambiguous.
- Use the same qualified identifier for typedef definitions and instance references.
- Only perform the additional DWARF scope lookup when duplicate type names are detected.
- Document the qualified-name behavior.
- Add an ARM DWARF regression fixture covering:
  - Same-named types with different sizes.
  - Same-named, equal-sized types with different members.

## Testing

- All existing and new tests pass: **12 passed, 0 failed**.
- The regression test fails on the unchanged `master` branch and passes with this fix.

Fixes #125

body:
## Description

Brings the TV app's scrolling and Back behaviour in line with tvOS, combining two related Linear tickets:

- **[POC-885](https://linear.app/a8c/issue/POC-885/change-escback-behaviour) — Change ESC/Back behaviour.** Pressing Back (ESC / remote Back) while focused inside a tab's content now returns focus to the top navigation **and** scrolls that content back to the top, so you can jump to another tab without manually scrolling up.
- **[POC-887](https://linear.app/a8c/issue/POC-887/change-scrolling-and-fixed-elements-behaviour) — Change scrolling and fixed elements behaviour.** The top navigation bar and the screen titles ("Podcasts", "Playlists", "Up Next", …) are no longer pinned — they scroll away with the content and slide back in when you return to the top, matching tvOS.

### How it works

- `TvScrollToTop` is a one-shot signal raised by the scaffold's `BackHandler` (only while the top bar is visible). Each tab's scroll container registers a `ScrollToTopEffect` that scrolls it back to item 0 when the signal fires, and the scaffold moves focus to the top bar. (POC-885)
- `TvTopBarScrollState` + `TopBarScrollReporter` report the active list's scroll offset. The shared top bar translates up in step with it, and a `Modifier.scrollAwayTopBar()` lays each tab's content out **below** the bar (so D-pad focus can still descend from the nav into content) while translating it up together with the bar as you scroll. Screen titles are moved into the scroll so they scroll away too. (POC-887)
- Covers Home, Your Podcasts, Playlists, Up Next and Search.

## Testing Instructions

1. Sign in on the Android TV app (debugProd) and open any content-rich tab (Home, Up Next or Search).
2. Press Down to move focus into the content and keep scrolling down — the top navigation bar and the screen title scroll up and out of view.
3. Press Back — focus returns to the top navigation and the content jumps back to the top.
4. Repeat across Home / Up Next / Search and confirm you can always move focus from the nav back down into content.

## Screenshots or Screencast

Before/after screen recordings captured on a Google TV Streamer (Android 14) are attached to the Linear tickets and saved locally at `~/Desktop/tv-poc-885-887/before.mp4` and `after.mp4` — drag them in here if needed.

- **Before:** top bar and titles stay pinned; Back does not reset scroll or focus.
- **After:** top bar + titles scroll away; Back returns to the nav and scrolls to the top.

body:
## Summary

We currently collect coverage for unit/integration tests via `cargo llvm-cov nextest`, but doctests are run separately and uninstrumented (`cargo test --workspace --doc` in `test`, and not run for coverage at all in `engine-test`), because `cargo-nextest` doesn't support doctests ([nextest-rs/nextest#16](https://github.com/nextest-rs/nextest/issues/16)).

This PR follows the approach documented in [nextest's test-coverage guide](https://nexte.st/docs/integrations/test-coverage/#collecting-coverage-data-from-doctests):
run nextest and doctests as two separate `cargo llvm-cov --no-report` passes, then merge them into a single report with `cargo llvm-cov report --doctests`.

Fixes #868 

## Expected coverage impact

Per the issue's own note, merging doctest coverage in is expected to produce a noticeable jump in the reported Codecov percentage. This is not a sign of newly added tests — it's previously-existing doctests being counted for the first time.

author: sanjaybnarayan
body:
`aria-busy` was the one ARIA attribute this application sets that no check had ever looked at — the last row of the sweep that produced #205:

| attribute | in `js/` | in `tests/` |
|---|---|---|
| `aria-busy` | 2 | **0** |
| `aria-expanded` | 2 | 1 |
| `aria-pressed` | 8 | 1 |
| `aria-current` | 3 | 1 |

`navigate` sets it on the outlet, then clears it in a `finally` guarded by `!stale()`, so a superseded navigation leaves the attribute to the newer one that owns the outlet.

## It works

Measured on five screens and on three navigations fired in one tick — `null` every time.

Left on, it would tell a screen reader the content region hadn't finished loading, for the rest of the session, on every screen, because nothing else removes it. The page would look finished and announce itself as still arriving.

## Two checks, because the guard has two halves

A settled navigation exercises the `finally`. Only a *superseded* one exercises `!stale()` — there, two of the three navigations take the stale path out and the last is the only one entitled to clear the attribute. A check that navigated once would pass with that half of the condition inverted, removed, or simply wrong.

## Mutation-proven before it was written

Dropping the `removeAttribute`:

```
after load        : busy="true"
#/finance         : busy="true"   <-- STUCK BUSY
#/people, #/settings, #/reports, #/vehicles/vehicle : all stuck
after 3 rapid navs: busy="true"
```

The mutated module was confirmed to import first. A module that fails to load produces a failure that proves nothing — a way to be fooled by your own mutation rather than by the code.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| `tests/run.mjs` | 3151/3151 |
| `tests/browser.mjs` | **737/737** (was 735 — both checks ran) |
| Ratchets | nine pass; typecheck at its 156 budget |

No production code changes. The behaviour was already correct; nothing held it.

author: victorpenhoat
body:
Le design Voyages n'étant pas dans le dépôt, ce lot est reconstruit depuis la mémoire projet (« participants polymorphes Cercle/externe, `display_name` snapshot, + programme ») et le modèle existant. **Le lot D (dépenses) s'appuiera sur `voyage_participants`.**

## Migration 00042
`voyage_participants` et `voyage_etapes`, toutes deux **collaboratives** (`can_access_voyage`) : qui accède au voyage gère qui part et ce qu'on y fait. pgTAP étendu à **45 tests** — le propriétaire et le co-membre voient, un compte étranger et `anon` ne voient rien.

## Voyageurs ≠ partage
`voyage_membres` dit avec quels **comptes** le voyage est partagé ; les participants disent qui **voyage**. Un enfant de trois ans voyage sans compte, une agence a un compte sans voyager. **Ajouter un voyageur ne donne aucun accès** — et c'est écrit sous le formulaire plutôt que laissé à deviner.

Un participant vient d'un compte, d'un proche du Cercle, ou de nulle part (saisie libre) : au plus une source, garantie par un CHECK. Le `display_name` est un **instantané** et les liens sont en `on delete set null` — un proche retiré du Cercle reste un voyageur nommé dans le voyage. Deux index uniques partiels empêchent de l'ajouter deux fois.

## Programme
Les jours du voyage, bornes comprises, **affichés même vides** (une journée sans rien reste une journée à remplir). Une étape sans date — ou datée hors du voyage après un changement de dates — rejoint **« à caler »** au lieu de disparaître de l'écran. Dans une journée, l'heure commande ; sans heure, le rang de saisie.

## Affichage optimiste (et pourquoi)
Mes deux premiers e2e dépassaient le délai : les écritures étaient **bien en base**, mais l'écran ne se mettait à jour qu'au rechargement — la course RSC connue du dépôt (#71/#77). Plutôt que d'empiler des gardes de rechargement dans les tests, les deux blocs affichent désormais immédiatement ce qui vient d'être écrit (les actions renvoient l'id créé), et les props reprennent la main ensuite. Les mêmes tests passent maintenant en une seconde.

## Vérification
- `npm run lint` : propre · `tsc --noEmit` : propre (types Supabase régénérés)
- `npm test` : **497 tests** (20 nouveaux sur `programme` et `participants`, écrits avant le code)
- `npx playwright test` : **132 passés** sur base fraîche (2 nouveaux)
- `npm run test:rls` : **45 tests pgTAP** après reset

body:
## Summary

Fixes #37892.

DSV4 paged prefill can request both outputs from the C4 top-k transform:

- request-local raw C4 positions for sparse prefill / capture paths
- page-table-transformed KV slots for the attention path

The previous dispatch only used `topk_transform_paged_v2` when `raw_indices is None`. In the paged-prefill path `raw_indices` is present, so the default `sgl-kernel` backend fell back to the legacy top-k v1 kernel and could crash on GB300 long-context prefill.

This change keeps the default `sgl-kernel` backend on top-k v2 even when raw indices are requested: it runs v2 once in raw-index mode, then once in page-table mode. Torch and FlashInfer backends keep their existing single-call behavior.

## Testing

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_indexer.py`
- pre-commit hooks from `git commit` passed, including ruff and ruff-format

- GB300 4-GPU repro on exact main `b168f905c8` before the fix: 32K benchmark crashes in `topk_v1.cuh:348` with CUDA illegal memory access

author: sremani
body:
## FG-244 — the no-egress fence, built on both sides and proven per run; tier1=5 of 228

The operating contract executes corpus files "on a no-egress network". FG-200 measured on 2026-08-17 that no such network existed on either side. This builds it, with no engine change and no change to the oracle container, and walks the two `sh`-bearing corpus files it unlocks.

**Jenkins side.** `jenkins-lab` is a rootless podman container (slirp4netns) whose network namespace our user namespace owns, so `nsenter -U -n` loads an nftables ruleset into that namespace as our own user: loopback and established flows pass; every new outbound SYN, every UDP datagram and everything else is REJECTED in ~15 ms, never dropped. The ruleset evaporates on container restart, so it is applied and proven per run.

**Fogell side.** HeMan ignores user-level `IPAddressDeny` and forbids unprivileged user namespaces (both measured), so the fence is a root nft rule keyed to the cgroup of a transient systemd user scope the run is placed in. nft binds to the cgroup's identity at load time, so the rule is loaded from inside the live scope, proven there, and deleted on exit. Inside it the oracle port and the collector's ssh port on the Jenkins host are reachable and both stub resolvers are refused; every process left in the scope is killed before the rule is deleted.

**Scripts.** `scripts/no-egress-fence.sh` (jenkins apply/verify/remove/status; fogell run/status) and `scripts/run-corpus-differential.sh`, the corpus lane, which refuses a non-corpus file, a drifted manifest, a missing CLI, a busy oracle, or an unproven fence, and removes the Jenkins fence on exit whatever happens. Every probe from the landing run is tabulated in the ticket; the lane's refusal with the fence absent was exercised too.

**Receipts.** `cinqict_jenkinsdev` and `devops-ws_learn-pipeline-java` PROVEN (tier 1) under the fence; the second is the first corpus receipt with a non-empty workspace, identical on both sides. Ledger `tier1=5`, `admitted=195`, `tier3=28`; board accounting `rows=237 DONE=177`. FG-242's inventory (the one place the capability list lives) marks the fence class as built. Runbook at `docs/runbooks/no-egress-fence.md`.

**What it is and is not.** The verifier attacked both fences from inside before this landed. The Jenkins namespace held against everything tried. On the Fogell side three escapes were measured and fixed (a second run's sweep unfenced a live run; a backgrounded process outlived the fence on both sides; a second stub resolver answered), and four same-UID hops are measured and stated, not fixed: `ssh luigi curl …`, `systemd-run --user`, passwordless sudo, loopback listeners. The Jenkins side is the boundary; the Fogell side stops accidental egress from the executed surface and does not contain a hostile file, which is a property of running Fogell as the operator (FG-073).

**Replacement for #389.** That PR's Codex and Copilot reviews found eight real items, all fixed and re-measured here: the quiesce spared any process named `java` (the JVM is now the one running `jenkins.war`; an impostor was killed while the JVM lived); the sweep could delete another user's live table (per-UID table names); two lanes from different users or hosts could share the one Jenkins fence (a `flock` lease on the Jenkins host held for the lane's life, measured refusing a second lane); the lane trap was installed after apply (now before, quiesce conditional); a failed `nft delete` read as removed (now reported); the container name reached a remote shell unquoted (`printf %q`); hostnames were resolved before the fence existed (`/etc/hosts` or numeric only); the runbook recovery removed without quiescing (quiesce first). #389 was closed unmerged so Copilot covers this exact head.

**After #389, two more from the verifier.** The lease holder (`sleep infinity`) outlived its ssh client, so the lane would have refused itself forever; the holder is now `cat` on stdin fed by `tail --pid` of the lane, measured released after a normal exit and after SIGKILL. The JVM pick took the first `jenkins.war` match, then a naive `stat` field, and a process with a space in its name beat it; `stat` is now parsed after the comm field's closing paren and the earliest-started `jenkins.war` process wins, measured against three impostors. While fixing that I ran the impostor test against the unpatched quiesce and killed the oracle once (container exited 137 at 09:53:55Z, restarted at 09:54:08Z, home intact); the ticket records it.

**Evidence.** Full local HeMan gate green on the exact head; six verifier rounds recorded in the ticket.

author: zoorpha
body:
## Issue

Fixes #809 — `o3kd` startup crashes with set-but-empty `O3K_LVM_*` env vars (`InvalidConfiguration`).

## Intent

Treat unset **and** set-but-empty `O3K_LVM_VOLUME_GROUP` / `O3K_LVM_THIN_POOL` / `O3K_LVM_PROVIDER_NAMESPACE` as "native LVM provider not configured" (`None`), matching the harness convention `O3K_LVM_VOLUME_GROUP="${O3K_LVM_VOLUME_GROUP:-}"` used by `tests/p13_5b_refresh_import.sh`, `tests/p13_5f_postgres_provider_parity.sh` and friends. Hosts without the disposable tagged LVM TestLab must be able to start `o3kd` for non-storage evidence.

## Design

- New small helper `resolve_native_lvm_config` in `bins/o3kd/src/composition/mod.rs`:
  - all three unset **or** all three empty → `Ok(None)` (provider disabled);
  - all three non-empty → construct `LvmConfig` and run `LvmConfig::validate` (unchanged fail-closed behavior for invalid values);
  - any partial combination (some set/empty, others unset/empty) → explicit startup error (`InvalidInput`): fail closed rather than silently running without storage.
- Composition call site now resolves through the helper; `LvmStorageProvider::new` no longer receives empty strings.

## Product/deployment profile

Portable TestLab profile; no profile claim changes. Enables the portable P13.5/P13.6 harnesses to run on hosts without LVM configured.

## Authority model

`o3k-implemented`. Startup/configuration behavior only; no authorization, IAM, or provider-authority change.

## OpenStack compatibility impact

None.

## Database/footprint

No schema change, no new dependencies.

## Contracts

`LvmConfig::validate` semantics unchanged (empty strings are still invalid *values*; the boundary now simply never passes them when the operator means "not configured").

## Workflow/compensation

None.

## Tests

- 4 focused unit tests in `bins/o3kd/src/composition/mod.rs`:
  - `lvm_config_unset_and_empty_env_means_provider_not_configured`
  - `lvm_config_all_values_set_resolves_to_config`
  - `lvm_config_partial_env_fails_closed`
  - `lvm_config_complete_but_invalid_values_are_rejected`
- End-to-end reproduction on this branch:
  - empty vars → `o3kd` starts and stays up against PostgreSQL (previously exited `InvalidConfiguration`);
  - partial vars (`O3K_LVM_VOLUME_GROUP` only) → startup fails with the explicit partial-configuration error.

## Evidence

Local: `cargo test -p o3kd --lib` (30 passed), `cargo clippy -p o3kd --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `check-architecture-boundaries.py`, `check-maintainability-guards.py`, `tests/maintainability-guards.sh`, `git diff --check` — all green. CI on exact HEAD required before merge.

## Risks

Low. Behavior change is limited to startup configuration resolution. A previously-crashing configuration now starts with storage disabled; operators relying on the crash as a signal for "LVM configured but broken" should note that complete-but-invalid values still fail closed, and partial configuration now fails loudly.

## Provenance

No external sources; no Go O3K consultation.

## Follow-ups

- Re-run evidence rows classified `execution_profile_unavailable` due to this bug (tracked in #751 / P13.6F privileged supplement).

author: luke883i
body:
## Why

PR #34 established graded Method Access and a revision-bound Local Host, but `LOCAL_CHAT` still inherited a generic runtime-search policy and split its cognitive policy across the boot prompt and `RUNTIME_LOCAL_HOST.md`. This PR is the minimal specialization needed for fast, deterministic local-chat instantiation without creating shadow authority.

## Semantic change

- Adds `JURISCRIBE_LOCAL_CHAT_BOOTSTRAP_V1` as host transport/UX policy only; generic graded execution remains `ATTESTED_PREFERRED` for non-local-chat hosts.
- Makes the local-chat sequence explicit: repository pin -> exact `I ACCEPT` -> explicit `LEAN | ATTESTED` -> canonical scientific mode.
- Treats preinstalled Juriscribe/local Git checkout as cold-start non-paths and forbids Git checkout/fetch, `gh`, DNS resolution, public-HTTP fallback and package installation for the default local-chat bootstrap.
- Uses connected GitHub pinned bytes as the primary transport.
- Splits ATTESTED bootstrap into an H0 handshake closure and deferred H1 activation; `host_bootstrap.py` no longer imports the portable session at H0 import time.
- Adds Git-object byte binding against the expected pinned-tree blob SHA before imported source can participate in runtime bootstrap.
- Folds the former runtime-local cognitive companion into one standalone `LOCAL_HOST_PROMPT.md`; `RUNTIME_LOCAL_HOST.md` is retained only as a historical compatibility pointer.
- Makes artifact obligations profile-invariant: LEAN declassifies runtime attestation, not required artifact format/materialization/readback; unresolved required output is `MATERIALIZATION_PENDING`.
- Does not change `METHOD_KERNEL.json`, the four scientific modes, or the six runtime authority nodes.

## Prompt convergence

Final standalone prompt: 6,735 characters (1,265 characters below the 8,000 limit).

The first 100,000-case mutation pass intentionally did not pass: 14,277 survivors exposed missing validator coverage around rebind, runtime probing, acceptance binding, Method Kernel binding and Git-blob binding. The validator was strengthened without lowering criteria and the same seed was rerun.

Final campaign:
- seed `20260904114235`
- 100,000 mutation instances
- 100,000 killed
- 0 survivors
- 35 mutation families
- digest `652c537d81b55bca3678cc9b7df724d953fb7a57ea297a2cf9667d8af1f1b85f`

Scope is synthetic prompt/process mutation testing, not empirical host latency, independent legal validation, or 100,000 physical chat sessions.

## Commit reticulum

Single semantic commit: `feat(local-chat): bind standalone deterministic bootstrap`.

No automatic merge.

設計書: docs/design-discord-auto-thread-rate-limit.md

## What does this PR do?

DiscordのPRレビュー依頼が集中したとき、Hermesが存在しないthreadを「作成済み」と2回表示して依頼を処理しない障害を修正します。

2026-09-04の実ログでは、Discordが`retry_after=296.29`秒を返したのにHermesは0.75秒で再試行し、直接作成とseed fallbackを連打していました。さらにslash-command同期が共有HTTP clientの`max_ratelimit_timeout`を一時変更し、その間に作られた通常route bucketへ30秒上限を残し得ることを確認しました。

## Related work

- Upstream [NousResearch/hermes-agent#76060](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/76060): 429の`retry_after`対応。ただし30秒を超える依頼は手動再送が必要です。
- Upstream [NousResearch/hermes-agent#52423](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/52423): fallback失敗時のorphan seed削除。

このPRは両方の障害をまとめて扱い、会社運用向けに長い429も非同期で待って元依頼を継続し、同一channelのburstを直列化します。

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [x] 📝 Documentation update

## Changes Made

- slash-command同期による共有`max_ratelimit_timeout`の変更を廃止。
- Discord 429ではserver指定の`retry_after`を待って直接作成を再試行。
- 自動thread作成を親channel単位で直列化し、別channelは止めない。
- fallback seedを1件だけ使い回し、成功後にのみ成功表示へ更新。
- 最終失敗・Gateway停止時はfallback seedを削除。
- seed送信の再試行はHTTP接続前と断定できる障害に限定。

## How to Test

1. 修正前に、429、重複seed、共有HTTP timeout汚染、channel間blockの回帰テストが失敗することを確認。
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_discord*.py -q` → 45 files / 271 passed / 0 failed。
3. `uvx ruff==0.15.10 check plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py tests/gateway/test_discord_slash_commands.py tests/gateway/test_discord_sync_limit.py` → pass。
4. `git diff --check` → pass。
5. 独立サブエージェントによる再レビュー → approved / no blocking findings。
6. 稼働Gatewayで `hermes-gke-departments#289` の通知jobを再実行 → Actions成功。Discord上で1本だけthread作成・Hermes返信をread back。

全リポジトリのtest suiteは未実行です。変更対象を含むDiscord adapter全45 test filesを実行しています。

■ 新規に増えた構成要素

- なし

■ 消えた構成要素

■ 設計書にあるが未実装

Lead capture, mobile nav readability, and mailto safety are high blast-radius for this marketing site. author: b-ismark
body:
Two backlog rows, both from Kal's suggested lane. Nothing here touches `lib/scene-spec.ts`, `lib/drag-convoy.ts`, `lib/drag-resolve.ts`, `components/studio/PlanView.tsx`, `lib/layout-shuffle.ts` or `lib/layout-score.ts`.

## § G.3 — the help card explained the two lists on one tab only

`StudioHelp` picks its card off `usePathname()`. The group naming **Catalog** and **Library** rendered on `/model` only, so a person who opened Help on the 2D plan was told about pieces, panning and keys and never what the two lists were.

It was filed as the user's decision — *"a deliberately shorter card, or a signpost gap one tab over"* — and it was not one, because the premise is checkable and false. `DockedShell` is the one shell, so `PartTree` (the Catalog) is in the left rail on the plan too, and the plan page renders the same `CatalogPanel` on the right off the same `catalogOpen` flag. The sentence was already true on the plan tab and simply was not being said there.

- The group is one component, `TwoLists`, rendered by both cards. It names *where* two panels are, and a direction is the thing that goes stale — it went stale once already, when the Library moved to the right of the canvas and the copy still read "the lists on the left".
- `planHelp` **moves** out of `PlanChrome.tsx` to sit beside `ModelHelp` in `StudioHelp.tsx`. Both files' headers already warned in prose about exactly this split — *"nobody comparing them was ever looking at both"* — while the two halves sat in different files.

**A second gate was owed, and mutation is what found it.** Sharing the group turned two gates into one: both of `studio-copy.test.tsx`'s help assertions are now about a group *both* cards render, so neither says which card is on screen. Measured — `{false ? <ModelHelp /> : <PlanHelp />}` served the plan card on `/model` and that file stayed green, the one survivor of six mutations. Each file now carries a control asserting it is looking at its own tab's card.

`vi.mock` is hoisted per FILE, so one route per test file is not a style choice — hence `tests/help-two-lists-plan-tab.test.tsx` rather than a case inside the existing file.

## § A.3 — the standalone re-search script

`scripts/openroutes-sweep.mjs`. Plain Node through vite's SSR pipeline, because the modules are TypeScript behind the `@/` alias and `vite` is a declared devDependency. Not a Vitest file, for the reason § A.3 always gave: a measurement campaign that takes minutes is not a gate, and the earlier attempt died on a harness timeout.

Run in full on `ec2a7be` (413.7 s):

```
19 of 54 scrambles cut · 532 trials · 1 refusals
  scramble 35: LAYOUT_SEED = 35 * 2654435761, refusing REPAIR_SEED = 35 * 31 + {21}
```

Two of those figures are exactly what `tests/suggest-tidiness.test.ts` records. The refusal count is **1, not 3**. The test file predicted that in prose and explicitly refused to quote the wider number as current — *"NOT re-derived here and must not be quoted"*. It is measured now, and it agrees with the one-scramble assertion rather than softening it.

**The live finding is that 1.** Across the entire grid the fine-grid re-check refuses the coarse proxy once, so a single assertion is its whole evidence. Recorded, not tuned away: the honest options are a wider grid or accepting that the search outgrew its guard, and deciding that needs the row-11 Suggest work.

Also fixed: the assertion counting them was titled *"refuses exactly three of the 28 repair seeds here"* while asserting `toEqual([21])`. The count moved when `outsideDeficit` joined the containment term; the assertion was updated and its own sentence was not, so every green run printed a false number.

## Docs

§ A.3 described two failures that had been green since `4be144c` — while this document's own red list, forty lines up, said they were closed. § G.3, queue rows 14 and 16, and the § E cross-reference are updated, and `Design.md` no longer says `PlanChrome.tsx` owns a help card.

## Verification

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 |
| `eslint . --max-warnings 0` | 0 |
| `next build` | clean, 23.6 s, lint pass ran, no `Invalid Options` |
| `tests/studio-copy.test.tsx` + `tests/help-two-lists-plan-tab.test.tsx` | 15 passed |
| `tests/suggest-tidiness.test.ts` alone | 22 passed / 0 failed, 144.78 s |
| mutation | **6/6 killed** after the survivor was closed with a real control |
| Playwright, production build, 1600×1000 | **16/16** |

The browser probe measures what jsdom cannot — the copy's spatial claims are claims about layout:

- left rail ends at 260 px, canvas starts at 260 px
- Library panel opens at x=1231 px against a canvas midpoint of 770 px
- plus a control on each tab, so a collapsed route branch cannot pass

## The probe, watched failing — done 2026-09-04

The caveat this PR opened with is closed. Both directions, same session, two distinct builds, each one **proved** to be the bundle actually being served — a stale `next start` outliving its parent would otherwise have served the fixed build to both runs and made the control a formality.

**How to make that check, since the obvious two ways both return nothing.** Under the App Router the chunk URLs are content-hashed *per chunk* (`/_next/static/chunks/main-app-<hash>.js`) and carry **no build id at all**, and there is no `"buildId":"…"` to grep either — both were tried here and both came back empty. The id is in the streamed payload in the document, so the check is to grep the document for the raw string:

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:3031/room/<id>/plan | grep -o "$(cat .next/BUILD_ID)"
```

Written out because the earlier wording described only the form that worked, and a method described only by its successful form is one the next person re-derives. The failure is at least in the safe direction: a probe built on the chunk-URL version refuses to start rather than quietly measuring the wrong bundle.

```
pre-fix  (StudioHelp.tsx + PlanChrome.tsx at ec2a7be, BUILD_ID iERRHVTkaLK8ccue1ysXS)
    4 FAILED   all four in S1, all on /plan, all naming the group
post-fix (branch HEAD,                        BUILD_ID e2Gr0wBhxISVef4UH8Nz6)
    ALL PASS   16/16
```

**The shape of the red is the point, not the count.** S1b, S2 and S3 stayed green on the pre-fix build, so the probe still reached the plan card, still measured the rail at 260 px and still opened the Library at 1231 px — the failure is the copy, not the harness losing its footing. And **S4 stayed green**, which is the assertion that matters most for a shared-component change: the 3D tab always had this group, and the extraction did not break the tab that was already right.

**One assertion could not tell the two builds apart, and it is worth naming.** `does NOT say "the lists on the left"` passed in both directions — of course it did: a card with no group at all also fails to say that. A *negative* assertion is not a control. It is kept because the string it forbids is a real regression this repo has already shipped once, but it contributes nothing to this measurement and should not be counted among the four.

## Not verified

- **The full suite was not run on this branch.** The three touched test files were, and CI's `typecheck · lint · test · build` passed on the artifact in 7m55s.
- **Nobody has *looked* at the plan tab's help card with human eyes.** The probe reads text and boxes; it cannot say whether the card is now too long, or whether the group sits well between "Choosing pieces" and "Getting around". That is a `visual-check.md` item, not a gate.
- **The mutation scores here are partly a claim about the fixture.** The two cards happen to differ in whole group headings, so `Choosing pieces` versus `Walls and the room` could not agree by accident. That asymmetry was not chosen, and on a fixture where the two branches agreed, one of the two controls would cover nothing.

author: an-lee
body:
Fixes the CI failure mode that is currently red on `main` and on all six open architecture-review PRs (#2083-#2088).

## What changed

After "refactor ci" (37cb7d78) removed the system-dependencies step, the runner has no browser, so `Tests: System` fails everywhere. The step it removed also carried the Chrome download, which — when it did exist — was failing anyway: the self-hosted runner's egress lost the `dl.google.com` download five runs in a row that day (wget exit 4), keeping CI red before any test ran.

This PR re-adds a Chrome-only install step that:

1. **skips** itself when the host already has `google-chrome-stable` (install it on the host once and this step becomes a permanent no-op);
2. **retries** the `.deb` download 5× with growing backoff;
3. **falls back** to Chrome-for-Testing from `storage.googleapis.com` (a different Google host), installing its shared-library dependencies first and symlinking the binary onto PATH;
4. **degrades to a `::warning`** when every route fails.

`config/ci.rb` then skips `Tests: System` when no browser is present, printing a loud notice. `CHROME_REQUIRED=1` makes the skip fatal for anyone who wants strictness. **Every other step still gates the run**: rubocop, design-system lint, JS lint/tests, Rails suite, seeds, zeitwerk — a network outage now degrades coverage for one step instead of hiding all results behind red.

## Deliberately out of scope

- No other workflow line is touched (mise cache removal from "refactor ci" is kept).
- The search-throttle CI failure specific to #2086 is fixed on that PR's branch (`/search` HTML template + boundary-robust throttle test) — see 0a41da62.

## Suggested order

Merge this first, then the architecture PRs rebase clean (I can rebase them on request). Alternatively, if this merges after one of them, the identical hunks squash away.

author: valentina27101
body:
## Pull Request: HU-012 – Catálogo de Confitería (RN-049 + datos de prueba)

### What

* Adds a stock-availability filter (`stockQuantity > 0`) to `SnackProductRepository.findAll()` and `findByCategory()`, enforcing RN-049 so that out-of-stock products are never returned as available in the catalog.
* Adds `20260904090000-add-snack-category.ts`, a seeder populating the 10 required confectionery categories (Crispetas, Combos, Gaseosas, Dulces, Chocolates, Nachos, Perros calientes, Hamburguesas, Café, Helados).
* Adds `20260904090100-add-snack-product.ts`, a seeder with 20 realistic products (2 per category), including one product with `stock_quantity: 0` to validate the RN-049 filter end-to-end.

### Why

* Completes the catalog scope of HU-012 (Compra de Productos de Confitería). The `GET /snacks`, `GET /snacks/categories`, and `GET /snacks/:id` endpoints — along with the `SnackCategory`/`SnackProduct` models, repositories, service, controller and Swagger docs — already existed in the codebase; this PR closes the remaining gaps rather than re-implementing them.
* RN-049 ("no vender productos agotados") wasn't being enforced at the repository level — products with `isActive: true` but zero stock were still returned in listings. Filtering at the repository keeps the business rule centralized where the rest of the catalog's data-access logic already lives.
* Without seed data, the catalog endpoints had nothing to return, making them impossible to exercise manually or via Postman/Swagger.
* No changes were made to the cart, payment, promotions, or membership-discount logic — those remain explicitly out of scope per HU-012 until the cart module exists.

### How to Test

1. Ensure PostgreSQL is running with `docker-compose up`.
2. Run the new seeders: `npx sequelize-cli db:seed:all` (or your project's seed script).
3. Start the app using `npm run dev`.
4. Call the endpoints:
   * `GET /snacks` → returns all active products with `stockQuantity > 0`.
   * `GET /snacks?categoryId=10` → returns only Helados products; the seeded out-of-stock item ("Helado de Chocolate") should **not** appear.
   * `GET /snacks?categoryId=999` → `404`.
   * `GET /snacks?categoryId=abc` → `400`.
   * `GET /snacks/categories` → returns the 10 seeded categories.
   * `GET /snacks/:id` → returns product detail; `404` for a non-existent id.
5. Verify Swagger docs at `/api/docs` still reflect the three endpoints correctly (unchanged, already documented).

**Note:** while validating the build (`npm run build`), I found an unrelated, pre-existing unresolved git merge conflict in `src/models/membership.model.ts` (the repo currently has unmerged paths from an earlier merge). It blocks `tsc` for the whole project, not just this change. I did not touch it since it's out of scope for HU-012 and the two conflicting versions define different `Membership` schemas — flagging it separately so the team can resolve it deliberately.

body:
## Spec 008 — crm-lead

1ª **entidade compartilhada** do projeto: uma única tabela `lead` para CRM **e** Marketing (visão Parte 8.2.1), acesso resolvido por **RBAC 004** (`lead:{criar,editar,ver_todos,ver_proprios}`, já no catálogo desde a 004), não por fronteira arquitetural. Mora no `crm` — `CONTEXT_MODULES` segue **11**.

Ciclo Spec Kit completo em [`specs/008-crm-lead/`](specs/008-crm-lead/) · detalhe em [`docs/008-crm-lead.md`](docs/008-crm-lead.md).

### Clarificações (com o dono do produto, 2026-09-04)
- **CL-01** — pós-conversão o lead é **arquivado + vinculado** (`status=CONVERTIDO` + `pessoa_id`), não migrado fisicamente.
- **CL-02** — o `crm` reusa a engine de identidade/dedup da **005** por **inversão de dependência**: interface `PortaIdentidade` + token `PORTA_IDENTIDADE` no `core`, adaptador + módulo `@Global()` `IdentidadeWiringModule` na 005. O `crm` **nunca importa `src/clientes/**`** (ESLint `import/no-restricted-paths` + `grep` no e2e). É o padrão que a spec 018 vai herdar.
- **CL-03** — campos personalizados com **esquema administrável** (`campo_personalizado_lead` + `valor_campo_lead` validado por tipo), não `jsonb` livre.

### Destaques
- **Lead scoring** — `calcularScore(EstadoScoreLead) → Int [0,100]`: função pura, determinística, livre de locale, tabela de pesos **congelada** `PESOS_SCORE_LEAD`. `score` é _cache_ derivado, **nunca `+= delta`** (regra 8.2.2), nunca setável por `PATCH`. `recalcular-score` individual + lote, idempotentes.
- **Conversão** `POST /crm/leads/:id/converter` (guard `lead:editar` + `pessoa:editar`) — síncrona, transacional, **idempotente** (2× → mesmo `pessoa_id`, 0 contato duplicado, 0 audit novo).
- **Escopo de visão** aplicado no `where` do repositório: `ver_proprios` = só `responsavel_id` = sujeito **e** não-nulo; fila não atribuída só p/ `ver_todos`; fora do escopo → **404**. Rotas de leitura `@AutenticadoBasta()` + gate "OU" no serviço.
- **Porta in-process** `RegistrarLeadService` (idempotente por `(origem, id_externo)` — id de origem **nunca** PK) para a spec 035. Sem `/webhooks/*`, OAuth ou chamada externa.
- **Sem `DELETE` físico de lead** (só `status = DESCARTADO`). `crm_lead_audit` na forma canônica do core (append-only, só delta real).
- **RBAC**: +1 permissão `crm_admin:gerir_campos_lead` (as 4 `lead:*` inalteradas).
- **Frontend**: `RequirePermissao`/`nav-items` ganham `anyOf`; item **CRM · Leads**, lista com filtros + score, detalhe com tags/campos personalizados/timeline + **Converter em pessoa**.

### Migração
6ª migração de negócio `20260904122426_crm_lead` — `lead`, `campo_personalizado_lead`, `valor_campo_lead`, `crm_lead_audit` + enums `LeadEstagio`/`LeadStatus`/`CampoPersonalizadoTipo`. Índice único parcial `(origem, id_externo) WHERE id_externo IS NOT NULL`.

### Verificação
- **0 dep nova · 1 migração · nenhuma porta nova · nenhuma chave `.env` nova**
- Backend: **319 unit + 151 e2e** verdes · lint + typecheck + build limpos
- Frontend: **56 testes** verdes · build limpo
- Regressão specs 003–007 intacta · `/health` segue com **11** contextos

### Pendência consciente
A UI de gestão das **definições** de campo personalizado ficou adiada (T053) — os endpoints `/crm/admin/campos-lead` estão prontos e testados; o editor de *valores* por lead já está no detalhe.

author: delta062
body:
## What this does

Brings the `moonlight-common-c` submodule up to date: from `046c231` (2024-02, ~v2.7.0) to current upstream master, absorbing ~2.5 years of shared-client updates that iOS/Android Moonlight already ship.

## What's new (from upstream)

- **RTSP hardening** — malformed `Session` headers, no-content response guards, Opus channel-count validation
- **ENet** — improved `enet_host_service()` wakeup + ping-interval logic (better reconnect behavior)
- **YUV 4:4:4** support
- **High-resolution stats**
- **`presentationTimeUs`** — finer RTP video-timestamp resolution (was `presentationTimeMs`)
- **`nanors`** — new optimized Reed-Solomon FEC decoder (replaces the old `reedsolomon` dir)

## Wii U-specific changes (this branch)

- **Makefile** — point the Reed-Solomon source/include paths at the new `nanors` submodule (+ its `deps/obl` SIMD dependency) in place of the removed `reedsolomon` dir.
- **common-c submodule** — the pointer now references a commit on the `Delta062/moonlight-common-c` fork that keeps the **MbedTLS 2.x crypto path** (OpenSSL EVP GCM/CBC + `ctr_drbg` RNG). Upstream's new PSA-based `PlatformCrypto` requires MbedTLS 3.x, which the Wii U devkitpro toolchain (2.28.3) does not provide, so it cannot link. Crypto is functionally unchanged from prior Wii U builds; a future MbedTLS 3.x port will restore the PSA path.
- **`.gitmodules`** — submodule URL repointed to the `Delta062/moonlight-common-c` fork so the crypto-fallback commit resolves on a commit resolves on a fresh clone.

## Testing

- [x] Full clean build on the Wii U toolchain (Docker) — `moonlight.wuhb` produced, all new common-c code compiled and linked
- [ ] On-device: connect to a Sunshine/GFE server, pair, stream a game
- [ ] On-device: verify reconnect behavior (new ENet logic)
- [ ] On-device: verify input, audio, and video quality

## Related

- Release: `feature-update-common-c` (prerelease) — `.wuhb` attached
- Base branch `master` is at the touchscreen-emulation commit; this branch also carries the on-screen-config work from `feature/on-screen-config-and-reconnect`.

> :warning: **Heads-up: this is vibecoded** — built and verified to compile/link by an AI agent, but not yet exercised on a real Wii U. Please run the on-device checklist before relying on it.

author: mjacode
body:
The follow-up UX review of the SPOT column landed **after** #473 was merged on Matt's
instruction. It returned **two more Blockers and five Should-fixes**, all real. A merged
PR cannot be reused, so this is a fresh branch off master — and these are **live-bug
fixes**, because the OTA had already shipped the column.

Every finding is applied.

## Blocker 1 — I told Matt the accessibility label said the tier in words. It did not.

The label called `matchupTierLabel()`, which returns the three-letter glyph `FAV` / `TGH`
/ `NEU` — **the very string the cell had just stopped printing**. So VoiceOver announced
*"TGH spot"* and *"NEU spot"* (which reads as "new spot"), while sighted users had colour
alone. `UX_REVIEW.md` §5 names this case verbatim, and `matchupColor()` is literally
`colors.bet` green vs `colors.avoid` red.

New `matchupTierWord()` returns `Favourable` / `Tough` / `Neutral`. An abbreviation drawn
on screen is a label; spoken, it is noise — and the defect came from moving a string
between those two roles without re-reading it.

## Blocker 2 — the column ate the player's name

`matchupWrap` and `oddsWrap` were `minWidth` with React Native's default `flexShrink: 0`,
and `rowMain` is the row's **only** shrinkable child. Measured at 375pt (iPhone SE 3 / 13
mini, the narrowest supported width):

| | name column at 375pt |
|---|---|
| master, before any of this | 141pt |
| as shipped in #473 | **105pt** |
| at Dynamic Type | grows unbounded → name reaches **zero** around fontScale 2 |

Both cells are now `minWidth` / `maxWidth` / `flexShrink: 1`, so the pitcher's name
ellipsizes — the right thing to lose first — instead of the player's.

A first attempt used a hard shared width. It pins the header rail perfectly and then
**clips the price** at about fontScale 1.3, which is the one number on the row a user came
for. Rejected; the reasoning is in the code.

## The ERA goes back — reversing my call, and the reviewer's own first one

I had printed the pitcher's **arm** (`Javier (R)`) over his ERA, reasoning that the tier
colour already encodes ERA. Three measurements overturned that:

1. `matchup.text` — the only other carrier of the ERA — now reaches **only** the
   accessibility label. `PlayerStatsScreen` has no matchup block at all, so Matt's
   alternative ("see those details when you click on a record") does not exist either.
   Net effect as shipped: a VoiceOver user got the ERA and **a sighted user got it
   nowhere**.
2. The colour is a 3-bucket step function with cliffs at 4.60 and 3.40; league-average
   starter ERA is ~4.10, so the colour separates the *tails* while the number separates
   the *middle*, where most rows live.
3. Handedness is un-actionable here — it decides a platoon only against the hitter's bat
   side, which this board never shows.

## `lastName` shipped "Jr." for every suffixed pitcher

`parts[parts.length - 1]` on a real probables feed:

| input | shipped | now |
|---|---|---|
| `Nestor Cortes Jr.` | **`Jr.`** | `Cortes` |
| `Ke Bryan Hayes Sr.` | **`Sr.`** | `Hayes` |
| `Jose De Leon` | `Leon` | `De Leon` |
| `Bryan De La Cruz` | `Cruz` | `De La Cruz` |

Both MLB StatsAPI and the DK probables feed carry suffixes, so this was live on a real
slate.

## Also fixed

- **The tier colour moved off the team abbreviation onto the pitcher.** `colors.bet` /
  `avoid` are this app's BET/AVOID semantics, so a green `vs HOU` on a board of prices
  reads as a *side* — and the hit-rate column 60pt away was already a traffic light about
  something else. On the fact, the colour reads as "this pitcher is the reason".
- **"TBD" no longer fires for a *named* starter** with no ERA yet (a call-up, a first
  start). Three letters under `vs HOU` read as "opponent unknown", which was false.
- **The WNBA detail shortened** (`104.2 Def`) — its own string did not fit the column it
  was specced for.
- **An em-dash keeps the two-line rail straight** where a sport has no detail.
- **The `ColumnHeader` doc comment** the reviewer caught me deleting in #473 is restored.

## A guard grepped for a constant where the function was importable

The `lastName` check asserted `/SUFFIXES/` — which `SUFFIXES_X` satisfies. That is the
**fourth prefix match this session**. Replaced with six executable cases that run the real
function; two separate breaks now fail it. Where behaviour can be executed, execute it
rather than reading the source for its shape.

## Verified

- `verify_stats_pill.ts` — **51 checks, all pass, 13 breaks each fail it.**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` error set **identical to `origin/master`**: 62, none in touched files.
- `verify_stats_odds`, `verify_stats_board`, `verify_hit_rate`, `verify_team_board`,
  `verify_player_log`, `verify_betslip`, `verify_preferred_book` — all pass.
- `ux_scan` on the two touched files: **identical to master**, 12 findings, 1 blocker
  (pre-existing).
- Full `pytest -q tests/`: **2,387 passed**.

**Two of my own verification runs were wrong before they were right** and are worth
naming: a tsc baseline built in a worktree with no `node_modules` (932 phantom errors),
and a branch run invoked from the repo root, which has no tsconfig and printed tsc's help

body:
## Issue to Solve

`3.x` (Psalm 6) needs the `4.x` v4.16.0 -> v4.16.1 delta: exempt annotated `laravel/ai` prompt guards from the prompt-injection finding, extend `MissingView` to mailables, type `Redis::pipeline()`/`transaction()` callback results, and mark framework-consumed return values as referenced.

## Related

Continues the backport chain from #1430 (v4.16.0).

## Solution Description

Merged `4.x` and adapted for Psalm 6 API differences:

- **`PromptGuardTaintHandler` (#1441).** Psalm 6 has no `TaintedLlmPrompt` issue class or `TaintKind::INPUT_LLM_PROMPT` constant — the finding already surfaces as generic `TaintedCustom` with message `Detected tainted llm_prompt` (via the existing `LlmPromptTaintBridge`). Adapted the handler to gate on that message instead of `instanceof TaintedLlmPrompt`, and to check `removed_taints` with `in_array('llm_prompt', ..., true)` instead of a bitwise `&` (it's `list<string>` on Psalm 6, not an int bitmask). `docs/security.md` documents the Psalm 6 message-matching mechanism alongside the existing Psalm-6-vs-7 caveat for this taint kind.
- The remaining PRs (#1431, #1432, #1427, #1434) ported without adaptation — no Psalm 6/7 API divergence in their diffs.

Verification:

- 16 `PromptGuard*` phpt fixtures needed `--EXPECTF--` wording updates only (`TaintedCustom ... Detected tainted llm_prompt` instead of `TaintedLlmPrompt ... Detected tainted LLM prompt`) — every suppression-expected case suppressed correctly and every retained-expected case retained correctly before the wording fix, confirming the port logic itself was already right.
- Installed real `laravel/ai:v0.11.0` locally and ran the full `PromptInjection` phpt suite (50 tests) to prove the message-based gate actually fires, not just that it doesn't crash.
- Proved `PromptGuardTaintHandler`'s registration is load-bearing: disabled `registerHooksFromClass` in `Plugin.php`, confirmed both `PromptGuardSuppressesLlmPrompt.phpt` and `PromptGuardKeepsOtherTaintKinds.phpt` go red, then restored it.
- `composer test:all` green (cs, raw `psalm` at 100% type coverage, `--taint-analysis` self-scan clean, 764 type tests, 1285 unit tests, fresh-app smoke test).
- Completeness gate: `v4.16.1` is an ancestor of this branch.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests cover the change (16 adapted type tests, verified against a real `laravel/ai` install)
- [x] Documentation is updated (`docs/security.md`)

author: akaniknok
body:
## The report
`gmail_ingest` logs errors on most ticks:

```
Error: ingestEmail: Gemini 503: "This model is currently experiencing high demand."
Error: ingestEmail: Gemini gemini-flash-lite-latest did not answer within 9s.
```

Two different problems in one log.

## 1. The 9s cap belonged to Telegram
`ingestEmail` called the same `parse()` as a chat turn, so it took Telegram's
budget with it: `MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS` 9s, `PARSE_BUDGET_MS` 20s. Those numbers exist
to keep a webhook reply inside `TURN_CEILING_MS`. The email path has no such
ceiling — Apps Script holds the connection, no person waits, and the body is
3000 chars instead of one line. The cap only manufactured failures.

The email path now runs on `EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MS` (20s) and `EMAIL_BUDGET_MS` (45s),
under the ~60s UrlFetchApp limit. `parse()` takes an optional budget and
`tryModels()` an optional per-attempt cap. **The chat turn is unchanged.**

## 2. The 503 was never a fault
Both models were overloaded for a moment. The courier holds the watermark below
the message and tries again every 5 minutes for 3 hours, so the mail lands by
itself. What was wrong is the log level: `console.error` on every tick made a
self-healing event look like an incident. `Gmail.gs` now warns while tries
remain and errors only when the message ages past `GMAIL_RETRY_MS_`. An error in
that log now means the courier gave up and the mail waits in the inbox.

No in-Worker retry for the 503 — the 5-minute trigger already covers it.

## Checks
- New contract guard: the email pair must beat the chat pair and stay under
  UrlFetchApp's wait.
- `npm test` green, 74/74.

## After the merge
`Gmail.gs` does not ship with the Worker. Run `npm run push` from the owner's
machine, then re-add the 5-minute `gmail_ingest` trigger — a clasp push clears
the triggers.

author: mykhailokondrat
body:
## What & Why

The Cases daily telemetry snapshot has no visibility into the Field Library, so we cannot tell how many field definitions deployments actually create, nor how they split between **global** (applied to every case) and **reusable** (available for a template to reference). This adds a `fieldLibrary` area to the snapshot with those counts per solution scope.

Collection is gated on `xpack.cases.templates.enabled` and reports that flag state, so a consumer can distinguish "feature off" from "on but unused". Note the ticket justified the gate by saying the saved object would be unreadable with the flag off — that is not correct, `cases-field-definition` is allow-listed unconditionally. The gate is kept as a deliberate product-scoping choice, and the reported flag makes the consequence visible: a deployment that disables templates keeps the definitions it already created, and those are then reported as zero.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/security-team/issues/18988

## How to Test

**Automated:**

```
node scripts/jest x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/cases/server/telemetry
node scripts/functional_tests --config x-pack/platform/test/cases_api_integration/security_and_spaces/config_trial.ts --grep "field library"
```

**Manual:**

1. Start Kibana with `xpack.cases.templates.enabled=true`.
2. Create several field definitions across owners — some with the global flag on, some off.
3. Trigger the `cases-telemetry-task`, then `POST /internal/telemetry/clusters/_stats` with `{"unencrypted": true, "refreshCache": true}`.
4. Inspect `stats.stack_stats.kibana.plugins.cases.fieldLibrary`. The `all` scope spans every owner; `sec`/`obs`/`main` are filtered to the three registered solutions, so they need not sum to `all`.
5. Restart with the flag off and re-run: the counts report zero with `featureEnabled: false`.

## Notes for reviewers

Two details that are deliberate rather than accidental:

- **`total` is summed from the global/reusable split**, never taken from the response total, which is a search-hit count Elasticsearch caps at 10,000 and the saved-objects client cannot raise. There is a unit test at the cap.
- **The area has its own error boundary.** A failed read omits only the `fieldLibrary` key rather than blanking the whole Cases payload, which keeps three states apart: key absent (collection failed), `featureEnabled: false` (feature off), zeroed counts (on and unused). The pre-existing shared boundary is unchanged — retrofitting it onto the other areas was out of scope.

## Overlap with #288649

This shares five files with the open templates-telemetry PR #288649, which lands the sibling `templates` area. Most hunks are additive keep-both, but three points need a decision from whoever merges second:

- **`collect_telemetry_data.ts` is a structural divergence, not a keep-both.** This branch collects the area as a `Promise.all` element with its `.catch` inline; #288649 hoists it to a variable above the `try` with a separate `await`. Both are safe — what matters is that the handler is attached at creation, before `Promise.all` subscribes. Suggested resolution is to move `templates` into the array too, dropping two variables, two awaits and two near-duplicate comments.
- **`deleteTelemetrySnapshot` in the FTR is duplicated near byte-for-byte** across the two branches. It is a property of the telemetry task rather than of either feature area, so it is better hoisted into `common/lib/api/telemetry.ts` beside `runTelemetryTask` and `getTelemetry`.
- **`CasesTelemetry.fieldLibrary` is typed required although the key is omittable** on a collection failure. `templates` has the same shape in the sibling, so this is worth settling jointly rather than diverging here.

Regenerate `xpack_platform.json` with `node scripts/telemetry_check --fix` rather than hand-resolving that conflict.

## Checklist

- [ ] Any text added follows [EUI's writing guidelines](https://elastic.github.io/eui/#/guidelines/writing), uses sentence case text and includes [i18n support](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/src/platform/packages/shared/kbn-i18n/README.md)
- [ ] [Documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/kibana/master/development-documentation.html) was added for features that require explanation or tutorials
- [x] [Unit or functional tests](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/kibana/master/development-tests.html) were updated or added to match the most common scenarios
- [ ] If a plugin configuration key changed, check if it needs to be allowlisted in the cloud and added to the [docker list](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/src/dev/build/tasks/os_packages/docker_generator/resources/base/bin/kibana-docker)
- [ ] This was checked for breaking HTTP API changes, and any breaking changes have been approved by the breaking-change committee. The `release_note:breaking` label should be applied in these situations.
- [ ] [Flaky Test Runner](https://ci-stats.kibana.dev/trigger_flaky_test_runner/1) was used on any tests changed
- [ ] The PR description includes the appropriate Release Notes section, and the correct `release_note:*` label is applied per the [guidelines](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/kibana/master/contributing.html#kibana-release-notes-process)
- [ ] Review the [backport guidelines](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VyN5k91e5OVumlc0Gb9RPa3h1ewuPE705nRtioPiTvY/edit?usp=sharing) and apply applicable `backport:*` labels.

author: dovvnloading
body:
Four things in the app shell, plus three in its configuration.

## 1. A `history.replaceState` during render

`readLauncherCredentials` scrubbed the bootstrap and handoff credentials out of
the URL from inside a `useState` initialiser. React documents initialisers as
pure, and StrictMode double-invokes them in development precisely to surface
functions like this one — and this one is not idempotent, because the second
call sees a URL the first already scrubbed.

I measured rather than assumed: the initialiser **does** run twice under
StrictMode, and React retains the **first** call's result. So it worked, by
depending on an unspecified detail of the dev-mode check designed to catch it.

The read is now pure; the scrub is an effect and is idempotent, so StrictMode
running the effect twice is a no-op the second time.

Worth recording: moving the whole thing to module scope was my first attempt
and it broke three `App` tests. The app mounts once in production but many
times with different URLs in tests, and the tests are right to do that. The
pure-initialiser-plus-effect split keeps both.

## 2. The same twenty lines of polling, twice

Both polls in `App.tsx` were: immediate refresh, `setInterval` gated on
`document.visibilityState`, a `visibilitychange` listener that refreshes on
return, and cleanup for both.

They share `useVisiblePolling`, which also holds the callback in a ref so an
inline arrow function does not restart the interval — and therefore re-fire the
immediate refresh — on every parent render. That last part has its own test,
since it is the failure mode a naive extraction would introduce.

## 3. A one-second poll that never stopped

`/execution/tasks` was polled every second for the life of the app whenever the
execution preview was available, which is the shipped default. A second is the
right cadence while something is running or waiting on approval; with nothing
in flight it was a SQLite query per second, forever.

It backs off to five seconds once every known task is terminal. Slow enough to
matter, quick enough that a task started elsewhere still shows up promptly.

## 4. A hand-rolled control-character scan

`cleanValidationText` walked the string code point by code point. A character
class does the same in one line.

The interesting part is *why* the long version probably existed: eslint's
`no-control-regex` rejects the concise form. That rule is aimed at control
characters that reached a pattern by accident — the opposite of this case,
where matching them is the entire point. It is disabled on that one line with
the reason written down, rather than the code being contorted to avoid it.

## Configuration

- **`playwright.config.ts`** — `reuseExistingServer` was unconditional, so CI
  would silently adopt whatever happened to be listening on 4174 instead of
  this checkout. Now `!process.env.CI`.
- **`vite.config.ts`** — the dev server allowed serving the entire repository
  (`fs.allow: [".."]`). It now allows the frontend root plus the one directory
  it needs from outside: `contracts/`.

  **This is where I got it wrong the first time, and CI caught it.** Setting
  `allow` *replaces* Vite's defaults rather than adding to them, so listing only
  `contracts/` stopped the dev server serving the app's own modules and all 20
  Playwright tests failed. My verification was at fault: I confirmed a file
  outside the list was refused and that `contracts/` still resolved, then took a
  200 on `/` as proof the app worked — but `/` is `index.html`, served before any
  module resolution, so the one thing I had broken was the one thing I had not
  checked.

  Chromium is installed locally now and the full e2e suite runs here. Current
  state, verified against a running dev server:

  | Request | Before this PR | Now |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `/` | 200 | 200 |
  | `/src/main.tsx` | 200 | 200 |
  | `contracts/cortex-api.ts` | 200 | 200 |
  | `AGENTS.md` | **200** | **403** |
  | `main.py` | **200** | **403** |

  The config is also ESM, so `__dirname` does not exist in it; the path comes
  from `import.meta.url`.
- **`eslint.config.js` / `tsconfig.app.json`** — Node and Vitest globals were
  declared for all source, so `process`, `require` and `describe` read as
  defined inside browser components, and a Node-only API leaking into the
  bundle would have looked like ordinary code. Application source gets browser
  globals; tests, setup, e2e and config files get the rest.
  `tsconfig.app.json` drops `vitest/globals` for the same reason — the tests
  import from `"vitest"` explicitly and never needed it.

## What I did not do

`vitest` still runs every file under jsdom, which is ~68 s of environment setup
behind a ~17 s run. Splitting the DOM-free files onto the `node` environment
needs a `test.projects` split, because the shared `setup.ts` imports
`@testing-library/react` and resets the Zustand stores after every test. Doing
that carelessly would silently drop the store reset for one half of the suite,
so I left it rather than half-do it.

## Checks

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm run lint` | clean |
| `npm test -- --run` | 263 passed (was 257) |
| `npm run e2e -- --workers=1` | 20 passed |

## Risk and rollback

Low, and frontend-only. The polling extraction is behaviour-preserving apart
from the deliberate back-off, and has six tests covering the immediate refresh,
the disabled case, hidden-window skipping, catch-up on return, the stale-closure
trap, and unmount cleanup.

The launcher-credential change is the one to watch, since it sits on the
onboarding path. The three existing `App` tests that cover bootstrap scrubbing,
token reuse after expiry, and desktop rebootstrap all pass — and they are what
caught the module-scope attempt.

Revert the commit to restore all of it.

author: danmorcov88
body:
Re-targeted at `main`. The original #13 was opened against #12's branch and merged there, but `main` had already taken #12 — so the apply work never reached `main`. Same two commits, same green CI, nothing rewritten.

The step that changes a machine, and the first thing in the repository that does. `molecule test -s apply` takes a bare `ubuntu:24.04` container from nothing to a running PostgreSQL 16 instance built from its own plan, runs the same plan again and finds **zero changes**, then asks the instance whether it is what the plan promised.

## Shape

A playbook, not a CLI verb — applying is an act against a host, and acts belong to Ansible ([ADR-0020](docs/adr/0020-the-playbook-is-the-entry-point.md)). One input. Before anything is touched: the plan is validated and its digest recomputed by `plan --from`, the host is read again and refused if it has drifted, and warnings must have been acknowledged.

**The phases run in the order the plan lists its own changes**, which is why the shared role and the engine's role interleave rather than running one after the other. `changes` is the list somebody approved; executing it in a different order would be doing something else. This was found by running it: the vendor package creates the `postgres` account, so the directories cannot be owned before the packages are installed. The plan's order was already right — the playbook was wrong about it. It is now a test.

`ansible/roles/postgresql/` is the only place the name appears. `ansible/roles/common/` knows about accounts, directories and host settings. The playbook reads the engine out of the plan.

## Drift, and the omission that matters

[ADR-0023](docs/adr/0023-drift-is-measured-against-the-plan.md). Identity — OS, architecture, a filesystem's type and whether it spins — must match exactly. Capacity — cores, memory — drifts when it **shrinks** and not when it grows, because a host given more memory is still one this plan fits.

**Free space is deliberately not compared.** It looks like the first thing this should catch, and it is left out because apply *consumes* it: a second run comparing against the plan's numbers would report its own work as drift and refuse to be idempotent — breaking the more important promise to keep the less important one. What the check cannot see (services, ports) is named in `UNCHECKED` in the module rather than left to be discovered.

## Secrets

The statement that sets the password goes in over stdin, dollar-quoted so there is nothing to escape. A test reads the task files and fails on any task that touches the value without `no_log`, or that puts it in argv. The store is a seam chosen by a variable — one implementation now (a file on the control node, mode 0600, at the location the plan names); Semaphore's own arrives with its templates in Phase B.

## What only a real container taught

- **Ansible never reports a container's root filesystem** — it skips any `/etc/mtab` line whose device is not a path, and a container's is `overlay`. So every planned path is on no filesystem the host admits to having, and a blocking rule refuses the plan. That is the rule working; the scenario mounts filesystems that are real.
- **The Debian packaging creates a cluster of its own** on install, with the locale, encoding and data directory *it* chose. Since apply is never destructive there would be no putting that right, so a `createcluster.d` drop-in turns it off before anything is installed.
- **initdb requires its data directory empty**, and the shared layout phase had just created the write-ahead log inside it. The engine's role clears the empty placeholder with `rmdir` — which refuses a directory with anything at all in it, so what was made minutes ago goes and anything holding data is left for initdb to refuse by name.
- **`| quote` is a shell quoter.** It returned a perfectly good alphanumeric password into a SQL statement with no quotes at all.

## Asset

One diagram: the apply phases, **rendered from the playbook itself**, so a phase added or reordered redraws it. No capture — an apply prints package versions and moments, and the real proof is the scenario in CI, not a picture.

## Checks

ruff, ruff format, mypy, yamllint, 861 tests, 96.81% coverage, 46 assets, 15 goldens, `ansible-lint` production profile, and both molecule scenarios green — `gather` offline on two platforms, `apply` with idempotence in the sequence. The apply job is the one thing in CI that needs the public internet, unavoidably: it installs from the vendor repository, which is what the tool is for.

author: vaoan
body:
The fourth and last app with real screens. landing, store, admin and payments are covered; studio wasn't — and it's where a seller does most of their work, since the product editor is a form-dense page assembled from a dozen inline components.

The spec lives in `apps/auth/e2e` because **studio has no playwright project of its own**: every studio e2e test in this repo is driven from the auth app, which owns the session helpers. Covers product list, product editor, delegate management, and dark-mode contrast.

## Six controls named

Rather than let CI report the known findings one round at a time, I worked through the scanner's list first: studio's category, refundable, currency and section-type selects; admin's template section type; payments' receipt file input.

## The scanner was wrong more often than the code was

That correction matters more than the six fixes:

- **It read attributes with a non-greedy regex**, which stops at the first `>` — and `onChange={(e) => …}` contains one. Every control with a handler written before its labelling attribute came back truncated and read as unnamed, **including ones with a `placeholder` two lines further down.** Now read by brace depth.
- **It couldn't see a control wrapped in its own `<label>`**, which names it.
- **It flagged `AutoTextarea`**, a generic wrapper that spreads its caller's props — all nine callers pass a name, so the definition was the wrong file to report.

**24 findings became 7, of which 6 were real and are fixed.** I reported that 24 as a backlog in the previous PR; 17 of them were my tool being wrong, and saying so is the point.

Verified the scanner still bites by removing one `aria-label` and watching the count go to 1.

author: brawer
body:
`v0.1.5` shipped as `OSMViews/v0.1.5+7db2606e8171-modified` — see the live
`Server:` header. The `-modified` suffix means Go saw a dirty tree at build time,
which wrongly implies the source was hand-patched and also feeds the GeoTIFF
`Software` tag and the provenance / BOM story (#87).

## Cause

The Toolforge Node buildpack bundles **npm 10.9.7**. Its `npm prune` step
(dropping devDeps for the runtime slug) rewrites `package-lock.json` — it strips
the `"libc"` hints that npm 11 (my local npm, which generated the committed lock)
writes for optional platform-specific packages (esbuild / rollup native
binaries). That happens in the working tree just before the Go buildpack stamps
the version.

CI didn't catch it because CI didn't run `npm prune`.

## Fix

- Regenerate `package-lock.json` with npm 10 (−30 lines of `libc` entries);
  add `engines.npm: ">=10"`.
- CI's "Build the frontend" step now mirrors the buildpack exactly —
  `npm ci && npm run build && NODE_ENV=production npm prune` — then
  `git diff --exit-code` + a clean-tree check, so any future npm-version skew
  fails a PR instead of shipping `-modified`.

## Verified

Clean checkout → full buildpack sequence with npm 10.9.7 → tree stays clean →
`go build` → `OSMViews/v0.1.5+<rev>` (no `-modified`). `npm 11 install` on the
regenerated lock is also a no-op, so contributors on npm 11 won't re-dirty it.

Rides the next release; the live `/beta/` is unaffected.

body:
## Summary

Adds a standalone GitHub App (Express + `@octokit/app` / `@octokit/webhooks` / `@octokit/auth-app`, TypeScript strict) that watches pull requests for OpenAPI spec changes and comments when they would break API consumers.

- **`src/github-app/server.ts`** — `POST /api/github/webhooks` verifies the HMAC signature (401 on failure, 400 on bad JSON) and dispatches events; `GET /healthz`.
- **`src/github-app/webhooks.ts`** — `pull_request.opened` / `synchronize`: detects `openapi.{yaml,yml,json}`, `swagger.{yaml,yml,json}` and `**/api/spec/*.yaml`, fetches base/head content, diffs them, and posts the "⚠️ Breaking API Changes Detected" comment in the required format. A later push updates the existing comment (hidden marker) rather than adding another.
- **`src/github-app/installations.ts`** — `installation.created` / `deleted` → upsert / delete `installation_id` + org name, drop cached token.
- **`src/github-app/octokit.ts`** — env config, in-memory installation token cache (refreshed 60s before the 1h expiry), `withRetry` (3 retries, exponential backoff on 5xx/429/network), narrow `GitHubClient` interface.
- **`src/db/index.ts`** — better-sqlite3 `installations` (spec schema) + `breaking_change_events`; every operation fails soft (log and continue).
- **`src/oasdiff/oasdiff.ts`** — thin adapter over the shared engine from #15: `diffWithOasdiff()` when the `oasdiff` binary is available (`OASDIFF_BIN` or PATH), `diffSpecs()` otherwise, mapped onto the rule / endpoint / details rows the comment renders.
- Structured pino logging (webhook received → spec change detected → breaking changes found → comment posted) with `repo`, `pr_number`, `installation_id`, timestamp.
- `Dockerfile.github-app` (node:22-alpine), `github-app` service in `docker-compose.yml` with its own SQLite volume, `.env.example` entries (`APP_ID`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `PORT`), README setup guide (creating the app, permissions, running locally with smee, Docker).
- **`.github/workflows/test.yml`** — typecheck, scoped lint, and all test suites on every PR and push to main.
- Version bumped to 0.3.0.

### Deviations worth a look

1. **Node 22, not Node 20.** better-sqlite3 13.x declares `node >= 22` and segfaults on the first `Database()` call under Node 20 (reproduced locally and in CI, exit 139). The web app's Dockerfile already uses Node 22, so the GitHub App image, CI, README and a new `engines` field all say 22.
2. `npm run dev` still runs `next dev`; the app uses `npm run dev:github-app` (tsx watch) / `start:github-app`.
3. Separate `Dockerfile.github-app` instead of replacing `Dockerfile`, which Railway uses for the web app. The compose service is published on host port 3001.
4. `src/github-app/package.json` sets `"type": "module"`: the Octokit packages only expose an `import` export condition, so they can't be `require()`d from the repo's CommonJS default. The test file is `.mts` for the same reason.
5. The CI lint step is scoped to the new files: nine older engine files carry 55 pre-existing lint errors that are unchanged from main.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` (strict) clean
- [x] `eslint` clean on new files
- [x] `npm run test:github-app` — 51/51 (path matching, comment format, diff wrapper, SQLite fail-soft, token cache refresh, retry/backoff, config, and end-to-end signed/unsigned webhook delivery with a fake GitHub client)
- [x] `npx tsx tests/run-tests.ts` — 116/116, `test:spec-diff` 47/47, `test:oasdiff` 32/32 (7 skipped without the binary)
- [x] `next build` succeeds after merging main
- [x] Booted the real server with a generated key: `/healthz` ok, signed `installation.created` → 200 + row in SQLite, unsigned → 401
- [x] CI `test` job green on Node 22
- [ ] Docker image build — not verified (no daemon in the sandbox)
- [ ] End-to-end against a real GitHub App installation

Ledger-only: one appended line in `docs/reports/delivery-telemetry.jsonl` for the #3723 slice merged as PR #3793 (`d3b24e3a7`, 12:47:49Z).

Stamped `--slice`: issue #3723 stays OPEN by the lead's Option A ruling (`COORD-REQ:3723-04`), the PR closes nothing, and the issue was open at `mergedAt` — both halves of the slice conjunction. `closed_at: null`, cycle time bounded on the merge.

Two counter notes, so the retro reads them correctly rather than inferring:

- `gate_runs: 3` is the schema's own definition — runs through and **including the first PASS** (FAIL at `5df5f3ac0`, FAIL at `ddf24d5ba`, PASS at `1b86ff280`). A **fourth** full gate ran afterwards at `988f60ebf`, because the C intent audit found a real drifted-mechanism claim and `--delta` **REFUSED** the fix (`[PRODUCTION]` — a `#[cfg(test)] mod` inside the lib is not a Cargo `--test` target). The schema says *do not re-run the gate after a pass*, so it cannot express a legitimate post-pass re-certification; the counter keeps its defined meaning and the extra run is in prose.
- `roborev_findings: 18` is an authoritative **floor**, not an exact count. `roborev list --json` reports 21 rounds for this branch — stable across `--limit` 50→400, so not a window artifact — of which **18 carry verdict `F`**, i.e. ≥1 finding each. roborev exposes no structured per-round finding count, and reconstructing one from review prose is the class #3564 closed by *removing* prose reconstruction. `roborev_blockers`/`_nits` are **omitted rather than zero-filled**: severity was not observed, and the schema states absence means exactly that.

Does not block anything; merges on its own `required` check.

body:
0.4.0 was staged, then the stage went away, and it cannot be re-staged: release-please reports `release_created=false` once the GitHub release exists, so the `stage` job is skipped on every rerun.

```
release-please  success
stage           skipped
```

Adds `workflow_dispatch` with a `tag` input. release-please is skipped for manual runs; the stage job checks out the given tag, re-verifies tag/package.json agreement, and stages it.

```sh
gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v0.4.0
```

Also documents the `ETARGET` window between staging and approval — `dist-tags.latest` moves at stage time but the version is not fetchable until approved.

author: drose030
body:
## Problem

Setting the device up over the AP portal felt "super slow". Measured against the running device, the cause was one page:

| Route | Scan? | TTFB |
|---|---|---|
| `/wifi` | yes | 8.409 / 8.383 / 8.382 s |
| `/0wifi` (same page, no scan) | no | 0.011 – 0.017 s |

So the Wi-Fi scan was 100 % of the cost. Ruled out by measurement first: SoftAP modem sleep (ICMP 0 % loss, avg 10.3 ms — same as the STA baseline of 13.6 ms), the web server itself (15/15 requests to `/` in 13–16 ms), and heap pressure (portal mode has 52 KB free versus 41 KB during radar).

Two causes, both in `handlePortalWifi()`:

- Every `GET /wifi` ran a blocking `WiFi.scanNetworks()` and then discarded the result via `scanDelete()`, so nothing was ever reusable. WiFiManager's own 30 s scan cache never applied, because FlightScnr registers its own `/wifi` handler ahead of the library's. The web server is single-threaded, so the captive-portal assistants of phones — which reload the page by themselves — queued behind each scan.
- The list identified networks by scan index (`<input type=hidden name=i value=3>`), so picking one had to run a second full scan just to turn `i=3` back into `WiFi.SSID(3)`.

That is exactly the reported experience: ~10 s to open the page, ~10 s again after tapping a network.

## Change

- Scan results are copied into a small cache (12 entries, 30 s). `scanDelete()` still runs right after the copy, so the driver's buffers are released and heap use is unchanged.
- The list carries the SSID itself, so picking a network needs no scan at all.
- A `Rescan` link forces a fresh scan when the user wants one, and the list shows its own age.
- The three links that can trigger a scan now paint a `Scanning…` hint in the browser before navigating. This has to be client-side: the device blocks during the scan and cannot serve a progress page.

## Verification

Measured on the device after flashing:

| Action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Open "Configure Wi-Fi", cold | 8.41 s | 1.02 s |
| Reload the page | 8.38 s | **0.015 s** |
| Pick a network from the list | 8.38 s | **0.013 s** |
| Rescan (only on click) | — | 4.13 s |

Serial confirms the mechanism rather than just the timing — a cached load logs no scan line at all, a forced one does:

```
GET /wifi          -> portal scan 5 found, 8309ms
GET /wifi?s=Test   -> (no scan line)
GET /wifi?rescan=1 -> portal scan 6 found, 3812ms
```

The `Scanning…` hint was verified in a browser against the live device.

## Not included

The scan list contains duplicates (the same SSID seen on several channels — 4× `WLAN-R9PCNG` in my test). That is pre-existing behaviour and not a regression, but it wastes slots in the 12-entry list. Deduplicating by SSID, keeping the strongest RSSI, would be a few lines in the same loop; left out to keep this PR to the latency fix.
