author: mendematthias
body:
Closes the gap between "easyNode is open source" and "a stranger
can find it, download it, build it, and cut a release from it".

Everything below was measured on an Ubuntu 22.04 / RTX 3060 box running a live
mainnet validator on 2026-09-04, and the numbers are re-verified rather than
carried over. Where something is unproven it says so.

## The download path was broken on GitHub

The README's only download link pointed at `EasyBTX-releases`, whose repo-global
"Latest" is the **miner** — deliberately, because a node release that captured
that pointer would break the miner's updater. Verified: `/releases/latest`
returns `v0.24.0`, "easyBTX v0.24.0 (macOS)". Anyone following the README landed
on a different product.

It now points at [easybtx.com/node](https://easybtx.com/node) and says plainly
why not to use the Latest button. Every link on that page was checked and returns
200: the mac `.dmg`, the Linux `.AppImage` and `.deb`, the Windows `.exe`. No
version numbers are hardcoded, because they go stale.

Mac and Linux are both current and consistent at 0.6.17 — `package.json`,
`tauri.conf.json`, `Cargo.toml`, the CHANGELOG and the live updater feed all
agree. Windows lags at 0.6.6 with no update path, and the README now says so
instead of leaving a reader to discover it at the download page.

## A live bug: the conf's prune posture was being silently overridden

btxd loads the datadir's `btx_rw.conf` on every start regardless of `-conf`, and
a read-write setting outranks a config-file one. From btxd's own log on the
validator:

```
Config file arg:     prune="0"
R/W config file arg: prune="4096"
Prune configured to target 4096 MiB on disk for block and undo files.
```

`disk.rs` opens by stating this app runs btxd un-pruned **on purpose**, because a
pruned node cannot rebuild shielded state after an unclean shutdown and SIGABRTs
instead. The node had been running pruned for weeks against the conf the app
wrote, and nothing in the UI said so. Every install that ran the mirror era
carries this leftover — the same population the `-matmulvalidation=consensus`
line right below already exists to rescue.

Fixed by re-asserting the **conf's own** value on the command line. Deliberately
not a hardcoded `prune=0`: the keeper profile is pruned on purpose and forcing 0
would silently convert every keeper into a full node.

## A collision, resolved in main's favour

While this branch was being written, **#13 merged a publish script** and **#14
merged real disk numbers**. I had written a publish script too, not knowing #13
existed. Main's landed first, is reviewed, and is good — same draft → upload →
re-download → verify → flip ordering, `make_latest` as the string `"false"`,
signatures checked against the released bytes, and a Latest-pointer check
afterwards. It is more careful than mine in two places I had not considered: it
refuses to publish a version the tree does not claim, and it avoids `mapfile`
because the release Mac runs bash 3.2.

**So mine is withdrawn, not renamed.** A second implementation of the same thing
is the definition of chaos. My test suite went with it (it exercised a flag
interface nobody ships), and the `scripts` job is out of `ci.yml` accordingly.

Two things mine did that main's does not, recorded rather than grafted on
unilaterally:

- it keyed "untested bytes" to the gate run's `SHA256SUMS` **plus a freshness
  check** — an artifact newer than the sums file was rebuilt after the gates ran
  and is refused — where main's keys it to the presence of a `.sig`
- it needed only `curl` and `python3`; main's requires `gh`, which the
  Windows/WSL publishing box does not have

Either is a small follow-up against main's script if wanted. Neither is worth
reopening a merged decision without your say.

## All four release workflows, brought forward rather than copied

easynode could not cut its own release; the workflows lived only in the private
monorepo. **A verbatim copy would have been worse than nothing:**

- Both Linux workflows were from the v0.33.2 era with **zero CUDA references**.
  Since the MatMul v4.7 fork, validation is exactly what needs the GPU, so an
  engine built that way can never advertise `NODE_MATMUL_CONSENSUS` — it syncs,
  holds peers, reports itself healthy and silently does not validate.
- Both installers pinned their engine to specific Actions **run ids that exist
  only in the private repo**, which resolve to nothing here.

So `btxd-linux.yml` is rewritten against the procedure that actually built
0.6.15–0.6.17, with the recipe's cmake invocation copied line for line: CUDA 13.3
(12.6 segfaults on the tree), architectures `75;86;89;120`, ubuntu-22.04 for
glibc 2.35 because the ELF must run on strangers' distros. It reads
`NODE_RELEASE_TAG` through `engine-pin.sh`, so CI cannot drift from what the app
provisions.

It also gained the gate that was missing: after building it asks `cuobjdump`
which architectures are in the ELF and fails if any requested one is absent. The
installer re-checks the same thing on the staged package.

Every `PROVEN_*` pin is cleared with the bootstrap written out, including a stale
Windows engine tag (`v0.33.3-pr105b`) that the app on v0.34.5 would refuse.

⚠ **These have never cut a shipped release.** GitHub Actions cannot be run
locally. The recipe's new "Cutting a release from CI" section says so, gives the
bootstrap order, and states that the hand procedure stays the authority until CI
has earned the job.

## What a node does for the other nodes

The roles table listed what each role "gives BTX", but nothing explained that
nodes **cooperate** — that a witness produces signed evidence other people's
nodes consume, and that nodes which cannot do the MatMul maths follow those
signatures instead. A reader could finish the README without meeting the entire
argument for running one.

Measured, on one home RTX 3060 holding the tip:

```
stored attestations    3,023
blocks with quorum     3,008
signed frontier        at the tip, 0 blocks behind
```

And the scarcity, from a node with 19 peers: 12 advertised `NETWORK`, exactly
**one** was archival *and* current. Ten of the twelve were older versions
faithfully archiving a chain nobody is on any more.

The README also now states plainly that this is open source, what was opened,
and why — software that asks people to help decide which chain is real has no
business being unauditable.

## Three new docs, all measurements

- **`docs/archival-capacity.md`** — the peer count above, and the disk
  question. It continues what #14 landed rather than answering it. The
  "26.7 GB pruned chain" figure was measuring the wrong directory: the live
  chain is 284 MB of blocks, and the 26 GB is a stale `blocks.preadopt` backup
  nothing reads. It also records that **the repo disagrees with itself** on the
  full-chain size — `setup.rs` says ~105 GB, `datadir.rs` says ~50 GB — and that
  `DISK_REQUIRED_FRESH` refuses a fresh install below **120 GB** on the larger
  figure. If the true number is nearer 50, the app is turning away home machines
  that could run a node. That wants one completed unpruned sync to settle, and
  the doc says so rather than guessing.
- **`docs/appimage-size.md`** — a negative result, published so nobody repeats
  it. The 445 MB download is 75% `libcublasLt`; our own kernels across all five
  architectures are under 2% of it. `nvprune` refuses linked shared libraries
  outright, and the static route keeps sm_80 beside sm_86 and saves ~48 MB via
  an upstream build change. The per-architecture split does not pay.
- **`docs/gpu-qualification-rtx3060.md`** — the full transcript, including the
  part that does not flatter us: the card is admitted by
  `admission=self_qualification` with `outcome=missing_golden`, because the
  sealed manifest has no `cuda/sm_86` row. Every non-sm_120 CUDA machine on the
  network is in that position.

## Verification

```
btx-core          270 passed, 0 failed      (268 before; +2 for the prune fix)
web

**มันคือ hold ที่มีความจำ** ไม่ใช่ปลายทางธรรมดา — นี่คือเหตุผลที่ alias ไป `In Stock` ไม่ได้: `prev_status` อาจเป็น `Ready To Sell` ก็ได้ ถ้า alias ความต่างนั้นหายตั้งแต่ตอนอ่าน (และเทสเดิมบังคับอยู่แล้วว่าทุก key ใน `LEGACY_ALIAS` ต้องแปลงเป็นค่าอื่น — `Reserved` จึงเข้า alias ไม่ได้โดยโครงสร้าง)

หน้า `/inventory` มีช่อง Manual Status Override ที่เลือกค่านี้ได้ด้วย แต่บล็อกไว้เมื่อเครื่องมี `lot_id` — สองทางเขียนคนละความหมาย

## ผลของการอยู่นอก enum

`normalizeStatus` คืน `null` → engine ตอบ `unreadable_status` **ก่อนถึง from-list** → งานที่ถูกล็อตจองไว้ยิง transition ไม่ได้เลยสักตัว

## การเปลี่ยนพฤติกรรมหนึ่งข้อ ที่ไม่มีเทสไหนจับ

`jobListPhaseOf('Reserved')` เดิมคืน `null` **เพราะอ่านไม่ออก ไม่ใช่เพราะตั้งใจ** — เครื่องที่ล็อตจองไว้จึงไม่อยู่ในแท็บไหนเลย โผล่เฉพาะ "ทั้งหมด" ทั้งที่พี่น้องของมัน (In Stock / Sold) นั่งอยู่ในแท็บปิดงาน

พอเข้า enum แล้วได้ `PHASE.INVENTORY` เหมือนกัน → ตกแท็บปิดงานด้วย **ซึ่งคือผลที่ถูก**

รูปเดียวกับบั๊ก P3-a เป๊ะ (สถานะ B2B เข้า enum แล้วไหลเข้าแท็บ "เปิดงาน" ของ B2C) ต่างกันที่รอบนั้น**เทสเดิมจับได้ รอบนี้ไม่มีเทสไหนจับ** จึงเขียนเทสตรึงไว้ พร้อมข้อที่ยืนยันว่ามันไม่ใช่ terminal และไม่จาง (ปลดกลับมาขายได้)

## tripwire สองตัวจาก P0-b แดงตามที่ออกแบบ — เขียนใหม่ทั้งคู่ ไม่ได้ลบ

`statusWriterCensus.test.ts` และ `functions/test/legacy-status-readable.test.mjs`

**ตัวที่สองผมพลาดไปหนึ่งรอบ และต้องบอกไว้:** มันแดงบน tree สะอาดตั้งแต่ก่อนเริ่ม injection เพราะผมรัน vitest อย่างเดียวแล้วสรุปว่า "มีแค่ tripwire เดียวที่แดง" — ผล injection รอบแรกจึงปนเปื้อน (บาง suite แดงอยู่แล้ว ไม่ใช่เพราะ injection) แก้แล้วรันใหม่ทั้งชุด ตัวเลขข้างล่างมาจากรอบที่สะอาด

## สิ่งที่ยังไม่ย้าย — และเหตุผลเปลี่ยนไปแล้ว

`handleSavePricing` เคยติดที่ enum **ตอนนี้ไม่ใช่แล้ว** แต่ช่องนั้นชื่อ "Manual Status Override" ให้แอดมินกระโดดไปสถานะไหนก็ได้ใน 3 ค่า ซึ่งเป็น**รูป "ไคลเอนต์เลือกปลายทางเอง" ที่งานทั้งชุดนี้กำจัด**

การย้ายโดยไม่ตัดสินใจก่อนว่าช่องนี้ควรมีอยู่ไหม = สร้าง event ที่รับปลายทางจากไคลเอนต์ ซึ่งแย่กว่าปล่อยให้เขียนตรงแล้วนับไว้ในสำมะโน — เขียนเหตุผลใหม่ไว้ในเทสแทนของเดิมแล้ว

---

injection **4 ตัวแดงครบ**: ถอด `RESERVED` ออกจาก enum · จัดให้เป็น terminal · กัน Reserved ออกจากแท็บลิสต์แบบเดียวกับ B2B · แก้ TS แล้วลืม regenerate vocab

author: matthewhammer
body:
An experimental integration between Hazel and **Fumola**, a language whose execution model uses Adapton / demanded computation graphs, so that editing and re-running a program can reuse prior computation rather than starting over.

**Try it:** `hazel.org/build/fumola-livelit-mvp`, or `make && make serve`. No setup — the Fumola runtime is fetched from its published build. Type `^fumola_thunk` or `^fumola_editor` then space.

**Depends on** [Adapton/fumola#45](https://github.com/Adapton/fumola/pull/45) and [#46](https://github.com/Adapton/fumola/pull/46), both merged. Nothing binary is tracked here.

# Purpose of the MVP

Hazel and Fumola are each exploring live, responsive evaluation, and each relates itself to spreadsheets. Hazel's livelits are one such semantics; Fumola's demanded computation graph, where editing a program repairs prior computation rather than redoing it, is another.

This branch puts the second one *inside* the first: a Fumola runtime becomes something a Hazel program can hold and name, so two live evaluation models sit in one document, side by side, where they can be compared and composed.

Two livelits are the ways of reaching across. A **thunk** livelit holds a program whose value you are editing: it is wrapped in a named thunk, so re-forcing that name on each edit is what lets Fumola repair rather than recompute. An **editor** livelit holds a program run at the top level, for setting things up and for the operations a thunk cannot host — writing cells that thunks will read, making bindings that outlive the program, and reaching Adapton's own introspection.

**Instance ids are what keep Fumolas apart.** An id names a runtime, so a document can hold several independent ones, and livelits sharing an id share a store, a set of bindings and a demanded computation graph. Isolation and communication are both just a question of which id you write.

That framing is what makes the rest of this interesting. Every livelit shipped today is self-contained: `^slider`'s model *is* its value. These are the first whose model holds a **name for state that lives outside Hazel**, so the interesting question is not the widget but what it means for a Hazel value to denote something a foreign runtime owns.

A livelit's model names an entry of an external store

```text
Σ : FumolaInstanceId -> FumolaRuntimeState
```

held by the Fumola wasm module and reached through the `window.fumola` shim. The Fumola interpreter and its demanded computation graph are deliberately *not* serialized into the model; only the name is. Three consequences, each implemented explicitly rather than inherited:

- **Editing preserves the name**, so an edit re-evaluates against the same live runtime and state written in one edit is there in the next.
- **Expansion is an observation of Σ**, never a second source of truth in the model.
- **The runtime does the work.** There is no repair API in Fumola and none was needed: a thunk livelit wraps its program as ``force(`name := thunk { ... })``, and re-assigning that name and forcing it again is what makes the edit incremental. `:=` and `thunk` do the rest.

## Two livelits and a value

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `^fumola_thunk(instance, name, program)` | wraps its program in a named thunk; incremental across edits |
| `^fumola_editor(instance, program)` | evaluates at the top level; no reuse, but bindings outlive it |
| `FumolaPeek` | not a livelit — what a returned *pointer* becomes |

`^fumola_editor` is strictly more expressive: you can write the ``force(... := thunk { ... })`` yourself. What the thunk livelit adds is generating that wrapper with a distinct name. The editor is also the only way to reach what the wrapper forbids — `Adapton.reset()` clears the store the enclosing force is still inside, and `Adapton.peekForce` asserts there.

The **thunk name** is Fumola source for a symbol, parsed by Fumola itself, so ``​`myThunk``, `7` and ``​`a(`b)`` all work and Hazel needs to know about none of them. It is written rather than derived on purpose: a name taken from a Hazel id would start a *new* thunk whenever that id changed, quietly losing the history the thunk exists to keep.

Both name an instance, so **two livelits carrying the same id share one runtime**.

# Simple programs to try

Both livelits require an annotation — they only expand in checking mode, since the result's shape depends on the program.

**State surviving an edit.** Run this, then edit the program to just `get(1)`; it still reads `2`.

```
let n : Int = ^fumola_thunk(0, "`a", "1 := 2; get(1)") in n
```

**The worked example**, also in Documentation → Livelits → builtins. Three livelits over one runtime:

```
let x  : Int = ^fumola_thunk(0, "`t", "`x := 137 + 137; 137") in
let x_ : Int = ^fumola_editor(0, "pointer(`x)") in
let y  : Int = ^fumola_editor(0, "force(pointer(`t))") in
(x, x_, y)                    ->  (137, peek(`x)! = 274, 137)
```

The thunk writes a cell and returns 137. The first editor asks for a pointer to that cell, which arrives as a peek value showing **both the reference and what it holds**, typing as `Int` so the ascription is satisfied and evaluation continues through it. The second editor forces the thunk the *first livelit* made, by its name ``​`t`` — which is why explicit thunk names matter.

**Values that cross the boundary**, each verified against the runtime:

```
1 + 2                       ->  3
`counter := 41; get(`counter) + 1
                            ->  42
(1 := 10, 2 := 20)          ->  a pair of peek values
{x = 1; y = true}           ->  a Hazel record
peek(1)                     ->  Some(10)
peek(404)                   ->  None
`hello                      ->  "hello"
Gcd.gcd(12, 18)             ->  6     (module library, no import)
```

**Things needing `^fumola_editor`**, since they cannot run inside a thunk:

```
Adapton.reset()             ->  ()
Adapton.peekEvents()        ->  a list of records carrying events, spaces and times
```

**Always in scope:** `pointer(s)`, `get(s)`, `peek(s)`. They exist because Hazel string literals admit no escapes — `Token.is_string` permits at most two quote characters in a token — so a livelit's program can never contain a `"`, and every adapton primitive needs one. Note that `:=` coerces its left side into a pointer but `@` does not, so a cell is read back with `get(s)`.

**The module library is compiled into the runtime** and bound at the top level: `Adapton`, `List`, `LazyList`, `PureList`, `LevelTree`, `HashMap`, `Counters`, `RandomInput`, `MergeSort`, `Gcd`, `DelayedPut`. Anything else is reachable by path.

# Future work to explore

**Expansions are not typed.** Statics splices a livelit's expansion in as an already-elaborated term and never traverses it ([Statics.re](src/language/statics/Statics.re)). Three things follow: a livelit nested in an expansion is never expanded, so `FumolaPeek` cannot render as a widget; constructors inside an expansion are never resolved; and no annotation anywhere in the program can reach inside one. This branch works around it with type-directed expansion, but making expansions real syntax is the change that would dissolve several problems at once.

**Sum types across the boundary.** Fumola tags are structural and live in one flat namespace: `#Bar(3)` is a value whether or not anyone declared `Bar`. Hazel constructors are declaration-bound. So the boundary is lossy in the direction that matters — Fumola hands you a tag, Hazel needs a tag *plus* a home type. Expansion now resolves tags against the expected type, but round-tripping Hazel → Fumola → Hazel can still land in a different sum type.

**`Space` and `Time` both declare a `Symbol` constructor.** With an expected type it resolves correctly; without one it falls back to a context lookup that could pick either.

**Generative copy is not implemented.** A copied livelit inherits its original's instance id and shares its execution history. Doing it properly needs a projector identity that survives

author: jateeter
body:
Three accessor modules, all deleted:

    visualizer/frontend/src/lib/corpusEventKeys.ts        6 consumers
    perception-engine/backend/src/corpusEventKeys.ts      server.ts + its test
    perception-engine/frontend/src/types.ts               AddSourceModal

Fourteen call sites in the visualizer become direct canonical reads —
`seq.events ?? []`, `v.outputEvents?.length ?? 0`, `v.nextEventIds ?? []` — and
`VectorNode` now declares `outputEvents` alone.

The PE's `bootstrapSourcesFromMachines` reads `seq?.events ?? []`. That read is
the one this whole layering was sequenced around: against a corpus it could not
parse it created **0 sources instead of 1328** and logged
`created=0 skipped=1328 errors=0`. It now has one spelling to get right.

The backend accessor's five tests go with it. They pinned a fallback that no
longer exists, and keeping them would assert that the legacy spelling still
resolves — which after this commit it must not. 299 tests pass, from 304.

## What this changes about failure

Until now a reader looking for the wrong key got an empty array and reported
success. From here, `undefined` propagates: an empty graph, an empty source, a
`.length` on undefined. Louder, and in the frontend often immediately visible.
That is the trade this layer is making, deliberately.

## Verified

visualizer `tsc && vite build` clean; PE backend build clean with 299 tests;
PE frontend build clean.

Corpus-load counts across all four runtimes, unchanged from the tolerant
baseline:

    cpp     1328 machines / 5077 sequences / 9546 events
    scala   1328 / 5077 / 9546
    lsp     1328 / 5077 / 9546
    ts-pe   1328 sources / 10688 input rows

author: chekol1
body:
Adds local-deploy/: a self-contained installer for running the full stack on a single Linux VM against Floci. Clone, run install-prereqs.sh, run deploy.sh.

  local-deploy/install-prereqs.sh  docker, terraform, aws cli, gettext (idempotent)
  local-deploy/deploy.sh           9-step orchestrator, idempotent (~60s re-run)
  local-deploy/teardown.sh         stop everything; --all drops caches
  local-deploy/fetch-models.sh     download spleeter models once into .cache/
  local-deploy/floci-compose.yml   self-contained Floci stack
  local-deploy/k8s/*.tmpl          manifests templated via envsubst

Nothing is hardcoded: the host LAN IP, the Floci/registry/k3s container IPs, the RDS host and port, the NodePort and the queue URL are all detected at deploy time, because they differ per machine and change between rebuilds. Images are keyed by a hash of their build context so a source change forces a rebuild.

Terraform changes for Floci:
  - floci_override.tf points 9 services at the emulator. It is a _override.tf file, so main.tf's provider block is untouched.
  - inspector.tf removed: Floci has no inspector2 (UnknownOperationException).
  - github_oidc.tf: the four EKS access-entry resources removed. Floci does not route those APIs; requests fall through to its S3 handler.
  - eks.tf: access_config removed. Floci never persists authentication_mode, so terraform saw permanent drift and every re-apply attempted UpdateClusterConfig, which Floci cannot serve. This made the installer non-re-runnable.

App fixes (real bugs, applied here only; eks-showcase is untouched):
  - api/app.py: DB_PORT is now configurable. It was pinned to 5432, so the app could not reach a Postgres on any other port. Defaults to 5432.
  - api/app.py: init_db() no longer runs at import. It did, so gunicorn's import crashed the container whenever the DB was not yet reachable and the pod CrashLoopBackOff'd -- the retry loop inside init_db never got a chance. /api/health no longer depends on the DB.
  - web/nginx.conf -> nginx.conf.template: nginx resolved its upstream once at startup and exited with 'host not found in upstream "api-service"' if CoreDNS was not ready. Now resolved per-request via a resolver plus a variable. The upstream is an env var because nginx's resolver ignores the search domains in /etc/resolv.conf and needs an FQDN under Kubernetes.

Verified end to end: 46 resources applied, all pods Running, browser-path upload through the LoadBalancer with a CORS preflight, real Spleeter separation producing genuine 44.1kHz stereo stems, and no model re-download.

Floci emulates AWS APIs only. IAM is not enforced, the node group is a mock with no real instances, VPC/security groups are inert, and EFS is a stub. See local-deploy/README.md for the full list.

body: `npm test` on Windows (PowerShell) failed 5 tests: all three CLI cases (`status` was `null`) and both eval cases (`testsPassed` was `false`). **Cause:** `spawnSync("npx")` and `spawnSync("npm")` cannot run `.cmd` shims on Windows without a shell. uv_spawn returns `status: null` (ENOENT-style), so the CLI assertions fail and eval treats the fixture suite as not passing. **Fix:** - `src/run-command.ts` — `spawnSync` with `shell: true` on Windows - `eval` uses that helper for `npm test` - CLI tests spawn `node` + `tsx` from `node_modules` with `shell: false`, so OneDrive / `Program Files` paths stay on argv macOS/Linux behavior is unchanged. Re-run `npm test` in that PowerShell clone after this lands. I cannot run Windows here; Linux suite is run after this PR is opened.

author: phahadek
body:
## Summary
Rewrites 9 backend test files' fixed absolute-millisecond latency assertions (index-lookup speed, off-main-thread dispatch, fire-and-forget timing, timeout bounds, concurrency vs. serial execution) into relative-ordering, self-calibrated-baseline, or widened-margin checks so they can't fail purely from host scheduling jitter, while still catching the original regressions.

## Notion Task
https://app.notion.com/p/Replace-the-backend-suite-s-wall-clock-latency-assertions-with-checks-that-do-not-fail-on-host-jitte-3d022f9152f381d5b273cc514a0d1776

## Automated Tests
- Rewrote assertions in place (no new test files) in the 9 listed files. Each rewritten assertion still targets its original regression:
  - `hasActiveSessionForTaskIndex.test.ts`: compares indexed lookup time against an unindexed-scan baseline measured on the same host (relative ratio) instead of an absolute ms bound.
  - `walTruncateCheckpointOffMainThread.test.ts` / `flakyTestRollupOffMainThread.test.ts`: drop the absolute "<delayMs*fraction" bound, keep/add the pure ordering check (timer fires before the worker's blocking delay completes).
  - `AutoLauncher.test.ts`: replaced the `<1000ms` poll-cycle bound with a promise-resolution-ordering check (pollOnce resolves before a gated "bootstrap" promise settles).
  - `PRReviewService.verdictTimeout.test.ts`: widened the bound to stay well under vitest's own per-test timeout backstop, with a comment explaining why.
  - `WorktreeReconciler.test.ts`: measures a serial (cap=1) baseline and a concurrent (cap=4) run back-to-back in the same test and compares them relatively.
  - `stagedIntents.groupCommit.test.ts`: replaced total-elapsed-time bound with a check on the spread between each member's call-start timestamps (concurrent dispatch vs. sequential).
  - `planningCandidateQueriesIndex.test.ts`: widened the already-generous absolute bound further with an explanatory comment (lowest priority per task spec).
  - `Scheduler.eventLoopBlocking.test.ts`: widened the two real-event-loop-blocking upper-bound multipliers further with comments explaining the remaining real-timer dependency (this file measures genuine event-loop blocking, which has no fake-timer equivalent).
- Files listed as out-of-scope in the task spec were left untouched.

## Files Changed
- `packages/backend/src/db/__tests__/hasActiveSessionForTaskIndex.test.ts` — relative indexed-vs-scan comparison
- `packages/backend/src/db/__tests__/walTruncateCheckpointOffMainThread.test.ts` — dropped absolute timer bound, kept ordering check
- `packages/backend/src/db/__tests__/flakyTestRollupOffMainThread.test.ts` — added ordering check (timer vs. worker), dropped absolute bound
- `packages/backend/src/orchestration/__tests__/AutoLauncher.test.ts` — replaced elapsed-time bound with promise-ordering check
- `packages/backend/src/__tests__/PRReviewService.verdictTimeout.test.ts` — widened bound with explanatory comment
- `packages/backend/src/__tests__/WorktreeReconciler.test.ts` — self-calibrated serial-vs-concurrent baseline comparison
- `packages/backend/src/routes/__tests__/stagedIntents.groupCommit.test.ts` — call-start-time spread check instead of total elapsed time
- `packages/backend/src/db/__tests__/planningCandidateQueriesIndex.test.ts` — widened absolute bound (x3)
- `packages/backend/src/__tests__/Scheduler.eventLoopBlocking.test.ts` — widened real-timer upper-bound multipliers with comments

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent ncurses from redrawing tig while a foreground external command (like `nvim`) is suspended and resumed, which left the terminal screen in a corrupted/unclean state after exiting the editor and tig.

### Description

- In `open_external_viewer` (in `src/display.c`) temporarily set `SIGTSTP` to `SIG_DFL` before running a foreground command so the child/foreground process receives the standard suspend handler.
- Restore the previous `SIGTSTP` handler after the foreground command completes (only if the previous handler was valid) to preserve tig's normal suspension behaviour.
- Added a short explanatory comment and a local `void (*sig_tstp)(int)` variable to hold and restore the previous handler.

body:
## Summary

- Implements the issue owner's decision that only observed runtime evidence (`detected`) may score a runtime-capability question. The decision, its structural cost, and the accepted rationale are recorded in the [#558 owner comment](https://github.com/MongLong0214/agent-operator-score/issues/558#issuecomment-5543551699).
- Keeps an adapter-table record visible as `aos-known`, but reports it truthfully as an unmeasured runtime: `unmeasured-owner` is distinct from `unknown-owner` throughout the capability, minimality, and delegation paths.
- Makes the operator posture visible in all four READMEs and in `aos report`. A report now identifies `aos-known` as the withholding source and tells the operator to run `aos assess --probe-capabilities`.
- Bumps the ECD contract to 1.4.0 and records both canonical and file-byte digest transitions.

## Default `aos assess` posture

This is a product-wide consequence, not an artifact of an unattended fixture. Without `--probe-capabilities`, `aos-known` stays in the record but cannot answer runtime capability:

| Surface | Default posture |
| --- | --- |
| `capability-matches-task` | `null` |
| `simplest-adequate-route` | `null` (`NO_SCORABLE_OWNER`) |
| C2.RF.01 | one answered opportunity of three; `INSUFFICIENT_OPPORTUNITIES` |
| O4 / outcome index / composite | withheld |

`aos assess --probe-capabilities` observes the runtime and writes `detected` evidence, returning these questions to the existing scoring path.

## E1.4a · Tests de caracterización del matcheo actual

**Solo tests · no se toca código de producción.** Es la red de seguridad de E1.4b, que va a dar a las rutas del matcheo una entrada por LÍNEA (`lineasExtracto`) y tendrá que demostrar que con el mismo lote sale el mismo resultado.

**PR sin mergear** · el preflight (mapa de lo que cubrían los 13 y lo que se añade) va en el primer comentario.

### Qué se añade
`src/services/__tests__/caracterizacionMatcheo.test.ts` · 28 tests · un **lote de agosto de 19 líneas conocidas** que pasa por las cuatro rutas, fijando la salida EXACTA de hoy (score y reasons, via/confidence/action/metadata, orígenes y atribuciones, qué funde y qué borra).

### El contrato que E1.4b tendrá que mantener idéntico
| Ruta | Fichero:línea | Qué queda fijado |
|---|---|---|
| `matchBatch` | `movementMatchingService.ts:80-106` | el `MatchResult` completo del lote (5 cuadres con `score`/`reasons` exactos, 0 multiMatch, 14 sinMatch en orden de entrada) · reparto de dos rentas iguales · multiMatch sin nombre (75/75) · agua a 7 días y el mismo día → sinMatch · pago múltiple → sinMatch · duplicado intra-lote → gana el id menor · previsto descartado excluido · id inexistente desaparece · alias aprendido (+25) |
| `suggestForUnmatched` | `movementSuggestionService.ts:79-89` | el mapa completo de las 14 sin match (6 heurísticas, regla aprendida a 74 con cortocircuito, compromiso a 90 con cortocircuito, el signo tirando una regla PERSONAL sobre un abono, «no sé qué es» a 30) · Bizum con contrato vivo → `assign_to_contract` · solo nombre de pila → pregunta abierta · regla sin aplicaciones → 50 + heurística · «CUOTA PRESTAMO» → 65 · id inexistente no aparece |
| `reconocerDeterministas` | `deterministas/matcheoDeterminista.ts:39` | cuota (con desglose), venta, rendimiento (con desglose) y nómina, en ese orden de fuentes · atribución IBI por un solo piso · comunidad declarada por dos → no se atribuye · un origen tapa la atribución · una fuente rota no tumba a las demás (y atribuciones en orden de líneas) · empate de dos préstamos → sin origen · lista vacía → no lee la base |
| Conciliación con confirmados | `conciliacionConfirmados.ts:139-145` + `reconciliarConfirmado.ts:45-140` (vía `confirmDecisions`) | `confirmadosPorLinea` 1:1 por cercanía y luego id menor · solo lo manual, ni import ni tarjeta ni otra cuenta · ventana de 5 días · al guardar: la línea del import hereda categoría/ámbito/inmueble/`descripcionPrevision` y sube a `conciliado`/`match_automatico`, el texto del banco no se toca, el confirmado se borra, el previsto punteado y la línea de gasto se repuntan con el dato del banco, el duplicado ignorado no se borra, un confirmado inexistente no impide subir |

- **HOY:** la luz por 108,44 € **cuadra** con un previsto de 45 € (fecha + cuenta + recibo recurrente + proveedor = 80 ≥ 70): sin ningún punto por importe. Es la regla del «recibo variable» llevada al extremo.

author: kensac
body:
## Objective

`data_health` records the alerts it finds, instead of crashing on exactly the findings that matter.

## Reason

`data_health` has failed 11 times between 2026-09-03 13:13 and 2026-09-04 16:00 with `Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable`, succeeding in between. `health_alerts` has had no row written since 2026-09-01.

The intermittency is the bug, not noise around it. A detector builds `detail` from `dict(row)`, so an empty result carries nothing serialisable-unfriendly and a real finding carries a `Decimal` rate. The task passed whenever it had nothing to say and crashed whenever it had something.

`db.jsonb()` was a bare `Jsonb(value)`, and it is the single funnel for every jsonb write in the app — 18 call sites across 10 modules. All of them carried the same latent failure against any `Decimal` or `datetime` that SQL hands back; the detectors just reach it first because `dict(row)` is their whole payload.

## Requirements

- `jsonb()` serialises `Decimal` and `datetime` rather than raising.
- Fixed at the funnel, not at the twelve `"detail": dict(r)` call sites.

## Passing criteria

`detect()` against production returns one finding right now (`batch_failed_whole`). Before this change `json.dumps` on its detail raises; after it, it serialises. Verified by dry-running `detect()` against production read-only:

```
detectors returned 1 findings
  OLD dumps fails: batch_failed_whole | Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable
would fail under old dumps: 1 of 1
all serialize cleanly with the fix
```

`tests/test_db_jsonb.py` covers Decimal, datetime, a detector-shaped row, and that plain values still pass through.

## Notes

`Decimal` becomes a number rather than a string so `/admin/health` can still compare it. The authoritative money values live in numeric columns, not in a jsonb detail blob.

## Not verified

The full suite was not run here — it needs a pgvector test database. The new test runs standalone and passes; CI covers the rest.

author: mpowell95
body:
Matt filmed the reference's meter and ours side by side. Both clips were measured **frame by frame at 60 fps** — 201 and 203 frames, tracking the needle's angle and the accuracy bar's marker in every single frame.

```
frames   0-33    the needle is parked DEAD CENTRE IN THE ACCURACY BAR (89-90 deg)
frames  33-127   it climbs the arc at 2.22 deg/frame - the backswing
frame  127       A MARKER IS PLANTED AT 297 deg AND STAYS THERE, and the needle REVERSES
frames 130-188   it runs back down at 3.24 deg/frame - 1.46x faster
frames 188-201   it STOPS at 96 deg and holds: a small miss, right of centre
```

And the clincher: **the accuracy bar's marker position is a linear function of the needle's angle**, same slope (−0.0175 per degree) on the way up and on the way down. The bar is not a second meter. **It is the same needle**, and the bar is a magnified view of the last ~12% of arc either side of zero — which is why it has to sit in the ring's mouth. It's the same scale, unrolled.

So the reference is the classic three-click swing, and ours now is too:

| tap | what it does |
|---|---|
| 1 | start the backswing |
| 2 | set **power** — a marker is planted where you stopped it, and the needle reverses |
| 3 | set **accuracy** — stop the needle as near zero as you can on the way back down |

Everything is on **one scale**, `pos`, in power units: `0` is the accuracy point, `1` is 100%, `SWING_MAX` (1.12) is the top of the over-swing block, `±BAR_HALF` (0.12) is the window the bar magnifies. The needle is drawn at `ang(pos)` and lands inside the bar or on the band from the same expression — no special case, no discontinuity.

## Measured against measured

| | reference | old build | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| backswing 0 → 100% | 1.56 s | 0.75 s | **1.65 s** |
| downswing 100% → 0 | 1.07 s | 0.75 s | **1.15 s** |
| downswing vs backswing | 1.46× faster | identical | **1.43× faster** |
| over-swing zone | +11.7% | +10% | **+12%** |
| accuracy green band | 54% of the bar | 40% | **54%** |

**Holding past the top is no longer a free extra lap.** The power is spent at `SWING_MAX` and the needle is already coming back down, so the next tap is the *accuracy* tap. And if the needle runs off the bottom of the bar with no third tap, the shot fires at the worst accuracy the bar can express — a swing that hangs waiting for a tap the player already failed to make is worse than a bad shot.

**Putting got easier.** The tap window is now the backswing's own rate, and the backswing is more than twice as slow as the old ring: 2.2 ft went from 7.5 frames of tolerance to **16.5**, and 40 ft from 3.2 to **7.1**.

## The look, measured rather than eyeballed

- band thickness / outer radius **0.345** (measured 51/148 by radial cross-section)
- zero at 90°, 100% at 311°, block 311–337°
- **outline is BLACK OUTSIDE WHITE on both edges** — ours had no black, and that key is most of why the original stays crisp over grass
- the band is genuinely **see-through** (`#616736` over fairway, `#474d32` over a dark patch). It has to be punched through its own white rim with `destination-out` first, or it lands on 255 and comes out light grey — which is exactly what my first attempt looked like
- the green stripe is at **91–93%** and thin, *not* adjacent to 100%
- the bar's trapezoid corners are the band's inner and outer radii at the two ends of the window, so it really is the arc straightened out — which is why the needle in it is radial, and vertical only at dead centre
- colours sampled: green `#01da04`, red `#fd0001`, orange `#f07c03`/`#fb8f20`

### A correction

**The over-swing block does not jut outside the arc.** Measured radially at 324°, its colour runs r90–r142 — exactly the plain band's radii, with the outer white outline at 143–148 in both places. Batch 1 built ours as a fan sticking a third of a radius past the edge and this repo's docs said that was what the reference did. That was read off a downscaled contact sheet instead of a cross-section, and it was wrong.

## Tests

`golf/js/test.js` sections 7 and 8 rewritten, with `[KNOWN-BUG PROBE]`s for the two things the old build got structurally wrong: **the needle keeps moving after the power is locked**, and **the downswing is faster than the backswing**.

`test-visual.mjs`'s play probe now computes its third tap from the power rather than tapping immediately — which under the new mechanic would fire at maximum miss.

Verified: golf engine tests all pass · `test-visual.mjs golf` **14/14** including the play probe (tee shot plus holed putt) · conventions 11/11 · i18n 0 failures · sw-strategy 82/82. Rendered at 393×852 dpr3 at address, mid-backswing, mid-downswing and from a trees lie, and checked against the reference frames.

author: tjirsch
body:
Phase 2. A pack declares its params and its claims; it can now declare **what a human must be asked** before those params can be filled, and what getting the answer wrong costs. Metadata: a question emits nothing, never enters the fold, never reaches the emission manifest.

### Two costs, because conflating them is the mistake the design exists to avoid

`reversal` is what changing the answer does to the **estate** (`edit` | `state_surgery` | `recreate`). `blast` is what it does to the **running organisation** (`none` | `low` | `high`). They are orthogonal — enforcing OS Login is one boolean to reverse and cuts every existing SSH path. An answer is only safely deferred when both are low.

`why` is required exactly where satz will refuse or warn, so it can quote the pack's own sentence rather than a generic one — the rule that already makes `reason` mandatory on a deviation.

### Three deliberate departures from `docs/interview-design.md`

- **A question must live in the file that declares its param**, checked at parse time. Questions are absorbed *after* the `use … when` guard, like claims — so a question that *gates* a pack would be invisible until the answer was already yes. The repo avoided this by accident (`cis_require_shielded_vm` is declared in the CIS pack, not the extension it gates); now the accident is the rule and the chicken-and-egg is unrepresentable.
- **`defer_to` becomes `recommend`.** The sketch's version was a second default channel. `recommend` is what an interview offers; the `params` default is what applies when nobody asked.
- **`question oneof` for exclusive choices**, which the sketch does not cover. Options name *existing boolean params*, so an answer set stays a plain param map — and satz gains a check it could not make before:

```
Error: group_model: Which security-group model does this customer run? — but
group_model_flat and group_model_split are both true. Exactly one branch of this
choice may be set.
```

Today that same mistake surfaces as an opaque fold conflict on whatever address the branches happen to share. This is a user-visible win with **no interview built at all**, which is what makes the phase shippable on its own.

### The canonical-form decision — the one flagged as quietly load-bearing

Questions are a **third product**, `canonical_questions`, beside params and body.

- In `canonical.body`, a prompt typo would auto-fork every estate using the pack and report it as "N resource line(s) differ" — a lie.
- Out of everything, a `reversal: recreate → edit` downgrade would ship silently, and that is a governance fact.

So `check-presets` grows a verdict that is loud and never forks. Verified against a real library:

```
  questions [included]: essential-contacts-organization.satz — v1.2 — 1 question(s), wording or costs differ
    the pack emits the same HCL, so this is not drift to adopt or fork —
    but what a customer is ASKED, or what an answer costs, has changed.
```

Reported, counted clean, exit 0.

### The new-statement checklist, including the two items that fail silently

`canonical_parts` (via the separate product above) and `NEVER_A_TYPE_KEY` in `migrate.rs` — without which `satz import x.yaml` rewrites the keyword into `google_question`. The parse arm sits **before** the generic `IDENT IDENT "{"` arm, which also closes a footgun: `question foo { … }` used to parse as a resource map and fail later in the walk with an error about a type nobody wrote.

### Where they surface

`satz questions <estate>` (offline and schema-free — an interview happens before anyone runs `update-schema`), a **Questions** section per pack in `doc-packs`, and the prompt as the `description` of the generated `variables.tf` variable, which nothing else in the pipeline had a sentence for.

**Zero churn**, as the plan predicted: corpus snapshots are `main.tf` + tfvars only.

The showcase gains a question, a one-way door and a `oneof`; smoke asserts the command, the JSON, the emitted description, that a question reaches `main.tf` **not at all**, and that two true branches are refused naming both.

author: aibeshkov
body:
## Summary

Closes GAP-1 from `docs/product-claim-gaps-2026-09-02.md` — the decision (Option 1: fleet mode cleans up, not a restated claim).

- `dsd fleet --bin` now removes the uploaded binary via a **fresh SSH connection**, after every run: success, WARN/CRIT, or a failed/timed-out remote command. Uses the caller's outer `ctx`, not the per-host `RunTimeout` context — a wedged remote command that already exhausted its deadline must not also poison the cleanup attempt.
- Cleanup failure never masks the health verdict, but is reported: `Result.CleanupError` / `"cleanup_error"` in `--json`. Never silently swallowed.
- `docs/fleet-design.md` updated with the new step and the honesty note.

## Verified two ways — not a unit test over a command string

**1. `scripts/check-fleet-cleanup.sh`** (new, wired into `ci.yml`'s `fleet-cleanup-invariant` job): spins up a real sshd container, runs a real `dsd fleet --bin` deploy over a real SSH connection through a `~/.ssh/config` Host alias (exactly how an operator points fleet at a nonstandard port — fleet deliberately has no `--port`/`--identity` flags), then `docker exec`s into the *same* container and asserts the binary is gone.

This script's own first draft was wrong, and finding that out is itself worth flagging: it faked `$HOME` to avoid touching the real `~/.ssh/config`, which seemed safe — but OpenSSH resolves its *default* config path via the passwd-database home directory (`getpwuid`), not the `$HOME` env var, specifically so an attacker-controlled `$HOME` can't redirect config/key lookups. Every run was silently failing to connect at all, and the script's own success didn't notice because a sanity-check step had `2>/dev/null` on it — the exact "PASS is not did-not-fail" trap this whole project's testing discipline exists to catch. Rewritten to back up the real `~/.ssh/config`, append one uniquely-named Host block, and restore it in the `EXIT` trap regardless of how the script exits.

**2. `internal/fleet/sshexec_test.go`** (three new tests): cleanup runs on the success path; cleanup runs even when the remote health command itself fails; a cleanup failure is reported, not swallowed. Also fixed a silent gap in the *existing* `TestRunHost_BinPathSuccess`'s fake ssh — it didn't have a case arm for the cleanup call at all, so cleanup was "failing" against an `unexpected argv` branch without the test ever noticing (nothing asserted on it). Now it does, with a marker file proving cleanup actually ran.

## The structural ask

`write_capable_callsites_test.go` (new, root package): enumerates every write-capable call site in non-test code (`os.Create`, `os.WriteFile`, `os.OpenFile` with write flags, `os.Remove*`, `os.Rename`, `os.Mkdir*`, `os.Chmod`, `os.Symlink`/`Link`) and classifies each **file** into "the operator's own output artifact" via a closed allowlist with a reason per entry. Fails if a write-capable call site exists outside `internal/fleet/` and outside the allowlist. Confirmed red by injecting a throwaway write call into an unrelated package, confirmed green after removing it.

## Ledger

Three rows in `docs/product-closures.tsv`. The primary real-run proof (the shell script) isn't a `go test` name, so it isn't ledgered — cited instead as the `fleet-cleanup-invariant` CI job.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/check-fleet-cleanup.sh` — real run against a real sshd container, confirmed the binary is uploaded, `dsd health` runs (real CRIT/WARN findings from the container's actual state — NTP unsync'd, btrfs unresized, unexpected port), and the binary is gone afterward (verified via a separate `docker exec`, not the same channel that deleted it)
- [x] `internal/fleet` full package green, including the 3 new cleanup tests
- [x] `write_capable_callsites_test.go` confirmed red (injected an unclassified write call) and green (removed it)
- [x] `./scripts/check-closures.sh --self-test` + full ledger verify green (linux container, matching CI)
- [x] `actionlint`/`shellcheck` clean
- [x] Full local test suite green (pre-commit `tests (short)`, pre-push `tests (race)` + golangci-lint + staticcheck + gosec + semgrep + govulncheck)

## Review before merging

- **Release guidance — Concern:** Checked the official protobufjs v7.6.5 GitHub release note and npm metadata. The v7.6.5 note describes the EOF options-parsing bug fix and no migration guidance; the full candidate still moves legacy consumers from protobufjs 5/6 ranges to major 7, so release compatibility remains a concern.
- **Dependency contracts — Concern:** Checked root package.json \(Yarn 1.22.22 and TypeScript 3.5.3\), workspace manifests, and final yarn.lock. author: fingolfin
body:
Add two hooks, GAP_GC_SAVE_STACK_STATE and GAP_GC_RESTORE_STACK_STATE, and call them wherever GAP sets up a setjmp for its error handling: the reader's TRY_IF_NO_ERROR, the GAP_TRY/GAP_CATCH helpers, and the libgap entry points. The state is saved before the setjmp and restored on the error path, next to the recursion depth that is already handled there.

The point of this is the Julia GC integration. The Julia GC keeps a chain of root frames on the C stack. A GAP error longjmps out of the call chain that raised it, so the frames that chain registered are never unregistered, and after the jump they point into stack that no longer exists; the next collection then walks garbage. With the hooks, the head of that chain is saved and restored like the rest of the error state, which fixes this for every error GAP catches.

GASMAN and Boehm find their roots by scanning the C stack and have nothing to record; for them the hooks compile to nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---

You may be wondering why this isn't using the existing hook system: well, that only works for `GAP_TRY`/`GAP_CATCH`, but not `TRY_IF_NO_ERROR`. One of these days, I'll think again about whether we can unify these systems. But for now, I think this doesn't add too much complexity and is required for the "precise Julia GC" work.

body:
The Clear data panel offered "everything" or "older than 30 days" — too blunt for a destructive action. It now asks two questions.

## What

A chip per kind of entry — feeds, night sleep, naps, tummy time, wet, poop, baths, weigh-ins, vitamin D, massage, exercise, notes — each carrying how many exist (`Naps · 20`). Empty kinds are shown disabled rather than hidden, so the list is stable. Select all or none in one tap.

## When

All time · Today · Older than 30 days · **Choose dates…** — a from and a to, down to the minute. The chosen "to" minute is included in full.

## The safety property

The delete button always says exactly how many entries match — **"Delete 20 entries"** — and is disabled when nothing does. Counting and deleting share one predicate, `matchEvents()` in `events.js`, so the number on the button is precisely what goes. Every deletion is still undoable from the toast.

## Verified in a browser with seeded data

- Armed with everything selected: "Delete 209 entries" (209 total).
- Naps only: "Delete 20 entries" (20 naps).
- Naps, custom range = yesterday 00:00–23:59: "Delete 2 entries" — matched an independent count.
- Deleting removed exactly 2; Undo restored all 209.
- Fixed a layout bug found on the way: the date inputs rendered ~180px tall, because a `flex: 1 1 150px` inside a column-direction label became a height. Now 38px.

3 new tests on the predicate (type union, from-inclusive/to-exclusive range, combined, no filter). 98 pass.

author: luojiyin1987
body:
## Summary

- replace the six-platform reusable workflow on pull requests/main with one local Linux x64 CI job
- keep `go test ./...` and a native `go build` as the daily correctness gate
- make the full Go compatibility matrix manual-only
- leave release builds unchanged

## Daily CI

Pull requests and pushes to `main` now run one job on `ubuntu-latest`:

```text
checkout
setup Go from go.mod
go test ./...
go build -trimpath -o cxq ./cmd/cxq
```

The checkout explicitly disables persisted credentials.

## Compatibility probe

`Go compatibility probe` now runs only through `workflow_dispatch`.

The existing 9-job matrix is intentionally retained for manual investigations of:

- minimum Go version changes
- SQLite/toolchain compatibility
- macOS ARM64 runtime behavior
- Mach-O LC_UUID diagnostics

This removes repeated compatibility evidence from every Go pull request without deleting the probe itself.

## Release

`.github/workflows/release.yml` is unchanged.

Tagged releases still use the pinned reusable workflow to build all six native targets:

- Linux x64 / ARM64
- Windows x64 / ARM64
- macOS x64 / ARM64

## Effect

Typical pull-request checks drop from:

```text
6 cross-platform jobs
+ 9 compatibility jobs
= 15 jobs
```

to:

```text
1 Linux x64 test/build job
```

Cross-platform binary validation remains attached to the release path, where those binaries are actually published.

## Scope

This PR only changes:

- `.github/workflows/cross-platform.yml`
- `.github/workflows/go-compatibility.yml`

It does not change production code, tests, release packaging, the compatibility matrix itself, or the pinned release workflow revision.

author: s7strategy
body:
Estudo de viabilidade de uma açaiteria self-service por peso na Praia da Ferrugem (Garopaba/SC), no ponto de ~35 m² fechado com pátio e deck. O equipamento pesado já está comprado — o estudo trata só do que falta decidir e gastar.

**A marca é própria.** A comparação com manter a plotagem de rede está encerrada; as seções que a discutem ficam no estudo como registro de como se chegou aqui. O que segue em aberto é de quem se compra a polpa.

## O que entra

**`ESTUDO-Acai-Ferrugem.md`** — o estudo escrito, da curva de faturamento à ficha técnica item a item e ao que pedir em cada orçamento de fornecedor.

**`analise/`** — os modelos em Python que geram cada número, mais as cópias das duas páginas publicadas:
- `curva-conservadora.py` — modelo corrente: curva do ano, DRE, sensibilidade, investimento e payback por cenário
- `preco-da-polpa.py` — o lucro do ano em função do preço do quilo da polpa, e a lista de perguntas de orçamento
- `ficha-tecnica-balcao.py` — 18 itens do balcão, custo por kg de atacado contra o preço de venda
- `curva-do-dono-e-espaco-kids.py`, `cenario-enxuto.py`, `plano-500k-e-margem-30.py`, `reconciliacao-margem-capex.py`, `modelo-acai-ferrugem.py` — modelos anteriores, mantidos para rastrear como cada premissa mudou
- `estudo-acai-ferrugem.html`, `plano-marca-propria.html` — cópias das páginas publicadas

## A curva do ano

Faturamento de **R$ 639.000**, com sazonalidade de praia:

| | Jan | Fev | Mar | Abr | Mai | Jun | Jul | Ago | Set | Out | Nov | Dez |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R$ mil | 170 | 130 | 55 | 25 | 16 | 15 | 17 | 15 | 17 | 24 | 45 | 110 |

Dezembro, janeiro e fevereiro somam R$ 410.000 — **64% do ano**. Janeiro fica em 171 clientes/dia, 49% do teto físico do ponto (350/dia com 2 balanças e 2 operadores).

## O investimento

| Item | R$ |
|---|---|
| Reforma do ponto | 8.000 |
| Frete e transporte do equipamento | 8.000 |
| Insumos iniciais | 5.000 |
| **Abrir a porta** | **21.000** |
| Embalagem personalizada | 7.000 |
| Plotagem | 6.000 |
| Decoração do local | 3.000 |
| **A nossa marca** | **16.000** |
| Espaço kids | 25.550 |
| **Total** | **62.550** |

Balcão refrigerado, freezers, vitrine, PDV e balança vieram no lote da unidade comprada e ficam fora da conta. Não há capital de giro no investimento.

Lucro de **R$ 252.097** no primeiro ano (margem de 39,5%), com o investimento voltando em **3,0 meses**. Sem o espaço kids, R$ 259.636.

## O preço da polpa é a última linha em aberto

São **539 baldes de 10 kg por ano** — 5.392 kg. Cada R$ 1,00 no quilo vale **R$ 5.392 de lucro por ano**, todo ano.

| Balde de 10 kg | R$/kg | Insumo | Lucro do ano | Payback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R$ 145 | 14,50 | 24,9% | R$ 268.272 | 2,8 m |
| R$ 155 | 15,50 | 25,7% | R$ 262.880 | 2,9 m |
| **R$ 175 (o plano)** | **17,50** | **27,4%** | **R$ 252.097** | **3,0 m** |
| R$ 195 | 19,50 | 29,1% | R$ 241.314 | 3,1 m |
| R$ 230 | 23,00 | 32,0% | R$ 222.443 | 3,4 m |
| R$ 350 (a polpa ao dobro) | 35,00 | 42,2% | R$ 157.745 | 4,8 m |

Nenhum preço realista de polpa derruba o negócio — o que ele muda é o tamanho da sobra. Doze orçamentos em andamento, nenhum recebido ainda: a página tem a tabela montada e vazia, uma linha por fornecedor, mais as 10 perguntas a fazer em cada um.

## A mecânica da margem

Tudo sai da mesma balança pelo mesmo preço por kg, mas cada item custa um preço diferente. Banana a R$ 6/kg dá 10% de CMV; castanha de caju a R$ 75/kg dá 125% — vende no prejuízo. Nutella (109%) e ovomaltine (117%) idem, a R$ 59,90/kg.

Duas alavancas controláveis:
- **Preço por kg** — de R$ 59,90 para R$ 74,90 tira 7 pontos do CMV
- **Layout do balcão** — premium em porção fechada, fora do self-service, tira mais 5 pontos

Comprando direto, o insumo fica em **27,4% da receita**, contra 31,5% comprando pronto de rede — R$ 26.199 a mais por ano, contra R$ 16.000 de custo da marca uma vez só.

## Sensibilidade

| Verão | Faturamento | Lucro | Margem | Payback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| −25% | R$ 479.250 | R$ 164.235 | 34,3% | 4,6 m |
| −15% | R$ 543.150 | R$ 199.380 | 36,7% | 3,8 m |
| conforme o plano | R$ 639.000 | R$ 252.097 | 39,5% | 3,0 m |
| +15% | R$ 734.850 | R$ 304.636 | 41,5% | 2,5 m |

Nenhum cenário fecha no vermelho.

## Espaço kids

R$ 25.550 de investimento e R$ 7.539/ano de custeio (seguro de responsabilidade civil e monitor em janeiro e fevereiro). Nenhuma açaiteria da Ferrugem tem um. Se trouxer 2% a mais de faturamento, se paga na segunda temporada.

## Correções de contraste

Duas regras de CSS pré-existentes deixavam texto ilegível em seções escuras da página, e este PR corrige as duas:

- `.tl.tot` — linhas de subtotal com fundo claro e texto creme herdado de `.escuro`. Afetava as tabelas da equipe e do investimento
- `.bar` — cartão branco com texto creme, mesma causa. Afetava a ficha técnica do balcão; os percentuais passam a usar cores que leem sobre roxo

## Premissas

Salário mínimo de 2026 (R$ 1.621) × 1,4 para custo CLT no Simples. Equipe de 5 em janeiro e fevereiro, 4 em dezembro, 3 em março e novembro, 1 de abril a outubro — sem família no balcão. Aluguel de R$ 2.500/mês com luz e água inclusas. Simples Nacional Anexo I. Reais correntes de 2026, sem pró-labore nem custo de capital.

## Páginas publicadas

- [Plano — a página de apresentação](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/98a0a127-5f35-48db-aa10-149d5ac79893)
- [Estudo detalhado](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2d036e30-6f79-48f0-a214-29150bddd062)

Ambas funcionam sem JavaScript e respeitam `prefers-reduced-motion`.

author: mikaelstaldal
body:
The web UI's Markdown editor parsed plain CommonMark while everything else in
awb is pinned to CommonMark plus GFM, so a table, a task marker and
`~~struck~~` were typed into an editor that did not know them. This enables the
GFM extension, and adds a formatting toolbar and a syntax reference above the
editor.

## Highlighting

`markdown()` takes GFM now, and a `tagHighlighter` fills the one gap
`classHighlighter` leaves — it has no rule for the strikethrough tag. Everything
else GFM adds inherits classes it already emits: a table header cell is
`tok-heading`, a `|` and a `~~` are `tok-meta`, a `[x]` task marker is
`tok-atom`, an autolink is `tok-url`. Those claims are checked against the
bundle, not assumed.

## Toolbar

A heading select (Normal, H1–H6, mirroring the cursor's line), bold, italic,
code, strikethrough, bullet/numbered/task list, blockquote, code block, table,
horizontal rule, link, image, and a help button — the pinned dialect and
nothing outside it.

What each button writes is a pure function of the document text and the
selection, so the behaviour is pinned by `web/ts/tests/markdown-toolbar.test.mjs`
rather than by driving CodeMirror. The toolbar is `role="group"` rather than
`role="toolbar"`: that role promises arrow-key navigation between the controls,
and every control here is in the tab order instead.

## Help

A modal dialog listing the dialect in the toolbar's order, ending with what the
gate refuses that the syntax allows: raw HTML outright, and any destination
outside `http`, `https` and `mailto`.

## Vendored bundle

The CodeMirror bundle grows three exports. `GFM` comes from `@lezer/markdown`,
now a direct dependency, because `@codemirror/lang-markdown` parses CommonMark
unless handed the extension, and its own GFM-enabled `markdownLanguage` also
carries Emoji and sub/superscript, which awb's dialect does not have.
`web/ts/vendor/rebuild.sh` was run by hand, as it must be; no pinned version
moved, so the filename and the import map are unchanged.

## Verification

`./build.sh` passes. Beyond the unit tests, the UI was driven in a headless
browser against a demo database: highlighting renders as described, the heading
select reports and rewrites a level without stacking `#`s, Bold on an empty
selection leaves the cursor between the markers, the hidden textarea mirrors
every change, clicking a button never takes the selection, and the help dialog
opens inside the modal create-issue dialog with Escape closing only the help.
No console messages.

The second commit is a cold review's findings: a code block took a
three-backtick fence whatever it was given, a selection ending at a line start
reached the line after it, and a link label carried a `]` or a backslash
verbatim. Each is fixed with a regression test.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a Markdown formatting toolbar with headings, lists, links, tables, code blocks, quotes, separators, and other common formatting options.
  * Added a help dialog with keyboard shortcuts and supported Markdown syntax.
  * Added support for GitHub-Flavored Markdown strikethrough and task lists.
* **Improvements**
  * The editor now expands to use the available space more effectively.
  * Formatting controls remain synchronized with the current document and selection.

author: mxamin
body:
The Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.9 jobs failed in "Install package" with AttributeError: ignore_egg_info_in_manifest.

python setup.py install builds in the ambient environment. Those two runner images ship an old bundled setuptools (56/58), and installing requirements_test.txt does not upgrade it because the unpinned setuptools requirement is already satisfied. Current setuptools_scm's egg_info integration reads self.ignore_egg_info_in_manifest, which only exists in setuptools >= 75, so the build blew up on the mismatch.

pip install . builds through PEP 517 with build isolation, so the build environment comes from pyproject.toml's requires (setuptools>=69, wheel, setuptools_scm[toml]>=8) and is consistent on every interpreter regardless of what the image carries. It also drops setup.py install, which setuptools 80 removed.

author: lobinuxsoft
body:
Third slice of #946. The three things that stood between the last two PRs and something you can click.

## 1. The plugin was never added to an app

`BlockPlugin` was exported from the facade and the prelude and **added to nothing**, so `sync_blocks` never ran and no mesh was ever generated. A full grep found three mentions, all of them re-exports.

The editor gets the **whole** plugin, not a components-only half like physics and gravity get. Those author data that another process simulates; a block's mesh is *generated* rather than loaded, so the process that draws it is the one that has to generate it.

## 2. Two ways to make one

**World panel → Spawn → Block.** Writes a fresh cube into `assets/blocks/` and spawns an entity pointing at it, in one action. A block's shape belongs to the entity standing in the level — sharing a source means editing either one moves both, which is occasionally wanted and never the default. Splitting it into "make the asset, then spawn from it" makes the common case three steps.

**Asset browser → New Block Mesh.** A standalone shape, for one meant to be shared.

The spawn honours its `SpawnTarget` rather than landing in whichever scene is active — the failure `SpawnCommand::place` documents, which `SpawnMesh` still has.

## 3. `write_asset_guid`, and the bug its test caught

`write_asset` requests a rescan. A rescan is a request the caller **cannot wait for**, and a component that has to point at the file needs its GUID on the same frame.

The test I wrote for it failed with `database holds: []` — the block was written, nothing registered it, and `Block.source` would have been `None`. So the identity is minted at write time (sidecar + `AssetDatabase::register`) and the GUID is returned.

## And a red test on `development`, fixed

`vendored_modules_all_resolve` **was already failing before this branch** — I checked by stashing. `src/goal_tests.rs` is declared under `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "physics"))]`, and the vendor's test detection matched only the exact line `#[cfg(test)]`. So it was read as production code: the vendored engine declared a module whose file never travelled, and a project built against it fails with `file not found for module`.

That predicate had been **written twice** — once in `copy.rs`, once in `reach_tests.rs` — and the two had drifted. There is one now, `gates_on_test`, and the reach test calls it. Five tests cover the forms, including that `any(test, …)` and `not(test)` are *not* gates.

## Verification

838 tests in `kooch_editor_core` (was 836 passing + 1 failing), 29 in `kooch_blockmesh`. Clippy reports nothing on the new files; the two warnings left in `asset_ops.rs` are pre-existing, confirmed by stashing.

⚠️ `examples/bake_colliders` does not compile under `--workspace --all-targets`. Also pre-existing — it needs the `physics` feature and does not declare it.

## What this still is not

There is no face selection, no extrude, and no toolbar. A block is a cube you can move with the existing handles, walk on, and nothing else yet.

⚠️ The facade's `blockmesh` feature is **opt-in**. The editor draws blocks; a game that wants them at runtime has to enable it. A finished level should not need it — bake the meshes and drop the component.

Refs #946

author: jianyuwang0623
body:
*Note: Please adhere to [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/apache/nuttx/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).*

## Summary

RP2040 defines `ROM_RESET_USB_BOOT` in `arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_rom.h`
(the bootrom `reset_usb_boot()` entry point), but it was never wired up.
`board_reset()` in `boards/arm/rp2040/common/src/rp2040_reset.c` was a
stub that always called `up_systemreset()` regardless of the requested
reset reason, so RP2040 boards had no way to re-enter the USB
mass-storage BOOTSEL bootloader from software.

This matches the pattern already implemented for rp23xx
(`boards/arm/rp23xx/common/src/rp23xx_reset.c` and
`boards/risc-v/rp23xx-rv/common/src/rp23xx_reset.c`), which look up a
ROM reboot function and call it when the reset reason is
`BOARDIOC_SOFTRESETCAUSE_ENTER_BOOTLOADER`.

Changes:

- `arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_rom.h`: add the `rom_reset_usb_boot_fn`
  function pointer typedef for the bootrom `reset_usb_boot(uint32_t,
  uint32_t)` entry (signature matches the official pico-sdk
  `pico/bootrom.h`).
- `boards/arm/rp2040/common/src/rp2040_reset.c`: in `board_reset()`,
  when `status == BOARDIOC_SOFTRESETCAUSE_ENTER_BOOTLOADER`, look up
  `ROM_RESET_USB_BOOT` via `ROM_LOOKUP()` and call it with
  `(0, 0)` (no GPIO activity LED, no interfaces disabled). All other
  status values keep the existing `up_systemreset()` behavior.

## Impact

- The change is in `boards/arm/rp2040/common/`, so it affects every
  RP2040 board that selects `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET`
  (`raspberrypi-pico`, `raspberrypi-pico-w`,
  `adafruit-feather-rp2040`, `seeed-xiao-rp2040`, `w5500-evb-pico`,
  `waveshare-rp2040-lcd-1.28`, etc.).
- No Kconfig/defconfig changes required; behavior for
  `nsh> reboot` / `reboot assert` / `reboot panic` / etc. is unchanged.
- New capability: `nsh> reboot bootloader` now re-enters the RP2040
  BOOTSEL USB mass-storage bootloader directly, without needing to
  hold the physical BOOTSEL button.

## Testing

Host: Ubuntu, `arm-none-eabi-gcc` toolchain.

**Build**

Compiled cleanly for both:
- `raspberrypi-pico:nsh`
- `waveshare-rp2040-lcd-1.28:usbnsh` (the board actually flashed for
  hardware testing below)

```
CC:  src/rp2040_reset.c
...
LD: nuttx
Generating: nuttx.uf2
Done.
```

`tools/nxstyle` reports no issues on either changed file.

**Hardware test** (Waveshare RP2040-LCD-1.28, RP2040, flash id
`0xE4634C65670D202F`)

Flashed `waveshare-rp2040-lcd-1.28:usbnsh` (includes this change) via
`picotool load -x`. Board enumerates as expected:

```
$ lsusb | grep -i 0525
Bus 001 Device 127: ID 0525:a4a7 Netchip Technology, Inc. Linux-USB Serial Gadget (CDC ACM mode)
$ udevadm info -a -n /dev/ttyACM4 | grep -E "manufacturer|product"
ATTRS{manufacturer}=="NuttX"
ATTRS{product}=="CDC/ACM Serial"
```

Connected to `/dev/ttyACM4` and got an nsh prompt:

```
NuttShell (NSH) NuttX-13.0.1-RC0
nsh>
```

Sent `reboot bootloader` over the USB serial console. The console
connection was torn down immediately (device disconnected):

```
exception: device reports readiness to read but returned no data
(device disconnected or multiple access on port?)
```

Polling `lsusb`/`lsblk` afterwards shows the board re-enumerated as
the RP2040 ROM USB bootloader, with no physical BOOTSEL button
pressed at any point during this test:

```
$ lsusb | grep -i 2e8a
Bus 001 Device 126: ID 2e8a:0003 Raspberry Pi RP2 Boot

$ lsblk
sdc           8:32   1   128M  0 disk
└─sdc1        8:33   1   128M  0 part

$ blkid /dev/sdc1
/dev/sdc1: SEC_TYPE="msdos" LABEL_FATBOOT="RPI-RP2" LABEL="RPI-RP2" TYPE="vfat"

$ udevadm info -a -n /dev/sdc1 | grep -E "idVendor|idProduct|manufacturer|product"
ATTRS{idVendor}=="2e8a"
ATTRS{idProduct}=="0003"
ATTRS{manufacturer}=="Raspberry Pi"
ATTRS{product}=="RP2 Boot"
```

This confirms `nsh> reboot bootloader` re-enters BOOTSEL purely in
software, matching the behavior of `boards/arm/rp23xx` /
`boards/risc-v/rp23xx-rv`. After the test, the same firmware image
was reflashed and the board returned to normal nsh operation.

Plain `nsh> reboot` (no argument) was not re-tested after the final
readability changes (using `BOARDIOC_SOFTRESETCAUSE_ENTER_BOOTLOADER`
instead of a raw literal is logically a no-op change), but the
`else` branch calling `up_systemreset()` is unchanged from upstream.

## What does this PR do?

Routes inbound gateway voice notes directly to models that support native audio while preserving the existing STT path as the conservative fallback. This is a clean rebuild of #100764 on the current decomposed gateway architecture.

The implementation resolves the effective per-session provider/model (including model switches), keeps regular audio files as file attachments, and never persists inline Base64 payloads in session history.

## Related Issue

Fixes #90206
Supersedes #100764

## Changes Made

- Added gateway.audio_mode with auto, native, and stt policies, including legacy top-level config compatibility.
- Added bounded native audio payload construction using shared magic-byte container detection and the existing local-file read guard.
- Enforced a 25 MiB per-clip ceiling on the Base64-encoded payload.
- Added OpenAI-style input_audio payloads and Gemini inlineData translation without fetching remote URLs.
- Kept Meta and Muse Spark routes on STT because those endpoints reject this payload shape.
- Mapped the official openai-api provider to the OpenAI capability catalog and added MP3 conversion for direct OpenAI/Azure routes when a recognized voice container is not already MP3/WAV.
- Preserved valid image/audio parts when another clip fails construction; only rejected clips fall back through the existing STT and transcript-echo path.

- Added focused routing, payload, mixed-media, config, and Gemini adapter tests and updated user configuration docs.

body:
## 📌 Resumen Ejecutivo de la Release

Este Pull Request agrupa la solución completa a la alerta de agotamiento de cuotas de Supabase en el plan Free (período de gracia con fecha límite al 21 de septiembre de 2026), resolviendo tanto el **Cached Egress** (Storage / imágenes) como el **Uncached Egress** (consultas directas a base de datos), además de optimizar assets locales y resolver advertencias de rendimiento.

---

### 1. 🖼️ Optimización de Storage Egress & CDN (Fase 1 y 2 - PR #231)
- **Compresión de imágenes en el cliente:** Implementado `lib/images/compressImage.ts` con HTML5 Canvas en los 4 formularios de subida (`CrearClaseForm`, `onboarding`, `ConvertirAcademiaClient` y `PerfilClient`). Las fotos pasan de ~4 MB a ~120 KB (>95% de reducción) antes de enviarse a Supabase Storage.
- **Cache-Control inmutable a 1 año:** Las subidas a Supabase Storage ahora configuran `cacheControl: '31536000'`.
- **Integración con ImageKit CDN:** Soporte para ImageKit con sanitización de endpoints y fallback automático a `wsrv.nl` en `image-loader.ts`.

### 2. ⚡ Optimización de Database Egress & Next.js Caching (Fase 3 - PR #232)
- **Cliente Supabase Público (`lib/supabase/public.ts`):** Cliente singleton con la clave anónima sin cookies ni persistencia de sesión (`persistSession: false`), evitando el error `Dynamic server usage: cookies() cannot be read inside unstable_cache`.
- **Caché en Consultas Públicas:**
  - `fetchDanceStyles` y `fetchClassLevels`: cacheados a 3600s (`tags: ['catalog']`).
  - `fetchStyleClassCounts` y `fetchHomeStats`: cacheados a 600s (`tags: ['catalog', 'classes', 'stats']`).
  - `fetchFeaturedProfiles`, `fetchTeacherBySlug`, `fetchAcademiasWithLocation`: cacheados a 600s (`tags: ['profiles']`).
  - `fetchPublishedClasses` y `fetchClassBySlug`: cacheados a 300s (`tags: ['classes']`).
- **Integridad de flujos privados y borradores:**
  - `fetchClassById`, `fetchTeacherClasses` y `fetchSavedClasses` se mantienen 100% dinámicos con cookies de sesión para garantizar que la edición de borradores y favoritos de alumnos funcionen en tiempo real.
- **Invalidación On-Demand en Server Actions:** Acciones en `lib/classes/actions.ts`, `lib/profiles/actions.ts`, `lib/admin/actions.ts` y `lib/auth/actions.ts` invalidan los tags correspondientes y revalidan `/`.
- **Generación Estática (ISR):** `/academias` y `/unete` ahora cuentan con prerendering estático seguro mediante boundaries de `<Suspense>`.

### 3. 🎨 Optimización de Assets Locales & Corrección de Warnings (PR #233)
- **Compresión WebP en `public/categorias/`:** 11 imágenes redimensionadas y convertidas a WebP, reduciendo la carpeta de **8.1 MB a 366 KB (-95.5%)** (ej. `salsa` de 5.2 MB a 42 KB).
- **Corrección de warnings en `next/image`:**
  - Dimensiones del logo en Header (`width: 110px, height: 37px`) evitando deformación o desbordamiento.
  - Propiedad `sizes` del Hero mobile en Home (`Background-Mobile.webp`) evitando descargas innecesarias de 3840px en pantallas desktop.

---

### 🧪 Validación y Pruebas
- **Pruebas unitarias:** 156 tests pasando (`npm run test`).
- **Linter:** 0 errores, 0 advertencias (`npm run lint`).
- **TypeScript:** 0 errores de compilación (`npx tsc --noEmit`).
- **Build de producción:** Compilado exitoso con Turbopack.

author: randyzwitch
body:
`y_err`/`y_err_lower`/`y_err_upper` were accepted only by `Plot.encode()` and drawn only for `POINT`/`LINE`/`EFFECT_SCATTER`, so a bar chart of means with standard-error whiskers — the most common statistical bar chart — wasn't expressible.

- `Plot.encode_categorical(x, y, y_err=, y_err_lower=, y_err_upper=)` mirrors `encode()`'s rules (mutually exclusive forms, every value `>= 0`, length-checked against `x`/`y`) via the same `y_err_data`/`y_err_lower_data`/`y_err_upper_data` fields `encode()` already uses — `Mark.BAR` only among the marks `encode_categorical()` feeds (`LOLLIPOP`, `WATERFALL`, `NIGHTINGALE`, `FUNNEL`, `POLAR_BAR`, `RADIALBAR`, ...), which raise if given one.
- `Plot.encode_grouped_bar(categories, series_names, values, errors=)` adds a new `_GroupedBarData.errors` field shaped like `values` (`errors[j][i]` per series/category), `Mark.GROUPED_BAR` only among `STACKED_BAR`/`BUMP`/`STREAMGRAPH`.
- `_draw_bar_rects` (bar.mojo) and `_draw_grouped_bars` (grouped_bar.mojo) draw a capped whisker at each bar's/sub-bar's value edge first (the same "whisker first, mark on top" order `_draw_point_layer` uses), using `Theme.error_bar_cap_width` and the bar's own resolved color (`_bar_fill_color`'s color-by-sign result, or the series palette color) — `_Orientation`'s `value_line`/`band_line` give horizontal bars the same drawing for free.
- `_bar_y_domain_data`/`_grouped_bar_domain_data` widen the value-axis domain to the whisker endpoints before `_zero_baseline_y_extent` runs, the same `y_domain_data` pattern `_render_generic` uses for `POINT`/`LINE`/`EFFECT_SCATTER`; `render_layers()`'s bar-combo path picks this up too.

15 new tests in `tests/test_encoding.mojo`: whisker endpoint pixels (both marks), the bar's/sub-bar's own resolved color, the value-axis domain widening, and every raise path (negative values, length mismatches, mutual exclusivity, and each mark this doesn't support yet). Full test suite (58/58) passes.

Closes #216.

author: willchilds-klein
body:
**Stack 1/4** -- bottom of the JDK 25 series. Targets `main`, no dependencies, mergeable on its own.

| # | Branch | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| **#583 (this PR)** | `accp-mac-jdk25-interim` | JDK 25 runtime job, builds/targets 21 |
| #580 | `accp-gradle9-compat` | `build.gradle` Gradle 9 compatibility |
| #581 | `accp-gradle9-wrapper` | Wrapper 8.11.1 -> 9.7.1 |
| #582 | `accp-jdk25-ci` | JDK 25 build/target job |

## What changed

`.github/workflows/macos_ci_jobs.yml` only, one new job (`JDK25ARM-TARGET-JDK21`). 46 added lines, nothing else touched.

Corretto 25 is the runtime under test. The build stays on Corretto 21 because this repo's Gradle wrapper (8.11.1) cannot execute on JDK 25 -- that needs Gradle 9.1+ -- so `TARGET_JDK_VERSION` stays at 21, the newest bytecode level javac 21 can emit. The job follows the same save-JAVA_HOME-then-install-build-JDK shape as the existing JDK 8 and JDK 11 jobs.

## Verification

Locally, with the unmodified 8.11.1 wrapper: build JDK Corretto 21, `--target-jdk-version 21`, `TEST_JAVA_HOME` Corretto 25. `./gradlew release` succeeded, exit 0.

## Why this is first in the stack

It gives JDK 25 signal without waiting on the Gradle 9 work, and it is the only one of the four with no prerequisites -- #581 additionally needs the internal CI Docker images rebuilt first.

#582 adds a `JDK25ARM-TARGET-JDK25` job that builds and targets 25 natively. Both jobs are kept: this one covers older bytecode running on the 25 runtime, the same way `JDK17ARM` and `JDK17ARM-TARGET-JDK17` coexist today. Since #582 sits above this PR in the stack, it also reworks this job's comment, which explains itself in terms of the wrapper being unable to run on 25 -- true here, but not after #581.

If you would rather not carry both jobs, say so and I will drop this PR and rebase the rest onto `main`.

Supersedes #539.
