## Summary

Quarkus consumers stop redeclaring `version.quarkus`. A new `cui-quarkus-parent` supplies it
as an **inherited property**, so `quarkus-maven-plugin` and the Quarkus artifacts are driven
by one value and cannot drift apart.

Per-consumer migration diffs are below. **No PRs are opened in the consumer repos** — each can
be applied and CI-verified separately, on its own schedule.

## §2 — the load-bearing finding: CONFIRMED

`de.cuioss:quarkus-bom` (1.6.2) carried a `<build><pluginManagement>` block for
`quarkus-maven-plugin`. It was **dead**. Verified against the real published artifact, not
assumed:

| consumed as | `quarkus-maven-plugin` | `version.quarkus` | managed deps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<scope>import</scope>` | **absent** | **absent** | present (`quarkus-arc`, `myfaces-quarkus`) |
| `<parent>` | **3.39.2**, `extensions=true`, 3 goals | **3.39.2** | present |

The managed deps arriving in the import case prove the BOM *was* imported — the `<build>`
section is simply ignored. The block is not new work; it is a block that was already written
and never reachable.

A child `<version.quarkus>` moves the plugin **and** the managed artifacts together
(3.28.0 / 3.28.0), which is what makes the emergency-pin escape hatch in §5 safe.

## The mechanic that shaped every decision below

**Probe, not proposed state.** To find out which side Maven prefers, I wrote a throwaway POM
that declared a deliberately mismatched literal version. This is a measurement of the rule, not
anything the migration produces:

```
parent imports io.quarkus:quarkus-bom 3.39.2 ; child imports io.quarkus:quarkus-bom 3.28.0
  -> managed quarkus-arc      3.28.0   (child wins)
  -> quarkus-maven-plugin     3.39.2   (parent's pluginManagement)
```

The rule: **a child-declared `dependencyManagement` import outranks an inherited one.** It
matters below because it determines whether a consumer may delete its BOM import outright.

## §3 — design decisions

**`cui-quarkus-parent`** — `pom` packaging, parented to `cui-java-parent`, released on the
existing `version.cui.parent` train. Carries `version.quarkus` (real property), the
`io.quarkus:quarkus-bom` import, and the `quarkus-maven-plugin` `pluginManagement` moved out
of `de.cuioss:quarkus-bom`.

Not parented to `java-ee-10-bom`, deliberately: that module manages the whole EE/JSF stack
(myfaces, primefaces, resteasy, weld) plus the `smallrye-config` pin, none of which TokenSheriff
or API-Sheriff should inherit.

**`de.cuioss:quarkus-bom` — narrowed, not left with its own copy.** It keeps the three JSF
extensions and drops `version.quarkus`, the `io.quarkus:quarkus-bom` import, and the dead
`<build>` block (which *moves*). Rationale: Maven is single-inheritance, and this BOM needs
`java-ee-10-bom` as its parent for the `smallrye-config` pin — so it cannot inherit
`cui-quarkus-parent`. Had it kept its own `version.quarkus`, cui-reference-documentation (which
inherits the parent *and* imports this BOM) would take its plugin from the parent and its
artifacts from the BOM, per the precedence rule above — reinstating the drift in the one project
that already had the outage.

`de.cuioss:quarkus-bom` has exactly **one consumer org-wide** (cui-reference-documentation;
`gh search code --owner cuioss`), so the narrowed contract is a contained change. It is still a
published-artifact contract change and is called out in its README.

## §4 — consumer state, verified not trusted

The spec's table held, with one addition — the Quarkus BOM import position is load-bearing in
both Sheriffs:

| repo | parent | `version.quarkus` | Quarkus BOM | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cui-reference-documentation | cui-java-parent **1.5.9** | 3.39.0 ×1 | `de.cuioss:quarkus-bom` (6th of 6 imports) | plugin 3.39.0 vs platform 3.39.2 — **still drifting today** |
| API-Sheriff | cui-java-parent 1.6.1 | 3.39.1 **×2** | `io.quarkus:quarkus-bom` **declared first, deliberately** | |
| TokenSheriff | cui-java-parent 1.6.2 | 3.39.2 ×1 | `io.quarkus:quarkus-bom` **declared first** | |

### Duplication: what this removes, and what it does not

The duplication the spec targets is **fully removed**. Across all three migrated consumers:

| | `<version.quarkus>` declarations | literal Quarkus versions outside comments |
|---|---|---|
| TokenSheriff | **0** | none |
| API-Sheriff | **0** | none |
| cui-reference-documentation | **0** | none |

There is exactly one declaration of the value, in `cui-quarkus-parent`.

What remains in **two of the three** is a different thing, and the spec's §4 wording conflated
them as I did initially. §4 said each consumer drops "its local `version.quarkus`, its Quarkus BOM
import, and the `<version>` on `quarkus-maven-plugin`". The property and the plugin `<version>` do
go. The **import** cannot, in TokenSheriff and API-Sheriff — and what stays is a `<dependency>`
block that carries no version of its own:

```xml
<version>${version.quarkus}</version>   <!-- inherited; never declared locally -->
```

That is a duplicated *ordering instruction*, not a duplicated value. Maven offers no way to say
"import this BOM at position N" other than writing it at position N, and inherited imports always
land last.

**cui-reference-documentation restates nothing at all** — no property, no `io.quarkus:quarkus-bom`
import — and measures 0 managed-version differences. That is the clean end state; the other two
cannot reach it yet, for a reason that has nothing to do with this parent.

### Why the two Sheriffs must keep the import — measured

Both import other BOMs (`java-ee-10-bom`, `token-sheriff-bom`) that also manage Quarkus and
smallrye artifacts, and both deliberately declare `io.quarkus:quarkus-bom` first to win that
convergence. Relying on the inherited import inverts that precedence. On TokenSheriff:

| variant | result |
|---|---|
| **keep the import** (recommended) | resolution **identical to control**, full reactor green, 1699 tests pass |
| drop the import | **BUILD FAILURE** — `TokenSheriffProcessor.java:[52,24] Package org.jboss.jandex ist nicht vorhanden` |

45 dependencies shift (resteasy `6.2.18.Final`→`7.0.0.Final`, `jakarta.servlet-api` `6.0.0`→`6.1.0`,
`io.smallrye:jandex` `compile`→`runtime`), and the deployment module stops compiling.

**Can the restatement be removed?** Investigated properly, with four measured TokenSheriff
variants (control = today's wiring on the same parent version):

| variant | build | resolution vs control |
|---|---|---|
| keep the restatement (**what this PR proposes**) | green, 1699 tests pass | **identical (0 changes)** |
| drop it | **compile failure** — `Package org.jboss.jandex ist nicht vorhanden` | 45 changed |
| drop it + remove `<scope>runtime</scope>` from `io.smallrye:jandex` in `java-ee-orthogonal` | compiles | 45 changed — EE stack still wins, `jakarta.*`/smallrye flip `compile`→`provided` |
| drop it + jandex fix + `token-sheriff-bom` drops its `java-ee-10-bom` import | compiles, CDI tests pass | 15 changed — all test-scope Weld `5.1.2`→`6.0.3` |

So zero restatement is *reachable*, but it needs three coordinated changes across two repos plus a
Weld major-version shift in the CDI test stack — and it only helps the two Sheriffs, since
cui-reference-documentation already restates nothing. That is a separate piece of work, not a
precondition for this PR. Note also that `java-ee-orthogonal` setting `<scope>runtime</scope>` on
`io.smallrye:jandex` is independently worth revisiting: it is invisible to JSF consumers but
removes the artifact from the compile classpath for any Quarkus deployment module.

**Root cause, and it predates this PR:** `token-sheriff-bom` imports `java-ee-10-bom`, which pins
an EE stack that conflicts with what Quarkus 3.39 ships. Those two BOMs fight; declaring the
Quarkus BOM first is how both Sheriffs already win that fight today. This PR does not create the
conflict — deleting the import merely exposed it. Reaching zero restatement means resolving that
conflict at its source

author: deliciousbuding
body:
## Observed failure

#1241 finished the two PostgreSQL gates and left an explicit candidate: *how many reconciliation gates have neither defence shape?* This answers it by census rather than by reading, and the census found exactly one gate left — which was not an oversight but a **documented, deliberate exemption that told the next reader not to fix it**.

**Census scope (mechanical, read-only):**

| | count |
|---|---|
| `*_test.go` files in the repo | 483 |
| …that walk a tree or parse an AST | 8 |
| …that already carry a vacuity defence (`vacuous` in a failure message) | 10 |
| union = census scope | **14 files / 15 gate functions** |
| reconciliation-shaped files *outside* that union (reads ≥2 artifacts and compares sets) | **0** |

The union of 14 independently agrees with the census command #1241 corrected in `docs/testing.md` an hour ago — a structural classification and a keyword grep landing on the same set is the cross-check that neither is a mirage. So this was the last gate, not one of many.

**Fourteen of fifteen were defended.** The exception is `TestStorefrontDoesNotLinkInternalDocs`.

## Why the exemption was wrong

#1238 considered this gate and exempted it on purpose. `docs/testing.md` still says:

> A gate that reads two or three *named* files needs no counter — failing to read them is already fatal, as in `TestStorefrontDoesNotLinkInternalDocs`.

and the #1238 commit body adds that this was recorded "so the next reader does not 'fix' it".

The reasoning is right about one surface and silent about the other:

- **Input surface** — it reads `README.md` and `README_EN.md` by name and `t.Fatalf`s on a read error. A missing input *is* already fatal. Correct.
- **Predicate surface** — it then filters what it read through `markdownLinkRE` and `isExternalLinkTarget`, **the same two predicates its sibling `TestRelativeMarkdownLinksResolve` uses**. Narrow either and this gate examines zero links while both files still read fine.

That second surface is precisely why #1238 gave the sibling the stronger defence. Two paragraphs *above* the exemption, the same document says the examined-count shape "also catches a parser or predicate that changed shape and now matches nothing". The document contradicted itself, and the contradiction resolved in favour of leaving the gap open with a note forbidding its closure.

## Probes (harness + log archived in the observation window)

| mutation | before: storefront gate | after: storefront gate | sibling (already had the counter) |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline, no mutation | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| `isExternalLinkTarget` forced true | **PASS** (silent) | **FAIL** | FAIL |
| `markdownLinkRE` narrowed to absolute URLs | **PASS** (silent) | **FAIL** | FAIL |

**6/6 as claimed.** Two mutations emptied one gate while the gate next to it — sharing both predicates — caught them every time. The counter is not a false-red risk on a clean tree: measured input today is **23 links examined in `README.md` + 24 in `README_EN.md` = 47**, none of them into `docs/internal/`. Versions re-materialised with `git show <rev>:<path> > <path>` before every run (never `git checkout --`); tree verified clean afterwards, full `./docs` package green on restore.

## Changes

- **`docs/doc_hygiene_test.go`** — the gate counts links examined and fails on zero, copying the sibling's idiom verbatim rather than inventing a second one. The comment states both surfaces and the measured number, so the floor is real rather than aspirational.
- **`docs/testing.md`** — the exemption bullet is **corrected, not deleted**, because the distinction is worth keeping: named files do defend the input surface, and a gate that reads three named files and compares them needs nothing more. What the bullet says now is that the defence stops where a predicate starts, with this gate as the worked example.

## Worth naming: the third written adjudication that was itself the wrong thing

- **#1236** — the CHANGELOG's writing contract described *itself* untrue in three places.
- **#1241** — `docs/testing.md` published a census command whose output contradicted the same section (10 files printed, 14 implementing the rule).
- **This** — an exemption that stopped a correction instead of preventing re-litigation.

An adjudication written down to end a question also ends the evidence's ability to reopen it. So it has to state **which surface it covered**. All three now do.

Tests and docs only: no production code, no behaviour change. `gofmt` clean, `go test ./docs/...` ok. No release — accumulates into v0.19.1 per Law 3.

author: chnlich
body:
## What changed

`GET /api/threads/{sid}/list` — the 3 s workers-panel poll — now carries a strong content-addressed ETag (sha1 of the body bytes) plus `Cache-Control: no-store`. The client poll repeats the ETag it rendered via `?etag=`; when the whole-body memo's file signature is unchanged the server answers **204 with no body**, and the client keeps its rendered rows and skips the JSON.parse. First paint and changed-row polls still serve the full 200 body, and requests without the etag param keep today's shape (verified against the live running instance, read-only).

The conditional rides a query param rather than If-None-Match: the browser's HTTP cache fulfils a revalidation itself and fetch never surfaces the 304, so a header-level tag would save the transfer but leave the client parse and its skip-branch dead code. `no-store` on every answer keeps each poll a real request.

Soundness: the whole-body memo (#646) already proves an unchanged (path, mtime_ns, size) signature serves the current body — every row-source writer publishes through atomic renames — so a tag derived from the body bytes needs no validity window of its own; a moved signature re-serves 200 with a new tag.

## Why

The worst on-disk corpus (339 rows, 2551 KB thread metadata) shipped a 168209 B body every 3 s per open panel — the largest standing poll payload on this host — for rows the client already held; the unchanged poll now transfers 0 B and the client skips the 339-row parse.

## Evidence

Collector: `docs/perf_baseline.md` M36 command (TestClient, worst worker-list corpus, live state read-only; managers built once as the server's dependency singletons are), main checkout before vs branch head after, back-to-back. Load at measurement: 0.85/1.13/0.89 and 1.42/2.84/2.64 (4 CPUs).

- Full poll (first paint / changed rows — byte-identical code path both arms):
  - before: median 4.27 ms, max 5.25 ms, body 168209 B; median 4.66 ms, max 6.63 ms, body 168209 B; median 6.09 ms, max 10.38 ms, body 168209 B
  - after: median 4.25 ms, max 5.46 ms, body 168209 B; median 5.06 ms, max 5.47 ms, body 168209 B; median 4.57 ms, max 5.36 ms, body 168209 B
- **Conditional poll (steady state, ?etag= repeat): body 168209 B → 0 B (204)**, handler median 4.22-4.75 ms, max 5.59 ms — the unchanged poll's transfer and client-side 339-row JSON.parse are gone; the server-side cost is the unchanged signature pass.
- Live read-only check while the running instance serves older code: `curl http://127.0.0.1:18498/api/threads/3b91d606-cb0d-42ed-9cbb-ca7127da5086/list` -> `http_code=200 size=168209` (no behavioral change for pre-fix clients).

## Baseline doc

- M36 definition row gains the conditional sub-metric (healthy range: full median < 0.02 s; full body < 200 KB; conditional body 0 B (204)) and the collector gains the conditional round.
- Sampling history row appended.

## Tests

- `tests/test_threads_list_api.py`: etag repeat -> 204 no body; signature move -> stale tag re-serves 200 with a new tag; fresh tag -> 204 again; no-store on every answer.
- `tests/workers_list_conditional_poll.test.js`: initial load unconditional + stores ETag; poll sends `?etag=` with `cache: 'no-store'`, 204 skips the repaint; 200 after 204 refreshes the stored tag.
- Full suite: `pytest -q -m "not local_only"` -> 4263 passed.

author: brandburrell2026
body:
Server-only. **No client change, no schema change, no new monitoring vendor, no build.** Framed as finishing the `intakeFailure.ts` remediation on the one route that never got it.

> ⚠️ **Merging this deploys it** — Railway auto-deploys every push to `main`. Do not merge until you intend it live.

## Why

`/journal/rollups` answered `400 rollups_failed` for *every* throw — a malformed `?days=`, a missing column, a dead connection, a bug. And it selects `aforce_user_state.history_start_at` **unconditionally**, for sparse callers as well as dense, so when that column was missing from production every rollups request threw and was reported as a *client* error.

The only counter that could have seen it, `requests_total.api_aforce.4xx`, buckets by the first two path segments and is shared by every AForce route. A total outage was indistinguishable from someone sending a bad query string. **It ran for over a day.** This canary would have caught it on the first request.

## What it adds

| Counter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `rollups_requested.dense` / `.sparse` | Both arms — so "no dense-capable builds in the field" is distinguishable from "nobody called rollups" |
| `rollups_served.dense` / `.sparse` | Read off the **built response**, never the request flag |
| `rollups_contract_violation.dense_not_served` | Invariant tripwire; should read zero forever |
| `rollups_failures.{bad_request,schema,db,aggregation}` | Whose fault it was |

Plus the honest status: **400 only when the request was genuinely at fault, 500 for everything of ours.**

## The one thing that must not be got wrong

`err.code === "42703"` is **dead code here, and it fails silently.** drizzle-orm wraps every driver error in a `DrizzleQueryError` that sets `this.cause` and copies nothing else. Verified by executing it:

```
top-level .code : undefined
cause .code     : 42703
name            : Error        ← not even a distinctive name to match on
```

`serializeError` returns only `{type, message, stack}`, dropping both `.code` and `.cause` — which is why today's log line can't tell the two apart either, even for a human reading it afterwards. So the classifier **walks the cause chain**, depth-limited against cyclic causes, and the SQLSTATE is logged as its own structured field.

A classifier shipped the naive way would typecheck, pass every other test in the repo, and report every schema outage as an aggregation bug — the exact inversion it exists to prevent, in production only.

**The status change is invisible to clients:** `getJson` throws on any non-ok status without inspecting it, and `fetchJournalRollups` is its only caller.

## Evidence

**15 classifier laws + 14 executed HTTP laws** on the real router. The load-bearing law builds a **real `DrizzleQueryError`** rather than a hand-made `{code}` object — the latter would pass against the broken implementation and prove nothing.

Also covered: the **zod trap** (the query parse is inside the same `try`, so a bad `?days=` must stay a 400 and not fall through to `aggregation`), cyclic cause chains, the depth limit, non-string codes, and that no response body leaks SQL, table or column names.

**Mutations — all killed:**

top-level `.code` read (the dead-code trap) · schema/db collapsed into one kind · server faults back to 400 · ZodError check removed · sparse request arm dropped · tripwire deleted · tripwire inverted · **`served` counted off the request**

That last one **survived the first pass** and is worth calling out: no healthy server can produce "dense asked, sparse served", so the two counters were indistinguishable in every natural fixture. The aggregation is now mocked to force the divergence — the only way to prove `served` reads the response. Same for the tripwire, which is now proven to actually fire rather than asserted by source scan.

## Note for reviewers

`journalRollupsRouteWiring`'s guard pinned `return res.json(buildJournalRollupsResponse({`. The response is now bound to a `const` so the served-counter can read it. The guarantee is unchanged — the returned value is still the function's own return value, whole — and I added a prohibition on reshaping it on the way out.

**Suite 8978 passing / 0 failing. Both typechecks clean.** Invariants untouched: `ios: 0`, `android: 0`, `FORCED_UPDATE_UI_ENABLED = false`, no `expo-updates`, no `runtimeVersion` change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: neich
body:
## Summary

- Introduces a path-lazy skill catalog wired through the swarm so agents receive relevant skills without eager loading.
- Extends sleeptime processing with cross-scope promotion and multi-store fan-out, allowing sleep-consolidated memories to propagate across workspace stores.
- Adds a constitution filter that gates which memories are injected on the first turn of a chat session.

## Changes

- **`gaviero-core/src/skills/mod.rs`** — new skill catalog with path-lazy auto-attach logic (~149 lines added).
- **`gaviero-core/src/memory/sleeptime.rs` / `sleeptime_ops.rs`** — cross-scope promotion and multi-store fan-out for sleep-time memory consolidation.
- **`gaviero-core/src/context_planner/chat_memory.rs` / `mod.rs`** — constitution filter applied before first-turn memory injection.
- **`gaviero-core/src/swarm/context_bundle.rs` / `pipeline.rs` / `backend/`** — skill catalog threaded through context bundle and swarm pipeline.
- **`gaviero-core/src/memory/retrieval.rs`** — retrieval logic extended (~250 lines) to support fan-out and filtered injection.
- **`gaviero-core/src/workspace.rs`** — workspace wires new skill and memory config.
- **`gaviero-cli/src/main.rs`** — CLI updated to expose new options.
- **`gaviero-tui/src/app/`** — side panel and commands updated for skill/memory surface.
- Docs: `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `CLAUDE.md` updated to reflect new subsystems.

## Testing

- [x] `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passes, no whitespace errors.
- [ ] `cargo test` — skipped (not run; `--run-tests` not set). Existing e2e test files (`memory_session_e2e.rs`, `memory_testbed_e2e.rs`, `swarm_loop_gate_feedback.rs`, `swarm_pipeline_validation.rs`) have minor additions but no new test coverage was verified in this pass.

## Risks / Notes

- `cargo test` was not executed; regressions in memory retrieval, sleeptime fan-out, or skill injection are unverified.
- The pre-existing tree-sitter grammar drift and `gaviero-remote` snapshot failures noted in project memory are unrelated but will appear in any full test run.
- Skill catalog auto-attach is path-lazy — confirm behavior is correct when a workspace has no matching skill paths.
- Multi-store fan-out touches multiple SQLite stores in sequence; verify writer-task lock discipline holds under concurrent sleeptime triggers.

author: ivanlukianenko
body:
**Bug (user-reported):** with a small all-green suite (e.g. 2/2 tasks passing), R_best saturates at 1.00 and evolution stops **permanently** — harvesting was capped at 3 tasks, and nothing can strictly beat 1.0.

**Fix — two coupled changes:**

1. **Continuous harvesting from daily traces** (the user's proposal): consolidation now harvests up to 2 new validation tasks **every** iteration, not just while the suite has <3. Failure-derived tasks come first — a task the current skill set doesn't trivially pass is exactly the headroom evolution needs. Semantic dedupe, suite capped at ~12.
2. **Suite-anchored gating**: a pass rate is only comparable within one suite, so R_best is now anchored to a suite fingerprint (hash of `## VT-<n>` headers, stored at baseline). When harvesting changes the suite, `record-validation` refuses with **SUITE CHANGED** and demands a fresh `--baseline`; the loop's new step 1b re-anchors automatically after consolidation. A saturated R_best = 1.00 therefore only *pauses* evolution until the next harvested task — never freezes it.

Also fixed along the way: the seed template's example header no longer counts as a task (matcher requires `## VT-<digits>`); `status` shows the suite hash and changed-state; wording updated across guide/README/methodology/commands/opencode mirrors. This repo's own dogfood workspace now correctly reports CHANGED and will re-anchor on its next auto-loop (already DUE by the day trigger). Plugin **0.5.0**.

**Tested end-to-end** on the exact reported scenario: saturated 2/2 baseline → tie correctly rejected → harvest adds a task → gating refused with SUITE CHANGED → re-anchor at 2/3 → proposal accepted at 3/3 (> 0.67).

author: joshuajbouw
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #1843

## Summary

Skip a completed matching capsule install before `KernelRequest::InstallCapsule`. Completion is per-principal and binds capsule identity, package generation, and canonical archive digest. Production skip requires a caller-scoped durable resume receipt whose expected generation is `Some` and equal; `expected_generation = None` does not skip. Distro.lock freshness is not completion proof, and a partial lock never short-circuits or invokes grants.

## Changes

- Resume skip lives in `install_local_via_daemon_for_target`, covering Distro.toml and `.shuttle` without changing `shuttle_install.rs`.
- Canonical source digesting is local and fail-closed: unreadable or malformed sources do not skip and do not abort the ordinary install request.
- Production skip loads `GetCapsuleInstallResumeReceipt { id }` first and derives the expected generation from that receipt. `GetInstalledCapsuleIdentity { id }` remains the matching installed-package query. Neither request carries a principal selector; the kernel resolves the owner from authenticated caller context. Receipt wire data is id, archive digest, and generation object IDs only.
- After a successful same-principal `InstallCapsule`, `PutCapsuleInstallResumeReceipt` persists the caller-scoped receipt. Put/CAS/read-back failure does not fail an already-installed capsule. Cross-principal installs do not write a caller-owned receipt for the selected target.
- `kernel_router/resume_receipt.rs` stores receipts under suffix-free principal control `capsule-install-resume`. `StateOwnerResolver` admits exactly `distro` and `capsule-install-resume`; neighboring and extended spellings still reject. Env/secret/native/Admin grammar is unchanged.
- `kernel_router/installed_identity.rs` verifies the durable package for that caller and fails closed on missing, partial, malformed, or raced state. A canonical wasm hash is optional corroboration and is not a completion-key field; exact identity+generation+archive digest still skips when `wasm_hash` is absent.
- Capability strings keep `(InstallCapsule, Self_) | (GetInstalledCapsuleIdentity, _) | (GetCapsuleInstallResumeReceipt, _) | (PutCapsuleInstallResumeReceipt, _) => "self:capsule:install"` and `(InstallCapsule, _) => "capsule:install"`.
- `GetInstalledCapsuleIdentity`, `GetCapsuleInstallResumeReceipt`, and `PutCapsuleInstallResumeReceipt` are rate-limited `None`. `InstallCapsule` remains `Some(10)`.
- Distro apply stays `grant_capsules: false` with no `--target-principal`. Grants run only for newly installed names. DistroSelfGrant after `run_init` is unchanged.
- Partial Distro.lock is never fresh. `--var` resume skip is allowed only when the typed values map is empty.
- `init.rs` stays within the 1000-line source cap; no new modules and no lint suppressions.

## Verification

Lead-run on exact head `455f9a0338940ebea9165284b2e8697fcc0f0f7d` (parent `7e3a508f`, unique range onto `c3d0cf08` / origin/main, GPG Good/full, DCO) with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/joshuaj.bouw/.cache/cargo-target-lanes/capsule-resume`:

- `cargo test -p astrid --bin astrid -- matching_identity_skips_when_wasm_hash_absent matching_skip_carries_canonical_wasm_hash none_expected_generation_does_not_skip archive_digest_mismatch_does_not_skip generation_mismatch_does_not_skip` (5 passed)
- Writer also ran the broader resume filter (8 passed) and `cargo clippy -p astrid --bin astrid -- -D warnings`
- `install_daemon.rs` 681/1000; `init.rs` 998/1000; `kernel_router/mod.rs` 986; `kernel_api/mod.rs` 974

Falsifiers: matching receipt skip does not send `InstallCapsule`; exact identity+generation+archive digest skips even when `wasm_hash` is absent; same-archive different-generation, missing/partial/corrupt receipt, and `None` expected generation fail closed; principal B does not inherit principal A; 22 members schedule `10+10+2`; Distro apply grant surface unchanged; AOS is not edited.

## AI / Tool Assistance

Assisted-by: Codex:gpt-5.6-luna
Assisted-by: Codex:grok-4.6

Implementation of the principal-scoped resume skip, durable generation receipt, suffix-free `capsule-install-resume` admission, and focused falsifiers. Independently reviewed exact-head gates above before updating this PR.

author: danathar
body:
**#88 was merged, and none of its content is on `main`.** Recovering it.

## What happened

I based #88 on `docs/second-pass-drift-audit` (#87's branch) and never retargeted it to `main`. #87 merged at 14:28; #88 merged at 14:39 — **into the branch #87 had already merged and closed.** GitHub reports #88 as MERGED, its merge commit `0e78972` exists, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0e78972 origin/main` says **NO**.

So all fifteen review-finding fixes have been sitting orphaned. `gh pr list` showed nothing open and every thread resolved, which is exactly how it went unnoticed — every signal said done.

This PR cherry-picks the three commits onto `main` unchanged.

## Safety-critical statement

`build.yml` is an AGENTS.md section 0 rule 2 file.

**What could reach a booted machine if this is wrong:** the `paths-ignore` addition can only *prevent* a production build, never cause one — the failure mode is a change that should rebuild not rebuilding. Restricted to paths neither copied into the image nor read by a build; `cosign.pub` deliberately excluded because `build-image.sh` installs it into the image. GitHub skips a push only when *every* changed path matches, so a commit touching `ci_tools/` and `.editorconfig` still builds.

**What is currently wrong on `main` because this was lost** is the more relevant statement:

- A push touching only `.editorconfig` still builds, signs and promotes a production image — every tracking machine pulls a new image for a whitespace config change.
- `nightly-compliance.yml` still verifies the *tag* rather than the digest it inspected, so a green job can report an artifact verified without having checked it.
- `git push origin --force` still falls through to `ask` rather than deny.
- Both completeness gates still glob `*.yml` only, so a `.yaml` workflow escapes them.
- The replay prompt still tells an agent to push a branch and dispatch production, and still omits that a "diagnostic" replay can republish the shared akmods cache.
- The diagnose prompt still tells an agent to restore `:latest`.

## Rollback impact

Not applicable.

## Contents

Unchanged from #88 plus its two follow-up commits — full rationale in those commit messages and in #88's description. Summary:

| Fix | Was |
| --- | --- |
| `build.yml` `paths-ignore` | metadata-only pushes built and promoted production |
| `nightly-compliance.yml` digest pin | verified the tag, not the digest it inspected (`${IMAGE%:*}`, not `%%`, for ported registries) |
| `settings.json` push denies | `git push origin --force` matched nothing; now documented as best-effort, since a `+refspec` forces with no flag |
| `.yaml` globs in two gates | a `.yaml` workflow escaped both while they stayed green |
| Replay prompt ×4 | partial-not-exact, missing `--ref`, workaround is itself a production build, and `allow_cache_rebuild` defaults true |
| Diagnose prompt ×3 | `:latest` already moved on digest mismatch; TUF 403 means different things per job; `cancelled` is a hypothesis |
| Host-side claim ×4 docs | image-side *Python* does have host-side tests and coverage floors |
| `quality.md` badge | "still boots" → reports existence and age |
| `maintenance-watchlist.md` | records that `production-signing` is **not** branch-restricted despite two docs saying it is |

## Verification against current `main`

Cherry-picked cleanly over #90, which landed in the meantime.

- `ruff check` clean
- `pytest tests/ -q` → **323 passed, 43 subtests** (up from 307; #90 added 16)
- `unittest discover -s tests` → Ran 323, OK
- coverage gate → all 27 per-file decisions hold
- Each of the seven changes confirmed present by grep, not assumed from the cherry-pick exit code

## Process

Second time this session a stacked PR caused a defect — the first was `SECURITY-AI.md` contradicting itself across #81/#82. Stacking is not worth this. Anything further goes on `main` directly, or gets retargeted the moment its base merges.

author: joren-vangoethem
body:
## What was wrong

Two of the shell's three `PopupWindow` users were bar tooltips that each built their own,
neither of them going through the popup infrastructure that exists for exactly this:

- `Modules/Bar/BatteryIndicator.qml:114` — `PopupWindow` + `GlassPanel`, `implicitWidth: 224`
  wrapped around a 200px card, leaving a 24px transparent gutter.
- `Modules/Bar/TrayPill.qml:159` — `PopupWindow` + an **inline re-implementation of
  `GlassPanel`**: `Theme.alpha(Theme.glassBase, Theme.glassAlphaPanel)`, `Theme.hairline`,
  1px border — the three lines that component is.

Neither set `mask`. `Common/PopupSurface.qml:77-80` is careful about this everywhere else,
and says why:

> Only the panel takes pointer input, or the transparent gutter would swallow both the
> outside click that dismisses this and the clicks meant for the windows below.

In practice it costs nothing today: the tooltips are only up while the cursor is on the bar,
so the gutter has nothing to swallow. It is the same latent bug `PopupSurface`'s mask was
written to avoid, and it bites the first tooltip anchored somewhere other than a bar the
cursor is already in.

## The change

`Common/Tooltip.qml` — `PopupWindow` + `GlassPanel` + `mask: Region { item: card }` +
`anchorItem`, content in the default property.

A **sibling** of `PopupSurface`, not a use of it. It keeps the masking discipline and the
same "owners size their own card" contract (`panelWidth` / `panelHeight` / `panelRadius`),
and drops the focus grab, the `PopoverManager` wiring and the fade — which is most of what
`PopupSurface` is, and none of what a hover tooltip wants.

Both call sites become their content plus four property assignments. `BatteryIndicator`
keeps `radiusMenu`, `TrayPill` keeps `radiusChip`, as they did.

Sizing is owner-driven rather than derived from `childrenRect`: the battery card's rows are
`width: parent.width`, so a self-sizing wrapper would bind-loop against them.

## One deliberate visual change

The tray tooltip had no gutter and sat flush against the bar; the battery one hung 6px below
it. Both now use `Tooltip`'s 12×6 default, so the tray tooltip drops by 6px and the two
match. That consistency is the point of the issue — say the word if you would rather keep
the flush placement, it is a `gutterY: 0` override on one line.

## Verification

- `tests/test-qml-hygiene.sh` — passes.
- Load-checked all three files under a real `quickshell` run (a throwaway `ShellRoot`
  instantiating `BatteryIndicator`, `TrayPill` and `Tooltip`): clean, no warnings. Confirmed
  the harness actually catches failures by feeding `Tooltip` a bad `panelWidth` and watching
  it abort with `Invalid property assignment: int expected`.
- `qmllint` reports only the pre-existing `qs.*` import-resolution noise tracked in #121.

No screenshots: running the branch's bar means a second full bar over the live session, and
the intended visual delta is the 6px above. Happy to capture a before/after if you want it.

Closes #90

---

## Second commit: the empty tooltip that hangs around

Reported while reviewing this branch: *"sometimes when I quickly hover over a tray item
there is a small popup with nothing in it that remains."* Reproduced, and it is a
pre-existing defect in `TrayPill`, not something this refactor introduced.

Caught on the live bar — an empty glass card parked under the tray, with nothing in it:

![empty-tooltip.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d6e31ce-bc0f-49d5-bb20-0e70a0e2607b)

It measures ~15×25px, which is exactly `label.implicitWidth + 12` by
`label.implicitHeight + 8` **with an empty label**. So the card was drawn with no text.

### Mechanism

The tooltip was shown off the cursor rather than off its content:

```qml
visible: root.hovered !== null
```

`hovered` holds the Repeater **delegate**, and the delegate's lifetime is not the tray
item's. An SNI that unregisters while the cursor is on it leaves the delegate alive holding
a `modelData` Qt has already torn down; every field on it reads back `undefined`, the label
collapses to `""`, and `hovered` is still a live object — so the window stays mapped. Nothing
takes it down either, because no further enter or leave will ever reach that delegate.

Confirmed with a probe holding the delegate alive and destroying the item under it:

```
hovered, item alive : before=true after=true  text="Spotify"
item destroyed      : before=true after=false text=""
```

`before` is the old condition, `after` is the new one. The old one stays true with an empty
label; the new one goes false.

### Fix

- `TrayPill` gains `hoveredName`, and the tooltip shows on `hoveredName !== ""` — no name,
  no window.
- `hovered` is also cleared when an entry is hidden under the cursor (an id moving into
  `hiddenItems`), which Qt sends no leave for.
- `Tooltip.visible` is now derived: `open && anchorItem !== null`. Owners set `open`, so an
  anchorless tooltip can no longer map itself into the corner of a screen. This is why
  `visible:` became `open:` at both call sites.

author: danielcarletti
body:
## Problem

A reset resync of an xmin schema replaces the whole warehouse table with only the rows written since the last run. A 42M-row table came back as 2M rows, with the job reporting `Completed`.

- A reset deletes the Delta table before the read and overwrites it from the first batch.
- The activity drops the incremental cursor for a reset run so the read covers the whole table again: [import_data_sync.py:428](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/d61da5f73cd/products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/workflow_activities/import_data_sync.py#L428).
- The xmin cursor is not on `SourceInputs`. `PostgresSource` reads it straight off the schema and passes it through regardless of the reset.
- With a cursor present the read takes the bounded `xmin >= last AND xmin < ceiling` window instead of the full scan, and the overwrite collapses the table to that window.
- The run then advances the ceiling, so nothing about the schema shows it happened.

The comment on the incremental branch in the activity describes this exact failure. It was never wired for xmin.

## Changes

Nothing user-visible changes shape. A reset resync of an xmin schema now rebuilds the whole table.

- `PostgresSource` passes `xmin_last_value=None` and `xmin_num_wraparound=None` to the read when the run rebuilds the table: a reset, or a pending corrupt-delta revive. With no cursor the read takes the full scan, which is what a rebuild means.
- A normal xmin run is unchanged.

The check lives in the Postgres source rather than the activity because that is where the cursor is read. `SourceInputs` stays Postgres-agnostic, as the existing comment at that call site says.

The revive is included on review. The activity already drops the incremental cursor for both triggers, and the rebuild runs inside the pipeline after the read, so the collapse is identical.

Repairing a table this already collapsed needs the cursor cleared and a reset staged. `reset_wrapped_xmin_cursors --schema-id <id> --live-run` clears it; a `--reset` resync then rebuilds.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only. Not exercised against a live source.

- `test_table_rebuild_drops_the_xmin_cursor` in `tests/e2e/test_import_data.py`, parametrized over a staged reset and a pending revive, catches a rebuild run that passes the stored xmin cursor through to the read. It asserts only the three cursor kwargs, so it does not pin the rest of the call. Both cases fail with `assert 100 is None` before the fix; the revive case fails the same way against a reset-only gate.

Not checked: the rest of `test_postgres.py` that needs a live Postgres, which errors on the shared test database from a concurrent session.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None. The [Postgres sync methods](https://posthog.com/docs/data-warehouse/sources/postgres#sync-methods) docs describe a reset as a full re-read, which is what this restores.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**No duplicate:** searched open PRs for `xmin cursor`, `reset_pipeline xmin`, and `clear_xmin_state`. Nothing addresses the reset path. #93392 and #95274 touch the xmin read but not its cursor.

Written by Claude Code, directed by @danielcarletti. Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.

Found while checking why a reset resync completed with a fraction of the expected rows. The run's own log showed `reset_pipeline = True` and a windowed `WHERE xmin >= ...` predicate in the same run, which is the whole diagnosis.

**Public artifact:** this work started from a customer support ticket. No customer material reached the diff, the tests, the comments, the commit messages, or this description. The test reuses the fixtures already in `test_import_data.py` with invented cursor values.

body:
사용자 판정 §3(*「일단 필요한 사항을 가정하여 설정하고, 추후 변경할 수 있게 설계해」*)에 따라 `fixtures/profiles/representative-day.yaml` 의 `seasons:` 둘을 **가정**으로 채운다.

### ⚠ 도중에 실재하는 결함 하나가 드러났다

배포 실행은 8,760스텝을 쓰지 않는다 — **앞 24스텝만 잘라 「대표일」로 쓰고 365배** 한다. 그래서 계절 넷을 선언하면 앞 24스텝이 *연평균 하루*에서 **첫 계절(봄)의 하루**로 조용히 바뀌고, 연간 발전이 **+281kWh 생기고** 연간 부하가 **−315kWh 사라진다.** 저장소가 그 성질을 이름으로 지키고 있다(`test_a_shape_moves_energy_but_does_not_create_it`).

⚠ 자산만 채웠으면 골든이 **+1,135,684원** 움직였고 **그 수는 계절 가정의 결과가 아니라 총량 파괴의 결과**였다 — 계절을 적는 *차례*만 바꿔도 부호가 뒤집힌다.

### 그래서 대표일을 「몫 가중 평균 하루」로 세웠다

`DailyShape.spread()`(계절을 차례로 이어 붙이는 것이 정의)는 **고치지 않고** 형제 메서드를 세웠다 — `rep[j] = Σ_계절 (total × share × weight[j]) / days`. `Σ_j rep[j] × days == total` 이 항등식으로 성립한다. 러너의 두 자리가 그 대표일을 365일 되풀이한 8,760 시계열을 넘긴다.

- **총량 보존** — 대표일 발전 10.8000kWh · 부하 9.8630kWh **그대로** · 불변 시험 둘을 **손대지 않고** 초록불
- **결론축이 움직였다** — 세 시나리오 모두 **−15,141원**(무보조 −11,537,129 → **−11,552,270원**). 총량은 그대로이고 **형상 혼합만** 바뀐 몫이다. `payback_period_years` 는 셋 다 `.inf` 그대로
- **남는 결손을 지우지 않고 신고한다** — 미반영 대장이 「계절은 가정으로 선언됐고, 배포 실행은 평균 하루를 돌므로 **계절 간 하루 차이는 결론에 서지 않는다**」와 해소 조건 셋(계절별 운전 · 요일 변동 · 8,760 실측)을 말한다. **항목 수를 늘리지 않았다**(하나가 본문 두 줄을 만들고 예산 여유가 1줄이다)
- 본문 상한(219)을 **올리지 않았다** · 골든을 손으로 고치지 않았다(스크립트로 다시 뽑았다)

커밋 둘 — 1판 시험 전부 / 2판 구현 전부. `check_test_accompaniment`·`check_commit_order` 둘 다 `--base origin/main` 에서 `rc=0`(짝 3건 · 경고 0줄).

author: pcalnon
body:
## Summary

**F-CANOPY-042 is two defects, not one.** The registered finding is the wiring; the second was found reading the code to write the fix brief, and is wrong with no user action at all.

**Defect A — the label was wired to the wrong thing.** `-depth-label.children` was the fourth Output of the clientside slider-bounds sync, whose only Input is `-topology-store.data`. The slider's value rode there as **State**, and a State is read when something *else* fires — so the label recomputed when the topology changed and never when the user moved the slider. Since canopy#542 identity-suppressed the topology store, at idle it never changed at all.

The obvious repair is **structurally unavailable**: adding `Input(-depth-slider, "value")` to that callback makes one component-property both an Input and an Output of a single callback, which Dash rejects at registration as a circular dependency. Hence the split — the label gets its own clientside callback with the slider value *and* the topology store as Inputs (the second because a `cascade_add` changes the denominator with no user action), and the bounds-sync callback returns three elements instead of four.

**Defect B — `0` meant two different things.**

| consumer | rule | at `value=0`, `n_hidden=40` |
|---|---|---|
| filter (`_apply_hierarchy_filter`) | `depth is None or depth <= 0 or depth >= total` → no filter, label `"all"` | shows **all 40** |
| label (clientside, old) | `(v === nHidden) ? "all" : v + " of " + nHidden` | renders **`"0 of 40"`** |

The slider ships `min=0, max=0, value=0`, so on a loaded 40-unit network the control read **"0 of 40" while all 40 units were displayed** — before anyone touched anything. Fixing the wiring alone would *not* have fixed this. The new rule is a condition-for-condition transliteration of the server guard, so the two agree by inspection, and the discard at the call site now says so in both directions.

## Why clientside and not the rebuild

`update_network_graph` already computes exactly the wanted label and throws it away (`depth_label`, never referenced), and it already takes `-depth-slider.value` as an Input — so routing the label through it would be correct *by construction*. It is also the starvation-prone callback (**1.5–31 s** measured; F-CANOPY-037 / -039 / -043), which would put the number under the user's thumb seconds behind the drag, and it has four return paths that would each need a ninth Output — two of them empty-figure paths with no meaningful label to give.

Options A1–A4 and the rejected alternatives, with costs, are recorded in juniper-ml's `notes/JUNIPER_2026-09-04_JUNIPER-CANOPY_F042-F046-FIX-DECISION-BRIEF.md`.

## Verified live — A/B, same fixture, minutes apart

A second canopy was launched on **:8052** from this branch, beside the arc's **:8051** instance which serves parent `ee2ec79`. Both point at the same cascor (:8202) and juniper-data (:8101), so the *only* thing differing between the two runs is which code the process imported. The 2/40/2/944 fixture was never touched.

| row | :8051 parent | :8052 this branch |
|---|---|---|
| M-TOPOLOGY-07 (at rest, no gesture) | `display='block' label='0 of 40'` → **FAIL** | `display='block' label='all'` → **PASS** |
| M-TOPOLOGY-06 (drag to depth 20) | `label='0 of 40' hidden='20 of 40'`, `label_ok=False counts_ok=True` → **FAIL** | `label='20 of 40' hidden='20 of 40'`, both `True` → **PASS** |
| step total | 7 PASS / 2 FAIL | **9 PASS / 0 FAIL** |

Both rows read FAIL on parent because **the scorers were tightened in the same pass** (juniper-ml `util/ad-hoc/e2e_seg17_topology_driver.py`):

- **M-TOPOLOGY-06**'s predicate was `label == want **OR** counts["hidden"] == want`, and it had been passing on the counts branch — the stats bar tracked the filter while the label beside the slider stayed at `"0 of 40"`. An OR over two independent claims scores the easier one, which is why this row was green while half of what it names was broken, and why F-CANOPY-042 had to be found by eye rather than by its own scorer.
- **M-TOPOLOGY-07** *read* the label and never asserted it — `label` went into the record as decoration while the verdict turned on `display` alone. It logged `'0 of 40'` on every run of this arc and scored PASS.

## Testing

`src/tests/unit/frontend/test_f042_depth_filter_label.py` — **11 tests**, layered so the JavaScript is not merely *described*:

1. **Wiring** is asserted against `app._callback_list` after a real `register_callbacks` — the registration Dash would actually serve. Includes a pin that no callback has `-depth-slider.value` as both Input and Output, so a future "simplification" that merges the two callbacks back together fails here rather than at Dash registration in production.
2. **The rule** is checked by *executing the registered clientside function under node* over a 48-case grid and comparing it, case for case, against `_apply_hierarchy_filter`. The Python function is the oracle; nothing re-types the rule. Arguments are built from the callback's declared **Input order** rather than an assumed signature.
3. A **source-level backstop** asserts all four arms of the server guard are present clientside, so a missing node cannot leave Defect B uncovered by a skip.

That shape is deliberate: `test_network_visualizer_callbacks.py` already "covers" this component with tests that re-type the production expression and assert against their own copy — the class that let F-CANOPY-041b and F-CANOPY-045 ship green.

**Falsified against parent**: 5 of 11 fail there — both wiring tests, the source backstop, and both node tests. Driven through its *own* registered Input list, parent's label writer ignores the depth entirely: it returns `"all"` for all 48 grid cases, including the 9 where the filter really is filtering (e.g. `depth=3, hidden=5` → filter says `"3 of 5"`).

- Full canopy unit + regression suite: **6004 tests across 253 files, exit 0**.
- `black`, `isort`, `flake8`, `mypy`, `bandit` clean via pre-commit.

## Documents changed

None in this repo. The design-of-record is juniper-ml's `notes/JUNIPER_2026-09-04_JUNIPER-CANOPY_F042-F046-FIX-DECISION-BRIEF.md`; the finding is tracked in `notes/JUNIPER_2026-08-09_JUNIPER-CANOPY_E2E-VALIDATION-EVIDENCE.md` and the rows in `notes/JUNIPER_2026-08-08_JUNIPER-CANOPY_E2E-CLICK-BY-CLICK-TEST-MATRIX.md`, both of which are updated in the companion juniper-ml PR.

Refs F-CANOPY-042, M-TOPOLOGY-06, M-TOPOLOGY-07.

## Summary

Prepares the 0.5.1 release. No source behavior changes — version declarations,
the changelog, and two stale doc counts.

- **Package version 0.5.0 → 0.5.1** at every site INV-10 registers:
  `pyproject.toml`, `__version__`, both `server.json` fields, `CITATION.cff`
  (with `date-released`), and the README, project-instruction, and onboarding
  banners. The wire version already moved to 0.5.1 with the confidence field;
  the two versions remain independent and happen to coincide here.
- **The Unreleased section is cut into a dated `## [0.5.1] — 2026-09-04`**, with
  its five `Added` blocks, two `Changed`, and two `Fixed` consolidated into one
  of each, comparison links added, and a fresh empty `Unreleased` above. The
  extension-registration entry moves from Added to Fixed.
- **Six behavior-affecting changes that merged without a changelog entry are
  written up**: `trace-mcp-init` writing the trace-learn `--with` extras; the
  decision-audit hook matcher derived from the MCP server key; the MCP
  initialize handshake reporting trace-mcp's own version; `trace-mcp validate`
  applying the specification's semantic rules; learn extraction skipping
  imported records and machine-measured decisions; and INV-10's spec-version
  site-set widening from three sites to eight.
- **The invariant count is corrected** in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ONBOARDING.md`:
  INV-12 is registered and enforced, but both still said eleven.
- **The README pinned-install example points at `@v0.5.1`** and a `New in 0.5.1`
  callout leads with decision confidence. The pinned VCS source is the one
  install path that avoids the unrelated PyPI distribution, so leaving it on the
  previous tag is the version staleness a reader actually acts on.
- **`CITATION.cff` keeps the concept DOI and the v0.5.0 version DOI.** The 0.5.1
  version DOI is added once the archive that mints it exists, so the file never
  names a DOI that does not resolve.

## Why

A release's changelog is the durable record of what shipped. Entries were
appended per change without consolidation, so the section had accumulated nine
sub-headings, and six merged changes — including three that alter what a
deployed consumer does — never got an entry at all. Both gaps are cheap to fix
before a tag and expensive afterwards, since the tag is what a DOI archives.

The version bump has to land on `main` before a tag can point at it.

## Verification

- Full suite: 1541 passed, 12 skipped.
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, and `pyright src/` clean.
- Invariant guard and version-declaration guard:
  `tests/test_invariants.py` + `tests/test_installation_health.py`, 47 passed.
- Shipped artifact: `uv build` then `tests/test_packaging_artifacts.py`, 11 passed.
- The built wheel launched over a real MCP stdio handshake in a scratch `HOME`
  reports `serverInfo.version = 0.5.1` and the full 22-tool surface — the
  end-to-end check that the version stamp and the trace-learn extras both
  survive into the artifact that gets installed.

## Risks / rollback

Documentation and metadata only; no runtime code path changes. Reverting the
commit restores 0.5.0 declarations exactly.

Publishing is unaffected: `release.yml` has no push or tag trigger, so creating
the tag and the GitHub Release for DOI archival cannot start a PyPI upload.

## References

- `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — INV-10 (version declaration sites), INV-12 (learning ids)
- Changes covered by the new entries: #47, #50, #52, #65, #67

author: laddtnov
body:
The portfolio pinned the CDN at **0.2.0** while the package it advertises has been at **0.6.2** — four minor releases behind its own design system.

13 files, 15 version references, 13 SRI hashes.

## Compatibility checked before bumping, not after

Diffed the two token files rather than trusting semver:

| | |
|---|---|
| Tokens removed in 0.6.2 | **none** |
| Consumed tokens missing | **none** (site uses 7) |
| Consumed tokens whose value changed | **none** |
| Added | `--cy-neon-gold`, `--cy-gold-rgb`, `--cy-backdrop`, `--cy-font-terminal` |

Purely additive, which is why this is a safe bump rather than a migration.

## The SRI hash is the dangerous part

A stale `integrity` makes the browser **refuse the stylesheet**, and that failure is silent. It would have been invisible on this site specifically: every `var()` carries a fallback equal to the token's own value, so a blocked sheet renders identically to a working one.

Two things were done about that:

1. **The hash method was validated first** — recomputing sha384 over 0.2.0's `tokens.css` reproduces the hash currently pinned in the repo exactly. So the tool producing the new hash is known-correct before it's trusted.
2. **Verified by a token that only exists in 0.6.2.** `--cy-neon-gold` resolves to `#d4af37` in the browser. That is only possible if the hash validated and the sheet parsed — a fallback cannot produce it.

## Test plan

- [x] Old hash reproduces from 0.2.0 content — hashing method proven.
- [x] `--cy-neon-gold #d4af37`, `--cy-gold-rgb 212, 175, 55`, `--cy-backdrop`, `--cy-font-terminal` all resolve → sheet loaded and parsed.
- [x] Stylesheet present in `document.styleSheets` with readable rules (CORS fine via `crossorigin="anonymous"`).
- [x] Shared tokens unchanged: `--cy-neon-cyan #00f2ff`, `--cy-neon-pink #ff00ff`, `--cy-bg #0a0a0c`.
- [x] **Light theme** exercised — 0.6.2 supplies proper light overrides (`--cy-neon-cyan` becomes `#00707f`, the accessible contrast variant); body background and text switch correctly and switch back.
- [x] Product page checked: sheet loaded, badge colour correct, zero failed resources.
- [x] No console errors. Screenshots in both themes match the existing design.
- [x] Nothing left on `0.2.0` or the old hash anywhere in the repo.

## Also

The install snippet on `products/cyberpunk-ui.html` was telling visitors to install `0.2.0`. Updated — it is documentation for the package, so being four versions stale there is worse than in a link tag.

## Summary

- canonicalize reviewed Stage paths to the trailing-slash form Stage now serves, while preserving reviewed scenario identity
- bind each active click to its serialized event with a per-invocation marker instead of timing or business-field similarity
- strip that marker before transport and independently abort any outbound request body that still contains it
- fail closed on ambiguous, duplicate, overlapping, or unprovable invocation lineage and reset an unsafe browser target before removing the guard
- apply the same canonical-path contract to scheduling, inventory, offline verification, analysis, and reporting

## Why

The replay was navigating slashless customer paths that Stage now answers with 404s, blocking most of the inventory. Separately, the production tracking SDK captures its original dispatch function before the harness can wrap it, so valid clicks could serialize without causal lineage and be missed. The new marker establishes exact per-click lineage without changing the customer event sent over the wire.

## Validation

- `npm run lint`
- replay-focused Vitest suite: 9 files, 226 tests passed
- independent correctness review: no blockers
- independent security review: no blockers
- authenticated Stage safe-sink validation: one Talk to Sales click linked through the captured-dispatch SDK path; marker removed before transport; cleanup fully restored

The repository-wide test command still has pre-existing failures in unrelated block tests; this PR does not touch those paths.

## Preview

https://codex-fix-parity-canonical-lineage--intuit-erp--aemsites.aem.page/accounting/business-intelligence-reports/

This is replay/diff tooling only and does not change customer-facing page behavior.

author: amantidesigns
body:
## Incident

A caregiver replied "Stop" to the daily brief. The agent replied "Got it, stopping the repeated messages" — then sent the identical brief at 8:00 AM the next morning, and for two mornings after that. In the same exchange the agent asserted the earlier messages "were a system glitch" and asked whether "the dose changed too", when the caregiver had reported no dose change.

**⚠️ This PR contains one open question that needs a human decision before merge. See "Open question" at the bottom — I implemented the safe half and deliberately did not decide the rest.**

---

## Audit findings

### 1. Stop-intent persistence: the two paths were never connected

**Inbound.** For the primary coordinator there was no stop handling of any kind. `handleMessage` (`convex/handler.ts`) resolves the user, logs the inbound message, and hands the turn to the model. "Stop" was just text in a prompt. The reply "Got it, stopping the repeated messages" was a model utterance with zero runtime effect — nothing was written to `users`, `careCases`, or anywhere else.

**Scheduled.** `reminders.sendDailyDigest` gated on exactly three things: the care case is non-archived with a `chatId` and inbound activity in the last 14 days (`admin.listActiveCareCasesForDigest`), a same-day `response_sent` audit row does not already exist, and there is at least one schedule item for today. It read no suppression state, because none existed to read.

So the paths were not merely disconnected — there was nothing on one end to connect to. The 8:00 AM cron behaved exactly as designed.

**The inversion.** `listActiveCareCasesForDigest` keeps a care case eligible if there is an inbound message in the last 14 days. Replying "Stop" is an inbound message. Saying "Stop" actively *refreshed* the window that kept the brief alive. A user who stopped texting entirely would have gone quiet after 14 days; the user who explicitly asked for silence kept the channel warm.

**Care contacts.** `contactReplies.classifyCareContactReply` did have a `stop_requested` status that durably sets `active: false, canReceiveTexts: false, consentToContact: false`. But its pattern was `/\b(stop texting|stop messaging|do not text|don't text|dont text|unsubscribe|remove me)\b/i` — a bare "Stop" matched none of it and fell through to `needs_clarification`. The one path in the system that did persist an opt-out missed the single most common way people opt out.

### 2. Confabulation: reply turns wrote to the patient record, ungrounded and unaudited

Yes — reply turns could write to the care record, on any turn, with no grounding and no audit trail.

After parsing, `handler.ts` applied every model-emitted structured field unconditionally: `medicationUpdates` → `mutations.upsertMedication`, plus `scheduleUpdates`, `careCaseMemoryUpdates` (including the `care_note` category — the care log), `careContactUpdates`, and `coordinationEventUpdates`. Three specific problems:

- **No grounding.** Nothing checked that a medication name, dose, or schedule corresponded to anything a human said. The agent asking "did the dose change too?" and then writing an answer nobody gave was a supported code path. `upsertMedication` patches `dose`/`schedule`/`notes` on any existing row whose name matches, so a phantom insulin dose change would land silently in the record.
- **No audit event.** `medications` had no entry in the `auditEvent` union at all. A medication write left no trace anywhere — it could not be reviewed, attributed, or reconstructed after the fact. This is what makes the phantom-dose bug the serious one: it is both possible and invisible.
- **No actor gate.** The medication and memory writes were not gated on `careContactReply`, so a care contact answering "can you cover Tuesday?" could mutate the care recipient's medication record. (By contrast, the outreach inference path *was* gated on `!careContactReply`, and both outreach and calendar already had honesty guards — `doesReplyClaimOutreachExecution`, `doesReplyClaimCalendarWrite`. Medications had neither.)

The "system glitch" assertion is the same class of failure in the reply channel: a fabricated causal explanation for real, correct system behavior.

### 3. Idempotency: no key, no diff

The only duplicate guard was: scan `auditLogs` from the last two days for a `response_sent` row whose `details.triggerMessage` string equals `"scheduled_digest"`, and compare its timestamp's local date to today. That is a heuristic over log text, not a key. It also says nothing about content.

And the content genuinely never changed. `composeDigestMessage` produces `Good morning, {name}. / Today: {items}. / Text me if anything changes.` — no date, no diff against yesterday. For a `recurrence: "daily"` item like an 8 AM insulin reminder, the composed body is byte-identical forever. Three identical sends was the system working as specified.

---

## Changes

**Stop-intent persistence**
- New `notificationSuppressions` table: care-case scoped, channel-aware, with the request text, a scope hint, and the source message id.
- `convex/lib/stopIntent.ts` — `detectStopIntent` / `detectResumeIntent`, resolved in `handleMessage` **before the model runs**. The suppression row and the confirmation text are produced by the same code path, so the reply cannot diverge from the state again.
- `sendDailyDigest`, `sendScheduleItemReminder`, and coordinator status updates in `dispatchCoordinationFollowUps` all read suppression state before sending, and audit the skip. `claimDelivery` re-checks it in the same transaction that reserves the send, so a STOP landing mid-send still wins.
- `classifyCareContactReply` now uses the shared detector, so a bare "Stop" from a care contact deactivates them.
- Bare-keyword matches must be the whole message. "The doctor said to stop her metformin" and "can you stop by at 3" are care instructions; muting an insulin thread on either would be its own incident. Likewise "remove me" / "take me off" need a messaging target, so "take me off Tuesday's shift" is not an opt-out. Covered by tests.
- `cancel` / `end` / `quit` are conventional SMS opt-out keywords but are **not** honored bare — in a care thread "Cancel" much more often means "cancel that appointment". They are honored in phrase form ("cancel these texts"). Flagging in case you want them added back.
- Suppression covers scheduled, agent-initiated sends only. Replies to an inbound message are never suppressed — going silent on someone who just texted us would be worse than the bug being fixed.

**Confabulation guard**
- `convex/lib/careWriteGuards.ts` — a medication write must trace back to human-authored text (this turn plus the most recent inbound turns). An invented name, dose, or clock time is dropped and audited rather than written. Numbers are compared as whole values, and every component must be accounted for, so a model-authored "5 mg" does not pass against a human's "25 mg" and "08:00" does not pass against "08:30"; clock times normalize so "8am" and "08:00" match. Multi-turn flows still work ("add her Lantus" → "10 units").
- Care contact reply turns cannot write medications at all, however well-grounded.
- Medication writes now emit `medication_updated` / `medication_write_blocked` audit events.
- `doesReplyClaimNotificationStop` rewrites any reply claiming messages were stopped when no suppression is active — same shape as the existing calendar and outreach honesty guards. Offers and questions ("want me to stop those?") are not treated as claims.
- `care_case` memory entries are stamped with provenance back to their source turn and actor.
- Prompt additions telling the model it cannot stop messages by saying so, not to explain past messages as a "glitch" without evidence in history, and not to write a dose it asked about but did not receive. The prompt is the soft layer; the guards above are the enforcement.

**Idempotency**
- New `notificationDeliveries` table. Sends **claim a dedupe key before going out**: `dai

## Summary

Ports two security fixes from upstream `in2code/powermail`'s `typo3-v13` branch (13.2.1 security release) that this fork's `typo3-v14` branch never received:

- `7e25b498` — Fluid viewhelper injection via sender name/email fields. Fixed with an allowlist (`RestrictedStringRenderer` + `ViewHelperPolicy`), config key `allowedViewHelpersInParsedStrings` (default `f:cObject`).
- `eed587e9` — Backend module IDOR: `ModuleController::initializeAction()` resolved the page id from the parsed body before query params with a raw `(int)` cast and no access check, letting a non-admin backend editor list/export another page's submissions (sender names, emails, IPs, answers) via a foreign or non-canonical page id. Kept that port and took upstream's `fluidParseString()` as-is — `RestrictedStringRenderer` already targets the same v14 view APIs.

author: ptal
body:
Removes `interpret`, `interpret_tell`, `interpret_ask` and the four `deinterpret` overloads from `PIR`. They now live in Turbo's `interpretation.hpp` as free functions (ptal/turbo#33). PIR no longer depends on a logical formula representation.

`subdomain()` is added so the interpretation, now outside the class, can reach the sub-domain in order to interpret the constraints PIR cannot represent itself.

Depends on lattice-land/lala-core#11.

### Tests

`pir_test.cpp` builds every domain it tests with `create_and_interpret_and_tell`, so it follows the interpretation into Turbo (`tests/src/pir_interpret_test.cpp`, part of Turbo's 106-test suite).

`bound_consistency_test.hpp` and the three tests built on it (`TernaryPropagatorSoundnessTest`, `TernaryPropagatorCompletenessTest`, `TernaryPropagatorSoundnessExhaustiveTest`) are **deleted**, not moved. They were already disabled on the working tree, and not because they fail: a five-minute partial run produced 1.2M lines of output and zero assertion failures — it simply had not finished. Each of the 23³ domain triples per predicate re-formats a FlatZinc string, re-parses it, re-interprets it and prints the normalized formula, for 14 predicates; the exhaustive variant is ~231³ iterations per predicate.

Their intent is worth keeping. Reviving them means building the domain once and re-`embed`ing per iteration instead of re-parsing a formula each time (the exhaustive variant already does this with `snapshot`/`restore`; the other two do not), and dropping the `printf` from the interpretation helper. `deduce_and_test2` survives inline in Turbo's `pir_interpret_test.cpp`, used by the small `int_ediv` case.

**This leaves lala-pc without tests.** The propagator tests are really about PIR's *deduction*, not about interpretation — they only used a formula to build the domain — so they belong here rather than in Turbo once rewritten. The CMake test wiring is deliberately left in place for that.

author: mrkeithelliott
body:
`datasheet.generate_guidance` was failing **roughly two runs in three** against a real datasheet. It skips in CI for want of an API key, so nothing ever reported it.

## Two gaps, compounding

The model occasionally returns a malformed array, notices, and writes the correct one after it:

```
["Figure 13-1 shows a typical application circuit...","page":8]

Wait, must output JSON array only.

[{"quote":"Figure 13-1 shows a typical application circuit...","page":8}]
```

The right answer is sitting there and `json.loads` cannot reach it. And unlike `component_pipeline`, which has retried extraction since SPEC-202, **this route had no retry** — so one bad response failed the whole job.

## Fixed upstream, where the gap actually was

AgentFlow had no JSON-response parser, so this repo had hand-rolled a weaker one **twice**. [agentflow#13](https://github.com/GittieLabs/agentflow/pull/13) adds `parse_json_response`, now on PyPI as 0.12.0 and pinned here. The retry mirrors `component_pipeline`'s existing shape, and never retries a citation failure — that is the model being wrong about the datasheet, not about JSON.

## Measured, not asserted

**5 of 5** consecutive live runs pass, against a baseline of roughly 2 in 3 failing. Five runs cannot distinguish a real fix from a quiet afternoon at the provider, so what supports it beyond the count is that one failure shape is now handled deterministically and pinned by a test, and the other is what the retry exists for.

Frozen sidecar re-built and probed — 81 routes, no degraded modules, which is itself the check that 0.12.0 is really bundled: the old version would fail `datasheet_guidance`'s import and show as degraded.

## Two things the existing tests stopped me doing

`expect=dict` broke `search_components`, whose response is legitimately an array — the `-> dict` annotation had been describing one of its two callers. `expect=list` turned `test_014`'s documented "a non-list response is a real empty result" into an error. Both constraints dropped; two tests I did not write prevented a behaviour change disguised as a bug fix.

## Correction worth recording

I reported this to the maintainer as an AgentFlow bug. It wasn't — the log line reads `agentflow.workflow: Node validate failed`, but the exception came from this repo. Reading which module raised it would have cost one grep.

author: bruno-pannunzio
body:
## Summary

Makes the histogram usable for comparing distributions that differ in scale or in
kind. Curves can be normalized to their own maximum, several component fractions
can be plotted at once (each in its own layer's colours), and merging now pools
layers rather than blending different quantities into one meaningless curve. The
statistics table names the quantity it reports and widens into one column block
per quantity. Grouping moves onto the analysed image layer, so one grouping is
shared by every histogram tab and by the Plot Settings tab, with group colours
and colormaps translating between the dialogs. Also fixes three bugs found along
the way: stale phasor-center dots, contour group styles lost on save, and
component renames reaching only the primary image.

Closes #379
Closes #380 

## Normalize to maximum

New option in the Histogram Settings dialog: every curve is divided by its own
peak, so distributions whose pixel counts differ by orders of magnitude can be
compared on one scale. Applies in all display modes (the SD band is scaled with
its curve), labels the y axis *(normalized)*, and scales the CSV export to match.
Batch exports honour it too.

## Several component distributions at once

The **Component** selector above the histogram and statistics table is now
checkable, so more than one component fraction can be plotted at a time.

- The fraction range slider spans every checked component and layer.
- Each component's curve is drawn in the colormap of its own fraction layer and
  follows it live. A Linear Projection pair is drawn in solid colours instead,
  since its two colormaps are mirror images; **Curve colours** in the settings
  dialog switches between colormap and solid and picks a colour per component.
- The fraction image layers follow the selection: checking a component shows its
  layers and hides the ones whose component is unchecked.

## Merging pools layers, never quantities

Merged mode draws one curve per quantity, each averaging only its own layers,
and Grouped mode draws one curve per group **and** quantity (group colour,
dash pattern per quantity) — three components in two groups give six outlines
whatever the number of layers per group. The CSV export and the statistics
follow the same split. Tabs plotting a single quantity are unaffected.

## Statistics table

Columns now name the quantity they summarise (*FRET efficiency Mean*, *Lifetime
(ns) Center of Mass*, *Component 1 Median*), carrying into the CSV exports. With
several quantities on screen the table widens instead of repeating rows: one row
per analysed layer or group, one column block per quantity.

## Grouping is shared across tabs

Groups are stored on the analysed image layer rather than on the derived output
layer, so one grouping is shared by the Component, FRET and Phasor Mapping
histograms and by the grouped contour and phasor-center modes of the Plot
Settings tab. The group rows list the analysed layers — one entry per layer even
when several components of it are plotted — and a layer's group covers every
curve derived from it. Colours and colormaps bridge between dialogs: a group
given a colormap shows up elsewhere in that colormap's top colour, and a group
created with a solid colour is drawn by the contour plot as a ramp from it.

## Fixes

- Phasor center dots outlived the selection that produced them: unchecking a
  group's layers could change the primary layer and switch centers off without
  clearing the dots. Centers are now refreshed on every plot update, so a group
  whose layers are all unchecked loses its dot while the others keep theirs.
- A contour group's style never survived being written to layer metadata (the
  dialog writes `mode`, the metadata read `style`), so restored groups silently
  reverted to the default styling.
- Renaming a component only reached the primary image, leaving the other
  analysed images reporting the old name as a separate component. It now updates
  every image, and the histogram, selector and statistics columns follow.

## Tests and docs

New tests cover normalization, the merged/grouped per-quantity curves and their
exports, the range-slider span, curve colouring, quantity-named and wide
statistics columns, component renaming, layer visibility, shared grouping and
the colour/colormap bridge, plus the phasor-center regressions. Guides updated:
`docs/guides/histogram_statistics.md`, `docs/guides/component_analysis.md`.

body:
Six changes to `/delegates`:

1. **Nav order** — Delegation moves between Create proposal and Security Council. It is something a token holder does, not a council function, and it sat behind two council pages.
2. **One panel** — "Your delegation" and the directory are separated by a rule instead of a panel boundary. They were never independent: the directory re-reads after a delegation change, so the panel you act in was above the panel that answers whether it worked.
3. Search kept.
4. **Sort select removed**; rows stay ordered by voting power. Flagging one thing: the ticket asked for a sort *other* than power precisely because a directory that only ranks by power reads as a leaderboard. At six addresses it makes no difference; if it matters at scale, a column header would restore it without a control in the filter row.
5. **Hide excluded starts checked** — an excluded address can never vote or delegate, so it is noise by default, and the box still shows they exist. Its label was a bare inline `<label>`, which sat the box a few pixels above the inputs beside it; it is a flex row now.
6. **Explorer link is named** — the last column was a bare `↗`. An arrow in a table cell says nothing about where it goes, especially here where the row already links the address to its own profile, so it reads "View on explorer" like the proposal page.

Lint, typecheck, 16/16 tests and build pass.
