author: tallpasolutions
body:
Três pedidos numa mudança só. O primeiro é o grande; os outros dois são da Troca de Poste e vão junto porque tocam a mesma tela.

## 1. Acesso aos módulos por usuário

Até aqui a visibilidade era **código**: `ve_troca_poste` valia `not eh_supervisor or eh_admin`, e mudar quem vê o quê exigia deploy. Os outros cinco módulos não tinham controle nenhum — quem entrava via tudo.

Agora o admin marca em *Configurações → Acesso aos módulos*: 12 usuários × 6 módulos, um Salvar por linha.

⚠️ **A tabela guarda o que foi TIRADO, não o que foi liberado.** É contraintuitivo, e foi decidido assim porque o padrão combinado é "vê tudo até ser configurado": com linhas de liberação, os 12 usuários perderiam o portal no instante do deploy e usuário novo nasceria cego. A tabela se chama `usuario_modulos_bloqueados` para a inversão não passar despercebida em nenhuma query futura.

**Três coisas que não podiam falhar:**

- **o admin nunca perde módulo** — é ele quem edita a lista, e trancá-lo exigiria um UPDATE no banco para destravar;
- **esconder no menu não é permissão** — `modulo_obrigatorio()` fecha a rota com **404**, inclusive as internas do módulo (`/troca-poste/rede.json`, `/troca-poste/os/<id>`). 404 e não 403 pela mesma razão do módulo Ações: 403 confirmaria que a tela existe;
- **quem ficar sem módulo nenhum não pode cair num 404** logo depois de digitar a senha. O pós-login passou a apontar para `dash.home`, que escolhe a primeira tela que a pessoa enxerga, e Configurações nunca entra na lista — é onde cada um troca a própria senha.

**O recorte de DADO do supervisor continua no código.** Ver só o próprio time em Produtividade e IQI é sobre quais linhas ele lê, não sobre qual tela ele abre; liberar o módulo não amplia o que ele enxerga dentro dele.

## 2. Ordens de Serviço mostrava só as críticas

Passou a mostrar todas as do recorte — 39 grupos em vez de 18. A classificação continua ordenando (crítico primeiro) e aparece no badge de cada linha, mas esconder o resto tirava da tela desligamento que a operação quer abrir, inclusive os `indeterminado`, que são exatamente os que esperam revisão. Os KPIs passaram a mostrar o total e, ao lado, quantos são críticos.

## 3. Filtro por tipo de serviço

Novo select na toolbar, ao lado de Risco. Usa `causa_categoria`, **não** o texto de `causa`: o texto cru vem com pontuação variável (`- PROG. - ALTERAÇÃO PARA AMPLIAÇÃO`) e filtrar por ele perderia linha sem erro na tela. São os 5 tipos que a Celesc publica, e o select lista só os **presentes no recorte**, com a contagem — oferecer um tipo que não existe ali leva a pessoa a filtrar e ver tabela vazia sem entender por quê.

Medido em 04/09/2026: ampliação 107, preventiva 38, melhoria 30, corretiva 11 e *SERVICO COMERCIAL,OUTROS ( ESPECIFICAR )* 5. Filtrando por serviço comercial, a aba de OS vai de 39 para 4 grupos.

## Verificação

Permissão exercitada contra produção com um usuário real, e **desfeita no fim** (a tabela terminou com 0 linhas):

| Caso | Resultado |
|---|---|
| sem configuração | as 6 rotas em 200 |
| bloqueando iqi, massivas e troca-poste | as três em **404**, as outras em 200 |
| sidebar servida | os três somem do HTML; os outros ficam |
| rotas internas do módulo bloqueado | `/troca-poste/rede.json` e `/troca-poste/os/x` em 404 |
| admin com tudo bloqueado no banco | as 6 rotas em 200 |
| usuário com TUDO bloqueado | `/` redireciona para `/configuracoes`, que segue 200 |

Navegador contra o Supabase de produção, console limpo: o bloco monta 12 linhas × 6 caixas, todas marcadas (o padrão), com um formulário por usuário; a aba de OS mostra 39 grupos e o filtro de tipo de serviço recorta para 4.

Migration `0014` — **já aplicada em produção**, aditiva, e a tabela nasceu vazia, que é exatamente "todo mundo vê tudo, como antes".

author: detail-app[bot]
body:
**Detail bug report:** [View on Detail](https://app.detail.dev/org_9d5e1ae3-1dc1-48fb-ac64-cc04171ac042/bugs/bug_634a18c8-48d1-4567-9c90-0a896a497ee6)

Closes #10

## Bug

`makeGeometry()` in `src/components/PrimitiveRenderer.tsx` creates the `BufferGeometry` for every primitive asset (cube/sphere/cylinder), mounted by R3F via `<primitive object={geometry} attach="geometry" />`. R3F intentionally does not dispose objects passed via `<primitive>` (their state may be kept outside React), and three.js never reclaims `WebGLBuffer`s from GC — `BufferGeometry.dispose()` is the only way to free the GPU vertex/index buffers.

The disposing `useEffect(() => () => geometry?.dispose(), [geometry])` that lived on the old `<PrimitiveRenderer>` was deleted during the d6f22db refactor (which moved the geometry `useMemo` into a new `PrimitiveEditable` component in `EditableMesh.tsx`) and re-added nowhere. That same commit also added a JSDoc on `makeGeometry` falsely claiming disposal happens "via the `useEffect` cleanup in `EditableMeshBody`" — a cleanup that does not exist.

Result: every unmount of a primitive asset (delete, or toggling paint mode, which swaps `<EditableMesh>` for `<PaintMesh>`) leaked a dead `WebGLBuffer` until page reload, accumulating toward WebGL context loss on long sessions. No error or warning is emitted.

## Fix

- Restored the disposing cleanup where the `useMemo` now lives, in `PrimitiveEditable` (`src/components/EditableMesh.tsx`): `useEffect(() => () => { geometry.dispose(); }, [geometry])`. The `[geometry]` dep re-arms the cleanup if the geometry identity ever changes. This restores exactly what d6f22db removed.
- Deliberately scoped to `PrimitiveEditable` only. `GLBEditable`/`OBJEditable` geometries come from `useGLTF`/`useLoader` caches; disposing them here would over-release the shared loader cache and corrupt re-mounts and sibling assets.
- Corrected the stale JSDoc on `makeGeometry` to point at `PrimitiveEditable`'s `useEffect` cleanup and to note that R3F does not auto-dispose `<primitive>`, so a future maintainer isn't misled into removing the effect again.

## Testing

- New regression test `scripts/verify-primitive-dispose.mts` (matches the existing `verify-*.mts` idiom, including the sibling `verify-persistent-edits.mts` for d6f22db). It guards that `PrimitiveEditable` keeps a disposing `useEffect` keyed on `[geometry]` (the exact line d6f22db removed — a future removal fails the test), that `makeGeometry` remains the allocator, that the JSDoc no longer references the non-existent `EditableMeshBody` cleanup, and behaviorally that `dispose()` fires three's `dispose` event on all three primitive types and that distinct `makeGeometry` calls don't alias (disposing one never disposes a sibling — the property that keeps the GLB/OBJ loader cache out of scope). Stashing the two source files drops the test from 29/29 to 25 pass / 4 fail; restoring returns it to 29/29.
- Routine checks pass: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `npm run verify` (store + physics + collider-input). The sibling mesh-edit regression scripts (`verify-persistent-edits.mts`, `verify-mesh-edit.mts`, `verify-vertex-drag.mts`) are unchanged — no regression to the d6f22db vertex-edit-persistence fix or the mesh-edit pipeline.
- End-to-end (one-off, not committed): a headless WebGL-capable Chromium (Playwright + SwiftShader) against the production `vite preview` build, driving the editor via `window.__editor` and reading three's authoritative `gl.info.memory.geometries` counter (temporary instrumentation, fully reverted before the commit). With the fix, `removeAsset` frees the primitive geometry at the GPU level (geometries drop by exactly 1 per delete and on paint-mode toggle exit); without the fix, `removeAsset` freed 0 geometries and every delete/toggle leaked the cube's geometry (10/10 leak cycles; ~+40 across 20 paint⇄mesh round-trips). Vertex-edit offsets still persist across active-asset switches, so no regression to d6f22db. A separate, pre-existing drei `TransformControls`/gizmo leak (~17 geometries/cycle) appears in both fixed and unfixed builds; it is outside the primitive pipeline this bug covers and is recorded as a follow-up.

`qs.stringify` throws `TypeError` on a `null`/`undefined` element of an `arrayFormat: 'comma'` array when `encodeValuesOnly: true` — the comma branch maps through the raw encoder before the per-element loop, so neither `skipNulls` nor `strictNullHandling` guards it. Màn Sprint đang hiển thị **chuỗi `flow_backend.menu.sprints`** làm phụ đề — cho mọi người mở nó, ở **cả hai ngôn ngữ**.

Khoá đó được `screens/sprints.tsx` gọi và **chưa bao giờ được định nghĩa** trong `messages.ts`. Translator trả về chính khoá khi không tìm thấy, nên nó đi thẳng ra màn hình.

## Tìm ra thế nào

Bằng **ảnh chụp màn hình**, khi tôi xem lại bằng chứng của Wave 5:

```
Nền tảng Két Việt
flow_backend.menu.sprints        ← phụ đề
```

Mọi cổng của suite đều xanh trước đó: `tsc`, `lint`, `audit:terminology`, `audit:ui`, `type-proof`, 133 test. Không cổng nào nhìn thấy được lỗi này.

## Sửa

Hai dòng: định nghĩa `menu.sprints` ở cả `vi` và `en`.

## Phần đáng giá là test

`test/flow-backend-messages.test.ts`, hai khẳng định:

1. **Mọi khoá `flow_backend.<key>` mà màn hình hoặc route gọi tên đều phải tồn tại**, ở cả hai ngôn ngữ. Bốn function key `flow_backend.sync.*` bị loại trừ — chúng dùng chung tiền tố và không có gì khác giống.
2. **Hai ngôn ngữ mang đúng cùng một tập khoá.** Một khoá có ở `vi` mà thiếu ở `en` sẽ fallback im lặng, và đọc ra như tiếng Anh lọt vào màn tiếng Việt chứ không như một lỗi.

Đã kiểm rằng test **fail nếu không có bản sửa** — và nó nêu đúng tên khoá lẫn đúng file:

```
+ 'vi menu.sprints — packages/ketsuite/src/modules/flow_backend/screens/sprints.tsx',
+ 'en menu.sprints — packages/ketsuite/src/modules/flow_backend/screens/sprints.tsx'
```

## Vì sao `audit:terminology` không bắt được

Nó đọc **những chữ đang có**, không đọc **những chữ được gọi mà không có**. Một translator trả lời bằng chính khoá được đưa cho nó tạo ra thứ output mà không phép kiểm nào trên file thông điệp nhìn thấy được — phải đi từ **phía người gọi**.

Đây là khuôn có thể áp cho module khác nếu thấy đáng.

## Đã kiểm tại chỗ

Bộ test Flow 133/133; `format:check`, `lint`, `audit:terminology`, `audit:ui`, `type-proof` sạch.

After merging, nothing else is needed: the vendored `.context/design-system` tree in this pull request was re-synced by the bot, and `design-client sync --check` in CI proves it matches the pin.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>ByteDeskAI/design-system (@​bytedesk/design-client)</summary>

### [`v2.2.1`](https://redirect.github.com/ByteDeskAI/design-system/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#221-2026-09-04)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ByteDeskAI/design-system/compare/v2.2.0...v2.2.1)

##### Fixed

- **Theming now nests completely.** 2.2.0 gave `[data-bd-theme="dark"]` its own declarations so a
  dark region inside a light page resolves dark, but six tokens escaped it. One,
  `--bd-material-ambient-blue`, was simply missing from the dark stamp. The other five —
  `--bd-bg-hover`, `--bd-focus-ring`, `--bd-glow-interactive`, `--bd-overlay-backdrop` and the
  gateway product accent — are derivations that live in the overlay and were declared only on
  `:root`. A custom property is substituted at computed-value time on the element that declares it,
  so a derivation on `:root` resolves once against `:root` and inherits that frozen result inward:
  a nested dark region drew a light focus halo. The generator now works out which overlay
  derivations transitively reach a themed token and restates those inside each stamp, so one added
  later is covered without anyone remembering. This reaches consumers through the shipped component
  layer — `components.css` uses `--bd-focus-ring` twelve times and `--bd-bg-hover` seven — so it
  could not be found by grepping a consumer's own source.
- **Two contract tests that could not fail.** The dark stamp is now asserted to declare the same
  token set as the light stamp in both directions, which the rendered check could not catch: it
  samples four properties and skips entirely without Chrome. The light-subtree assertion compared a
  nested light region against a light-rooted page, where a derivation frozen on `:root` is already
  light — it passed on 2.2.0 whether or not the stamp restated anything. It now hangs off the
  dark-root fixture.

##### Changed

- **Publishing to the CDN takes twelve seconds instead of ten minutes.** The publisher made three
  sequential round trips per object — a HEAD for the immutability check, the PUT, then a GET that
  read the whole body back to verify it — about fifteen hundred requests one at a time. Verification
  now uses the object's ETag, which is R2's own checksum of what it stored, and objects upload
  twelve at a time: 514 objects and 45.7 MB measured at 12.2 seconds against the live bucket, down
  from 607. R2 answers a HEAD with a weak validator (`W/"<md5>"`), so the comparison strips that
  prefix; without it every object looks changed. The discovery catalog, which every consumer
  resolves against, can no longer be moved backwards by a run carrying a lower version — that is
  refused before anything uploads unless `--allow-rollback` says otherwise.

</details>

author: thanhhaixn92
body:
## M08 Production failure — follow-up fix

### Confirmed live failure
On 2026-09-05, Production dispatched:

`sleep 60; printf 'M08-SHOULD-NOT-EXIST\n' > smoke/after-stop.txt`

The command had been running for ~35s when Stop was pressed. After waiting beyond the 60s mutation point, `workspace_list_files` + `workspace_read_file` returned:

`EXISTS M08-SHOULD-NOT-EXIST`

Therefore M08 remains **BLOCKED** on the currently deployed `main` build `7ae2ae2fbf0519dcab2cc46c41eee7b96f8c92f5` until the fixed head is promoted and the live test returns `ABSENT`.

### Root cause and review-driven hardening
The original Stop path could target a different request-scoped sandbox than the one running the MCP command. Successive RED tests and Codex review then exposed additional concurrency/lifecycle gaps:

- RED `33914027420`: Stop killed the Stop-request sandbox instead of the active command sandbox.
- RED `33915139457`: overlapping commands could leave an earlier sandbox alive.
- RED `33916496139`: a synchronous `kill()` throw could prevent later sandboxes from being attempted.
- RED `33917069538`: late command registration after the Stop snapshot, unregistered `sandbox_wait`, and command/checkpoint scope races were all reproduced by dedicated regressions.

### Current implementation
- maintain a process-local, per-conversation registry of active sandbox executions;
- Stop marks a conversation as stopping **before** snapshotting active handles, so late registrations fail closed with `WORKSPACE_STOPPING`;
- kill every distinct active sandbox in parallel and isolate synchronous kill failures per sandbox;
- register `sandbox_wait` for its actual wait execution lifetime;
- register `workspace_run_command` only around the actual shell execution and release the sandbox before checkpoint persistence begins;
- clear the Stop registration barrier only when a new MCP bridge starts for the replacement sidecar;
- use the Stop-request sandbox only as a fallback when no active command sandbox exists;
- preserve stable non-secret Stop result codes and parallel sidecar/platform/sandbox cancellation.

### GREEN evidence
Current head: `39cbb77398cf74d641e1047b4a4d4d55d1584a46`

Quality run `33917623728`: **SUCCESS**
- generated-artifact drift guard: PASS
- typecheck: PASS
- tests: **110/110 PASS**
- production build: PASS
- npm install audit: 563 packages / 0 known vulnerabilities at this point in time

All previously raised Codex review threads have been answered with RED/GREEN evidence and resolved. A fresh `@codex review` has also been requested against the current head.

### Owner approval and remaining live gate
Owner approval to merge was given in the project workflow on 2026-09-05. Source-side gates are green; M08 itself is **not closed** until the protected `main` promotion is deployed, `/build-meta.json` confirms the promoted build identity, and the same delayed-mutation Production test returns `ABSENT` after waiting beyond the mutation deadline.

The separately observed approval UI issue (approval prompt appears only after refresh) and raw `MCP error -32001: [object Object]` cancellation UX remain M10/runtime-browser findings; they are not treated as proof of M08 closure.

author: whispersofj
body:
## Summary

`nzbdav_rclone`'s `command:` is a folded YAML scalar executed by `/bin/sh -c` as **one line**. The `#` rationale lines written *inside* that block were literal content, so the shell treated everything from the first `#` as a comment — silently dropping the vfs/timeout tuning flags and the **entire `--rc` server block** (`--rc-addr`, `--rc-user`, `--rc-pass`).

**Impact found live today:** rclone ran without RC → nzbdav's `vfs/forget` invalidation failed with `Connection refused (nzbdav_rclone:5572)` → the FUSE VFS dir cache went stale → every completed NzbDAV download was invisible to Sonarr at import time → imports failed with *"path does not exist"* and the queue piled up in `importPending`.

## Changes

- Move the tuning rationale out of the block into proper YAML comments above `command:`.
- New offline guard `scripts/check_compose_commands.py`: fails if any rendered service command contains `#` (shell truncation) or if `nzbdav_rclone` drops `--rc-addr=:5572` / `--vfs-cache-max-size=100G`.
- `scripts/test_check_compose_commands.py` covers the real compose + fixtures; wired into `preflight.sh`, `validate.yml`, and `nightly-healthcheck.yml`.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/test_check_compose_commands.py` — all assertions pass
- `scripts/preflight.sh` — ALL CHECKS PASSED (including new `compose commands`)
- `docker compose config` renders the rclone command with no `#` and all flags intact
- actionlint clean on workflow changes

author: impoiler
body:
## Summary

Bifrost now ships first-party Databricks support. This PR adds a guided, multi-step migration dialog that automatically detects when a user has a custom provider named `databricks` and walks them through converting it to the official Databricks provider — preserving keys, network settings, proxy config, and model aliases — without any manual copy-paste.

## Changes

- **`ui/lib/utils/databricksMigration.ts`** — Pure (React-free) orchestration module containing:
  - `isCustomDatabricksProvider` — detects a custom provider named exactly `databricks`
  - `deriveDatabricksWorkspace` — splits a custom base URL into a workspace origin and infers the inference surface (`model_serving`, `ai_gateway`, or `auto`)
  - `extractAuthFromHeaders` — reads a personal access token from an `Authorization: Bearer` extra header, including secret references (`env.*`, `vault.*`)
  - `buildDatabricksMigrationPlan` — constructs a full migration plan from the source provider, its keys, and an optional existing Databricks target; handles keyless providers, masked secrets, name clashes, and existing target merging
  - `runDatabricksMigration` — executes the plan step-by-step with rollback on failure; the normal path only deletes the custom provider after the new one is verified; the name-clash path (source is literally named `databricks`) deletes first and restores from a snapshot if a later step fails
  - `buildMigrationSteps` — produces the ordered step list shown in the progress UI, varying by whether a name clash or existing target is involved

- **`ui/app/workspace/providers/dialogs/databricksMigrationDialog.tsx`** — New dialog component with four stages (`intro → loading → preview → running → finished`):
  - Preview stage shows workspace URL, inference surface selector, per-key token inputs (masked or editable), and provider settings summary
  - Running stage shows live step-by-step progress with status icons
  - RBAC-gated: requires create + update + delete access; dirty-form guard prevents migration while unsaved changes exist

- **`ui/app/workspace/providers/page.tsx`** — Wires the dialog into the providers page:
  - Opens the migration dialog automatically when a custom `databricks` provider is selected, unless the user deferred it for that selection
  - Suppresses the existing "first-party provider available" advisory dialog for Databricks (it gets the richer migration dialog instead)
  - Holds off the "switch to another provider when current is unconfigured" effect while a migration session is active, since the migration intentionally removes the source provider mid-flight
  - On successful migration, navigates to the new Databricks provider and invalidates relevant RTK cache tags

- **`ui/lib/utils/databricksMigration.test.ts`** — Comprehensive unit tests covering detection, URL derivation, auth extraction, secret masking, plan building (keyless, keyed, name-clash, existing-target, warnings), and the full orchestrator (happy path, rollback on key failure, 409 handling, partial success on delete failure, verification failure, refresh-models tolerance).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [x] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [x] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd ui
pnpm i
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

1. Configure a custom provider with the name `databricks` pointing at a Databricks workspace (with a base URL of `https://<workspace>.azuredatabricks.net/serving-endpoints` and an `Authorization: Bearer dapi...` extra header).
2. Select that provider in the UI — the migration dialog should open automatically.
3. Verify the preview shows the correct workspace URL, inferred inference surface, and masked or editable token fields.
4. Click **Migrate** and confirm all steps complete successfully.
5. Confirm the custom provider is removed and the UI navigates to the new first-party Databricks provider.
6. Repeat with a provider that has explicit keys (non-keyless) to verify token re-entry is required for masked secrets.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Security considerations

- Personal access tokens stored as masked literals cannot be read back from the API and are never transmitted during migration; users must re-enter them.
- Secret references (`env.*`, `vault.*`) round-trip as-is and are never logged or displayed in plaintext.
- Proxy passwords and CA certificates that are stored as masked literals are explicitly dropped from the migrated settings with a warning, rather than silently omitted or sent as redacted placeholders.
- The name-clash rollback path restores the source provider from an in-memory snapshot; any key whose secret is masked and for which the user did not provide a value is skipped with an explicit note rather than restored with a broken placeholder.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [ ] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [x] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #62.

## Problem

Issue #44 gave `status:changes-requested` re-review a reliable wake-up via a real GitHub `ready_for_review` event, but a freshly created `status:ready` PR was always opened **Ready**, so round 1's Chief wake still depended solely on GitHub's `opened` PR event plus the (proven-unreliable) `KBH_CHIEF_REVIEW_READY_V1` comment marker — exactly the gap observed on issue #58 / PR #61.

## Fix

Smallest change that reuses issue #44's already-proven mechanism instead of building a second one:

- `claude-agent-bridge.yml`: the `status:ready` branch of the Claude prompt now instructs `gh pr create --draft` (one-argument change, still the already-allowed `Bash(gh pr create *)` rule — no `--allowedTools`/permission-model change).
- Every later step in the Draft → Ready pipeline (issue #44) already only checks the PR's live `isDraft` flag, never the trigger label, so a Draft round-1 PR now flows through the exact same deliverable-gate → Chief-ready-marker → refetch → `gh pr ready` sequence a changes-requested round already uses, producing a real `ready_for_review` event for round 1 too.
- `pr_draft_handoff.py` (the *pre-Claude* Draft conversion for an *existing* PR) is untouched — it still only ever fires for `status:changes-requested`, since round 1 has no PR to convert yet at that point; docstring updated to explain why status:ready remains out of scope.
- `pr_ready_handoff.py`: generalized the "PR already Ready" idempotency check to require the `KBH_PR_READY_TRANSITION_DONE_V1` proof marker for **every** trigger label (previously `status:changes-requested` only) — closing the same fail-open gap Chief's PR #45 review fixed there, now for round 1 too, since round 1 can legitimately reach this branch once it also creates Draft PRs.
- No new workflow steps, no new script module.

## Tests

- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_agent_bridge_pr_ready_handoff` — 61 tests (updated + new: `TestRunde1BrukerSammeOvergangSomChangesRequested`, `TestRunde1DraftPromptIssue62`), all pass.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_agent_bridge_pr_draft_handoff tests.test_agent_bridge_chief_ready_signal tests.test_agent_bridge_deliverable_guard tests.test_agent_bridge_branch_policy tests.test_agent_bridge_labels tests.test_agent_bridge_trigger_guard tests.test_agent_bridge_permission_config` — 162 tests, all pass.
- `pip install -r requirements.txt && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -b` — full suite, 1760 tests, 32 skipped, 0 failures.

## Deliverable checklist (issue #62 scope item 6)

- ✅ First-round PR: Draft → Ready → one review-ready signal/event path (`TestRunde1BrukerSammeOvergangSomChangesRequested`, `TestRunde1DraftPromptIssue62`).
- ✅ Re-review path still works (existing `TestChangesRequestedReadyFailOpen`/`TestVurderReadyFailClosed`/`TestVurderReadyGodkjenner` unchanged, still pass).
- ✅ No duplicate transition on retries (same `KBH_PR_READY_TRANSITION_DONE_V1` idempotency mechanism, now applied uniformly).
- ✅ No auto-merge or scope expansion (`test_allowedtools_utvides_ikke` + unchanged `TestWorkflowKildetekst` merge-command checks).

## Documentation

`docs/development/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`: new section "Round 1 also uses the Draft -> Ready lifecycle (V1, issue #62)"; the superseded "Round 1 / initial-review safety (issue #44 requirement)" paragraph is kept verbatim as historical record with a pointer to the new section, per this repo's convention of not rewriting prior fix-round history.

## Assumptions / unresolved questions

- Whether a live round-1 Draft PR actually produces a `ready_for_review` event the native Work task reliably wakes on can only be confirmed by a real, controlled round-1 E2E on a live issue — the same honest limit already noted throughout AGENT_WORKFLOW.md for every prior Chief-ready signal iteration. Nothing here claims that E2E has already passed.
- Left as PR #45/issue #44 already did: the hourly `Kvernhaug Approval Watch` remains the fallback if this event is ever missed.

Opened as **Draft**, matching the very mechanism this PR implements — the Bridge will flip a normal round's PR to Ready automatically once its own gates pass; this one is Claude-authored infra work, so please flip it to Ready for review manually once you're ready for Chief review.

author: eth-interchained
body:
## Summary
Embedded durability parity with `nedbd`, and the Node exit-flush wrapper actually ships and works. v2.8.5.

## The defect (found by CHALK / Sports-Rater, 2026-09-04)
Fan writes acknowledged with a hash by an embedded `NedbCore.open()` store were gone after `kill -9`. Reproduced in a controlled trial on 2.8.4.

**Root cause 1 — no ticker in the bindings.** `nedbd` has always run `start_manifest_ticker(db, 1000)`; the napi and pyo3 `open()` paths never started one, so the id-index WAL + MANIFEST were flushed only by exit hooks. SIGKILL / OOM / power loss runs no hook → every write since open lost, unbounded.

**Root cause 2 — the Node wrapper never shipped and could not have worked.** `index.js` (exit flush on SIGINT/SIGTERM/exit) assigns `NedbCore.open = …`, but the napi static is non-writable + non-configurable → throws on load. And the release workflow's `napi build` wrote the generated loader to `index.js`, overwriting the wrapper — the published package carried no exit flush at all, so DURABILITY.md's "automatic on durable open" was false for every npm embedder.

## Fix
- `Db::embedded_flush_interval_ms()` — `NEDB_FLUSH_MS` (default 1000 ms, min 50, `0`/`off` disables); `nedb-node` and `nedb-py` `open()` start the ticker. Contract: **an acknowledged write is on disk within one tick, or at exit — whichever comes first.**
- `index.js` wraps by subclass (own static shadows the parent's non-writable one). CI builds with `--js native.js --dts native.d.ts`; a wrapper gate fails the build if `index.js` is the generated loader; the smoke gate now also runs `test/durability.test.mjs`.
- `test/durability.test.mjs`: SIGKILLed child keeps its write (ticker) · ticker-off SIGKILL loses it (negative control) · ticker-off SIGTERM keeps it (wrapper).
- docs (DURABILITY.md, README), COMMITS.md, version 2.8.5 in all nine version sites.

## Verified
- `cargo check` (core, nedb-node, nedb-py); `cargo test -p nedb-engine --lib` 65/65; `npm run build` (linux-x64); `npm test` = smoke (five acts) + durability (3/3).
- Production-shaped: CHALK's `serve` with the 2.8.5 addon swapped in → fan write acknowledged → `kill -9` 3 s later → restart → **FOUND**. Same sequence on 2.8.4 → GONE.
- Not built here: macOS/Windows addons and Python wheels (CI matrix + Codemagic on the tag).

body:
Executes ADR-052 T5 via `/quality-harness:adr-execute`. `adr-lint` PASS, fence exit 0, two killed mutants, `go test ./...` exit 0. Stacked on #232 (merged as cd82000).

## What changed

- `Repo` carries `db` (writer) and `reader`; `NewRepo(reader, writer)`. Every read method's handle moved to the reader — 74 lines across twelve files, **derived from the AST** (each method classified by the gorm write verbs its body reaches) rather than from a hand list.
- **A read inside a `Transaction` stays on the transaction.** `repoOn(tx)` builds a `Repo` whose reader is `tx`; the three `&Repo{db: tx}` literals use it. Without it the ADR-045 relocation's read inside `Repo.Update` dereferenced a nil reader — the exact read-then-write the task's S6 names.
- The composition root selects the split: `buildServicesWith` passes `svc.rdb` on the serving path and `gdb` for both on the inspection path (already `query_only` end to end). CLI paths and the mcptest harness pass one handle as both (S5).
- **The palace test fixture is strict**: `newTestServiceWith` opens a `query_only` twin over the same file, so the whole existing palace suite proves no read writes and no transaction runs on the reader. `TestReadMethodsUseTheReadHandle` additionally closes the reader to prove routing (reads succeed on either handle, so success alone cannot see a reader field nobody consults). `TestEveryTransactionUsesTheWriteHandle` drives relocation, correction, ending, fact supersession, hallway recompute and wing merge against the strict reader.

## Mutants

- constructor ignores the reader → the closed-reader check sees `Get` keep answering
- `moveMemory` opens its transaction on the reader → the relocation fails readonly

## Not in this PR

T6 (the source-level gate) follows on this branch or the next.

author: frankzk
body:
El aviso decía **«5 leads en hora dorada»** y su propio botón, al lado, decía **«Ver la última hora (8)»**. Dos cifras contradictorias a diez centímetros una de otra: la asesora no tiene forma de saber cuál mirar, y deja de fiarse de las dos.

## No era un fallo de cálculo, era el diseño

El aviso contaba solo carrito e interés (5); el botón contaba la hora entera (8). Lo justifiqué en #542 con que meter conversó y frío llenaría el aviso de ruido —son 243 leads/día contra 168 de los otros dos— y el argumento estaba mal por dos motivos:

1. **Es sobre la cola entera y no aplica dentro de la hora**, donde la población es de un puñado. Medido ahora mismo: 5 de interés, 2 conversó, 1 frío.
2. **El valor va al revés de lo que supuse.** En Kenku, dentro de la primera hora:

| segmento | <1 h | 1-6 h | 6-24 h | +24 h |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| conversó | **16,7 %** | 4,8 % | 3,5 % | 1,5 % |
| frío | **11,3 %** | 8,1 % | 5,8 % | 0,1 % |

16,7 % y 11,3 % están **por encima de un `interes` de 6-24 h (12,9 %)** y muy por encima de casi toda la cola. Esconderlos del aviso ocultaba leads que sí conviene llamar.

## Qué cambia

- El total pasa a ser el de la hora completa y el desglose dice qué hay dentro: **«8 leads en hora dorada · 5 de interés · 2 conversó · 1 frío»**. Se omiten los ceros, así que lo que se pinta siempre suma el total.
- El botón ya no lee `edadCounts` —que se calcula sobre otra base faceteada— sino el mismo `goldenTally`. Ahora dice «Ver estos 8».
- Al filtrar, **limpia el segmento**: el aviso cuenta sin mirar el chip activo, así que con un segmento puesto la lista habría mostrado menos filas que el número del botón. El mismo desajuste, un clic más tarde.

## Verificación

5 mutaciones nuevas, las 5 caen:

| # | mutación | resultado |
|---|---|---|
| M22 | `tallyGolden` vuelve a contar solo carrito e interés en el total | 3 caen |
| M23 | el botón vuelve a leer el contador del chip | 2 caen |
| M24 | al filtrar ya no se limpia el segmento | 1 cae |
| M25 | `goldenBreakdown` deja de omitir los ceros | 2 caen |
| M26 | el desglose se pinta en otro orden (frío antes que carrito) | 1 cae |

Dos de ellas son guardas de que **las dos cifras salen del mismo conteo**, que es exactamente la propiedad que se había roto.

`tsc --noEmit` limpio · `next build` limpio · suite completa **3.325 tests, todos verdes** — incluidos los dos de `test/return-recovery.test.ts` que estaban rojos antes y quedaron arreglados en #543.

Rebasado sobre `main` después de #542 y #543; las 51 líneas que #543 añadió a `components/leads.tsx` están intactas.

author: dav-1987
body:
На 390px админка рендерилась шириной 781px — вдвое шире экрана. «Сохранить» была полностью за правым краем, у строки товара название сжималось в ноль, а фото нельзя было ни переставить, ни удалить: HTML5 drag на тач не срабатывает, а кнопки «Заменить/Удалить» показывались только при наведении мыши.

## Что сделано

- **Панель:** в строке остаётся «Сохранить», остальное («Заявки», «История», «Пересобрать сайт», «Выйти») — в меню «⋯». Предупреждение о несохранённых правках — отдельной строкой.
- **Строки категории и товара:** название обрезается вместо того, чтобы выталкивать кнопки за экран; действия строки, а также видимость и наличие, уходят в такое же меню.
- **Фото:** 3 колонки вместо 4, тап по плитке открывает меню — заменить, удалить, левее/правее и новое «Сделать обложкой» (раньше обложка назначалась только перетаскиванием на первое место).
- **Контролы:** 16px текст и 44px тап-таргеты ниже `sm:`, подписи читаемые.

## Измерено (390×844)

| | было | стало |
|---|---|---|
| вылет вправо | 391 px | 0 px |
| шрифт контролов | 12 px | 16 px |
| тап-таргеты < 44px | 189 | 18 |

Десктоп намеренно не тронут: та же разметка, и замер (0px вылета, 12px контролы, те же счётчики тап-таргетов) совпадает со снимком до правок.

## Тесты

522 прошли (было 488). Новое: `RowActions.test.jsx`, `ProductImagesEditor.test.jsx`, `CatalogEditor.test.jsx`, плюс блок в `ProductEditor.test.jsx`.

## Инструмент

`scripts/shot-admin.mjs` (`npm run shot:admin`) снимает админку на любой ширине без пароля: отвечает на `/api/*` фикстурами из репозитория и глушит любые записи, так что прогон не может тронуть боевой каталог. Оба бага, найденные по ходу — попап, обрезанный своей обёрткой, и попап, вылезающий за правый край, — нашлись именно им.

author: felixarntz
body:
## Background

ACP-backed harness adapters without a native system prompt mapping (such as Grok Build and fx) previously fell back to prepending instructions to the first user message. This is obviously fragile across multi-turn sessions. But there is a better solution: for harness adapters where the underlying SDKs do not support passing system instructions, we can still rely on each runtime's native filesystem-based instruction discovery (such as `.fx/AGENTS.md`).

## Summary

This PR adds support for synchronizing session instructions via the filesystem in ACP harness adapters and introduces a reusable `writeInstructions` utility:

- Add `writeInstructions` in `harness/utils` to safely write and update instructions in a relative file within `$HOME`, preserving pre-existing user content and cleaning up when instructions are removed.
- Add `{ type: 'filesystem', path: string }` instruction mapping support to `harness-acp`, synchronizing instructions on prompt and continue turns and suppressing in-prompt instruction guidance.
- Configure `harness-grok-build` (`.grok/AGENTS.md`) and `harness-fx` (`.fx/AGENTS.md`) to use filesystem instruction mapping.
- Update ACP documentation and example harness implementations to cover filesystem-based instruction mappings.

## End-to-End Verification

Verified via e2e tests for ACP backed harness adapters.

author: isaacjgferreira
august2111
body:
Port::FullWrite() asserted that every Write() call moved at least one byte.  The Windows serial port does not promise that: its writes run with a total timeout of one second (SetRxTimeout()), and when the driver cannot get the data out in time - a USB serial adapter still coming up right after the machine did, while the device drivers already send their initialisation - WriteFile() completes with zero bytes.  A debug build then died in the assertion ("nbytes > 0"), a release build spun on the port until FullWrite's own timeout.

Treat a zero-byte write as what it is: nothing happened yet.  Keep trying until the caller's timeout expires, with a short pause so that a port returning at once does not turn the loop into a busy one.

## Summary

`.claude/settings.local.json` records every approved agent tool call verbatim,
so a credential that appears in a command line gets written into it.

That is not hypothetical. An audit of this machine found **live GitHub App
installation tokens** frozen into `Bash(export GH_TOKEN='ghs_...')` allow-rules
in five such files across the fleet — written there when a command that a
`PreToolUse` hook had prefixed with a freshly minted token was approved. The
tokens' one-hour TTL was the only thing bounding the exposure; no control
actually stopped a credential reaching disk.

Until now the only thing keeping this file out of git was a developer's
machine-local `core.excludesFile`. That protects one machine, not the repo — a
fresh clone, a CI checkout, or a differently-configured workstation had no
guard at all. This ignores it in-repo, where the protection travels with the
code.

AffineDrift already had this rule; this brings the rest of the fleet in line.

No functional change; `.gitignore` only.

author: freekh
body:
Investigation of the `remoteFiles.spec.ts` CI flake. It turned out to be **half test race, half real product defect**, and the product half is the more serious one.

## The mechanism

CI's browser log named it exactly:

```
Current remote file bucket is not available
  { currentRemoteFileBucket: null, remoteFiles: { status: 'loading' } }
```

`status: 'loading'` means the `GET /remote/settings` request was **still in flight** when the file was picked — evidence, not inference.

A remote gallery cannot upload until several things have happened after intake:

1. schemas arrive (`schema:init`)
2. an effect computes `requiresRemoteFiles`
3. an effect fires `GET /remote/settings` and sets `status: "loading"`
4. the response sets `status: "ready"`
5. `useCurrentRemoteFileBucket` picks a bucket **in a further effect**

`openHttpStudio` returns at step 0. All three upload tests in the file then call `setInputFiles` immediately, so all three carry the race — one happened to lose.

## The product defect

`ModuleGallery.handleUpload` did two bad things when the bucket wasn't ready yet:

- **Cleared the input** (`ev.target.value = ""`), so the upload was *lost*, not delayed. There is no retry.
- Told the editor **"contact support"** for a state that resolves in milliseconds.

A real user quick enough to click the upload button during that window hits this. Measured with `/remote/settings` held for 5 s: **zero uploads after 15 s**, error banner shown.

Fixed by distinguishing the states — `loading`/`not-asked` is transient and now says so, `inactive` remains a real error — and by not offering the control at all until an upload can work (`uploadDisabled` on the gallery's upload button).

## The test fix

`uploadWhenReady` waits for the upload button to be enabled before handing over the file.

The button rather than the response, deliberately: it is downstream of **both** the response and the bucket-picking effect, so waiting on the response alone would still leave a render to race. It is also a boundary a person can see — the Studio does not offer the control until it works — rather than a reach into client state, per `e2e/README.md`.

## Verification

Two assumptions I had to measure rather than assume, both of which turned out **false** and would have produced a broken fix:

| assumption | measured |
|---|---|
| `setInputFiles` waits for `disabled` to clear | **No** — sets files on a disabled input after 95 ms |
| a disabled file input won't fire `change` | **It does** — `handleUpload` runs anyway |

So disabling the input alone would have fixed nothing for the test. The explicit wait is required.

Mechanism and fix proven under identical conditions, with `/remote/settings` held 5 s:

| | result |
|---|---|
| old shape (`setInputFiles` immediately) | `refs=[]` after 15 s, error banner shown |
| new shape (`uploadWhenReady`) | uploads, gets a proper `https://remote.val.build/file/p/…` ref |

Also green: full `chromium-http` `remoteFiles.spec.ts` (4/4), and `media.spec.ts` + `gallery-backed-image.spec.ts` (23 tests) — local galleries are unaffected because `canUpload` is `true` wherever remote is not required. `lint`, `format`, `typecheck` clean.

author: azimafroozeh
body:
## What & why

**TL;DR:** To turn Arrow batches into JSON we kept our own conversion layer: two hand-written encoders that copy every value into a `serde_json::Value` before serializing it. Arrow already ships that conversion as `arrow-json`, typed at each cell's own width. Using it deletes both encoders and the copy: less code, faster output, and the narrow-float bug class cannot come back. What OmniGraph still owns is small: the `base64:` blob substitution, a date-range check, and the export line envelope. Exact types come from Arrow IPC on request. Three implementation PRs follow this one.

This PR adds RFC 0051, JSON output via Arrow: every JSON body OmniGraph writes for graph data becomes the `arrow-json` rendering of the result batches with the crate's default options, replacing the two hand-written encoders; a client that needs exact types requests Arrow IPC instead.

- Motivation: the query-result encoder and the entity-fetch/export encoder disagree on the spelling of several types, and both widen every cell through `serde_json::Value`; #618 is that shape made visible, since the `F32` fix has to land in both encoders.
- The RFC fixes the contract as a per-type spelling table plus a complete per-phase list of the spelling changes a JSON consumer can observe; `arrow-json` is pinned by the lock file and an upgrade that changes a spelling is treated as a wire change.
- OmniGraph keeps three pieces of its own: the `base64:` blob substitution on export and entity fetch, a date-range check before the writer, and the export line envelope.
- Three phases, one PR each, independently revertible: query results; entity fetch and export; Arrow IPC selected by `Accept` on the query routes.
- Registry: one row added; the next available number moves from 0050 to 0052 (0050 is held by the `rfc/0050-engine-crate-topology` branch, 0047 and 0048 by #606).

## Backing issue / RFC

- [x] Is an RFC PR: `docs/rfcs/0051-json-output-via-arrow.md` (no issue; maintainer-track RFC)

## Checklist

- [x] Change is focused (one RFC file plus its registry row and next-number bump)
- [x] Tests added/updated for behavior changes (N/A, docs-only; the RFC names the gates each implementation phase carries: a differential test over every Arrow type, the RFC 0045 corpus, the export round trip)
- [x] Public docs updated if user-facing surface changed (N/A; nothing user-facing changes in this PR, the RFC's Rollout names the OpenAPI and user-doc updates for phase 3)
- [x] Reviewed against docs/dev/invariants.md — no Hard Invariant weakened, no deny-list item hit (the RFC's Invariants section covers 8, 9, 10, 12, 13; the "swallowed errors" deny-list entry is the shape the RFC removes)

## Local verification

- `python3 scripts/check-docs.py`: OK, 125 Markdown files checked (the CI "Verify documentation structure and RFC registry" step)
- `git diff --check upstream/main`: clean
- `cargo check --workspace`: not run, docs-only change, no Rust file touched

## Notes for reviewers

- Writer defaults everywhere: no date format strings, null keys omitted from row objects, non-finite floats written as `null`. Each default is a spelling change listed in the phase table; the alternative of per-type overrides was rejected because every override is OmniGraph deciding a spelling, which is the thing being removed.
- Two inputs that succeed silently today become typed errors: a query whose return names collide (the old encoder collapsed them to the last value; the writer would emit both keys) and a `Date` or `DateTime` count outside the formatter's range (`arrow-json` writes an `ERROR:` string with `Ok` for those, so OmniGraph checks the range itself).
- `ReadOutput.rows` and `LegacyReadOutput.rows` change type to `RawValue` in phase 1: the OpenAPI schema is unchanged, Rust consumers of `omnigraph-api-types` see the type change.
- The spelling table and the phase rows describe `arrow-json` 58.3.0's actual output, not a reading of its source; the differential test in Evidence pins them.
- Phase 1 assumes the #618 fix has landed; if it has not, phase 1 carries the engine-encoder half of that fix.
- Number: 0051 assumes 0050 stays reserved by the `rfc/0050-engine-crate-topology` branch; if that branch opens no PR, this RFC takes 0050 and the registry line moves to 0051.

author: anasokasha-chambaam
body:
Adds **Cloudflare Workers** as a second deploy target alongside Vercel, using the OpenNext adapter and targeting the `triplet-ai` Worker that already exists in the dashboard. Both hosts stay first-class.

> [!WARNING]
> **Do not merge until the dashboard settings at the bottom are in place.** Workers Builds is connected to this repo, so merging triggers a build immediately. Without the build command and variables set, that first build fails.

All version claims were **verified live on 2026-09-04** against `nodejs.org/dist`, `registry.npmjs.org`, the GitHub advisory API, and the Cloudflare/OpenNext/pnpm docs — not from memory.

---

## 1. The deploy gate came first: Next 15.1.12 is on a dead line

Querying the advisory API for `next` returned 64 advisories. Split into the two tiers:

**(a) Fixed on the current 15.1 line — one, already clear:**
`GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf` (high, RSC deserialization DoS), fixed in 15.1.12.

**(b) No fix exists on the 15.1 line — this is what makes it EOL.** Their lowest 15.x fix is 15.5.16 or higher, so no 15.1 patch could ever clear them:

| Advisory | Severity | Lowest 15.x fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x` — SSRF in Server Actions | High | 15.5.21 |
| `GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4` — SSRF via rewrite destination | High | 15.5.21 |
| `GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj` — DoS in App Router Server Actions | High | 15.5.21 |
| `GHSA-26hh-7cqf-hhc6` — middleware bypass (segment prefix) | High | 15.5.18 |
| `GHSA-mg66-mrh9-m8jx` — DoS via connection exhaustion | High | 15.5.16 |
| `GHSA-c4j6-fc7j-m34r` — SSRF via WebSocket | High | 15.5.16 |
| `GHSA-8h8q-6873-q5fj` — DoS with Server Components | High | 15.5.16 |
| `GHSA-267c-6grr-h53f`, `GHSA-492v-c6pp-mqqv`, `GHSA-36qx-fr4f-26g5` — middleware bypasses | High | 15.5.16 |
| ~20 more (cache poisoning, XSS, image-optimizer DoS) | Med/Low | 15.5.13–15.5.21 |

**Decision: `next@15.5.25`.** The binding floor across both tiers is 15.5.21; 15.5.25 is the newest patch on that line.

**Why not Next 16.** `16.3.4` is `latest` and also clears everything (floor 16.2.11), but it is a higher line than the lowest that clears both tiers, and a major bump brings route-prop and lint-config churn for no security gain here. 15.5.25 also sits inside the adapter's peer range, so the major upgrade is genuinely optional. **Why not 14.** Rejected outright — `GHSA-89xv` and `GHSA-p9j2` have no 14.x fix at all.

## 2. Version choices, and what was excluded

| Package | Pinned | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node | `24.20.0` (unchanged) | Newest `nodejs.org/dist` entry whose `lts` is a codename ("Krypton"). Already correct. |
| **Node 26 — excluded** | — | `26.8.1` exists but `lts: false`. Per `Release/main/schedule.json` it **becomes LTS on 2026-10-28**. Not yet. |
| pnpm | `11.25.0` (unchanged) | `dist-tags.latest`. Surfacing rather than silently taking: `latest-12` is `12.3.4`, published the same day. pnpm 12 is not on `latest`, and a same-day release would trip the release-age gate anyway. |
| `@opennextjs/cloudflare` | `1.20.6` | `latest`. `peerDependencies.next` is `>=15.5.24 <16 \|\| >=16.3.3` — 15.5.25 falls inside. |
| `wrangler` | **`4.128.0`, not `4.129.0`** | Deliberate. The adapter peer is `^4.125.0`. `4.129.0` was ~7 hours old and pnpm 11's `minimumReleaseAge` (default `1440` min) would have blocked it, forcing a `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entry that should not be committed. 4.128.0 clears the gate on its own. |
| `@cloudflare/next-on-pages` | **never an option** | Confirmed deprecated on npm (`"Please use the OpenNext adapter instead"`), repo archived, and its peer range caps at `next <=15.5.2`. It could not support 15.5.25. It was not installed here, so there was nothing to remove. |

## 3. Runtime changes — required, and not caught by any build

Three things in this repo are documented Workers failures that a green build hides.

**`lib/dbConnect.ts` read `MONGODB_URI` at module scope and threw if absent.** On Workers the environment is populated per request, so that took the worker down before it could serve anything. Moved inside `dbConnect()`.

**`lib/dbConnect.ts` cached the connection on `global` across requests** — the exact pattern Cloudflare names as the cause of `Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request`. **Bypassing that cache alone was not sufficient**, which only surfaced by actually running it: the models in `lib/models` register on the *default mongoose singleton*, which keeps its own connection state across requests. `mongoose.connect()` therefore returned instantly reporting "connected" while the socket underneath belonged to a finished request, and every query then stalled until `socketTimeoutMS` expired.

Measured on `wrangler dev`, hitting a DB-backed route repeatedly:

| | Request 1 | Request 2 | Request 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bypassing our cache only | 2644 ms | **10854 ms** | **10872 ms** |
| Disconnecting the stale connection first | 2360 ms | **1546 ms** | **1574 ms** |

Vercel keeps the global cache and is completely unaffected.

**`lib/liveblocks.ts` built its client at module scope**, so the secret read as `undefined` on Workers and every call would have failed with an opaque auth error at runtime. Now lazily constructed, and a missing secret throws a clear error instead of being cast away with `as string`.

## 4. Bundle size — this would have been rejected on deploy

The first build came out at **3523 KiB gzipped**, against the **3072 KiB Workers Free limit**. Cause: `app/twitter-image.png` was a 1.21 MB PNG, and Next inlines metadata images into the server bundle as routes — that one file was 1.23 MiB of the total.

Re-encoded both social cards as JPEG q90 at the same 1200×630 (1.21 MB → 273 KiB each). **Worker is now 2818 KiB gzipped**, under the cap.

> [!NOTE]
> That leaves roughly **255 KiB of headroom (~8%)**. It is thin. Run `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` before adding a large dependency or another binary asset under `app/`. Upgrading to Workers Paid raises the ceiling to 10 MiB if that becomes annoying.

**Also fixed a pre-existing bug found on the way:** `app/opnegraph-image.png` was **misspelled** (`opnegraph`). Next only recognizes the exact `opengraph-image` name, so the OpenGraph card had never worked, while `opengraph-image.alt.txt` sat there expecting it. Renamed — `/opengraph-image.jpg` now serves 200.

- **Lint — identical set.** 10 pre-existing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings across 6 component files, unchanged. (`next lint` also now prints a deprecation notice; it is removed in Next 16, and migrating is out of scope for this PR.)

author: bloknayrb
body:
## Summary

- attach one child-stream error seam immediately after `spawn()` and before the bootstrap stdin write
- treat every stdin `'error'` as evidence that the current live child can no longer be woken: log the code verbatim, then best-effort `SIGTERM` that child so the existing exit/restart ladder recovers it
- consume and log stdout/stderr `'error'` events without routing them through the child-gone callback
- add unit coverage for registration, repeated errors, unknown codes, callback delivery, and all production guards, plus a POSIX end-to-end wake/restart/resume contract

## Why

`sendTurn` already receives a failed write in its callback and re-arms the pending wake, but Node also emits `'error'` on the stdin `Writable`. With no stream listener, that event escapes as `uncaughtException`. The `ChildProcess`-level `'error'` listener only covers process spawn failures, so `handleFatalError` captures the exception and then exits the entire Tandem server under open documents.

The original plan proposed allowing known pipe codes and rethrowing everything else. This implementation deliberately does not use an allowlist: Windows reported `EOF`, not `EPIPE`, in all 12 measured child-exit races. Any stdin stream error means that this child cannot be trusted to accept later wakes, so keeping it alive is not a useful recovery policy. Unknown codes remain visible in the log rather than becoming process-fatal.

The same EventEmitter failure mode existed on stdout and stderr. Their listeners are log-only because a read error does not prove that the child stopped accepting writes; killing on a read error would introduce unmeasured behavior.

## Measurements behind the policy

| Measured behavior | Result | Environment |
|---|---|---|
| Child exits under a turn-sized write; code observed by parent | `EOF`, 12/12; never `EPIPE` | Windows, Node 24.14.1 |
| `exitCode` / `signalCode` inside the stdin `'error'` listener | both `null`, 12/12 | Windows |
| Write callback vs. stream `'error'` ordering | callback first, 12/12 | Windows |
| Live child closes fd 0; parent writes | no error; six writes all succeeded | Windows |
| Live child closes pipe read end; parent writes three times with SIGPIPE ignored | `EPIPE` on all three, including the first | WSL2 6.6.87 syscall layer |
| `kill()` after child exit | returns `false`, does not throw, leaves `killed === false` | Windows |
| Unhandled stdin `'error'` | `uncaughtException`; `ChildProcess.on("error")` catches nothing | Windows |

The probe files lived in the review session scratchpad and are not committed, so these measurements were not rerun as part of this branch.

## Recovery semantics and accepted tradeoffs

For a wake-write failure, the write callback clears the latch and re-arms `pendingWake`; teardown promotes that intent to `wakeOwedAcrossSpawns`; and the replacement process resumes the saved session and receives exactly one wake turn. The new stream handler does not schedule a restart directly; the existing child-process error and exit handlers own restart scheduling.

There are limits this PR does not hide:

- A write callback that arrives after `teardownTurnDelivery` has already run sets `pendingWake` in a dead closure, so that wake is stranded.
- A live child that stops reading can accept a small write into the OS pipe buffer with no error. The turn stays latched until the 10-minute breaker; this silent outcome is more likely than `EOF` on Windows.
- If the bootstrap write fails, Tandem may next attempt to resume a UUID persisted before Claude created the conversation. That resume self-heals after failing, but costs a doomed intermediate spawn.
- A persistently broken stdin can now restart Claude quietly on every annotation. The breaker allows 10 restarts per rolling 5 minutes; a regular loop at or slower than roughly one wake per 30 seconds never trips it, and the backoff resets after 30 seconds.
- This condition previously reached `captureFatal` before server exit. After this change its only immediate signal is `console.error`, which the desktop app writes to the Tauri log and does not aggregate.
- On macOS, the reaper has no SIGTERM handler or PDEATHSIG equivalent. Killing the reaper may orphan Claude while the restart ladder starts another process. Windows job-object teardown and Linux PDEATHSIG/`execvp` avoid that shape. A user `stop()` in the small post-kill window sees `spawned.killed === true` and returns without escalation; on macOS that escalation would not recover the already-orphaned Claude.
- In the measured Windows exit race, the handler calls `kill()` while `exitCode` and `signalCode` are still null, but that kill is a harmless no-op against the already-exiting process. The consequential live-child/closed-read-end path is covered only by the POSIX end-to-end test.

## Follow-ups

- [Stranded callback-after-teardown wake (#1866)](https://github.com/bloknayrb/tandem/issues/1866)
- [Silent no-error loss on an alive-not-reading child (#1867)](https://github.com/bloknayrb/tandem/issues/1867)
- [Windows reaper does not forward stdin to Claude (stdin wakes may be inert) (#1869)](https://github.com/bloknayrb/tandem/issues/1869)
- [Count consecutive stdin-error kills in the exit handler and set a `LauncherErrorCode` (#1868)](https://github.com/bloknayrb/tandem/issues/1868)

Draft issue bodies for all four are prepared alongside this PR body.

## Testing

- `npm test -- --run tests/server/launcher/supervisor.test.ts tests/server/launcher/stream-json-protocol.test.ts` — 121 passed, 2 skipped on Windows (the POSIX EPIPE cases)
- `npm test -- --run` — 10,491 passed and 40 skipped; one unrelated search-worker negative-control timing test exceeded its 15-second budget under full-suite load
- `npm test -- --run tests/server/search-worker.test.ts` — isolated rerun passed 18/18
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:tests`
- `npx biome check src/server/launcher/supervisor.ts tests/server/launcher/supervisor.test.ts tests/server/launcher/stream-json-protocol.test.ts tests/server/launcher/stub-claude-cli.cjs`
- `npx eslint src/server/launcher/supervisor.ts tests/server/launcher/supervisor.test.ts tests/server/launcher/stream-json-protocol.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Not tested

- the Windows `EOF` race end to end; the error-code and handler policy are pinned by Windows unit tests
- the macOS orphan behavior; no macOS hardware was available
- a consequential stdin-error kill on Windows; the measured Windows error occurs during exit and `kill()` is a no-op
- the source-order call site behaviorally on Windows; it is covered by the structural source pin, code review, and the Ubuntu end-to-end test

Closes #1757

body:
## Summary

Replaces the `Onboarding — coming soon` placeholder with the minimum real production onboarding step: an authenticated, email-verified founder creates their organization (business name + slug) and lands in `/app`.

No auth redesign, no security weakening, no direct multi-step organization inserts.

## Onboarding flow

1. `/onboarding` runs `checkAppGuardFn()` in `beforeLoad` (server-side, never an effect).
   - no session → `/sign-in`
   - unverified email → `/verify-email`
   - revoked membership → `/access-denied`
   - already an active member → `/app` (onboarding is done)
2. Founder enters **business name** and **slug** (slug is suggested from the name until they edit it).
3. Submit calls `createOrganizationFn` (server function).
4. `createOrganizationFn` validates the session cookie, enforces email verification, then hands off to the server-only service, which calls the `create_organization_for_founder` RPC under the founder's own JWT.
5. Success → `navigate({ to: "/app" })`. Slug conflict → friendly field-level error. Backend failure → a real error, never a fake success.

Only the two v1 fields are collected. No staff invite, products, payments, or business-profile steps were added.

## RPC used

`public.create_organization_for_founder` (migration `009_create_organization_rpc.sql`) — it creates the organization **and** the founder's OWNER membership in one transaction. The application layer performs no inserts.

## Auth / security invariants preserved

| Invariant | How |
|---|---|
| `user_id` only from the validated JWT | `getSessionFn()` reads the HttpOnly cookie; the RPC derives the founder from `auth.uid()` |
| `organization_id` never trusted from client | not part of the input schema; extra keys are stripped by zod (covered by a test) |
| Org creation only via the RPC | `createOrganizationForFounder` calls the RPC; no `.insert(...)` anywhere in the path |
| Founder membership created by the RPC | unchanged migration 009 behaviour |
| No slug uniqueness pre-check | no availability query in the route, the API boundary, or the service |
| DB constraint is authoritative | `organizations_slug_unique` decides; client-side check is format-only |
| PG `23505` → `slug_taken` | RPC catches `unique_violation`; the service also maps a raw `23505` transport error to `slug_taken` rather than `internal_error` |
| Email verification enforced independently | in `getSessionFn`, again in `createOrganizationFn`, and re-asserted in the service as defence in depth |
| `/app` protected by `beforeLoad` | `src/routes/app.tsx` untouched |
| No browser-bundled static import of server-only modules | `src/routes/onboarding.tsx` → `src/api/org.ts` → **dynamic** `import("@/server/org/create-organization")`; verified by the bundle-boundary tests against the real build output |

## Structure

The organization module was split to satisfy TanStack Start's import-protection boundary (routes may not reach `src/server/**`), following the existing customers/products pattern:

- `src/lib/org-schema.ts` — client-safe zod contract (slug schema, input schema, result union)
- `src/api/org.ts` — server-function boundary: session + email verification, then dynamic import
- `src/server/org/create-organization.ts` — server-only service: the RPC call and result mapping

## UI

Mobile-first, existing design system components (`Button`, `Input`, `Label`, `ApsiIllustration`), full i18next coverage in Khmer and English, no hard-coded user-facing strings, no hard-coded hex colors, field-level `role="alert"` errors, `aria-invalid` / `aria-describedby`, double-submit guard and `aria-busy` loading state.

## Files changed

- `src/routes/onboarding.tsx` — placeholder replaced with the real flow
- `src/api/org.ts` *(new)*, `src/lib/org-schema.ts` *(new)*, `src/lib/slug.ts` *(new)*
- `src/server/org/create-organization.ts` — now a service; adds the `23505` mapping
- `src/locales/en.json`, `src/locales/km.json` — `onboarding.*` keys
- `src/tests/onboarding-flow.test.ts` + `src/tests/onboarding-flow.runtime.ts` *(new)*

## Tests

New focused suite (24 tests) covering: successful creation, exact RPC parameter contract (no `p_founder_user_id`), call under the founder's JWT, no slug pre-check, client-supplied `organization_id` stripped, `slug_taken` (RPC status **and** raw `23505`), unverified user denied with the RPC never called, unauthenticated user denied with the RPC never called, RPC/backend failure returning a real error, `invalid_input`, malformed slug rejected before any request, redirect to `/app`, server-side guard, double-submit guard, i18n coverage and en/km key parity.

## Verification

- `bun test` focused onboarding/auth tests — **99 pass, 0 fail**
- `bun test` (full) — **252 pass, 1 fail**
- `tsc --noEmit` — **clean**
- `bun run build` — **succeeds**; client bundle scanned, no `supabaseAdmin`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, or RPC name present

The one full-suite failure is `src/tests/auth-hardening.test.ts` → "runs isolated runtime checks without mutating the shared test module cache", a 5s timeout. It is **pre-existing and unrelated**: it reproduces identically on a clean checkout of this branch's base with these changes stashed. It was left alone rather than touched, since it sits in the auth area this task was told not to redesign.

author: roboclaw-bot
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool-heavy conversations showed a wall of `Exec` and `$ set -euo pipefail` rows. Nested calls lost their owning run identity in canonical display metadata, while useful purpose titles depended on an opt-in background model call.

This keeps Josh Lehman's shared Gateway grouping repair and makes execution purposes part of the acting agent's tool call. Code-mode and shell tools advertise an optional bounded `title`; the UI and shared progress formatter display it immediately. Expanding a call preserves the full command, JavaScript/TypeScript source, extra arguments, output, and result-owned status. Untitled shell previews skip setup lines through the existing parser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The nested activity producer records the owning run separately from each call's deduplication key. The Gateway now carries that validated run ID into canonical metadata, so history and live events share the correct grouping without changing identity-reader precedence or stored data. The regression was introduced by #132457; the baseline still reproduces it.

Removed the utility-model title generator, browser request queue/cache/subscriptions, and `gateway.controlUi.toolTitles` config surface. `openclaw doctor --fix` detects and removes the retired key regardless of its value, preserving neighboring settings. Viewing tool activity makes no additional model calls. The shipped `chat.toolTitles` RPC remains a validated `{ titles: {}, disabled: true }` response until a versioned protocol removal.

No new configuration, database schema, persisted representation, or protocol version. Existing calls without a title retain deterministic labels. Titles express intended work; tool results continue to own success/failure.

## User Impact

Execution activity is understandable by default without background model requests. Existing configs containing `gateway.controlUi.toolTitles` receive an actionable Doctor diagnostic; `openclaw doctor --fix` removes the retired key. Raw execution evidence remains expandable, including mixed command/code inputs.

The maintainer explicitly requested this retirement and Doctor cleanup. The compatibility tradeoff is accepted: untitled historical/generic calls retain deterministic labels, and automatic startup migration keeps its existing single-file ownership rules. `$include`, Nix-managed, or newer-version configs may need explicit Doctor recovery or removal of the retired key from their declared source before startup.

## Evidence

- New Doctor/schema/display regressions on unchanged main: **11 failed / 64 passed** for the intended missing behavior. Fixed versions pass.
- Shared Gateway projection, identity reader, nested history, run grouping, and transcript suites: **375 passed**.
- Tool schema, Code Mode, Doctor, and shared display checks: **99 passed**.
- UI cards: **45 passed**. A mixed `command`/`code` regression failed before the repair and passes afterward; both sources remain inspectable.
- CI-exposed schema contracts: **131 tests passed** after shortening the title guidance within the unchanged 550-character description budget and adding the title metadata to the node-only schema assertion.
- Chromium E2E: **8 passed**, including nested grouping after reload, desktop/mobile, restart recovery, cross-session isolation, and history/live titles with no title-generation requests.
- Changed-file validation: selected typechecks, formatting/lint, dead exports, i18n, config metadata, dependency/SDK boundaries, storage/import-cycle/auth guards all passed. File-length lint was repaired by extracting the same assertions into dedicated tests and rerunning their lint; all remaining planned checks passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview through P2: **clean**, after correcting its mixed-source visibility finding.

### Live isolated Gateway proof

Real Gateway and canonical SQLite transcript writes, served Control UI, and real Chromium. Synthetic messages reproduce the production nested-call deduplication keys. This proves the UI/history/RPC flow; no live provider inference or shell execution is claimed.

Before: **0 activity groups / 6 standalone rows**; the expected grouping assertion fails. After: **1 collapsed group / 0 standalone rows**; expansion retains all six calls, displays agent-supplied purposes, and shows `git status --short` instead of shell setup. Reload restores the collapsed group. The UI made **0** `chat.toolTitles` requests. Explicit valid RPC returned empty/disabled; malformed parameters were rejected. Both Gateways shut down cleanly.

| Before | After, collapsed | After, expanded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: separate Exec rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c9baa49-7fa5-43da-b335-19f578a39084) | ![After: one activity group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad2d61d4-7e21-44e5-864b-bc73122003bf) | ![After: purpose labels and useful shell preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c323d69c-261c-4ace-af49-d9d7763ca7a7) |

All captures were inspected: synthetic project/session content only, no secrets or unrelated desktop content.

Final integration CI exposed a separate dashboard-gallery fixture regression from #138635: the initial `chat.startup` succeeds, but switching to the dashboard face still calls `sessions.resolve`. The fixture omitted that second response, producing “Session not found.” The exact CI merge reproduced this locally. The equivalent shared-resolution fixture repair landed in #138769 and is included by rebase; production behavior and all original browser assertions remain unchanged.

The previous failed `settings-layout` E2E gate was fixed on main by #138482; this branch includes that repair through rebase. The prior ClawSweeper web live-proof rank-up is satisfied above. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33941234854) is green for `009e9d54118befb4d99113f4a55571e3f2bf28d1`, including all seven browser shards and the real-Gateway lane. The build-artifact job passed one bounded retry after the parallel-test port collision recorded below.

Production LOC: **+106 / -947 (net -841)**. Tests/support: **+379 / -1531 (net -1152)**. Removed generator/cache machinery accounts for the reduction; new production code is the bounded call-title contract and canonical metadata/migration work.

Full `pnpm build` passed after recovering a local disk-full interruption; the Control UI was rebuilt after the final unused-export cleanup.

### Review follow-through

The configuration retirement and historical-label tradeoff are explicitly accepted above. The data-model review flag refers to the Doctor config-key cleanup: no SQLite schema, stored transcript representation, or protocol version changes. Regression coverage verifies removal for every present legacy value, neighboring-setting preservation, unchanged caller input, and an idempotent second migration.

Telegram proof limitation: default status-only previews are unchanged, but optional command-detail progress and terminal logs use the shared purpose formatter. A title-bearing Telegram Test Server scenario was not run: this environment has no authenticated broker CLI or configured broker pair. The existing hosted smoke scenario emits untitled commands with detail hidden and cannot prove this change; its dispatch also does not accept this unpublished PR head. The review’s Telegram proof request is therefore explicitly skipped for this concrete unavailable prerequisite, rather than represented as covered by the web screenshots. Shared formatter regression tests and live Gateway/Control UI evidence remain the completed proof.

### Follow-up: shared test port reservation

The first final-head CI run reached a test infrastructure collision: the SQLite lifecycle proof tried to start its Gateway on a port already held by the parallel Discord widget proof. The log identifies the competing process. `test/helpers/openclaw-test-instance.ts` currently releases its ephemeral port before launchi

## Brief description

Fixes worker permission inheritance for AO orchestrators.

When an orchestrator runs `ao spawn`, the spawned worker now inherits the orchestrator’s saved Chat approval mode (for example, Auto-approve) instead of always falling back to the project worker default.

issue number #4898 

## Why

Previously, an orchestrator could run in Auto mode while every worker it spawned still required manual approvals.

## How

- Forward the existing `AO_SESSION_ID` as an internal `parentSessionId` on `ao spawn`.
- Validate the parent server-side and inherit permissions only when it is a same-project orchestrator.
- Read the parent’s durable Chat approval setting and apply it as the worker’s spawn override.
- Preserve existing behavior for manual spawns, worker-originated spawns, stale IDs, and cross-project IDs.
- Regenerated the OpenAPI spec and frontend API types.

OpenCode’s native Auto-mode mapping is intentionally unchanged; this PR fixes inheritance, not OpenCode’s separate permission-policy translation.

body:
## What

Append wide variant-TSV validation to `create_duckdb_from_tsv.py`: a header check
(`validate_variants_header`) and a legend-driven, null-safe per-population validator
(`read_and_validate_variants`), plus a `variants.tsv` fixture and a parametrized refusal-table test.

## Why

The pure-Python TSV path must reject malformed input up front. Validation is vectorized (polars) and
null-safe:

- Header: the fixed `contig,pos,ref,alt` plus `AC_<pop>`/`AF_<pop>` per population must be present;
  an `AC_`/`AF_` column naming an unknown population is rejected; other extra columns (e.g. `rsid`)
  are permitted and ignored.
- Rows: `pos >= 1`; `contig` a GRCh38 main-contig token; `ref`/`alt` are `A/C/G/T/N`; each pop's
  `AC_`/`AF_` is both-present-or-both-empty with `AC >= 0` and `AF in [0, 1]`; at least one defined
  AF per row. Failures name the first offending `(contig,pos,ref,alt)`; a null-derived comparison
  counts as a failure (`fill_null(False)`), never a silent pass.

## Notes

- Fixture `variants.tsv` covers a SNP, a missing-population cell, an insertion, and a deletion.
- Stacked on #127. Base: `feat/tsv-source-metadata`. Draft.

Related to #114

author: paananiruddh
body:
Per the build brief: a floating widget on every listing/city page that asks at most 3 questions (or parses one free-text sentence) and returns the best 3 listings with reasons. Runtime is a **deterministic slot-filling state machine + facet/text matcher over a prebuilt JSON index** — no LLM in the request path for this phase at all.

## What's built (`concierge/`, new pnpm workspace, TypeScript strict)

- **`packages/core`** — pure TS, zero deps, no DOM. Tokenizer, deterministic parser (place/facet/modifier phrase-matching), ranker (weighted scoring, a bounded "boosted but labelled" featured placement capped at 0.7× the top score — never fabricating relevance — with a guarantee that at least one non-featured listing survives into the top 3), a near-miss relaxation ladder, and a pure dialog engine enforcing "results within ≤3 questions, always."
- **`packages/build`** — a Node CLI reading straight from the live D1 database via Cloudflare's REST API (not scraping the site's own tRPC), filtered on `status='published'` — the same predicate `worker/directory.ts` uses. Rule-tags facets by synonym match, derives budget bands per city, shards the index per city, writes a build-report cross-referencing thin listings against the existing enrichment backlog.
- **`packages/widget`** — vanilla TS, Shadow DOM, zero framework, IIFE: **8.4 KB gzipped** against a 40 KB budget. Seeds from the page it opens on — a listing page reads its own city out of `window.__RQ_STATE__`, which `worker/ssr.tsx` already dehydrates for hydration, no extra request needed.
- **`worker/concierge.ts`** — `POST /api/concierge/events` (logs to new `concierge_events` table) and a stubbed `POST /api/concierge/parse` (P1's real hybrid LLM endpoint isn't built; returning "no slots" is safe by the dialog engine's own contract, not broken).
- **`<Concierge />`** — a two-line React wrapper that only injects the widget's script tag, so the site's bundle never doubles up with the widget's code. Mounted on `CityGuide.tsx` and `ListingDetail.tsx` only, per P0 scope.

## Validated against real production data, not just fixtures

Built the full live site — **1,564 published listings, 38 cities, 27 shards** — straight from D1. Biggest shard (Munich, 94 KB raw) gzips to **20 KB** against the 150 KB budget. Ran real dialog turns against the real Munich and Melbourne shards.

Worth being honest about one finding: only **2 listings site-wide** are currently marked featured, and neither scores within 0.7× of top for the queries tested — so the boost correctly never fires for them. That's the ranker doing exactly what it should (never fabricating relevance for paid placement that doesn't actually match), not a gap in this build. It does mean there's no compelling "buy featured and get shown" demo yet until either more listings go featured or those two get richer data.

## Tests

40 unit + golden tests, all against real logic (no snapshots) — found and fixed a real bug along the way: the pluralisation stemmer's "-es" branch had an off-by-one length guard that made "massages" stem to "massag" instead of "massage". Covers tokenizer edge cases, parser confidence and place-alias matching, ranker monotonicity and the 0.7× boost-band invariant, the near-miss relaxation ladder (including a real cross-city pull-in test, Fort Lauderdale → Miami, ~42km), and the brief's own golden conversation example — adapted honestly where vague phrasing ("for my back" alone) needs P1's hybrid LLM, not this phase's deterministic-only parser.

`pnpm check` clean, production build unchanged at 0.76 kB `index.html`, `wrangler deploy --dry-run` compiles. `pnpm test` has the same 2 pre-existing failures (`server/stripe.test.ts`, `server/contentQuality.api.test.ts`) that reproduce on `main`.

## Not in this PR — per the brief's own phases

P1 (real hybrid LLM parse, build-time LLM tagging, post-publish rebuild hook, th/zh flows), P2 (lashandnails), P3 (funnel/demand-report views — events are logging already, the views aren't built), P4 (portfolio rollout).

## Before it logs anything

`npx wrangler d1 migrations apply thaimassageforu --remote` — the new `concierge_events` table (migration `0016`). Fails closed either way; a logging failure never blocks the widget.
