author: fileri
body:
## What

A message row with neither a chat nor a handle no longer becomes a thread. Such rows are leftovers of deleted conversations; Messages shows them nowhere. Rows that have a handle are untouched.

## Why

Deleting a conversation removes its chat row and the `chat_message_join` rows, but Messages in iCloud keeps the message rows in sync regardless, and some carry no handle either (sent messages, older group announcements). Blip grouped them by their empty identity into **one thread with no name and no number**, dated by its newest member, that could not be opened. On one database: 21 such rows spanning 2018 to 2026, surfacing as a single nameless thread near the top of the list.

The obvious "require a chat join" filter would be wrong, and the data shows why: some SMS senders — banks, services, short codes — get a chat row that their messages are never joined to, and Blip shows them only because `chatKey()` falls back to the handle. Nine senders on the same database exist solely that way. So the rule is the narrowest one: no chat **and** no handle means no identity, and no identity means no thread.

## How

- **`collector.ts`** — `hasIdentity(m)` (`chatKey(m) !== ""`), applied in `fetchMessages()` where every message enters, so threads, toasts and the unread ledger never see such a row.
- **`collector.test.ts`** — a normal row, a handle-only row and an identity-less row in; the first two come out.
- CLAUDE.md's `chat:null` invariant gains the rule; CHANGELOG under Unreleased.

## How it was verified

- [x] `bun test` is green (CI will check) — 324 pass
- [x] Any send/receive behavior was exercised against **my own number only** — this change does not send
- [ ] UI change → none; one row disappears from the list
- [x] Touches an invariant in `CLAUDE.md` → **`chat:null` exists** — extended, not changed

Against the live bridge, running collector vs patched, `--deep`: threads 306 → 305, the nameless thread is the one that goes; short-code threads 3 → 3; alphanumeric-sender threads 160 → 160.

Note: like #31 and #32, this adds a line at the top of the CHANGELOG (and an invariant line in CLAUDE.md); whichever lands later gets a one-line rebase from me.

## TL;DR

- Scope: Choose where bulk and single-task QA reruns execute. Changes span 14 files: 10 application files, 3 test files, and 1 contributor guide.
- Size: app +112/-50; tests +81/-3; docs +5/-0 lines.

Bulk Run QA previously sent no execution environment, so new QA jobs used the worker default even when operators wanted to avoid a suspended Daytona account. The single-task audit proxy also discarded the environment body supported by the backend.

The QA controls now offer Worker default, Modal, and Daytona. Both hosted and standalone QA retry endpoints accept the selection, and new trials store it for subsequent retries. The task panel uses the same selection for manual pre-trial audits. Empty requests retain the existing default. This changes explicit reruns only; automatic follow-up QA and the global worker default are unchanged.

### Local testing

Ran the QA endpoint, evidence-preflight, and analysis-trial tests: **76 passed, 20 skipped**. The skipped tests require a configured PostgreSQL test database. Tests cover default/Modal/Daytona forwarding through admission and trial creation, plus rejection of unsupported providers. TypeScript checking and ESLint on the four changed frontend files passed. Ruff reports 15 existing E402 import-order errors in the standalone server; the same errors were verified on `staging`. No live Modal QA execution was performed.

### Core files changed

- **`experiment-trials-table.tsx` / `task-files-panel.tsx`** — Add the QA sandbox selector and send it with rerun requests.
- **QA proxy routes / `tasks.py`** — Forward and validate the optional environment without changing authentication or eligibility checks.
- **`qa.py` / `queue.py` / `analysis_trials.py`** — Carry the selected provider into the new QA trial's stored environment.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which sandbox runs explicit QA and audit reruns, but scope is limited to operator-triggered jobs with a validated provider enum and does not alter automatic QA admission.
> 
> **Overview**
> Operators can pick where **manual** QA and pre-trial audit jobs run instead of always using the worker default (often Daytona when that account is unavailable).
> 
> **API & schema:** `PreTrialAuditRequest` is renamed to **`QARunRequest`** and shared by `POST /tasks/{id}/qa/retry` and `POST /tasks/{id}/qa/pre-trial`. Both accept an optional JSON body with `environment: "modal" | "daytona"`; omitted or null keeps the deployed default. **`POST /tasks/{id}/qa/retry`** is new in accepting a body—the selected provider is threaded through `rerun_task_qa_core` → `start_qa_for_task` → `create_qa_trial` and stored on the new analysis trial. Invalid providers are rejected at validation.
> 
> **UI & proxies:** The experiment bulk **Run QA** toolbar and task panel add a **QA sandbox** selector (worker default / Modal / Daytona). Next.js QA proxy routes forward the request body to the backend. Pre-trial “static checks” rerun uses the same selector.
> 
> **Docs & tests:** `AGENTS.md` documents explicit-rerun-only behavior (automatic follow-up QA and the global default are unchanged). Tests cover route wiring and environment propagation through admission/trial creation.

The NixOS Python interpreter issue is fixed, but the GTK dashboard now fails during GI loading with:

```text
ImportError: Typelib file for namespace 'Graphene', version '1.0' not found
```

GTK4's introspection stack requires the Graphene typelib at runtime. This PR adds `pkgs.graphene` to the package's `GI_TYPELIB_PATH` inputs and build inputs so `yap-ui`, `yap-overlay`, and `yap-tray` can import GTK4 successfully on NixOS.

author: dinesh-1201
body:
Extends Phase 3 from baseline ORB discovery into robustness research. Current baseline: 15-minute OR, four-close confirmation, 0.60% stop, 3R target, one trade/day, entry until 11:00, conservative stop-first ambiguity.

Phase 3B tests gap regime/direction, opening-range size, breakout timing, weekday effects, volatility context, chronological validation, and slippage stress. The current research indicates a promising simple filter: restrict to opening-range width at or below the training-period 25th percentile (~0.2497% of price). This remains positive across train/validation/test; adding a Tuesday exclusion improves the untouched test but is treated as a hypothesis rather than frozen production logic because it may be more prone to overfitting.

No option P&L claims are made: options require historical option-chain/trade data and a separate IV/theta/spread/strike/expiry model. No live trading is enabled.

author: dbrattli
body:
## What

Add a new **ErrorShadowing** detector that flags functions whose error handling (try/catch/except) occupies most of the body, so the happy path it wraps is shadowed by failure handling.

This is a separation-of-concerns / cohesion signal — distinct from cyclomatic and cognitive complexity, which only count decision points. It catches both directions: logic buried under a single catch, and a function mostly made of handlers.

## How

- Grammar-agnostic metric: counts named descendant nodes inside an error-handling region vs. the whole function.
- New per-language `ErrorHandlingAnchorTypes` hook on the adapter (try_statement for Python/TS/C++, try_expression for F#/Kotlin).
- Severity scales with the error share; a min-node threshold keeps tiny defensive wrappers from tripping it.

## Wiring

- `Violation.fs` — new `ErrorShadowing` type + `"error-shadowing"` wire name
- `Config.fs` — thresholds (0.5 / 0.7 / min 8) with `.esaconfig.json` parsing; enable/disable is host-only
- `DetectorPipeline.fs`, extension setting reader, `package.json` schema, `ReportHuman.fs`
- New detector `src/Core/Detectors/ErrorShadowing.fs`

## Tests

Integration fixtures + tests across all five languages. **188 tests pass**; Fantomas and markdownlint clean. Dogfooding (`just analyze`) flags a few real error-handling-dominated functions in our own source (e.g. `readConfigJson`), which is the intended behavior and tunable via `.esaconfig.json`.

author: edgarmesquita
body:
Two regressions and two gaps reported by consumers running 0.2.0-preview.48. The regressions were
mine to fix, and every one of the four had a green suite standing behind it.

## 1 · The anchor offset published `0px` — reported from ui.equantic.tech

The `Sticky` → `Pinned` rename (#81) moved both **emitters** and missed the **reader**:

```
lowering.ts:3217      wrapper.attributes['data-eq-pinned'] = '1'   ← renamed
WebRealizer.cs:658    DataAttributes["eq-pinned"] = "1"            ← renamed
sticky-offset.ts:26   querySelectorAll('[data-eq-sticky]')         ← MISSED
```

`overlappingChrome()` found nothing, `--eq-anchor-offset` published `0px`, and every `Bookmark`'s
`scroll-margin-top` collapsed with it. Measured on the live site: four fragment targets went
**61px → 0px** between .47 and .48, landing each section behind the header — the exact bug
`Bookmark` exists to prevent.

**Why both suites stayed green**, which matters more than the typo: `sticky-offset.spec.ts` set the
attribute on a fixture it built itself. It tested the reader against markup nothing emits.

### The fix is that the name has one home

`shared/markers.ts` — a leaf module importing nothing, so `core/*` can never reach
`shared/lowering` through it — holds `PINNED_MARKER`. The lowering and the reader both take it from
there and can no longer disagree.

### Two instruments, each verified by putting the bug back

- the reader's spec now takes the attribute **from the lowering**: it lowers a real `Pinned` and
  copies the emitted attributes onto the element it measures. Restore the old literal and four
  cases fail with `expected '0px' to be '61px'`.
- `MarkerParityTests` pins what the **C# realizer** emits against `markers.ts` — that seam crosses
  languages, so no shared constant can span it. Point the realizer at `eq-sticky` and it fails.

## 2 · An assembly named `*.App` lost its executable — reported from OS Cleaner

`MacAppPayload.Includes` skipped nested bundles by testing every path segment for a `.app` suffix,
**including the segment that names the file**. A project called `OSCleaner.App` produces an apphost
called `OSCleaner.App` — so the one file `CFBundleExecutable` points at was the one file dropped.
`Contents/MacOS` got the DLLs and no binary, and the build failed two steps later on `chmod +x`,
with a message that mentions no packaging at all.

`Something.App` is the most ordinary layer name in .NET, and the default `AssemblyName` is the
project name. This reaches anyone with that convention, on both the dev bundle and the shipped one,
since they share the selector.

Structural, not a heuristic: **a bundle is a directory**, so only segments that name directories can
be one — every segment but the last. The new test is the symmetric twin of the one already there:
a `.app` FOLDER stays out, a `.app` FILE goes in. It fails against the old predicate.

## 3 · A contained failure said nothing on Photon — reported from OS Cleaner

`ComponentBoundary` catches a Build that throws and draws a card in its place — right, since one
broken section must not take the window with it. But on Photon **nothing was listening**: `Report`
was assigned only by the design tool, so a section that threw wrote nowhere. The web has had
`console.error` since the boundary shipped; native had silence.

What that cost, measured by the consumer: their headless render gate passes a section by measuring
the PNG, and **an error card is a perfectly good 42 KB image**. A broken section was green for days.

The host now arms `Report` by default with `??=` — preferring the app's `ILoggerFactory`, falling
back to stderr — so an app that assigns its own still wins. The reverse arrangement, silent until
asked, is not reachable in practice: by the time someone discovers they needed the report, the
exception has already been swallowed.

## 4 · `IDeepLinks`: read the HOST, not the PATH — documented, from the same report

On macOS `open myapp://refresh` arrives as `myapp://refresh/`. The platform appends a slash, so the
host is `refresh` and the path is `/`. An app that switches on `AbsolutePath` works everywhere it is
tested and fails on the platform it ships to. The contract now says so, and says why the capability
does **not** normalise: it would hide a difference the app is entitled to see.

## Verification

- every .NET suite green · 973 TypeScript tests · samples build
- both fixes A/B'd: each instrument was run against the restored bug and observed to fail

author: wittjosiah
body:
Registers `sdkVersion` as a PostHog super property in both the browser and node transports, so every event carries the version of the SDK that produced it.

## Why the SDK version

We want to know which SDK version every device of every identity last ran, and when that device was last seen, so deprecations rest on evidence rather than guesswork. The version that matters is the client's feature set, not the EDGE wire protocol and not the app release. Those already diverge: composer is at 0.11.3 while the SDK is at 0.11.1.

`release` (the app version) stays. "Did the 0.11.3 release break something" is a separate question worth keeping.

## Why now, ahead of the rollup

The property has to exist before any version rollup is built. History accumulated under the app version can't be converted to SDK versions after the fact, because the mapping isn't recoverable from the event. Every week without this is a week of data that can't answer the question.

## Notes on the implementation

The version comes from a local `packages/sdk/observability/src/version.ts` rather than importing `DXOS_VERSION` from `@dxos/client`. That keeps the client barrel out of the browser bundle for what is one string, and matches the existing note in `providers/client-observability.ts` about not reaching values through the client barrels. `scripts/sync-versions.mjs` stamps it alongside the three version files that already exist.

`posthog.register()` in the browser transport was previously gated on `release || environment`. It's now unconditional, since a host that sets neither still needs to be attributable to an SDK version.

`node.test.ts` asserts the exact registered property set, so it needed updating. Good sign the mechanism is actually covered.

## Not in this PR

The per-device rollup needs a device key that's reliably present on events, and `deviceKey` is currently session-scoped and truncated to 8 hex chars. That, the EDGE-side `/auth` inventory, the served version policy, and the client's deprecated/unsupported handling are all written up in DX-1256.

body:
## What and why

A hosted session showed the gateway listing in TUI chrome, for example `minimax/minimax-m3:free · openrouter`. The user did not pick that vendor. Route already answered who pays. Provider repeated the catalog partition and leaked the reseller.

This change drops the Provider column from `/model` and uses one Route string for the picker, the mode row, and the splash/session banner. Hosted coverage reads `seri`. ChatGPT reads `chatgpt`. Grok reads `grok`. BYOK names the provider. `/setup` still lists OpenRouter as a real key row.

## How

`formatRouteLabel` is the vocabulary. `formatRouteLabelFromResolved` maps a `ResolvedRoute` onto it. SplashBanner takes a required `via`. `runWelcomeSplash` and `runTui` pass that string. A live session overlays `state.route` so a `/model` pick updates the banner before the next turn.

A leftover key on the gateway listing still reads `seri` when `gatewayReachable` is true. Reroute to a sibling key still wins over hosted (`→ provider`), because picking that row actually uses the sibling key.

`matchesFilter` does not index `entry.provider` when Route is `seri`, so typing the gateway listing does not find hosted rows.

## Verification

- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [x] `bun test apps/cli/tests/tui/format.test.ts apps/cli/tests/tui/App.test.tsx apps/cli/tests/tui/modelPicker.test.tsx` (350 pass)
- [ ] `bun run build`, and ran the resulting binary
- [ ] Exercised the change by hand (say how, below)

OpenTUI App mounts pin hosted splash and session banners to `· seri` and assert they do not contain the gateway listing. `tuiPty` hosted zero-key splash asserts the same, but that file is `describe.skipIf(win32)` and was not run on this machine.

Relanzá a hosted TUI to confirm the header reads `model · seri`.

## Cross-platform impact

- [ ] Touches file paths, file I/O, process spawning, signals, or shell invocation

## Notes for the reviewer

Out of scope: collapsing duplicate hosted group rows, Cost `included` on gateway rows, portal `/models`, hiding OpenRouter in `/setup`.

body:
The published CLI installs, but its help command fails, its example is not self-contained, and several file paths resolve inside the installation. Capture failures can also escape the success status. This candidate adds a runnable local example, lightweight help/version/setup commands, explicit agent-skill installation, caller-relative browser inputs/outputs, and failure propagation through capture and verification.

The skill now uses a short workflow with focused references. README, contributing guidance, and a dated audit distinguish tested capabilities, current npm 0.3.0 behavior, and remaining limitations. The alternatives comparison uses current primary sources and makes no exclusivity claim.

## Release hold

This is an unpublished 0.3.1 candidate. `src/caprender.py` explicitly describes porting Cap rendering code/behavior, while DemoKit declares MIT and Cap's relevant source falls outside its MIT exceptions. The local Cap reference checkout (`ebe1cc2d2926be226276c1e544a32ba79d4a4932`, dated 2026-08-26) has the same license split, so this is not based only on today's upstream license. [Pinned reference license](https://github.com/CapSoftware/Cap/blob/ebe1cc2d2926be226276c1e544a32ba79d4a4932/LICENSE). The audit documents the evidence and possible resolution paths; this PR does not change the license or authorize npm publication. Renderer provenance and the owner's licensing decision need resolution before release. Previously committed captures also remain in Git history; no rewrite was performed.

## Validation

- `npm test`: all six CLI/package tests pass, including example and skill installation without overwrites and tarball content checks. Setup regressions failed before the implementation.
- `npm run test:smoke`: passed a packed-tarball installation outside the repository, from a path containing spaces; exercised probe, capture, render, verify, relative re-render, and a failed assertion. The exported frames were visually inspected.
- Skill validator: valid. Shell and changed module syntax checks: passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- `npm audit --omit=dev`: zero known advisories; not a full security audit.
- New GitHub Actions checks cover CLI/package behavior on macOS/Linux and the full example on Linux. Results are reported on this PR.

Only synthetic example source/data is included. No recordings, auth state, vendor checkouts, or media artifacts are added or uploaded. Legacy terminal/native/Docker/Chrome modes are not certified by the default-route smoke; their limitations are documented.

author: perezdap
body:
## Problem

Using Venice models that advertise cache pricing (e.g. `kimi-k3`) fails with:

```
Error: 400 "Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'tools[4].cache_control'"
```

## Cause

The extension sets `cacheControlFormat: "anthropic"` for models with cache pricing. pi's openai-completions adapter then stamps Anthropic-style `cache_control` markers on the system prompt, the last conversation message, **and the last tool definition**. Venice accepts `cache_control` on message content parts but its chat schema rejects it on `tools[]` entries.

## Fix

Strip `cache_control` from every tool definition in the existing `before_provider_request` hook (scoped to the Venice provider). Message-level `cache_control` is preserved, since Venice documents support for it on content parts.

author: marceloneppel
body:
## Issue

Follows the module-migration series (database 216-222, tls 180-189, ldap 235/236, backups 238-256): ports the watcher relation module from the VM charm's 16/edge into the library. The K8s charm has no watcher module — it offers no `postgresql_watcher` relation (Patroni uses the K8s API as its DCS) — so this handler is constructed on VM only, mirroring how K8sManager is K8s-only.

## Solution

`events/watcher.py` ports the VM charm's `PostgreSQLWatcherRelation` one-to-one as a substrate-neutral `WatcherEventsHandler`, part 1 of 3: the stereo-mode `watcher-offer` relation accessors (Raft address, `raft-status` gate), the enable/disable handshake, the watcher PostgreSQL user lifecycle, the secret get-or-create/update paths and the relation-data handout. The three relation event handlers and the charm wiring land in (2/3); the tests and the 16.3.14 bump in (3/3).

Adapter substitutions per the established contract:
- `charm._patroni.raft_password` → `state.application.raft_password`
- `charm._units_ips` → `state.units_ips` (new `CharmState` accessor reading the per-unit `ip` peer-databag key the lib's `ClusterManager.expose_ip_and_port` publishes — the lib equivalent of the charm's fresh-IP `_units_ips`)
- `charm.tls_manager.get_peer_ca_bundle()` / `is_tls_enabled` → injected `TLSManager`
- `charm._patroni.remove_raft_member` / `cleanup_raft_cluster` → charm-side bridges `charm.remove_raft_member` / `charm.cleanup_raft_cluster`
- `charm.async_replication.is_primary_cluster()` → charm-side bridge `charm.is_primary_cluster()`
- `charm.refresh.pinned_snap_revision` → `getattr(charm, "refresh", None)` (charm_refresh stays charm-side)

Relation keys, secret label/keys, leader gates, defer conditions and `cached_property` semantics are unchanged. `CharmState.units_ips` is added here because the handout reads it.

Vít Rýznar is speaking at an AI festival about how far generative AI can be
taken in consistent brand communication, and asked for a few slides or
screenshots showing how it works here. His thesis — *don't generate the visual,
generate the tools that apply it for you* — is exactly what we do, so a handful
of screenshots would undersell it. But the material he was sent is live client
work under NDA, and Jakub does not want hard-won know-how on a projector.

Nothing existed that answers him without either being useless or giving away
too much.

## Solution

`docs/talk/lide-obsah-a-design.html` — one self-contained page in seven blocks,
where a reader can stop at the first and still have a complete answer: the
sentence, the shift from chance to system, four principles, the wiring diagram,
four cases from live work, what AI is not allowed to do, and a signpost of
three slides for the talk itself. Vít needs three slides, Jakub needs certainty
that no implementation detail escapes, and a festival audience needs the
principle; each floor serves a different one of them.

Each layer is its own full-width band with an outlined number and the trail
blaze. Two are inverted to near-black: layer 2 because it carries the page's
thesis, layer 6 because it is its counterweight. An inverted block redefines
the same custom properties, so nothing inside it is styled by its parent.

**The graphics carry the argument, they don't decorate it.**

- *The hero* is the mark and its animation, both **taken from Volocal rather
  than redrawn** — the rules under `.kostka` are `docs/site/page.css`'s
  `.business-mark` block with a different selector prefix and without the sizes
  that belong to the small mark in a panel. A piece lifts out of its face,
  recolours from the face colour through a darkened shade to white, and settles
  back; that is how the shapes appear. `walls` — the same shape darkened to 45%
  — is the shadow in the socket while the piece is out. Red is lidé, green
  obsah, blue design, and the triangle on the red face is značkárna's own mark.
- *Layer 2* is the only thing on the page you can press: twenty-four tiles in
  two states. In `náhoda` each has its own offset, rotation and colour and
  re-rolls every two seconds; in `systém` they snap into line and go quiet in
  one red. It is the same grid either way, and that is the point.
- *Layer 3* gives each principle a small mechanism — a stamp that lands in the
  same place, a sheet that splits into readable and described, a ball that
  bounces between two lines, a barrier that lifts and drops.
- *Layer 4* runs a red dash along the diagram's connectors and blinks the
  gates, purely through `stroke-dashoffset` — no script inside the SVG, no
  library.

All motion sits behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; the mark falls
back to its own `mark-flat`. Nothing is parked at `opacity: 0`, and the
counters carry their target number in the document, so the page is complete and
truthful with no JavaScript at all.

**Anonymisation.** Clients are *město*, *výrobce* and *náš vlastní provoz* — no
names. Volocal is named, because it is ours and public. On the screenshots the
city's logo is painted out and a partner programme's name covered in two
places; word coordinates were found by scanning dark pixel columns, not
estimated (the first estimate was eleven pixels off and left an `E` showing).
On the knowledge-library screenshot four client names had been struck through
by hand in red; those are now covered by clean bars in the interface's own
tone, found the same way — saturated red pixels grouped into connected clusters
— and the image was re-scanned afterwards: zero red pixels left. Three
screenshots of client praise were dropped entirely, because there the hand-drawn
strikes left an initial readable.

**Brand from the source, not from a picture.** The Figma link returns 403, so
ABC Normal came off the live site, subset to Czech and converted to woff2 —
9 kB a weight against 170 kB — and inlined, because a published artifact accepts
no font host other than Google Fonts. The mark is the full lockup — a red
triangle, a green circle and a blue square — lifted verbatim from
`docs/site/index.html`, where Volocal's own footer uses it. It is set by the
brand's rule rather than by eye: the shapes are as tall as the type's x-height
(ABC Normal's `sxHeight` is 517/1000, measured from the font) and sit with their
bottom edge on the baseline. 539 kB total, nothing fetched from outside.

Four revisions were spent learning one thing. One used a red map pin from the
same site, which turned out to be the location icon beside their contact
details. One traced the cube off a JPEG, which lost the third shape and shifted
every colour. One invented an animation for it. One shipped a third of the
logo. Each time the original was at hand, and three times out of four it was
inside this repository. A mark is sourced, not redrawn.

**The Czech.** Four readers went over it, one per layer of the language,
returning literal strings and proposals but editing nothing — four agents
writing into one file would overwrite each other. 91 findings. The valuable
ones were not loanwords but sentences a Czech speaker does not build: *stojí to
skoro žádný čas* (a positive verb with a negative pronoun, from *costs us
almost no time*), *ví, jaký obsah systém obsahuje* (verb stranded at the end,
root repeated), *napříč zakázkami* for *across*.

Three terms were then put back at the owner's instruction: **vizuál**, **design
systém** and **konzistentně**. They are the working vocabulary of the field, and
a correction that overwrites them is not a correction but a shift in meaning.
They now sit in `ZDOMÁCNĚLÉ` in the checker with the date and the reason. That
exchange also caught a real error rather than a preference: layer 2's heading
said the tools *create* the visual, which contradicted layer 6, where the
designer makes it and the model only uses it.

**Two scripts, because a rule nobody notices while writing is a rule nobody
keeps.** `scripts/cesky-check.py` reads only what a person reads — headings,
paragraphs, captions, SVG text, `alt`, `aria-label` and the Czech comments, not
class names or file paths — and reports anglicisms, calques, filler and English
punctuation with a proposed replacement. `scripts/pevne-mezery.py` inserts
non-breaking spaces after one-letter prepositions, between figure and unit, in
thousands and in dates, and does not touch `<svg>`, `<style>` or `<script>`.

Both had a bug of their own. The spaces let two consecutive prepositions
(*fotek a z jedné věty*) steal each other's space, because `re.sub` consumes its
match — fixed with a lookbehind, which consumes nothing. And the check reported
spaces that are already non-breaking, because it turned ` ` into an
ordinary space before searching. Both surfaced only as nonsense findings; had
they reported less, the text would have looked clean.

## Behaviour that must remain unchanged

Nothing in the application. This adds one page under `docs/talk/`, two scripts
under `scripts/`, and appends to the change log. No TypeScript, no Rust, no CSS
or copy that ships in the program, and **`docs/site/page.css` and
`docs/site/index.html` are read but not modified** — the mark and its rules are
copied into the new page, not moved. The published page at `volocal.app` is
untouched. The two scripts are standalone and wired into no npm script, so no
existing check changes behaviour.

## Tests

- [x] `python3 scripts/cesky-check.py docs/talk/lide-obsah-a-design.html` —
      *Čisté*, exit 0, on the source and on the built page.
- [x] `npm run docs:check` — 5 documents match the code; the English page is
      complete at 273 sentences and labels.
- [x] `npm run i18n:check` — passes.
- [x] CI green on every earlier commit of this branch: *TypeScript and
      dictionaries* success, *Rust on Windows* success.
- [ ] `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` locally — `node_modules` is empty in this

author: mikalstill
body:
## What

A new consistency criterion, `fuzz-nightly-reporting`, generalized from instar's `coverage-fuzz.yml`.

Fuzzing has no natural end: a target runs until you stop it, and what it produces is a crash nobody knew about. That makes it the wrong shape for a merge gate and the right shape for a nightly — and *that* makes reporting the whole problem, because nobody reads a scheduled workflow's result and GitHub's only notification for one is an email to whoever pushed last.

A repository with fuzz targets is now held to three things:

1. **A `schedule:` trigger** on a workflow that runs the targets. Fuzzing that only happens when someone remembers to dispatch it is fuzzing that does not happen.
2. **`issues: write` plus a reachable `gh issue create`** on that workflow — directly, or through a script in the repository that it calls. The indirection is followed deliberately: the reporting logic belongs in something testable, so a check that only read the YAML would fail exactly the repositories that got it right.
3. **No `merge_group` trigger** on any fuzz lane. A short build-and-smoke on `pull_request` or `push` is explicitly not what this forbids — catching a target that stopped compiling is worth ten seconds of a PR. What it forbids is charging the lane's cost against the merge queue's timeout. `audit-ok: fuzz-in-merge-queue` marks a deliberate exception.

## Why

shakenfist/ryll#329. Ryll's four `Fuzz (*)` jobs were `merge_group`-only, so a merge group asked the six-worker `l` pool for four runners that ryll's pull request CI never requested. `check_response_timeout_minutes` caps at 360, it is a wall clock from when the merge group forms, and it does not distinguish a job running slowly from one that has not been given a runner.

Three times in eight days that timed out and the PR was evicted. On the third occasion the fuzz jobs got runners and passed *twenty minutes after* the eviction — leaving a merge group whose run was entirely green and a pull request that had silently failed to merge, with no red CI anywhere to find it by.

## The specification

`docs/audits/fuzz-nightly-reporting.md` carries the four details of instar's implementation that are worth copying and are not obvious:

- **Dedup before filing.** A crash that recurs nightly must become one issue with comments, not one issue per night. instar keys on the target plus a normalized panic location and message, with numbers collapsed — a panic that interpolates the fuzz-derived values that provoked it produces a different string every night for one bug.
- **A failure to report must not end the run.** The remaining targets still have to be fuzzed.
- **Decide deliberately what turns the run red.** For a crash campaign, red on a successfully-filed crash leaves the nightly permanently red and therefore ignored — the exact failure this criterion prevents, reintroduced one step along. For a build-and-smoke gate the opposite is right. Either way, a failure nobody could file an issue about must fail the run.
- **Persist the work before failing.** When issue filing is the thing that broke, the uploaded artifacts are how the crash reaches a human.

It also records why the reporter belongs in a script rather than inline YAML: instar's inline version broke the nightlies silently for a month when a large crash input pushed a `jq --arg` past `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` under `bash -e`.

## Verification

`pre-commit run --all-files` clean; the full audit suite passes (772 tests), including 27 for this criterion: the reference shape, the inline variant, each failure mode, the exception marker and its unmarked counterpart, a build-only lane on the queue, the alternative issue-filing forms, the reusable-workflow split, and the false-positive guards (a header comment mentioning fuzzing, a commented-out reporter, a vendored `fuzz_targets/` under `target/`, a script path pointing outside the clone). Every guard the review round added is mutation-checked: breaking it on purpose fails the test that covers it.

Against real clones:

| Repository | Result |
|---|---|
| instar | `pass` — coverage-fuzz.yml fuzzes on a schedule and files issues for crashes |
| ryll | `fail` — runs fuzz targets on merge_group in ci.yml…; no schedule trigger |
| kerbside, shakenfist, occystrap | `not_applicable` — No fuzz targets |

shakenfist/ryll#355 brings ryll into compliance.

author: jhadobe
body:
This PR updates the webapi guide with changes for the September release of ACCS. Currently these changes are scheduled to be published on 9/8.

This PR consists of the following PRs:

- #590 
- #600 
- #603 
- #607 
- #608 
- #609 

- [ ]  Update schema changes in this PR before merging

whatsnew
Added multiple changes as part of the Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service September release:
- Added [System configuration](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/saas-integrations/system-config), which covers the `/V1/system/config` REST endpoint that syncs configurations between Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service environments.
- Added a [storeConfig query example](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/graphql/schema/store/queries/store-config/#query-a-stores-persistent-cart-and-account-sharing-configuration) documenting the new persistent shopping cart and customer account sharing fields (`persistent_enabled`, `persistent_shopping_cart`, `persistent_options_wishlist`, `share_customer_accounts_scope`).
- Updated [Email triggering through the REST API](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/saas-integrations/custom-email/) with new `PUT` and `DELETE /V1/custom-email/templates/{id}` endpoints for updating and deleting custom email templates.
- Added [sourceAvailability query](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/graphql/schema/products/queries/source-availability) documentation for reading per-source inventory availability by SKU, scoped to the current sales channel.
- Added the [selectFreeGiftForCart mutation](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/graphql/schema/cart/mutations/select-free-gift), which lets shoppers select a gift SKU when a Free Gift cart price rule requires a choice, including support for configurable and bundle gift products.
- Added a `search` field to `CustomerOrdersFilterInput` on the [customer query](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/graphql/schema/customer/queries/customer), letting a signed-in customer search their order history by order number, product name, or SKU.

author: waleedzidan2020
body: Fixes the real antiX failure shown by the dashboard: tc/nft commands succeed, but the old verifier rejects the kernel state because older iproute2 formats `tc filter/class show` output differently. Adds a compatibility verifier that checks HTB root/classes and accepts old/new filter output forms without depending on exact `fw`/`flowid` strings. This prevents a valid speed limit from being immediately removed by the fail-open path. Fail-open remains active for genuine command/state failures. No Wi-Fi/hostapd restart is introduced.

author: spoor-nl
body:
## Why

Every dry-run of `STARTUP.md`'s onboarding flow so far has cost a human or an agent hand-simulating a fictional owner's answers, turn by turn, from scratch. That is the only way it has ever been exercised. It works and it does not scale — and it is also the wrong shape for an owner who would rather fill in a file than hold a back-and-forth.

## What

- **`profile.example.toml`** — a documented format holding the interview's answers. One field per thing `AGENTS.md`'s question list actually asks (read off that file, not invented), plus the two topics `STARTUP.md` steps 2 and 3 add. TOML because `tomllib` is stdlib, so this stays dependency-free like `spoor-doctor`, and because a format a human fills in needs comments.
- **`spoor-profile`** — consumes a filled-in profile and writes `.env` (mode 0600 from creation, exactly the keys `.env.example` declares, every blank carrying the reason it is blank) and the conventions doc (a section per bullet `STARTUP.md` step 6 asks that doc to record). It reads the schema through `spoor-doctor`'s own `# doctor:` parser rather than a second copy of it, so the two can't disagree; always writes the two secret fields blank and rejects a profile that names one; runs no git.
- **`examples/`** — three filled-in profiles, plus a README indexing them.
- **`docs/non-interactive-onboarding.md`** — when to reach for this, what it costs, where the boundary falls.
- **`.github/ci/test-profile.py`** + a `profile-generator` CI job.

## The judgement boundary, which is the point

Fields the format marks `judgment` may be left out. What lands in the doc for a missing one is a `TODO(owner)` line naming what is absent and who decides it — never a default. `./spoor-profile --explain` prints the list; today it is the autonomy deltas and the shipping gate, what may be done to the running deployment unattended, the stack and its rationale where `END_USER_TYPE` is technical (so `product-tech-stack` doesn't apply and there is nothing else stopping a guess), an existing repo's stack conflict, the bar for a tracked item, which private network internal tooling is reached over, who executes a refund, and the pipeline stage set.

`examples/kweekhuis.toml` omits all of them on purpose: no `[autonomy]` table at all. It generates a conventions doc that is nine explicit `TODO(owner)` lines where those answers belong, which is the honest state of a deployment nobody has had the autonomy conversation with yet.

Everything downstream of a credential, a network call or actual writing is reported as outstanding rather than faked: step 5's git identity, step 6's *shipping*, step 7's specialization pass and stage prompts, step 8's shopping list.

## Proof

`./spoor-doctor --offline` against the generated Northlight deployment: **15 passed, 0 warnings, 2 failures, 6 skipped**, and both failures are documented end states rather than generator bugs —

- `env-required`, on exactly `WORK_TRACKER_API_KEY`, `COMMS_CHANNEL_TOKEN` and `AGENT_EMAIL_ADDRESS`. The first two are the secrets step 4 mandates leaving blank; the third is that profile's own shopping-list item. `STARTUP.md` step 9 already names this as the one FAIL a correct first boot ends on.
- `skills-specialization`, which is step 7 — the half this tool deliberately does not do.

The CI job asserts that shape rather than just an exit code: it parses the `env-required` message and fails if it names any field that isn't actually blank in the generated `.env`, or if any problem in it is shaped as anything other than empty-but-required.

The load-bearing assertion is an equivalence. `examples/northlight.toml` is the same business with the same answers as `docs/example-walkthrough.md`, so the `.env` generated from it has to match the `.env` that walkthrough shows the interview producing. The test parses the expected values **out of the walkthrough itself** rather than restating them, so the two can't drift — a change to either side that breaks the equivalence fails CI. It currently matches on all 13 keys with no extras.

Also asserted: every profile under `examples/` generates a deployment the doctor accepts (the directory is globbed, so a new profile is covered for free); the judgement boundary holds, including that a profile asking for a dashboard must *not* get the settled "nothing internal exists yet" deferral `STARTUP.md` warns against; no invented stack where the profile left one blank; seven invalid profiles each refused without writing anything; an existing `.env` keeps its contents and gets its mode narrowed to 0600; `--dry-run` writes nothing.

## Two real gaps this surfaced, fixed where the fact lives

Both were found by having to map every interview answer to a destination, which is a thing no reader of the flow had been forced to do:

1. **`STARTUP.md` step 6 never asked for the per-person section that two `.env` fields point at it for.** `COMMS_ALLOWLIST`'s and `OWNER_TECH_LEVEL`'s own comments in `.env.example` both say the conventions doc is the home for who each identity belongs to, who with channel access is deliberately excluded, whose sign-off is whose, and the per-person register that overrides the single switch. Step 6's bullet list had no such bullet, so that answer got collected and had nowhere to land. Added as a bullet.
2. **`AGENTS.md`'s completeness claim was wrong, and question 8 was seven questions.** That file said its numbered list "is the complete set of what the interview covers" while `STARTUP.md` steps 2 and 3 ask two further topics — and step 1 repeated the claim. Both now scope it and point at each other. Separately, question 8 bundled repo location, business context location, existing conventions file, deploy pipeline, who else may merge, tracker-already-in-use and merge-deploys-to-prod into one question; each is independently answerable with its own destination and each is silently assumed by some later step. It now enumerates its parts (a)–(g), with the existing prose kept as the reasoning for each.

Neither was worked around in the tool.

## Notes

- No step renumbering anywhere, so every `STARTUP.md step N` cross-reference still resolves; `check-skills-consistency.py` passes.
- `test-doctor.py` still passes (32 cases), and `spoor-doctor`'s `doc-links` finds all relative links resolving across 37 tracked docs.
- Pushed over SSH rather than HTTPS: the branch touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which the credential-helper token lacks the `workflow` scope for.

author: hamidnoshady
body:
Found during a production security audit of this repo and `cafe-restaurant-pos`.

## The problem

`scopedPublicRead` / `scopedPublishedRead` (`src/access/siteRead.ts`) derive the tenant from the request's `Host`. When the host resolved to **no site**, they added no constraint and deferred to the collection's own access — which for every public collection is "any published row".

The control-plane host is exactly such a host, and nothing else was closing it:

- `Caddyfile`'s `https://{$CONTROL_PLANE_HOST}` block reverse-proxies everything; only `/api/domain-check*` is blocked.
- `src/proxy.ts`'s matcher is `'/((?!api|next|_next|media|favicon).*)'` — middleware never runs on `/api`.
- The multi-tenant plugin only ANDs its constraint for a logged-in member of the admin users collection.

So an **unauthenticated** request to the admin hostname returned every customer's published content:

```
GET https://<control-plane-host>/api/pages?limit=1000
GET https://<control-plane-host>/api/products
GET https://<control-plane-host>/api/media
POST https://<control-plane-host>/api/graphql
```

…and the same for `posts`, `categories`, `store` and `theme`. Drafts were not exposed (`_status: published` still applied), and `store.cardNumber` kept its own field-level lock — but the platform's whole content surface, media library and product catalogue were enumerable by anyone who knew the admin hostname.

This was a **known** fail-open, documented in `siteRead.ts` and pinned by an integration test that asserted a read on `localhost` spanned more than one site. The mitigation was scoped as proxy work in `WAVE-9.md` and never shipped.

## The fix

Close it in access control, where the tenant already lives, rather than at the proxy. An anonymous HTTP request whose host names no site now gets **no rows** — in practice a 403, since access returning `false` makes Payload throw rather than answer with an empty list.

The discriminator is **the presence of a `Host` header**, not the presence of a `headers` object. That distinction is the whole correctness of the change: `payload.find` called with no `req` — which is how `findForSite` calls it, and every seed, job and hook besides — gets a synthesized req carrying an *empty* `Headers`, so `headers.get` exists and answers null. Keying on the function denied the app's own render path (see the second commit; it failed 27 tests). Every request reachable from outside carries a Host — HTTP/1.1 requires it, HTTP/2 carries `:authority` — so nothing an attacker can send lands in the exempt branch.

Three callers are deliberately unaffected, because each already has a tenant by other means:

| Caller | Why it still works |
| --- | --- |
| Local API — seed, job, hook, `findForSite` | No `Host` to attribute; `findForSite` names its own site in an explicit `where`, which is what protected it all along |
| Admin session (`req.user`) | The multi-tenant plugin narrows it to that user's own sites |
| API key | Resolved to the one site it names — checked here as well as in `apiKeyAware`, since `media`/`categories`/`theme`/`store` are not wrapped in it |

Doing it here rather than at the proxy is what keeps the admin UI, the site keys and the provisioning platform key working — a blanket `/api/*` deny on the control plane would have broken all three.

## Testing

Run against a real Postgres 16 (installed locally for the audit, since this repo has no CI):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm test:int` | **193/193 passing**, all 16 spec files |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` on both changed files | clean |

`headless.int.spec.ts` confirms both halves: the control-plane read is refused for all five public collections (`pages`, `posts`, `products`, `categories`, `media`), and customer-host scoping, draft exclusion, the caller's-own-`where` narrowing, API keys and the site descriptor are all untouched.

**Not run:** `pnpm test:e2e` — Playwright needs a running dev server and browsers this environment does not have.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: kreneskyp
body:
Closes #2. Track A wave 4 of agent-ix/quoin#286, following the merged
`spec-objects-business#4` and `spec-artifacts-iso#34` as the model.

## What this is

`hazard` and `failure_mode` are now declared against the shared semantic core:
archetypes authored in `typespec/main.tsp` importing `@agent-ix/semantic-core`
0.1.0, **fifteen** emitted JSON Schema 2020-12 documents shipped under
`spec_objects_safety/schemas/` — every declared model, not a subset — and a
manifest `semantic` block referencing them by path and digest at version 0.3.0.
The skeletons are executable typed fixtures with `sysml` alternates, `ocl`
invariants, and seven negative counterparts.

## The safety content

Every scored axis — severity, likelihood, ISO 26262 exposure and
controllability, FMEA detection — admits **either** its own ordinal scale **or**
one of `unknown`, `not_assessed`, `not_applicable`. Those three share no member
with any scale, so an axis nobody looked at can never be read, sorted or scored
as `negligible`, `E0`, `C0` or `none`. Nothing declares a `default` anywhere.

`status: accepted` requires a `provenance` naming who accepted the risk and
when, **and** the `assessment` or `analysis` being accepted: an acceptance of
nothing scored is the same failure wearing a lifecycle state. Every record and
value model is sealed twice — `unevaluatedProperties` is a 2020-12 keyword a
consumer on an older dialect ignores wholesale, so `additionalProperties: false`
says the same thing back to draft-04.

The three advisory lint allow-lists are widened with the same three tokens. At
0.2.0 the only way past them was to write a scale value, so an author who had
not scored an axis was nudged towards `negligible` — the exact collapse this
module exists to prevent. Refusing the honest token was the defect.

`Severity` is recorded as the IEC 61508 / MIL-STD-882 four-band harm scale, not
ISO 26262 `S0..S3`: **no ASIL is derivable from these members and none is
claimed.**

## What it deliberately does not do

No `control`, `risk`, `asset`, `incident`, `interface` or evidence type is
declared — those belong to `spec-objects-security`, `-architecture`,
`-operational` and `engineering-assurance`, and are named by `SemanticId`.
`semantic.imports` stays `{}` with the reason in the manifest: the map pins
imported semantic *packages* at exact versions and none of those neighbours
publishes a semantic contract yet.

The `traceability` model is unchanged fact for fact and asserted so.
`spec-objects-security` reads it across the repository boundary — #13 is
migrating that module concurrently — so changing a verb, a direction or an
object type from this side would silently repoint a neighbour's coverage check.

## The finding worth more than the migration

**The incoming `mitigates` edge these checks require is authorable nowhere in
the catalog.** `spec-objects-security`'s `control` declares
`mitigates: [threat, risk, vulnerability]`, and the `spec-artifacts-iso`
`FR`/`NFR` archetypes declare no `mitigates` at all. So `unmitigated-hazard` —
the question StR-001 says the analysis exists to answer — cannot yet tell a
mitigated hazard from an unmitigated one. Filed as #4 for a coordinated fix, and
recorded in the Test Matrix's Coverage Gaps rather than papered over: the rows
that assert the model assert it as *data*, and say so.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `quire validate --scope . "spec/**/*.md"` | exit 0, structurally clean, **zero** grammar findings |
| `quire coverage --scope .` | **128/128 rows backed (100%)** — a binding census |
| `make test` | 70 passed, 2 xfailed |
| `make test-integrations` | 1 passed (Quoin install roundtrip) |
| `make lint` | ruff + black + the schema drift gate, green |

The two `xfail(strict=True)` rows are explicit expected failures against named
engine defects — quire-rs#221/#394 (a refusal that names nothing) and
quire-rs#391 (a legacy prose form that errors as well as warning). Neither
relaxes a schema and neither skips. The engine is pinned to `quire==0.46.0` and
the version asserted, because a strict expected failure reasoned against a
floating build is a mystery waiting to happen.

## Review round

Eight spec analyses ran in parallel (base, integrity, scope-boundary,
failure-domain, EARS, evidence, dependency, risk-complexity) plus an independent
code review and gap analysis; all eleven artifacts are committed. They caught
four real defects in this branch: a floating doc comment that shipped
`IdentityField` describing itself as sealed when it is the one model
deliberately left open; a matrix range `IT-001-SC-01..IT-001-SC-06` that mints
only its endpoints, leaving four of six steps unbacked while the row read
covered; `make test` collecting `tests_integration/` despite four places

author: calebbarnes
body:
## Summary

Part of COR-1183 (Improved Supervisor). Segment 1 of 5, base of the stack.

Today the Factory supervisor only learns about problems when its five-minute health sweep runs and a human happens to open the Attention rail. This PR gives the Factory a way to ring the supervisor's doorbell: when the sweep opens or reopens a finding, it sends a notification signal to that project's supervisor session so an idle supervisor wakes up and looks.

- `factory_supervisor_findings` gains a nullable `last_notified_at`, stamped occurrence-safely after a successful send and cleared when a finding reopens. One rule (open rows with a null stamp get emitted) covers newly opened, reopened, and crash-between-write-and-emit cases. The first sweep after deploy emits once for every pre-existing open finding (intended catch-up; core coalescing bounds it).
- `notifySupervisor` helper (`supervisor/notify.ts`): ensure-creates the supervisor session before sending (a never-created session would otherwise produce a model-less wake), `coalesceKey` = finding key, priority `high` for supervisor-actionable kinds (`decision-failed`, `decision-stuck`, `start-stalled`, `seat-orphaned`, `seat-missing`) and `low` for human-facing kinds.
- The health worker drains un-notified findings by keyset cursor after each reconciliation; a failing send is logged, left un-stamped for the next sweep, and never blocks the rows behind it.
- Signal-turn auth gap closed: a notification-woken turn carries no factory auth user, so previously it registered zero supervisor tools. `resolveSupervisorScope` now has a trusted session-state path requiring a supervisor-prefixed resourceId, a state project id equal to the resourceId's, a fresh project-ownership lookup, and no fallback for any authenticated caller (org-less or foreign-org auth fails closed). Signal turns register the supervisor read tools only; the seven approval-gated write tools and integration tools stay on authenticated human turns. A supervisor session that cannot prove its scope gets no tools.
- Fixes three `factory.test.ts` assertions left stale by #23001.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/supervisor src/storage/domains/work-items/base.test.ts src/factory.test.ts` in `mastracode/factory`: 8 files, 166 tests
- [x] `pnpm check` (factory) exit 0; root oxfmt check exit 0
- [x] Real-server harness (`mountAgentControllerOnMastra` + real libsql storage): sweep ensure-creates the supervisor session before sending, one `high` record delivered with `coalesceKey` = finding key, second sweep silent, resolve + re-detect re-rings; controller-only context resolves scope from session state and registers exactly the five read tools, forged org resolves no scope
- [ ] Rig finale (segment 5) covers a woken supervisor turn actually calling a tool

author: aryamurray
body:
## Problem

A manifest merged from platform harvests alone breaks on any platform nobody harvested — and only there, which is the worst place for a bug to hide.

Assembly *replaces* generic C. openssl's `aes_core.c`, `bn_asm.c`, `camellia.c`, `chacha_enc.c` and `rc4_enc.c` therefore appear in no asm-enabled platform's source list, so intersecting the harvests drops them. An unlisted architecture would compile 1071 files and fail to link.

`when` blocks are additive with no `else`, so the fallback cannot be expressed as another layer. The unconditional set itself has to be the thing that works everywhere.

## Solution

`--baseline` takes a harvest of a *portable* configure (openssl: `no-asm`) and becomes the unconditional set. Each architecture layer then `exclude`s the generic C its assembly supersedes — using a primitive `ConditionalSources` already had.

openssl across three platforms now merges to:

| condition | sources | exclude | defines |
|---|---|---|---|
| *(portable baseline)* | 1082 | — | — |
| `arch = "aarch64"` | +36 | −3 | +15 |
| `os = "linux", arch = "aarch64"` | +1 | −1 | — |
| `os = "linux", arch = "x86_64"` | +53 | −11 | +14 |
| `os = "macos", arch = "aarch64"` | — | −1 | +1 |

## Design decisions worth your attention

**`--baseline` is repeatable, because one is not enough in two separate ways.** Both were found by the build failing, not by reasoning about it:

- A single `Configure` run is portable in its *architecture* only and still carries that OS's own sources. A Linux `no-asm` baseline drags in `engines/e_afalg.c`, which includes `linux/version.h`, so the cross-build died there. Baselines are intersected, so pass one per OS.
- A baseline harvested from a merely-*configured* tree omitted ten template-generated `.c` files, and the fallback then failed to link on `ossl_der_oid_*`. The generated-source check now covers the baseline on the same terms as the harvests — a baseline with holes is worse than none, since it is exactly what an unharvested platform relies on.

**The exclusions are per-architecture and mechanically derived, not curated.** aarch64 excludes 3 files (chacha, mem_clr, keccak1600) and keeps `aes_core.c`, because arm has no assembly replacement for it; x86_64 excludes 11 including `aes_core.c`. I initially expected aarch64 to exclude `aes_core.c` too and was wrong — the tool was right and my assumption wasn't.

**No new Harbour features were needed.** This uses `when` + `exclude`, both of which already existed. The fix was in how the manifest is *composed*, not in what the manifest can express.

## Known limitations

The baseline only covers OSes you harvest a portable configure for. A platform whose *OS* is unlike both baselines can still carry surprises; two OSes is enough to eliminate the OS-specific sources, not enough to prove neutrality.

Nothing enforces harvesting from a generated tree — the tool now detects missing generated sources, but the operator still has to run the generators and re-harvest.

A shim still has to vendor the generated assembly and headers for the platforms it wants optimised, since regenerating at install time would mean depending on the upstream build system that Harbour exists to replace. That is a registry-shape question rather than a tooling one, and it is not settled here.

## Verification

Both directions from one manifest: native aarch64 builds with assembly (`aesv8-armx.o` present, `_aes_v8_encrypt` in the archive) and computes a SHA-256 matching `shasum`; a cross-build to `x86_64-apple-darwin`, which matches no `when` block, builds the portable baseline with zero assembly objects and computes the same digest under Rosetta.

author: wliang002
body:
Closes the gap #4's AC5 named and #289 split out: the app knew *how many* photos an entrance had
and nothing else, so six head-on shots and a proper view set looked identical to it.

It now knows the six named views from `docs/capture-protocol.md`, records which of them each
entrance has, and says in the viewfinder which one is next and why.

## The part to check rather than trust: this is coaching, not a gate

The 2026-09-01 pivot moved D-021's shot plan out of the instrument and onto paper. This brings back
the *knowledge* of the set without bringing back the refusal:

- every view stays selectable, **including one already covered** — an extra angle is a capture the
  protocol explicitly allows, and an instrument that refused a seventh would cost captures nobody
  can go back for;
- **the shutter never consults coverage** — guarded, not asserted in a comment;
- coverage is recorded **after** the write, so losing guidance can never cost a photo.

## Five of six is not silently "done"

Reported as `5 of 6 · missing Hardware close-up`. The protocol allows five *"if one genuinely
cannot be captured — note which one and why in the entrance record"*, and that is a judgement only
the operator standing at the doorway can make. The app states the position and leaves the call.

Marking a view uncapturable **with its reason** would need the entrance-notes surface, which does
not exist. I would rather say that here than invent a reason-entry UI on a screen whose canon
boards are still pending.

## Why a new store rather than widening the tally

`EntranceTally`'s file is `[String: Int]` and it returns an empty map when decoding fails — so
changing its shape would **silently reset every count already on the capture device**. They also
answer different questions: the tally counts photos including deviations, coverage answers which
named views exist. A count of six is not the same fact as a complete set.

## Verification

- **`xcodebuild test` on iPhone 15 Pro: 237 passed** (12 new) — the coverage states, the summary
  wording, the suggestion, and the store: an unknown slot in the file, an unreadable file, the same
  view recorded twice, two entrances not sharing coverage.
- **pytest: 1151 passed, 5 skipped** (5 new source guards). CI never builds Swift, so the rules
  that must hold are read out of the sources: the app names exactly the protocol's views **in
  order**, a renamed view is noticed (mutation-checked), the shutter does not consult coverage,
  coverage is recorded after the write, and nothing refuses a capture for a covered view.

## Two stale comments corrected

Both were made wrong by this change, so they are in scope: `EntranceTally`'s note that nothing in
the app marks an entrance complete now points at its sibling, and the conditions bar no longer
claims to be the only place an under-shot entrance is visible.

## Not done here

**Not verified on a real device** — same constraint as #290: every install costs a physical signing
session (slots 3/3, 7-day profiles, #255), so the scan flow goes on in one install after the Sep 6
session rather than one session per screen.

**The UI is plain**, deliberately. The canon boards are with James (#251); what is settled here is
which views exist and how coverage is reported, and restyling will not change either.

Refs #289, refs #275, refs #4.

author: nsticco
body:
## Summary

Adds the proposed canonical declarative design for the combined repository-credential overhaul and workspace decoupling:

- **Desired state:** [Repository Access and Workspace Design](https://github.com/MoonLadderStudios/MoonMind/blob/docs/repository-access-workspace-decoupling-plan/docs/RepositoryAccessAndWorkspaceDesign.md)
- **Execution companion:** [Repository Access and Workspace Decoupling Plan](https://github.com/MoonLadderStudios/MoonMind/blob/docs/repository-access-workspace-decoupling-plan/docs/tmp/RepositoryAccessAndWorkspaceDecouplingPlan.md)

The design is a `Canonical declarative` / `System / Feature Design View` with `Status: Proposed`. It defines behavior, ownership, contracts, invariants, rationale, UX, and conformance obligations. It does not claim the feature is implemented or that current APIs already accept its illustrative authoring shapes.

The temporary plan now derives from that design. It retains the inspected baseline, delivery slices, consumer-cutover inventory, migration/rollback, owning-document reconciliation, acceptance matrix, and deployment/upgrade procedures rather than duplicating the desired-state specification.

## Main design decisions

- Repository access is optional execution authority. Scratch, artifact, checkpoint, and explicitly anonymous public-repository work do not inherit a GitHub PAT requirement.
- Extend the existing `RepositoryConnection` domain and preserve Git/Lore provider authority instead of adding a competing Source Control Connection system.
- Use explicit authentication intent, deterministic per-role routing, immutable access snapshots, and bound transport/API consumers.
- Separate connection identity, credential revision, and runtime issuance so PAT rotation and future expiring credentials use the same consumer boundary.
- Preserve independent model, source, collaboration, destination, registry, and artifact permissions. No ambient identity fallback, credential shopping, or source-PAT fallback to GHCR.
- State routing and arbitrary-agent confinement as different guarantees. High-security policy requires a qualified confinement mechanism.
- Save verified content before destructive cleanup and keep compute, save, and publication outcomes distinct.
- Publish Saved Work reuses destination admission and the existing publisher without agent rerun by default, with safe import strategies and exact remote reconciliation.
- Preserve the existing free OpenCode profile/materializer identity, explicit pricing/privacy eligibility, and truthful unavailable states without paid fallback.
- Preserve original historical interpretation/digests while rejecting superseded aliases in new writes.

## Documentation structure

The design has 42 stable claim IDs across `DOC-REQ`, `CONTRACT`, `INV`, `QUALITY`, `TEST`, and `NON-GOAL`. The implementation plan maps its work areas to those claims. Both documents link to the existing module owners. The plan explicitly records the required reconciliation of remote-only recovery guidance rather than implying an unaccepted proposal authorizes bypassing a current gate.

## Scope and validation

Documentation only. This PR changes two Markdown files and does not modify runtime code, credentials, settings, or existing issues.

The original consolidated plan reviewed `main` at `63bce9852ffa33e33cb0b416bc24a654b1b6f92b`. The declarative design was derived from that complete plan and the conversation's agreed recommendations, using the repository's documentation-classification and stable-claim conventions. Current-state findings remain labeled with their reviewed baseline.

Validation performed:
- Checked Markdown table consistency and balanced code fences.
- Checked stable claim-ID uniqueness and that every claim reference in the plan resolves to the design.
- Checked the reciprocal design/plan relative paths.
- Verified stored Git blob hashes against the locally checked documents and confirmed the change diff is limited to the design and its implementation companion.

No runtime tests, full Compose journey, provider qualification, or new live-provider research were performed. The existing runtime behavior is unchanged.

author: seonghobae
body:
## Owner outcome

This Draft is the current-main owner lane for a real required-workflow failure observed in `ContextualWisdomLab/ConceptWeave`.

ConceptWeave Foundation PR #1 predecessor head `8e8783286eac7567803568d9a91010daaf028074` reached hosted Security Scan run `33886162808`. Dependency-review job `101108147137` checked out that exact head, then `Check dependency review support` observed HTTP `403` with curl exit `0` for public, non-fork `ContextualWisdomLab/ConceptWeave`; the job token had `contents: read` and `pull-requests: read`. The pinned dependency-review action never ran. This remains a real hosted owner-path RED, not queue or successor-head evidence.

## RED → minimum owner repair

- `3298df61d97d055050808e32eb27890189b5ea38` adds the test-first regression contract for anomalous public/non-fork 403 responses while preserving final non-200 fail-closed behavior.
- `894a7dbf65ab1567fdce7dc8a80b711958dc66e8` records the exact consumer evidence, GitHub endpoint contract, alternatives and GREEN criterion.
- `0d6c0eb4152576cf8d4595daab0c8d9ea2febbe1` is the minimum production repair: the same job token may re-observe a public/non-fork 403 at most three total attempts, captures bounded non-secret `X-GitHub-Request-Id`, `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` evidence, honors only a small numeric retry delay, and still refuses to set `supported=true` unless the final observation is HTTP 200. Private/internal repositories, forks, transport failures and every other non-200 remain immediate fail-closed paths.
- `0be4a07491322ce3a68fe769728a117452a43831` executes that exact extracted workflow Bash body against a deterministic curl double: 403→403→200 reaches `supported=true` only on the observed 200; persistent public/non-fork 403 fails after exactly three attempts; private or fork 403 fails after one attempt. It also verifies request-id diagnostics and response-body suppression.

The production workflow patch remains confined to the dependency-review support preflight; the pinned dependency-review action, severity policy and sibling scanners are unchanged.

## Current-main restack

Protected `.github/main` subsequently advanced through the queue/admission and test repairs to `b5efbc2762e472e4a380b0503b1f050f76fbb008`. The intervening main delta is disjoint from this PR's three owner files. It was adopted with a two-parent non-force restack: current exact head `41935494aa234eb458f1cc08f006daaa278b9760` has prior owner head `4e585ecd3d9f8e2b419ac82c06a5b363b6c7e20d` as first parent and protected `main@b5efbc2762e472e4a380b0503b1f050f76fbb008` as second parent. Comparing current main to this head reports `behind_by=0` and only these three effective files: `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml`, `docs/doctoring/dependency-review-public-required-workflow-403-20260905.md`, and `tests/test_dependency_review_public_required_workflow_403.py`.

## Exact-head execution evidence

The predecessor restack head `4e585ecd...` materialized Python Security `33929094887`, SAST Semgrep `33929094960`, CodeQL PR `33929094940`, and Security Scan `33929094962`; all reached terminal `cancelled` before useful execution. That non-passing evidence is retained as historical cancellation/admission evidence and is not transferred to the successor.

Fresh pull-request workflows have materialized for exact successor `41935494...`: SAST Semgrep `33934066968`, Python Security `33934066954`, CodeQL PR `33934067035`, and Security Scan `33934067074`. At the current observation all four are queued, so this successor is not GREEN and no predecessor/local evidence is substituted.

No blind/no-op rerun is authorized. Queueing blocks only this validation lane; if a run fails after execution, perform RCA against that exact head before another mutation.

## Relation to #1725

PR #1725 remains valid historical/canonical work for non-200 fail-closed behavior and least-privilege caller permissions, but its branch is deeply diverged from protected main. It was not force-restacked or discarded. This current-main successor carries the newly observed ConceptWeave consumer defect class without weakening #1725's core invariant: **only final HTTP 200 may authorize the pinned dependency-review action**.

An anonymous preflight is deliberately not used. GitHub permits unauthenticated reads for public dependency-diff resources, but the pinned action itself defaults to `github.token`; anonymous preflight success could therefore be false support evidence if the action fails with the same token.

## Exact-head GREEN gate

Require unchanged `41935494...` or a causally repaired non-force successor to obtain terminal owner CI/review evidence, then land through ordinary protection. After protected integration, obtain a fresh unchanged ConceptWeave consumer run where the dependency-review action itself reaches a terminal result. A repeated terminal 403 remains a hard failure with request/rate evidence for further RCA.

No 403-as-success, scanner skip, anonymous-success substitution, self-approval, admin bypass, force push, predecessor-evidence transfer, or no-op rerun is authorized.

Refs #1725.

## Summary

Reported live, right after wiring up real accounts: submitting the onboarding form failed with a generic "Something went wrong. Please try again." — exactly the situation where actually seeing the reason matters most.

**Root cause**: the catch block checked `err instanceof Error`, but Supabase's own errors (`PostgrestError` from a failed insert/select, `AuthError`) are plain objects with a `.message` string — not real `Error` instances. (GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx ve ona bağlı iki zincir bulgusu) kapatıldı.

`package.json`'a tek bir `overrides` girdisi eklendi:

```json
"overrides": { "deepmerge-ts": "^8.0.2" }
```

`npm audit` artık **sıfır** bulgu raporluyor — `--omit=dev` ile de, onsuz da.

Closes #227

## Kararlar

**Neden `overrides`.** Üç bulgunun da tek bir kökü vardı; kökü kaldırmak üçünü birden kapatıyor.

**Eşiğe DOKUNULMADI.** #228'in `--audit-level=critical` kararı olduğu gibi duruyor ve bu bilinçli:
zincirdeki advisory'yi kapatmak ile "hangi seviyede CI kırılsın" sorusunu yanıtlamak **farklı iki
sorudur**. İkincisi, ağaçtaki her yüksek seviyeli bulgunun kapıyı kapatmasını kabul etmek demektir
ve gürültü maliyeti ölçülmeden verilemez. README'deki karar kaydı bunu söyleyecek şekilde
güncellendi; **#227 o karar verilene kadar açık kalmalı** — bu yüzden PR "Closes #227" diyor ama
sabah kapatmadan önce eşiğin ayrı bir issue'ya mı taşınacağına bakmak gerekir (aşağıdaki "Açık
soru").

**Reddedilen alternatifler:**

| Alternatif | Neden reddedildi |
| --- | --- |
| `npm audit fix --force` → `prisma@6.12.0` | 6.19.3'ten **kırıcı** bir geri adım |
| Eşiği `high`'a çekmek | Ayrı bir karar; bu PR'ın konusu değil (yukarıda) |
| Beklemek (Prisma kendi bağımlılığını yükseltsin) | Bugün elde edilebilir bir sonucu belirsiz bir tarihe erteliyordu |

**KALAN RİSK — `overrides` bir zorlamadır.** `@prisma/config` `deepmerge-ts@^7` ilan ediyor; 8'i
biz veriyoruz, yani upstream'in desteklemediği bir bileşim kuruluyor. Bu yüzden **varsayılmadı,
koşuldu**:

```
prisma validate      ✅   prisma generate    ✅
prisma migrate status ✅  prisma migrate deploy ✅   prisma format ✅
```

Prisma CLI'ın bir sonraki yükseltmesinde bu girdinin **hâlâ gerekli olup olmadığı** yeniden
bakılmalıdır: gereksiz kalmış bir `overrides`, sessizce eski bir sürümü sabitleyen bir tuzağa
dönüşebilir. Bu not README'ye yazıldı.

## Nasıl test edildi

| | sonuç |
| --- | --- |
| `lint` | ✅ |
| `typecheck` | ✅ |
| `build` | ✅ |
| `test:integration` | ✅ **746 geçti**, 0 kırmızı |
| `test:security` | ✅ **283 geçti**, 0 kırmızı |
| `test:e2e` | ✅ **178 geçti**, 0 kırmızı |
| `npm audit` | ✅ **0 bulgu** (önce: 3 high) |

`integration/dependency-audit.spec.ts`'e üç kontrol eklendi:

1. `overrides` girdisi var mı ve **istenen** ana sürüm 8+ mı — girdi `^7`'ye çekilirse "var"
   görünüp açık geri gelirdi.
2. Lock dosyasında **çözülmüş** sürüm 8+ mı — `overrides` yazılıp `npm install` koşulmamış
   olabilir; asıl kurulan şey lock'takidir.
3. Karar README'de duruyor mu.

**Bu test, audit job'ının yapamayacağı şeyi yapar:** eşik `critical` olduğu için, `overrides`
düşürülüp üç `high` bulgu geri gelse **CI bunu bildirmez**.

**Duyarlılık kanıtı:** `overrides` geçici olarak `package.json`'dan kaldırıldı → ilgili test
kırmızıya döndü (`package.json'da overrides['deepmerge-ts'] bulunamadı`) → geri yüklendi.

## Bilinen sınırlar / merge sırası

- **`package-lock.json` çakışması olabilir.** #223 (dependabot, typescript 6.0) da lock
  dosyasına dokunuyor. Bu PR merge edilirse dependabot #223'ü kendisi rebase eder; ters sırada
  merge edilirse bu dalda `npm install` ile lock'un yeniden üretilmesi gerekir. #223'e
  dokunulmadı.
- README değişikliği mevcut `### npm audit CI job'ı` bölümünün **içindedir**, dosyanın sonuna
  ekleme yapılmadı — #230 ve #231 README'nin sonuna bölüm eklediği için o çakışmadan bilinçli
  olarak kaçınıldı.
- Advisory'nin kendisi kapandı ama **eşik kararı hâlâ `critical`**; kod yolunda gerçekten bulunan
  bir `high` bulgu yine CI'ı kırmaz. README'deki "KABUL EDİLEN KALAN RİSK" bölümü aynen duruyor.

## Sabah karar vermen gereken

**#227 kapatılsın mı, yoksa "eşiği `high`'a çek" kararı için açık mı kalsın?** README'deki karşı
önlem #1 eşiğin yükseltilmesini #227'ye bağlamıştı. Advisory'ler kapandığına göre o bağ artık
geçerli değil; ya #227 kapatılıp eşik için yeni bir issue açılmalı, ya da #227 eşik kararı için
açık tutulmalı. Muhafazakâr seçenek olarak PR'ı "Closes #227" ile açtım ama **eşiği
değiştirmedim**; merge etmeden önce bu tercihi netleştirmek isteyebilirsin.

показал оба сервиса на bc12cf5, задеплоенных 2026-09-04T21:14:57 — момент
мержа PR #23. Railway подписан на main внешнего репозитория и выкатывает
сам. Значит "деплой ручной, копим пачку, ждём отмашки" было неверно:
мерж в main = деплой на прод, промежутка "влито но не выкачено" нет.
Гейт качества надо ставить ДО мержа. Решение (отключать ли авто-деплой)
за владельцем.

Причина: env впрыскивается при старте контейнера, работавшие api/worker
держали старый пароль, любое новое подключение падало на AUTH
(redis.exceptions.AuthenticationError, connection.py:475). Симптом
обманчив: /health отдавал 200, потому что Redis не трогает, а все
Redis-пути — 500; worker был CRASHED.

Починка: railway redeploy без --from-source для обоих сервисов —
перезапуск существующего деплоя, без пересборки и без новых коммитов.
До рестарта программно сверено, что ссылочный REDIS_URL у обоих
потребителей уже содержит новый пароль (значения не печатались).

Восстановление подтверждено фактом:

- /exports/{uuid}/download 500 -> 404
- worker CRASHED -> RUNNING, в логах "Connected to redis://default:**@
  redis.railway.internal:6379//" и "celery@... ready."
- сквозная проба: задача принята и снята worker'ом с очереди
  (pending -> running -> стадия QA)

Уроки записаны: /health не индикатор живости (зависимости не трогает) —
проверять путём, который реально ходит в Redis, где 404 = здоров;
ротация секрета у работающих сервисов обязана сопровождаться рестартом
потребителей.
