author: mangokingtw
body:
Since a January 2026 Windows update, Auto-Type no longer reaches the "Windows Security" credential prompt. The prompt is owned by `CredentialUIBroker.exe` and runs at integrity `0x200a`, above the `0x2000` of an ordinary process, so UIPI discards the input — silently: `SendInput` returns the full count with `GetLastError() == 0` and the fields stay empty.

`uiAccess` is the exemption, but it is a property of a whole binary, which is why 13070 had to be reverted in 13116 — such a binary cannot start from a user-writable location, ending the portable ZIP. So this adds `keepassxc-uiaccess-helper`, built and installed the way `keepassxc-proxy` is, and `AutoTypePlatform::beginSequence()`/`endSequence()` around the action loop to start it for the credential prompt only (checked by window class *and* by the owning image being `credentialuibroker.exe`) and stop it afterwards. `raiseWindow()` cannot host the decision because the entry-level path passes no window and never calls it. Where the helper is absent or unsigned, `::SendInput` is used exactly as before and a warning says why.

The helper is a UIPI bypass for whatever can talk to it, so it takes one target window at startup, drops any batch whose target is not the foreground window, bounds batch sizes, holds no database handle, writes no files, and exits when KeePassXC closes the pipe.

Two questions for you. Delegation is **off by default** and enabled only by `Security/AutoTypeCredentialPrompts` in the ini — there is no settings-page entry, because whether to present this to users, and how, seemed yours to decide rather than something to settle in the same change as the mechanism. As it stands that means a user hitting this bug gets a log warning telling them the key exists and nothing else. Should it have a checkbox, or default on? And would you rather the helper were verified by signature as well as by location (see below)?

* Fixes 12956

## Verifying the peer

Both ends check the other before anything crosses the pipe, and there is **no signature check** — deliberately, and this is the part most worth arguing about:

- KeePassXC will only launch a helper that sits beside it **and** only when the application itself is under a directory Windows grants uiAccess from (`FOLDERID_ProgramFiles*`, `GetSystemDirectoryW`, asked of the OS rather than read from `%ProgramFiles%`, which is inherited and therefore settable by whoever starts the process). Elsewhere the grant cannot be issued anyway, so refusing costs nothing; where it can, the directory is one a standard user cannot write to.
- The helper requires the pipe's server to be the `KeePassXC.exe` beside it ([`GetNamedPipeServerProcessId`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-getnamedpipeserverprocessid)), and re-checks per batch that the target is a credential dialog owned by `CredentialUIBroker` and holds the foreground. It exits rather than run without the uiAccess it was started for.
- KeePassXC requires the connecting client to be the process it launched ([`GetNamedPipeClientProcessId`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-getnamedpipeclientprocessid)), holding the process handle across the check so the id cannot be recycled.
- The pipe is per-sequence, randomly named, `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`, single-instance, `PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS`, with a DACL admitting only the current user — the same restriction `QLocalServer::UserAccessOption` gives the browser integration socket.

[PowerToys authenticates the peer of its privilege-crossing pipe by image path **plus** Authenticode](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/common/interop/pipe_caller_auth.cpp) (microsoft/PowerToys#49527). It has to: its pipe is reachable from anywhere on the machine, and it pins the publisher by name, which is why it also re-anchors the chain in the machine root store. Here the pipe is per-sequence and the peer is a process this one launched from a fixed path inside a directory only an administrator can write, so the location rule carries what the signature would add. If you would rather have the signature check as well, say so and I will add it back — it was in an earlier revision.

What none of this defends against is a process that already holds `PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE` or `PROCESS_VM_READ` on KeePassXC; that attacker can read the master key directly, and is the case `SECURITY.md` excludes.

## Testing strategy

A patched and an unpatched build from the same steps, run against a real `CredentialUIBroker` prompt. Three preconditions are measured rather than assumed, because each of them can turn a passing run into a meaningless one: KeePassXC must be at Medium integrity (a High one reaches the prompt with or without the patch), the prompt must not be at High either (its integrity follows whatever raised it, so the host that raises it is Medium too), and the helper must be seen to start (otherwise "the prompt was not filled in" cannot be told apart from "the helper never ran").

```
                      patched                  control
keepassxc integrity   Medium (0x2000)          Medium (0x2000)
prompt integrity      0x200a                   0x200a
helper started        True (uiAccess 0x2010)   False
prompt submitted      True                     False
```

The refusals are measured in the same run as a positive control, because a run of refusals alone cannot tell "correctly refused" from "nothing worked at all": the setting off, the application installed where a standard user can write, and a target that is not a credential dialog, against a control that must start the helper.

The run is driven by [wintegrate](https://github.com/mangokingTW/wintegrate), a Windows GUI-automation library of mine, which handles window discovery, focus, UI Automation and the screen recording. Recordings and timelines: [credui-evidence-12956](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/releases/tag/credui-evidence-12956). The harness, the refusal cases and the workflow are in mangokingTW/keepassxc#3, stacked on this branch so that its diff is only the evidence -- kept out of this PR because it depends on that library.

No unit test: the window under test belongs to another process at a higher integrity level, so there is nothing to instantiate in-process.

## Type of change
- ✅ Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- ✅ New feature (change that adds functionality)

New feature as well as bug fix because it adds an installed executable and two virtuals to `AutoTypePlatformInterface`: the Windows installer has to ship and sign `keepassxc-uiaccess-helper.exe`, and a build that does not gets the old behaviour. Nothing changes on the other platforms, and `KPXC_FEATURE_UIACCESS_HELPER` is forced off outside Windows/MSVC.

body: ### Description The BCDC button has been removed from Block Checkout (express button section) under SDK v6, leaving merchants with BCDC and no ACDC with no card option there at all. This adds the redirect gateway to replace it: a "Debit & Credit Cards" row whose "Proceed to PayPal" button sends the buyer to PayPal's hosted **guest card** page. Also resolves reports that BCDC does not appear on block checkout, though not its account-specific 403 from find-eligible-methods. Includes an adjacent fix in `ReturnUrlEndpoint`: it resolved the order's gateway from available gateways, but continuation mode leaves only PayPal available, so any non-PayPal gateway that sent the buyer there failed with "Payment gateway is unavailable" on return. Now falls back to registered gateways (affects AXO too), and is untested because the method is private behind a caller that ends in `exit()`. ### Screenshots | Before - BCDC Missing | After - BCDC as a regular gateway | | :--- | :--- | ||| ### Steps to Test Requires the v6 SDK flag, BCDC enabled, ACDC disabled. **Use a private window** - PayPal shows the login screen to buyers it recognises from cookies, whatever the landing page says. 1. Set the PayPal landing page to **"Login page"** - the setting this gateway must override. 2. As a guest, add a product and open the **block** checkout. Express Checkout shows PayPal only, no card button. 3. Select **Debit & Credit Cards** - the order button reads **Proceed to PayPal**. 4. Click it. PayPal shows **card fields**, with the billing address pre-filled from checkout. 5. Complete payment. You land on order-received; the order is `processing` with payment method **Debit & Credit Cards** (`ppcp-card-button-gateway`), not PayPal. 6. Repeat with the **PayPal** method - it must still show the **login** screen, proving the override is scoped to cards. 7. Regression, classic checkout: the "Debit & Credit Cards" row still renders PayPal's card button inline. 8. Regression, block cart: no card option appears.

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
## The defect

The shipped `Case behandeling` flow triggers on `object.created` for schema `case`, **unscoped by case type**, and moved cases through six literal status names. **Exactly one case type in the app carried all six.**

Measured on the shipped demo caseload, on a rig: **8 of 18 runs died at `status-behandeling`** with `status_not_found_on_case_type` — every `Klacht behandeling` and every `Subsidieaanvraag`, because a complaint is under `Onderzoek` and a subsidy under `Beoordeling`, and both are right.

The suite stayed green because both `case-flow-live-journeys.spec.ts` and `testEveryStatusTheFlowUsesIsSeededOnTheCaseType()` file their cases against the one complete case type. That is the blind spot rather than the coverage.

## The scoping decision, and why the alternatives were rejected

**Scoping the trigger is not available.** `TriggerObjectNode::configKeys()` admits exactly `event`, `register`, `schema`; `validateConfig()` requires all three and the trigger index is keyed on that triple. There is no field-level filter — and there could not be a useful one here anyway, because a case type is a per-installation uuid, so a shipped flow can never name one. The trigger cannot be scoped, so **every case type the app ships runs this flow and every one of them has to be able to.**

**Giving every case type the six statuses is wrong, not merely heavy.** `Bij commissie` on a pothole report is not a missing status, it is a wrong one — that case never goes to a planning commission. And it does not survive first contact with a customer creating their own case type.

**So: statuses resolve by ROLE.** A `statusType` carries a `role` — `intake`, `pending-info`, `in-progress`, `review`, `closed`, `stranded` — and a step says which role it means. A role is a machine key and survives what a name does not: `statusType.name` is declared `x-translatable`, so a literal is broken by a language change alone, quite apart from every case type spelling its working phase differently. The literal name is **kept as the fallback**, so a case type nobody has annotated behaves exactly as it did before.

## What a case type that still cannot satisfy the flow does

Explicitly, not by crashing:

- A step the flow declares **`required: false`** — `pending-info`, `review`, `stranded` — is **skipped and records itself as skipped**, with the role it wanted and the reason `case_type_models_no_such_phase`. Optionality is a claim the flow author makes per step, never a fallback the handler chooses; `required` is read as "anything but an explicit `false` is required", because the cost of a wrongly-required step is a visible failure and the cost of a wrongly-optional one is a case that never moves and says nothing.
- A **required** role that does not resolve — `intake`, `in-progress`, `closed` — still fails the step, named. That failure is now queryable as a *failed* run rather than reading as a clean end (ConductionNL/openregister#3425), which is the half of this that hid the other half.

## Seeds

The four demo case types, the flow's own demo case type and the VTH set are annotated. **VTH is annotated only where the mapping is unambiguous** — `Advies`, `Bekendmaking`, `Zienswijze`, `Akkoord`, `Betaald` and the later inspection phases are deliberately left blank, because a guessed role would route a case to a phase that merely *looks* right, which is worse than the case type modelling no such phase.

Both seed files were edited textually rather than re-serialised: a `json.dump` round-trip produced a 1108-line diff for 20 semantic changes, which was thrown away.

## The guard test that was missing

`testEveryShippedCaseTypeCanRunEveryRequiredStepOfTheFlow` reads **every** case type the app ships, in all three seed shapes (the flat `objects` + `@ref` shape the demo caseload actually uses, and the two nested shapes), and fails naming the case type, the role and the node. Proven to bite by removing one role from a seed:

```
Case type "dossiq_register.json:omgevingsvergunning" models no status with role
"in-progress", so the shipped flow dies at node "status-behandeling" on every
case of that type.
```

## Verified locally

CI is bottlenecked, so this was verified locally and judged by exit code:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `phpunit` | **2963 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors** (exit 0) |
| `phpcs` (changed files) | exit 0 |
| `phpstan` (changed files) | exit 0 |
| `psalm` (changed files) | exit 0 |
| `phpmd` (changed files, both rulesets) | exit 0 |
| `hydra-gates --scope-to-diff` (v1.14.0) | exit 0 — ALL 40 APPLICABLE GATES PASSED, 40 of 40 ran |

`handle()` was split into `resolve()` and `unresolved()` because the added branching pushed it over phpmd's complexity ceiling.

## Rig evidence

Two throwaway Nextcloud 32 + Postgres 16 rigs on free ports (8641 / 8642), one running this branch and one running plain `development`, seeded identically with `occ dossiq:demo:seed` (18 cases) after `occ app:disable firstrunwizard`, flows adopted with `occ dossiq:flows:adopt --user=admin --enable`, and drained with `occ background-job:execute 138 --force-execute` — not `cron.php`, which is interval-gated. Markers were grepped inside the installed tree to confirm which code was running.

**`status-behandeling`, per case type:**

| case type | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Omgevingsvergunning | completed 6 | completed 6 |
| Melding openbare ruimte | completed 4 | completed 4 |
| **Klacht behandeling** | **failed 4** | **completed 4** |
| **Subsidieaanvraag** | **failed 4** | **completed 4** |

10 completed / 8 failed → **18 completed / 0 failed.** (All 18 then stop at `decide-register-b` because decidiq is not installed on the rig — an environment gap, and the thing that gave the openregister half a real failed run to show.)

Roles as actually stored, which is what made the two failing types work:

```
Klacht behandeling   | Onderzoek   | in-progress
Subsidieaanvraag     | Beoordeling | in-progress
```

**The optional path, proven live.** An incomplete case filed against `Melding openbare ruimte`, which models no `pending-info` status:

```
BEFORE  start ok -> status-ontvangen ok -> check-complete ok -> status-wacht FAILED
        run: status=stopped  error=NULL          (dead, and reads as a clean end)

AFTER   start ok -> status-ontvangen ok -> check-complete ok -> status-wacht ok
        -> count-round ok -> ask-aanvulling suspended
        run: status=suspended                    (correctly waiting on a person)
```

and the skip is recorded, not silent — the step's output item carries:

```json
{"skipped": true, "reason": "case_type_models_no_such_phase",
 "statusRole": "pending-info", "statusName": "Wacht op aanvulling"}
```

Both rigs torn down with `docker compose down -v`.

Pairs with ConductionNL/openregister#3425 — one story: the failed-run defect is what hid this one.

author: johnhenry
body:
Five commits, one concern each, from an audit of the pairing and transport path. Every finding was reproduced at runtime before it was written down, and every test added here was fault-injected — broken deliberately, watched go red, restored.

Closes #3, closes #4, closes #6, closes #7. Refs #5 (docstring corrected; the offer-in-QR design it describes is deliberately not implemented here).

## Test numbers

Full workspace suite, every package's own `npm test` script, exit codes read directly:

| | tests | pass | fail | non-zero exits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (`main`, b93f4d7) | 4506 | 4506 | 0 | 0 |
| after | 4533 | 4533 | 0 | 0 |

All five `examples/0*.mjs` still exit 0.

## The commits

**1. Make the pairing token actually single-use** (#3, security)

The nonce was generated and its presence checked, then never recorded or compared. Five redemptions of the same encoded token, five accepts. `validateToken()` now consumes on success; entries age out with the TTL and are capped so a flood cannot grow the set without bound. `{ consume: false }` peeks without spending.

*Behaviour change:* `validateToken()` is no longer pure. That is the point — a check that leaves the token spendable is not a single-use check. Callers who validate twice on the purpose path need `{ consume: false }` on the first.

**2. Keep connectViaToken's signaling channel open until the transport closes** (#4)

`negotiate()` returns a created-but-**not connected** transport — its own docstring says so. `connectViaToken()` closed the signaling WebSocket right after it resolved, so the documented QR-pairing flow could not complete a connection at all:

```
ws.send register
negotiate() returns unconnected transport
ws.close                                   <-- here
transport.connect(): signaler.connected = false
THREW: SignalingClient not connected
```

Teardown now hangs off the transport's close event. A signaler we created and cannot attach to is returned as `result.signaler` for the caller to dispose; a borrowed one is still never closed by us.

**3. Stop sending every peer to Google's STUN server by default** (#6, privacy)

`DEFAULT_ICE_SERVERS` is now `[]`, `NATTraversal` defaults to no STUN, and `mergeIceServers([])` returns `[]` — an explicit empty array is a decision, and it was previously overridden. `PUBLIC_STUN_SERVERS` is exported for callers who want the old behaviour, with the disclosure spelled out.

**4. Say what DirectInputHandshake actually does** (#5)

"Direct pairing without a signaling server" was true of the key exchange only; the token carries no SDP and `connectViaToken()` throws without a signaler. Docstring corrected, offer-in-QR recorded as the design that would make the original claim true, and a test pins the token's field list so this cannot drift silently.

**5. Feature-detect the platform floors instead of crashing on them** (#7)

`supportsSharedWorker()` added and `start()` now throws a named error instead of `ReferenceError: SharedWorker is not defined` (Android WebView has no SharedWorker at any API level). `probeEd25519Support()` added and `PodIdentity.generate()` names the Safari 17 / Chromium 137 requirement. And `supportsX25519()` — which was `!!crypto.subtle`, true in every browser since ~2015, gating a fallback that could therefore never fire — is now a real probe.

## On the tests

The prompt for this audit was that these suites are mock-heavy in a way that has hidden real breakage before. #4 is exactly that shape: 4506 tests passing, and the one `connectViaToken` test took the branch where the bug does not run, with a mock transport that never touched the signaler. So the new tests are written to fail against the old code specifically:

| injection | red |
|---|---|
| never reject a seen nonce | 5 tests |
| validate but never record the nonce (the original bug) | 6 tests |
| remove the replay-set cap | 1 test |
| restore the eager `signaler.disconnect()` (the original bug) | 2 tests |
| restore Google STUN as the default | 6 tests |
| put an `sdp` field in the token | 1 test |
| remove the SharedWorker guard | 1 test |
| make the Ed25519 probe optimistic | 1 test |
| revert X25519 to the presence check | 1 test |

## Still not covered

Nothing here has run in a real browser or moved a real packet. Every WebRTC test still mocks `RTCPeerConnection`, so #4's fix is verified against a transport stub shaped like the real one — created but not connected — and not against an actual DTLS handshake. The Android WebView and iOS 16 claims are reasoned from engine shipping history, not measured on a device. Those remain the gap worth closing next.

author: syang620
body:
## Change

Extract metric matching, ambiguity handling, target selection and ticker/year resolution from orchestration into a pure structured-fact resolver. Preserve merged-PR24 behavior, including first-match selection, single-target fallback, hint/metadata precedence and exact diagnostic reasons. The selected target is returned unchanged as opaque metadata; filing-form eligibility and capability permission remain in orchestration.

The oracle was frozen at `fae5bbf` before implementation: 170 cases capture actual merged-PR24 isolated resolution, capability decisions, complete execution results and exact ordered SEC metric arguments. Expected values are static observations, not recomputed by the new resolver. A recording SEC client makes this a resolution/execution-contract measurement, not a financial-data benchmark.

## Validation

Frozen implementation: `c149f73d073a306cf34d938955ae6cc739191528`, clean tracked worktree.

- Exact resolver/execution snapshot parity: **170/170**.
- Calculator: **20/20**; analyst output repair: **20/20**.
- Grounding: **37/37**; degradation: **14/14**, consistency rates **100%**.
- Full tests: **719 passed**, **47 subtests passed**, **2 known PR24 failures**, 1 warning. The existing failures are planner `alias_002` routing and retrieval no-tool-call attempt count. All 174 new resolver tests pass.
- Python 3.11.14, environment-only pytest 9.0.2; dependency manifests unchanged.

Fresh review of `c149f73` [found no major issues or inline findings](https://github.com/syang620/Finsearch-reboot/pull/25#issuecomment-5546911177). All SHA-keyed offline and live evidence is recorded in `docs/EVALUATION_BASELINES.md` and `artifacts/evals/agents/v1/` under `c149f73`.

## Live result — release blocked

The unchanged 15-case gate ran **once** and **failed: 8/15 non-critical cases**, score **0.859390**, seven critical cases, zero evaluator errors. No PR7 exception has been granted; this PR remains draft.

- Six `ANALYST_MODEL_TIMEOUT after 120.0s` failures: `KB_002`, `KB_003`, `HYBRID_002`, `HYBRID_003`, `ANALYST_001`, `ANALYST_003` (all IDs have the `AGENT_V1_` prefix).
- `HYBRID_001`: `ANALYST_GROUNDING_INVALID`, with evidence-type and row-text mismatches.

Routing, metadata, lane expectations, structured metric/status matching and applicable consistency checks remain **100%**. All seven structured executions yield visible typed evidence with complete measured provenance. Replaying the captured live planner inputs through the actual merged-PR24 executor with captured SEC responses reproduces **7/7 complete results and exact ordered SEC arguments**, without external calls.

The six timeouts exceed the plan's grounding-only exception scenario. The 120-second model-call limit and analyst source are unchanged; the underlying timeout cause is not established. The run contains a substantial wall-clock gap, so no performance comparison is claimed. Model digests, corpus, dataset, driver and before/after index fingerprint match PR24. This single run does not establish a causal resolver regression or a semantic-quality trend.

All failures are preserved. No live rerun, timeout increase, provider tuning, relaxed grounding, or expanded PR7 fix was performed. Further investigation, a rerun or any release exception requires new explicit owner direction.

## Release rule

Any resolver, routing or tool-argument mismatch blocks PR7. Run the unchanged 15-case live gate once after review. Preserve unrelated analyst grounding failures without tuning PR7; merging a failed gate requires a new explicit PR7 exception. `PR24-GROUNDING-001` does not carry forward.

PR6 grounding validation, capability aliases, retrieval, evidence admission, lane semantics, providers, retry budgets and gate thresholds are unchanged. Filing/amendment semantics remain PR8 scope.

body:
Follow-up to the merged #163. Two things: the **B/C proof** that was missing, and a closeout report of what actually merged.

## The B/C proof — no longer synthetic

The previous pass deleted its search-continuation tests because a synthetic vessel returned `impossible` and any assertion over an empty option list would pass vacuously. That is now unnecessary: **the owner's own run recovered and completed on the fixed build**, and its durable event log contains the exact transition.

| time | rev | option | finalMassG | BANANA % | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16:19:04Z | 1 | `restore_original_recipe` | 1149.9 | 30.0026 | refused on reload |
| 18:56:01Z | 2 | `restore_original_recipe` | **1150.1** | **29.9974** | **accepted** |

`CREAM 129.9 → 130` and `DEXTROSE 63.2 → 63.3` return the 0.1 g that tenth-gram rounding gave away — the whole difference between the two candidates.

Run `2fc85403…` is now `completed` (18:57:19Z) with a completion snapshot, `actual_revision` 15, `rescue_revision` 2, and a final actual vector equal to the accepted plan — so every top-up executed. The rev-2 `rescue_applied`/`rescue_accepted` events carry `supersededRescueRevision: 1`, so the durable supersession audit works on real data.

Four new cases assert the transition on those concrete vectors: candidate N refused by the terminal authority, candidate N+1 accepted by the **same** authority, BANANA inside its published hard limit and at/above the derived minimum legal batch (`345 / 0.30`, computed not hard-coded), and the accepted candidate reopenable by recovery. 12 cases in the file, none vacuous.

## App/Edge parity — probed live

A deliberately wrong `expectedEngineBundleSha256`, which the deployed function rejects **before** any DB access, returns its own value:

```
app  PRODUCTION_RESCUE_BUNDLE_SHA256 = 177c39a8…2db89878
edge actualEngineBundleSha256        = 177c39a8…2db89878   MATCH
```

`production-rescue-authorize` v27, `verify_jwt: true`, project `tunabqqrwabacxjcxxkz`. Nothing was mutated. Source closure `61e879e9…` is declared by the same generated metadata module that reported the matching bundle SHA — inferred from it, not probed independently.

## Closeout report

`reports/production-rescue/CLOSEOUT_163.md` is the technical authority for the merged behaviour. #163's body still describes the rejected `alreadyAuthorized` approach, and the merge also carries follow-up work that body predates (the supersession audit migration, store and Edge `logic.ts` changes, the `.fixture.ts` renaming). Rather than rewrite history, the report records what actually shipped: one terminal authority at practicalization, recovery that supersedes instead of blessing or stranding, the durable audit, and the fixture-fidelity repairs — including that **the tara scare was not tara** (3 g against a 5 g band max in both candidates; those tests were failing on the BANANA policy and carrier gaps).

author: antoniopalese
body:
Every Tensor method was const and allocated its result: one allocation and
one free per op per iteration in a training loop, and a peak footprint equal
to the whole expression graph rather than the working set.

Each op now has three forms, of which exactly one is a real implementation:

    auto c = a.add(b, s);      // allocates the result, then calls add_out
    a.add_out(b, out, s);      // <- the body
    a.add_(b, s);              // == a.add_out(b, a, s)

add_out returns Tensor& (the destination), add_ returns *this, so calls
chain; the no-stream spellings are one-line delegates. operator+= -= *= /=
delegate to the underscore family.

Families: add/sub/mul/div (tensor and scalar), apply, apply_binary, relu,
sigmoid and fill_ have all three forms. matmul, transpose and permute have
_out but no in-place form -- their kernels read elements they do not write,
so _check_alias_none rejects an aliased destination rather than returning a
plausible wrong answer.

The elementwise family may alias because the CPU loop, the contiguous GPU
fast path and the rank-specialized kernels all read index i and write index
i. That rests on each buffer being one flat run, so _check_alias_elementwise
re-checks is_contiguous(): the day a strided view can alias a different
region of the same allocation, it throws instead of computing the wrong
thing.

Consequences:

- contiguous.cuh drops __restrict__ from its three kernels. In-place calls
  them with dst equal to a source, which is precisely the aliasing the
  qualifier promises away. Measured, it cost nothing: add at 16 M went
  230.2-233.4 -> 228.6-230.7 GB/s and relu 232.9-234.6 -> 233.4-235.5, i.e.
  inside run-to-run spread. The read-only path comes from the explicit __ldg
  in device_load, not from restrict-driven inference.
- _out is where operand validation now lives, so a GPU add between
  mismatched shapes throws instead of running off the end of a buffer.
- fill_ takes a stream and no longer routes through the legacy _fill
  dispatch struct, which now has no callers at all.
- apply_binary gained the stream overload roadmap 4.4 was asking for, since
  apply_binary_out takes one by construction.

Numbers (benchmark_report.md section 9, harness scripts/bench_inplace.py):
1.2-1.6x below ~64 K on both backends where allocation is a large fraction
of the op, shrinking to 1.04x at 16 M where the kernel dominates and
HostPool/cudaMallocAsync already recycle the block. That is the honest
ceiling for the time argument. The memory argument does not shrink, and the
tests assert it: data_ptr unchanged across a 100-step loop, the property a
correct-but-reallocating implementation would fail while passing every value
check.

Python gets the whole family through int-returning C entry points (nothing
is allocated, no ownership changes hands), with __iadd__ and friends
returning self so `a += b` does not silently rebind the name.

tests/test_inplace.cpp (25 tests) and python/tests/test_inplace.py (35).
All 13 correctness suites and 174 Python tests pass; compute-sanitizer
memcheck clean over test_inplace, test_streams, test_allocator_stream and
test_stress.

author: playjukeff
body:
Connect a league by username: the worker looks it up, the picker chooses which one, and the connection lives on the **account** rather than in this browser — the handoff's own rule that connect routes through account creation, and the only way a league follows somebody to their phone.

Sleeper's public API needs no key and **has no write endpoints at all**, so "connecting is read-only" is a property of the integration rather than a promise somebody has to keep. No password reaches this app.

## Verified against a real league

The owner created one mid-review. "Juke Fantasy Football" turned out to be the *league* name — the username is `chasecantwell`, found from the invite link's `og:title` after five username guesses came back null against a demonstrably working API.

| | result |
|---|---|
| `lookupUser` | user + 1 league |
| unknown username | `not-found`, distinct from `offline` |
| `leagueSnapshot` | 10 rosters joined, roster 1 → owner, 9 → `Unclaimed` |
| metadata | 2026, 10 teams, week 1, waiver budget 100, 6 playoff spots |
| `live.js` methods | all three, against the real worker |
| League Room render | 10 rows, "You · chasecantwell" highlighted |

The `Unclaimed` fallback and the "don't print the manager twice when it equals the team name" guard both fired for the first time and both behaved.

## Real data found a defect a stub could not

The connected League Room drew real standings under an eyebrow reading **"IN-SEASON · PREVIEW"**, and a sub-line promising "power ranks" the live room deliberately doesn't draw. It was telling the reader to distrust numbers that are their own. Connected, the hero now reads `🏟 JUKE FANTASY FOOTBALL · 10 TEAMS · WEEK 1` — the handoff's own connected eyebrow. The other three rooms still say PREVIEW, correctly: their content really is still sample.

Fixing that introduced a hook-count bug (`useLeagueSnapshot` below three early returns, on a component that doesn't unmount between room routes) which was **caught by re-reading, then verified** by walking eight route switches with no error raised.

## A test seam, because a real league proves only the happy path

`SLEEPER_BASE` mirrors the existing `TANK01_BASE`. `node worker/test-sleeper.mjs` is **53 assertions against a stub with no network and no wrangler** — it imports the module and passes the base in. It is in CI beside the two Python suites.

Confirmed by mutation: dropping the roster cap, the username's `encodeURIComponent`, the league id's, and turning the catch into a rethrow each go red. The encoding case had to be **rewritten** — it first asserted a path-shaped username resolves to no user, and that passed with the encoding removed, because `/user/a/../state/nfl` normalises onto `/state/nfl`. It asserts the path the stub was *asked for* now.

## Also here

The phase strip gates on a connected league rather than on being signed in — its own comment already called a row of locked labels above the same locked cards "the same fact twice", and that applied to a signed-in reader with no league too. Verified in both directions: 0 strip cells without a league, 5 with one.

## Deployed

Worker version `ddcc3c5c`; D1 migration `0005_leagues.sql` applied to remote (verified via `sqlite_master` and `PRAGMA table_info`, not the ✅). Migration `0004` turned out to have been applied outside the migration system — both files are `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so it recorded itself as a no-op.

## Still unverified

**The connect write.** `/me/leagues` correctly 401s without a token; proving the 200 needs a real Clerk sign-in against this deploy. Everything upstream of it is proven against a real league.

Full suite: **145 passed, 0 failed.**

author: codingclub12
body:
`config/csa-slide-embeds.js` goes from an empty map to **152 ids**: 38 lessons, two teaching days each, a teacher and a student deck per day. Units 2, 3 and 4 serve real decks to an entitled teacher now. Unit 1 still serves none, deliberately.

## The importer reported success over an empty file

On its first real run:

```
Wrote 152 ids to config/csa-slide-embeds.js (generated 2026-09-04).

$ node -e 'console.log(require("./config/csa-slide-embeds.js").count())'
0
```

Two faults, and the second is what made the first invisible.

**The pattern.** `/const SLIDE_IDS = \{[\s\S]*?\n\};/` requires a newline before the closing brace. That matches a populated map and misses `const SLIDE_IDS = {};` on one line — which is the only form a **first** import ever meets. It survived every dry run and failed on the one run that mattered.

**The guard.** `if (next === src)` asked whether the *file* changed. The `GENERATED_AT` substitution beside it always succeeds, so the file always differed and the guard always passed.

That is the same shape as the grade-path audit bug fixed this morning in #527: a check satisfied by something other than the thing it exists to verify. It compares the ids replacement specifically now, and the date is applied afterwards so it cannot mask anything.

The script also re-reads its own output through `require()` and refuses if the count on disk disagrees with what it believes it wrote. Writing is not evidence that writing worked.

## Verified against the sheet, not against the script

```
CSV OK rows checked: 152
mismatches         : 0
config count()     : 152
VERDICT: every id in the config came from the sheet, and nothing else is in it
```

## Checks

**38 assertions to 57.** The suite pins the writer's pattern against the config's actual shape, including the empty form, because the two files must agree and neither imports the other.

Mutation tested: restoring the newline-requiring pattern fails the empty-map assertion **and only that one**, since the old pattern genuinely does match the other two cases. That is what makes it a real isolation rather than an aggregate red.

### The gate's own expectations moved

Four assertions read "reports zero decks until conversion runs", which stopped being true the moment it ran. The suite noticing that is the suite working. They assert the real invariant now:

- the 38 authored lessons each serve 4 decks
- the 15 Unit 1 lessons serve none
- **no lesson serves an odd number** — half a pair means handing a student the deck meant for the front of the room

## What is still between this and a teacher seeing slides

Landing this does not put decks on the storefront. Two theme-side things remain, both outside this repo:

1. `theme.liquid` injects the gate asset on a prefix match scoped to Unit 1 (`ap-csa-lesson-1-`). Units 2-4 handles do not match it, so the gate script is not loaded on those pages at all.
2. Board 212: Units 2-4 lesson pages lack `data-course` / `data-lesson-id`, and Unit 3 has no `#apcsa-lesson` wrapper at all, so even a loaded gate could not tell which lesson it is on.

I have not verified item 1 against the live storefront yet, only against this repo's record of it. Worth checking before anyone calls this shipped.

author: cmlibra71
body:
## A free-text Instructions box on a product page (card kyMjCmAw)

One row of the 0CDcCYmO Product Test matrix. The **Custom Stainless Steel** product needs an
"Instructions" box the shopper types into at **no price** — matching the Zoey reference page
`industrykitchens.com.au/custom-stainless-steel`, which renders one required text field titled
"Instructions" directly above Qty and ADD TO QUOTE — and the typed text has to reach the rep.

Pairs with portal **#668** (the authoring panel) and services **`2027f4c`** (already on
`main`).

### On the sequencing note, because it was half wrong

Every scan pass on this card said "sequenced behind portal #554 + channels #169, land those
first". Both are still OPEN and CONFLICTING and have not moved since 2026-08-24. But the
**services half of that work is already on services `main`**: `services/products/addons.ts` (the
whole model), `getProductPageData` already putting `addons` on the payload, `CartItemService`
already keying a cart line by its configuration, and the shared `ProductPurchaseProvider` /
`useProductPageHandlers` already carrying `selectedAddons` into both buy buttons. What those two
PRs still hold is the authoring UI for *priced* groups and the storefront panel that renders them.

So this is built **on top of that model** — a `text` control on the same
`products.metafields.addons.groups` — rather than stacked on a stale conflicting PR nothing was
landing. That is the one-option-model outcome the sequencing note was protecting: a typed sentence
and a ticked $245 blade go through one panel, one server-side re-resolution and one refusal, which
is what keeps 7bmpuqei's picks-travel rule true by construction instead of by two wirings.

### What is in the diff

* **`ProductInstructionsPanel`** — the boxed field, shared by both renderers. The node-tree page
  binds it to the shared purchase provider (`setAddonText`); the legacy monolithic buy box binds
  it to its own state, because two of the three forks still run a local provider that predates the
  addons model. One component either way, so the two renderers cannot show different fields (the
  arrangement `ProductKitBlock` already has).
* **`builder/product-instructions-node.ts`** — placed at RENDER time immediately before the buy
  row, following `silverchef-node.ts` exactly: pure, idempotent by node id, an author's own
  placement wins, nothing written to the stored tree, and a related-products **repeat** is never
  the anchor (descending into it would put a box on every tile and none in the buy column). Both
  live trees carry `actions-row`; fallbacks are the price panel, then the end of the root. 7 unit
  tests, including the repeat case and "the stored tree is never mutated".
* **`addToQuote` / `addToCart`** take the configuration and **re-resolve it against the product's
  own definition**, exactly as a bundle build is re-resolved: a hand-made request can neither
  invent an answer nor slip past a required one. The refusal is worded on both sides — this page
  carries no availability wording that could explain a dead control (CXnP1lrL), so the field
  carries its own asterisk and "Required" line, and a press raises a named prompt. A text field is
  FILLED IN, not chosen, so the dialog says "Please fill in Instructions", never "Please choose".
* **Quote line**: `attributes.addon_selection` **merged** into the bag, never over it — that column
  holds a rep's `indent` tick and `zoey_item_id` on 62,351 ingested rows, and
  `docs/behaviour/quotes.md` requires the merge. `customer_notes` gets the plain-words line, with
  **no money in it** (it prints to the customer on `/q/<uuid>`, outside the hide-prices gate).
* **Cart line**: the picks go on `modifier_selections` and are shown back under the product name.
  Line identity is product + variant + configuration key, and that key folds the **typed text** in
  — otherwise a 1200mm bench and an 800mm bench merge into one line of quantity 2 carrying
  whichever was typed first. A quantity change and a sign-in re-price re-read the product's
  CURRENT definition (`repriceConfiguredLine`); a text answer resolves at `0.00`, so an
  instruction never moves what is charged.
* **Checkout** copies the configuration onto `order_items.product_options`, and the customer's own
  order page now reads **both** shapes that column really holds — the BigCommerce array on all
  73,439 Zoey-imported lines (every one empty) and the object our checkout writes. Reading only the
  array meant the one screen where a customer checks we got it right showed them nothing.

### One trap worth naming

Client modules import `@keenan/services/product-addons`, **never** the barrel. The barrel drags
`sharp` → `child_process` into the browser bundle and 500s the product page. `tsc` is perfectly
happy with it; only loading the page in a browser finds it.

### Ladder

`tsc --noEmit` 0 on `template`, `chef-s-kitchen` and `industry-kitchens` · `npm test` **3301 pass
/ 0 fail** · `orchestrator/check-shared-sync.mjs` green (3 new shared modules registered).
No `npm run build` — the wave owns it.

### Browser-verified (screenshots read)

Chefs Depot dev server against production data. The field renders above Add to Quote on the Custom
Stainless Steel page with its asterisk, prompt and Required line; an empty press raises "One more
thing / Please fill in Instructions before adding this to your quote"; a typed press wrote quote
3250563 in production with `customer_notes = "Instructions: 1200mm bench, sink on the left, 100mm
splashback"`, `attributes.addon_selection` at price `"0.00"`, and `list_price` unchanged at
`0.0000`. The portal quote editor shows the rep that sentence in the line Comment.

`products`-table writes are forbidden for this runner, so the authored field was injected into the
local dev worktree's `node_modules/@keenan/services` build for the walk and reverted afterwards —
every line of this branch's own source ran for real, only the metafields value was stood in for,
and that value is exactly what pressing Save in the portal's Customisation panel produces.

### Test data

Quote 3250563 and its item **deleted** (0 rows remain). No `products` row was written.

---

## Revision after independent review (2026-09-05)

**The blocking defect.** `addToQuote(id, null)` and `addToCart(id, null, 1)` are live call shapes —
the React listing tile, the related-products rail and the authored `product-card` master all press
the buy button with the product id alone. Both actions skipped the required-answer check entirely
when the `addons` argument was absent, so the tile's button did not offer-and-get-refused the way
7vu2iEEZ's rule for `sf-catalog-browse` says it must: it SUCCEEDED, silently, and wrote a bare quote
line on Custom Stainless Steel — the exact outcome card kyMjCmAw exists to prevent, reachable from
the related rail of every Chefs Depot product page.

* **`src/lib/product-customisation.ts` (new, shared, unit-tested)** is now the ONE definition of
  "has this shopper answered what this product asks?", used by both actions. It runs whether or not
  a panel was offered; only the wording changes, because naming a box that is not on the screen
  sends a shopper hunting for it ("Please open the product page and fill in Instructions…"). An
  absent argument still never CLEARS a line's stored configuration — "no panel was offered" and
  "the shopper emptied the box" stay different events. Its last test case is exactly this
  regression.
* **`AddToCartButton` / `AddToQuoteButton` now SHOW the refusal** instead of dropping it. They were
  discarding every `{ error }` the actions return, so the tile was a control that silently did
  nothing (7bmpuqei). This also restores the pre-existing restricted-product and back-order
  refusals, which vanished the same way, and stops a refused add being reported to GA4 and Klaviyo
  as a completed one.
* **Clearing an optional box** on a quote now deletes `addon_selection` (a merge cannot remove a

author: soyjorgepilo
body:
Deja el código listo para que desplegar sea configurar variables y presionar un botón: PostgreSQL como único dialecto en todos los entornos, todo lo que no puede fallar en silencio diciéndolo en voz alta, las dos tareas programadas que el aviso de privacidad ya prometía, y un documento único que basta para poner el sitio en línea. El día que existan las cuentas de Vercel y Supabase, no hay que abrir el código: hay que seguir `docs/despliegue.md`.

**Ticket:** [T-013](docs/tickets/T-013-preparacion-deploy.md) (E0-3, P0) · **Change:** `openspec/changes/preparar-deploy-produccion` · **ADRs:** ADR-004 y ADR-007 pasan a *aceptada (ejecutada en E0-3/T-013)*; ADR-001 gana nota de enmienda.

## El arco de la corrida

- **Un solo Postgres, en todos lados.** `provider = "postgresql"`, el árbol de migraciones rehecho y consolidado en una migración inicial que cubre las siete de la era SQLite, con las **cuatro** constraints CHECK reescritas a mano y con nombre. La base local se levanta con `npm run db:local` (PostgreSQL 17 sobre PGlite, sin Docker) y el CI corre la suite entera contra un `postgres:17` efímero.
- **Las guardas dejaron de creerse la URL.** El host se resuelve con el mismo parser que usa el driver, así que `?host=db.….supabase.co` ya no disfraza de local una base remota; y ninguna conexión sale de la máquina sin TLS (`prefer`, `allow` y `disable` **no** cuentan como cifrado, adelantándonos a la semántica que `pg` v9 adoptará).
- **Los cupos anti-abuso que protegen una credencial, a la base.** El límite de intentos de acceso al panel se cuenta en un almacén compartido —en serverless, un contador en memoria le regala al atacante tantos intentos como instancias consiga—, guardando un **HMAC de la IP, nunca la IP**, con retención de una hora y techo de filas. Los otros dos cupos se quedan en memoria **a propósito**: moverlos haría falsa una frase del aviso de privacidad ya publicado, y el texto legal no se toca sin la revisión legal (E6-3). Está declarado, no escondido.
- **Las fotos, en Supabase Storage.** Detrás del puerto que ya existía, elegido por variables. Sin configurar y desplegado, el sistema **no cae al disco efímero**: lo dice al arrancar y falla a la vista.
- **R4 — el borrado se niega a mentir** (decisión del fundador). El borrado definitivo se lleva **los archivos antes que la fila**: si el almacén no se deja alcanzar, la ficha no se toca y el panel dice *"La ficha no se borró: no pude alcanzar el almacén de fotos…"*. Antes se borraba la fila primero, se contestaba "borrado" y la foto —dato personal— sobrevivía **sin ninguna fila que la nombrara**, fuera del alcance hasta del barrido de huérfanas. Se cambió un fallo silencioso e irreversible por uno ruidoso y reparable.
- **Cabeceras de seguridad globales:** CSP (con los **dos** dominios de la analítica: el del script y el del recolector), `nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy`, y `X-Powered-By` fuera. El panel conserva su política de referente más estricta.
- **`docs/despliegue.md`, el entregable estrella:** todas las variables acumuladas con su valor exacto (`REGISTRO_ENCABEZADO_IP` = `x-forwarded-for`), el orden de operaciones, los pasos que solo puede hacer una persona (cuentas, dominio, DNS, respaldos, bucket privado), lo que nunca se corre contra producción, el **checklist humano** de prueba de humo de 12 pasos y la deuda conocida. Una prueba barre `src/` y `prisma/` y **reprueba el PR si aparece una variable que el documento no menciona**.

## Criterios de aceptación (T-013)

- [x] El esquema Prisma funciona contra Postgres y el CI lo prueba contra un Postgres efímero — *la spec eligió la tercera opción que abría el ticket: un solo dialecto, también en desarrollo*
- [x] Los CHECK de estado/origen y toda constraint escrita a mano sobreviven en el dialecto de producción
- [x] Documento único de despliegue con todas las variables, el orden de operaciones y los pasos humanos
- [x] Las fotos tienen su adaptador de producción (Supabase Storage, ADR-006 + ADR-004)
- [x] `next build` sin base accesible, y sin `SITIO_URL` revienta a la vista
- [x] La purga de rechazados a los 90 días tiene mecanismo, con test
- [x] Guardas anti-producción verificadas contra `VERCEL_ENV`

## Gates (ejecutados por el validador, sobre el árbol ya fusionado con `main`)

| Gate | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` | ✅ limpio |
| `npm run build` **sin base alcanzable** | ✅ ninguna ruta consulta la base al construir |
| `npm test` | ✅ **95 archivos, 2619 pruebas, 2 saltadas** (`concurrencia-real`, que necesita un Postgres de verdad y corre en el CI) |
| `migrate deploy` sobre esquema vacío + `db:seed` | ✅ 8 categorías, 21 colonias, 49 giros |
| `prisma migrate diff` | ✅ sin drift |

Verificado además a mano, contra la base y contra un `next start` real: los cuatro CHECK rechazando `INSERT`/`UPDATE` crudos; 24 cadenas de conexión hostiles contra las guardas; los cuatro avisos de arranque, cada uno una sola vez y sin filtrar la contraseña de la base; la purga borrando **solo** el rechazado de 100 días (el de 89 y el publicado, intactos) e idempotente en la segunda corrida; el barrido respondiendo **500** cuando una salvaguarda lo detiene; las rutas de tareas devolviendo 404 sin secreto, con secreto equivocado y con el secreto truncado; y las cuatro cabeceras en página dinámica, estática, `robots.txt`, activo de `_next` y 404. Detalle completo en `openspec/changes/preparar-deploy-produccion/reports/d-validacion.md`.

## Correcciones del validador

1. `src/lib/purga/rechazados.ts` — el comentario decía "el borrado quita la FILA antes que los archivos", lo contrario de lo que hace el código desde R4.
2. `CLAUDE.md` — "Prisma + SQLite en dev" → PostgreSQL en todos los entornos.
3. `specs/modelo-datos/spec.md` — el scenario "una ficha falla y las demás se purgan" seguía describiendo el orden anterior a la decisión del fundador; era la única contradicción viva del contrato y se habría consolidado así.
4. `reports/c-seguridad.md` — traía un byte nulo crudo (residuo de un payload) que volvía el archivo binario para `grep`.

## Integración con `main`

Fusionado `origin/main` (checkpoints, PRD v0.9/ADR-011, proceso v0.5 y el fix visual del PR #17). Un solo conflicto, en `docs/backlog.md`: se conservó la lista de deuda de `main` retirando el ítem que este change resuelve (`fotos:barrer-huerfanos` sin spec). Cliente de Prisma regenerado, gates completos repetidos sobre el árbol fusionado y flujo crítico re-verificado en servidor real: home, listado, ficha, `/registro`, `/buscar`, `/admin`, `robots.txt` y `sitemap.xml` responden; los emoji por categoría del PR #17 siguen ahí; y una URL con `%00` responde **404** y no 500, que es el borde que destapó el cambio de dialecto.

## Pendientes conocidos (no bloquean el merge)

- **Prueba de humo con cuentas reales:** las llamadas de red a Supabase Storage no las cubre ninguna prueba automática (solo el adaptador contra un `fetch` simulado). Pasos 10 y 11 de `docs/despliegue.md` §9.
- **`Strict-Transport-Security`** la pone el hosting con su certificado, no la aplicación: paso humano al configurar el dominio.
- **`tests/concurrencia-real.test.ts`** (el tope atómico de reportes con dos conexiones de verdad) solo corre en el CI: la base local multiplexa todo sobre un backend.
- 4 avisos altos de `npm audit`, todos en la cadena del CLI de Prisma (`devDependency`, no viaja al despliegue); documentados en §10 con por qué no se corre `npm audit fix --force`.
- El índice `docs/decisiones/README.md` no lista ADR-011 (viene así de `main`; no se toca aquí).

**El CI de GitHub Actions tiene que quedar en verde antes de mergear: la validación local no lo sustituye. El merge lo hace un humano.**

author: kreneskyp
body:
Closes agent-ix/spec-artifacts-app#3.

Brings `spec-artifacts-app` onto the Wave 4 semantic-module contract, the same
migration `spec-objects-business#4` and `spec-artifacts-iso#34` already made.

## What the module gains

- **TypeSpec source** (`typespec/main.tsp`) importing `@agent-ix/semantic-core`
  0.1.0, projected by `scripts/generate-schemas.mjs` to **39 sealed JSON Schema
  2020-12 files** under `spec_artifacts_app/schemas/`, with
  `schemas/toolchain.json` recording the compiler, emitter, semantic-core
  version, the emitted file list, the post-emit normalization pass, and a digest
  recomputable from the shipped bytes.
- **Both declared artifact types get a real emitted schema** — `ApplicationSpec`
  and `MasterRequirements` — plus every support model and scalar they reach. Not
  a subset.
- **The manifest at 0.2.0** carries the quoin FR-070 `semantic` block
  (`contract_version`, `semantic_core`, `package`, `exports`, `imports`,
  `targets`, `mappings`, `compatibility_posture`, `legacy_forms: warning`) and a
  reference-form `data_schema: {schema, digest}` per exported type.
- **`body_extraction` locators on both types**, where the manifest previously
  declared none. Every locator this change adds is `required: false` except
  `title` and `purpose`, which the pre-change document already carries — so an
  application spec valid before this change is valid after it, measured against
  the branch point rather than asserted.
- **`mappings.yaml` + `mappings.schema.json`**, generated from the manifest so a
  column list, a locator name or an id pattern is written once and cannot drift.
- **Three skeletons as executable fixtures**: a typed `## Properties` table, a
  `sysml` fence as its alternate form, `ocl` clauses under `## Invariants`. All
  three validate under `validate_document` and extract under `extract_semantic`
  with zero engine diagnostics, in both `## Properties` forms.
- **Eight negative counterparts**, each declaring what it expects to be refused
  and why, each violating exactly one rule, each routed to the surface its
  `expect` names.

## Reference, don't duplicate

An application composite is mostly a roll-up of types other modules own. Rather
than restate a functional requirement's fields, an aggregated requirement or a
data source is an `ImportedTypeRef` — a `{module, type}` pair plus an id. No
`$ref` in the bundle leaves this module's base or semantic-core 0.1.0, so it
resolves offline; a cross-module `$ref` could not.

Four import failures have four distinct diagnostics: an unpinned package, an
undeclared type, an over-declared import nothing reaches, and a cycle. The cycle
graph is built from dynamic-module fixtures the test synthesizes, never from the
machine's installed module root — a graph whose nodes depend on what a developer
happens to have installed is not reproducible.

## What is deliberately not here

Every upstream gap is recorded and named, never worked around:

- `agent-ix/quire-rs#392` — the wheel exposing `extract_semantic` is on no index
  this repository may commit against, so `make dev-quire` provisions it and the
  semantic tests **fail rather than skip** when it is absent.
- `agent-ix/quire-rs#221`, `#394`, `#391` — silent module-load and
  record-validation defects.
- `agent-ix/filament-core-service#23` — a reference-form `data_schema` is not yet
  resolved into a stored snapshot.
- Generated-language fixtures (`filament-core-data#21`/`#22`/`#23`, published
  behind `quoin#290`; semantic-core language packages are

passing fails the suite, so a fixed upstream announces itself.

- The ambiguous-`data_schema` refusal of `agent-ix/quoin#341`.

`/specify` → Test Matrix → composite `/spec-review` (base plus all seven
analyses, run in parallel) → `/spec-to-plan` → implementation → `/code-review`
and gap analysis. The eight spec reviews are committed under

## Summary

The `/api/ocr/scan-document` route (`src/routes/ocr.ts`) is the alias endpoint the ServeIntakePage preview calls before an officer confirms intake. It had silently drifted from the canonical `serveIntake.ts` handler in four ways:

- **Stale timeout constants**: local `aiBudget()` / `withTimeout()` copies kept the old 35 s ceiling after `serveIntakeOcr.ts` raised it to 45 s (the live "stuck on upload" fix) — both are now imported from the single source
- **Missing `extractPdfMarkdown` tier**: the zero-neuron `env.AI.toMarkdown()` path (two-column safe) only existed in `serveIntake.ts`; `ocr.ts` went straight to the Tesseract container — now: toMarkdown → `client_text` pdfjs (if long enough) → container
- **Missing family-prompt context**: `familyFromFileName` was applied in `serveIntake.ts` but not in `ocr.ts`, so the preview got less layout guidance than the commit path; fixed by routing through `ocrText()` (which also adds Claude-first extraction)
- **Raw model output returned to officer**: `finalizeFields` (normalize + validate pair) was not applied, so the officer reviewed `"6/26/2026"` / `"Utah"` / `"(435) 986-1200"` in the preview modal while `/upload` committed `"2026-06-26"` / `"UT"` / `"4359861200"` — reviewing one value and saving another is a correctness failure in law enforcement records

Also wires `precleanText` + `detectHomoglyphs` across all PDF tiers so watermark stamp bleed and Cyrillic/Greek homoglyphs are scrubbed before the model sees them, with substitution audit trail via structured logger.

author: paulfidika
body:
Provider linking accepted stale sessions and silently replaced an existing identity; federated registration bound unverified provider email to an account. Require fresh sensitive authentication before OAuth/OIDC/Solana linking, reject same-issuer subject replacement atomically, and retain unverified email only as provider metadata. Return the account's own nullable email in the JSON callback. Both provider ownership constraints now apply to the simpler programmatic link API too; delete redundant unguarded insert/replacement queries.

An account invite is an existing unbound bearer code: email-less registration still validates and consumes that code in InviteOnly mode. Existing provider login remains available. Changing provider subject requires explicit unlink, and repeated linking of the same subject stays idempotent.

Validation:
- All packages pass `go test ./...` (database tests skipped in that unit-only pass).
- Focused PostgreSQL tests pass with race detection, driving actual OAuth2 HTTP exchanges and signed OIDC discovery/JWKS/token callbacks.
- Tests cover stale-token refusal, enrolled-MFA enforcement, successful fresh linking, preserved original on replacement, explicit unlink/re-link, concurrent link ownership, NULL-email registration, no password-reset delivery for unverified addresses, distinct later verified ownership, and unbound invite-only consumption/replay rejection.
- Full PostgreSQL HTTP/core race suites pass (authhttp 40.9s; authcore 16.9s). `sqlc generate` and `sqlc vet` pass against the isolated test database.

Tracks #283 and #284. #283's security notification and first-party frontend step-up adoption remain unfinished follow-ups; this PR does not claim that full issue complete. #284's first-party onboarding adoption also remains a consumer follow-up. No live provider requests or notifications, no schema migration, and no legacy compatibility layer.

author: dranakcorps-bot
body:
**E-2a of the signed Evolved plan (`FABLE.md` → Phase 1), and the deliverable that must exist BEFORE `tests/EQBuddy.Avalonia.Tests` is deleted.** No deletion here: E-2b (the shared-suite scanners) and E-2c (pipeline + deletion) follow as their own PRs, per the plan's "a deletion mixed with a port is a diff nobody can review".

## What the plan asked for, and what came back

**Attempt 1 — un-gate `e2e-windows`. It worked, and the reason it had been gated was never true.** `ci.yml` said the job was dispatch-only because it "needs a desktop session, which hosted runners don't guarantee a WPF window on". Nobody had tested that. A dispatch of the unmodified job on `main` ([run 33921376980](https://github.com/DranakCorps-bot/EQBuddy/actions/runs/33921376980)) launched the real `EQBuddy.exe` 44 times on `windows-latest`: **41 passed, 3 failed, four minutes** — and all three failures were ours.

| Failure | Cause |
|---|---|
| `SessionGoesLive_AndFreshKillUpdatesLiveStats` | `AppHarness.Launch` waits for the replay to **start**, while its doc comment claimed it waits for it to finish. Tests sample a baseline and wait for baseline + 1, and `WaitForDump` is an **equality** — a counter still climbing sails past the expected value between two polls. It failed with *"kills to reach 10; last seen 9"* beside a dump reading `kills=14`. |
| `KillThenLoot_ShowsUpOnTheLootSurface` | The same race on the other surface. |
| `DraggingTheWidgetTallerGrowsTheOpenThemesBody` | It asserted the **monitor**: the drag is clamped to the work area first, so on the runner's 1024×768 display the stack was granted 560 units and the cap correctly stayed at the floor. |

Fixed: `Launch` now waits for `killsTotal` and `lootTotal` to hold still for two ticks, and the `EQBUDDY_EXPAND` dump carries the cap's two **inputs** (`themeBodyRoom`, `themeBodyChrome`) so the test asserts the relationship — the cap in force is the tested formula over the room this machine granted — instead of a number that is a claim about a desk. `ThemeBodyCapHost.CapFor` is behaviour-identical; its two arguments became `RoomFor`/`ChromeFor` so the dump reads the same producers rather than re-deriving either (trap 33).

**The suite is now 44/44 in ~4 minutes and runs on every push and pull request.** That is load-bearing rather than tidy: `src/EQBuddy` has no unit tests at all (TestPlan §5), and E-2 removes the lane that was the repo's only rendering coverage running on a push. The new rule is written into CLAUDE.md, the suite's README and TestPlan §5 — **nothing in E2E may assert the SCREEN**.

## The table

`docs/v2/avalonia-test-disposition.md` — one row per file for all **24** (E-0c's `LegacyNoticeRenderTests` has its own row, as the E-0/E-1 review asked), each naming a destination test that runs today or a reason the assertion is accepted as lost. Three answers worth surfacing:

- **`AppThemeTests` needs no WPF twin** — the plan's open item 5. All four derived-tone formulas are pinned to exact hexes by `CompanionThemeTests.DerivedTonesMatchTheDesktopsOwn`, and every value of every catalog theme is parsed by `ThemePaletteTests.EveryValueIsParseableArgbHex`. Both in `EQBuddy.Tests`, both on push. What the Avalonia file uniquely held was `AppTheme`'s own wiring.
- **`LegacyNoticeRenderTests`: accepted loss, as recommended** — the surface ships frozen at `v1.99.18` on `legacy-v1`; `LegacyPlatformUpdatePolicyTests` and the six-call-site scanner survive.
- **`OptionsRenderTests` (32 assertions) is the largest loss and it is named as such.** E-3 replaces that surface outright, so porting to a window scheduled for demolition has a known expiry; it becomes a must-list row when the shell's Options is built.

## The two ports, both to the SHIPPING lane

- **`CompanionSourcesAreWiredTests`** (new, `EQBuddy.Tests`). The Avalonia test reflected over `CompanionSources` and asked the live widget which of ~20 callbacks were still null. The lane that actually serves phones is WPF, and **nothing checked its wiring at all.** The port keeps the reflection and scans the initializer in `MainWindow.xaml.cs`, in the shape `CompanionSnapshotArgumentTests` already uses. Proven to fail: removing `Raids = _raidLedger` reports *"EQBuddy Mobile would serve these surfaces empty: Raids"*. It ships its own anti-vacuity test (trap 39).
- **`IconGeometryTests`** moved to `EQBuddy.E2E`. `DesignSystemTests` says in as many words that its own icon check is "the cheap structural half" and the real one "cannot live here". E2E is the repo's one `net10.0-windows` project, so WPF's `Geometry.Parse` is reachable — 126 assertions, 93 ms, no window. Proven to fail by corrupting a path.

## Gates

- `scripts/check.ps1`: all green — what's-new, legacy notice, **evolved** (E-1's stage, untouched), build, 2,957 unit, 311 Avalonia.
- `e2e-windows` on this branch: **44/44**, and the eight-run stability record is posted below before this is called green.
- No player-visible change, so no `WhatsNew.json` entry; `<Version>` untouched.

Requesting Helm last-look.

— Dranak (Claude Code)

## Issue

Stacks on #274.

## Solution

- Completes the ported handler with the three relation events — joined (per-unit address share, leader-only watcher user + Raft secret creation with the defer-on-failure guard, cluster-information handout), changed (cleanup + config update on watcher address change) and broken (cleanup + config update) — and the matching framework observers, exactly as in the VM charm.
- The abstract charm constructs the `WatcherEventsHandler` before the config manager on VM (inert on K8s: no construction, no watcher-offer relation in the K8s charm's metadata) and constructor-injects it, mirroring the LDAP handler wiring.
- `ConfigManager.update_config` no longer threads `watcher_raft_address` from the charm: `render_patroni_yml_file` sources the Raft address from the injected handler itself inside the VM-only render branch (`watcher_raft_address if is_active else None`, matching the charm's `watcher_offer.is_active` gate). The `watcher_raft_address` parameter is dropped from both `update_config` and `render_patroni_yml_file`; the remaining ldap/async parameters stay for their own migration phases.
- `watcher_handler` is an optional keyword (default `None`): the production charms construct `ConfigManager` directly and do not import the abstract charm, so the K8s charm keeps working unchanged at the pin bump.

author: tamnd
body:
The last two groups that still wanted the database to themselves, which means every command group now takes it shared and the dispatch table hands out `&Db` throughout.

The keyspace group is the interesting half, because it holds the two commands that name two keys and the two that reach a database the session is not on.

`RENAME` across stripes takes both of them at once with `hold_many` rather than reaching for one, letting go, and reaching for the other. Between those two reaches the key was in neither stripe. Nothing could see that while one thread served everything, and a second thread would see it the moment there was one.

`COPY` and `MOVE` get a `Both` enum and a `hold_both` that takes the lower of the two spots first whichever direction the copy runs in, so two clients copying in opposite directions cannot each end up holding what the other is waiting for. Two spots that turn out to be one spot are held once, since holding a stripe twice is a wait for yourself.

`Holds` grows `stripe_mut` alongside `stripe`. One stripe at a time, because a command that writes into two of them at once would need the borrow checker told they are different ones and nothing here does that. A rename takes the record out of one and puts it in the other, and the record owns what it holds in between.

The blocking group needed no restructuring. `Db::lmove` and `Db::lmovem` already took the database shared from the earlier work, so the retry path and the six waits behind it came across by changing the types.

What is left before the listener is the rest of the multi key commands, which still take their stripes one at a time rather than all at once with `hold_many`. Nothing serves on more than one thread yet, so nothing can observe a half done multi key command in the meantime, and that work lands before `--threads N`.

The gate is green: workspace tests, fmt, clippy, `cargo xtask alloc`, docs and `cargo xtask check`.

author: davidkelly
body:
## Motivation

Setting `ClusterOptions.RedactionLevel` to `Partial` or `Full` redacted user data in the log stream but **not** in exception error contexts, which serialized every field raw. Exception dumps commonly land in the same logs, so redaction a customer enabled for compliance was silently defeated on that path — arguably worse than no redaction, because the logs look clean.

None of the ~33 error-context construction sites applied the redactor. Java redacts at every `put` (`redactUser`/`redactMeta`/`redactSystem`); we did not.

Redaction is off by default (`RedactionLevel.None`), so this was invisible unless a customer had deliberately opted in.

## What changed

Redact **at assignment** across all construction sites, matching Java, using the user/meta/system split already established in the SDK's log paths:

| Classification | Fields |
|---|---|
| user data | document keys, statements, query parameters, search queries |
| metadata | bucket, scope, collection, index, design-doc and view names |
| system data | endpoints, management URIs |

`TypedRedactor` gains `UserDataString`/`MetaDataString`/`SystemDataString` for the contexts, which store plain strings rather than `Redacted<T>`, mirrored as `IRedactor` extension methods so every call site reads the same way regardless of which abstraction the enclosing class holds. No public interface change.

`QueryClient`, `SearchClient` and `AnalyticsClient` now take an `IRedactor`, matching `ViewClient`. `ResponseStatusExtensions.CreateException` and `RetryOrchestrator.CreateKeyValueErrorContext` take one as a parameter.

### Notable details

- **Null and empty pass through untouched.** `Redacted<T>.ToString()` renders null as `""`, which would turn an absent context field into a present, empty one, and tagging an empty value yields a useless `<ud></ud>`. `GetClusterMap` passes `string.Empty` as the bucket name, so this was reachable.
- **`SelectBucket` carries the bucket name in `Key`** rather than a document key, so that one is tagged as metadata — as user data it would be stripped at `Partial`, losing diagnostics Couchbase treats as safe at that level.
- **Deliberately not redacted:** `ClientContextId`, which support correlates against server logs, and the server-authored `Message`/`Errors` text.
- **Out of scope**, both outside the context types this ticket covers: `GenericErrorContext.Fields` (Stellar) and `EventingFunctionErrorContext.Info`.

## Behaviour change

For anyone who has enabled redaction, error-context fields now hold the *tagged* value, so `ex.Context.DocumentKey` returns `<ud>the-key</ud>`. The affected properties are all `[InterfaceStability(Level.Uncommitted)]`, and nothing inside the SDK reads them back — only `Status` and `Errors` are consumed internally, neither of which is redacted. Flagged on the ticket as needing a release note.

## Testing

`Couchbase.UnitTests`: **3000 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped.** Main solution and the FIT performer solution both build clean.

Nine new tests in `ErrorContextRedactionTests` cover `None`/`Partial`/`Full`, tag survival through `ToString()`, null and empty preservation, and the query and search client paths end-to-end through mocked HTTP failures.

## Follow-ups recorded on NCBC-4297

- `QueryErrorContext` and `AnalyticsErrorContext` have no `ToString()` override, so their contexts never render in an exception dump. Must be fixed before NCBC-4297(c) appends `Context` to `Message`, or that would append a bare type name.
- System.Text.Json escapes `<` and `>` by default, so the tags serialize unicode-escaped and grep-based tooling such as `cblogredaction` will not match them. Not a one-line fix: `JsonSourceGenerationOptions` has no `Encoder` property and `InternalSerializationContext` is shared with `BucketConfig` and the other wire types.

author: kitenite
body:
## Problem

"Sign in with Google" from the in-app browser pane lands on `accounts.google.com/CookieMismatch` ("We've detected a problem with your cookie settings"), even though #7049 already keeps the popup in-app and on the pane's session.

## Root cause

The Chrome cookie importer passed Chrome's `host_key` as `domain` for every row. Electron normalizes any `domain` it is given into a `.host` domain cookie, so every host-only cookie in the source profile was imported as a domain cookie (in the tested Comet profile, 1023 of 3347 cookies are host-only; the Superset jar ended up with 2935 dotted and 86 host-only).

The moment a site refreshes one of those with its own host-only cookie of the same name, the jar holds two values under one name and the browser sends both. Google answers that with `CookieMismatch`. The same duplication hit Carta's `csrftoken`, Deel's `auth-token`, Notion's ALB stickiness cookies and GitHub's `_device_id` (40 pairs in the affected jar). `__Host-` cookies, which must not carry `Domain`, were rejected by the same bug and silently counted as skipped.

Bisected against a copy of the affected jar in a scratch Electron 41 session: deleting the single `.accounts.google.com` LSID row made the same jar reach the account chooser. Scheme-bound cookies were ruled out first (Electron 41 still sends http-sourced cookies to https).

## Fix

- `mapCookieRow` sets `domain` only for rows whose `host_key` starts with a dot; host-only rows travel by `url` alone.
- `importCookies` (extracted from `importCookiesIntoSession`) replaces a stale `.host` twin left by an earlier import when the source profile holds only the host-only cookie; if the source holds both, both are imported. Twins are dropped before any cookie is written, so a value restored from the old jar is overwritten by the source's.
- `cookies.remove(url, name)` is the only deletion Electron offers and it takes every cookie of that name the URL would receive, parent-domain and shorter-path cookies included. Twin removal snapshots what the call hits and restores everything except the doomed twins; if a restore is rejected, the whole slot, twin included, is put back.

No startup sweep. It could not tell a stale imported twin from a pair a site set on purpose, so nothing is touched unless the user runs an import. **A jar polluted by the old importer heals by re-importing from the same browser**, which the always-visible import banner offers; clearing cookies for the affected site also works.

## Verification

- Unit tests for the mapping, the import twin handling, collateral restore, overlapping twins, failed restores and protected hosts (mutation-checked: the old mapping fails the new test).
- Scratch Electron session on the real jar: `ServiceLogin` → `CookieMismatch` before; after re-importing the host-only `LSID` through the real import path the same session reaches `/v3/signin/accountchooser`.
- Synthetic Chrome-schema profile imported through the real code path: host-only cookies stay host-only, `__Host-GAPS` imports, a seeded stale twin is replaced and only one `LSID` is sent.

author: faustclaw
body:
`publish.yml` would have failed on its first run, **three times over**. Found while preparing to publish 0.1.0.

| # | Problem | Why it would have been confusing |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `prepublishOnly: n8n-node prerelease` exits 1 unless `RELEASE_MODE` is set — the workflow never set it | Fails *after* a successful build, with the CLI's "run `npm run release`" message |
| 2 | Pinned **Node 22**, whose bundled npm is 10.x; trusted publishing needs **npm ≥ 11.5.1** | Surfaces as an *authentication* error, not a version error |
| 3 | Used a stored `NPM_TOKEN` — not how this org publishes | Needs a secret that may not exist |

The `prepublishOnly` guard exists to stop an accidental `npm publish` from a laptop, so it **stays** — CI satisfies it rather than removing it.

## Trusted publishing

Rewritten to mirror `labelzoom-sdk/.github/workflows/release-node.yml`, which already solved all of this: **OIDC trusted publishing** — no token, no secret, and no `--provenance` flag, because OIDC supplies the credential and attaches provenance automatically.

That also matters for n8n verification, which has required publication from a GitHub Action with provenance since 2026-05-01. Doing it this way means **0.1.0 itself qualifies**, rather than starting with a version that never can.

Carried over from the SDK workflow: empty top-level `permissions` with `id-token` scoped to the job, pinned action SHAs, `persist-credentials: false`, and deliberately **no npm cache** on the release job — a restored cache is attacker-influenced input that would be baked into a provenance-signed artifact.

## Two guards that fail loudly

- **Tag ↔ `package.json`** must agree, or `v0.1.1` quietly ships whatever the manifest says.
- **Tarball contents** — the node and credential entry points, the codex JSON and the icon. A half-built package publishes happily and then fails to load in n8n.

Both were run against a real `npm pack` locally before committing; both pass.

> ⚠️ The workflow **filename** is now a matched claim in the npm trusted-publisher policy, so renaming it silently breaks publishing. There's a comment saying so at the top — npm doesn't validate the policy when you save it, and the failure only appears at publish time.

## Also

Adds `.nvmrc` (`v24.20.0`) and points `ci.yml` and `live-smoke.yml` at it, so every workflow runs one pinned version. Node 24 isn't optional here: **n8n 2.x requires ≥ 24.0.0**, so 22 was already the wrong target for the runtime this node loads into.

## Verification

`npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (the n8n community-node linter, strict mode), **101 tests** and `npm run build` all pass on Node 24. Tarball contains `dist/` with no tests, fixtures or sources.

Next step after merge is a **dry-run `workflow_dispatch`** — it exercises the whole workflow including both assertions without spending the version number.
