body:
## Qué cambia

En `Configuración > API`, la tabla:

- **Ninguna celda parte su dato en varios renglones.** Antes «Prueba Tienda 18:06:29», el correo de
  la cuenta dedicada y la fecha ocupaban **hasta 3 líneas cada uno**. Ahora **1 línea** en todos los
  anchos, cabeceras incluidas.
- **«Acciones» vuelve a ser la última columna** y **«Eliminar» es la última acción**, con el «Editar»
  del webhook delante. Esto deshace el reordenamiento del commit `a6448bdc`, que no se había pedido.
- **El correo sintético de la cuenta dedicada se acorta a 20 caracteres** (`apikey+prueba-tienda…`),
  con el valor completo en `title` **y** en un `sr-only` — porque un `title` no existe para quien usa
  lector de pantalla o teclado.

## Por qué se partía el texto, que no era lo que parecía

**A 1440 px la tabla no desbordaba y aun así el texto se partía en tres.** El plegado no venía del
scroll: con `w-full` y layout automático, el navegador estruja cada columna hasta su `min-content`.
Por eso «que no quepa» y «que se parta» eran dos problemas distintos.

Se usa `whitespace-nowrap` con el envoltorio que el repo **ya emplea** en la tabla de productos de
analítica (ficha 354). `components/shared/DataTable.tsx` **no se toca**: lo montan 55 archivos.

## Medido en pantalla, cuatro anchos

| viewport | scrollWidth antes | después | líneas/celda antes | después |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1100 | 1245 | 3 | **1** |
| 1280 | 1100 | 1245 | 3 | **1** |
| 1440 | 1100 | 1245 | 3 | **1** |
| 1920 | 1614 | 1614 | 1 | **1** |

**A 1440 hacen falta 111 px de desplazamiento**, y es una decisión tomada a sabiendas: el suelo de la
columna del correo son **133 px que fija el texto de su cabecera**, no el dato. Recortar más el dato
no baja de ahí, y acortar la etiqueta dejaría una columna que nadie entiende. El control de
desplazamiento horizontal de la tabla ya existe y se probó pulsándolo de verdad: lleva el scroll al
final y deja «Acciones» entera y clicable.

## Verificación

- Gate rápido: `INIT_EXIT=0` leído dentro del log · 186 archivos de guardia / **2801 tests**.
- Guard nuevo `api-keys-tabla-una-linea.guardia.test.tsx` (sustituye al anterior, que codificaba la
  regla contraria). **Muerde**: 5 mutaciones, las 5 rojas — volver a 12 caracteres, subir a 80,
  quitar el `title`, quitar el `sr-only` y quitar el `whitespace-nowrap`.
- Medido en Chromium con la barra lateral desplegada, y verificado a mano en las capturas.

## Lo que queda vivo, medido y NO tocado aquí

Dos defectos de `components/shared/DataTable.tsx`, que afectan a cualquier tabla con botones en la
última columna que desborde:

1. La flecha izquierda **tapa 36 px** de la primera columna.
2. La flecha derecha **se dibuja sobre los botones** de la última columna (36 px a 1440). Cuando cae
   sobre un botón vivo, **se come el clic**: quedó reproducido con un clic de ratón real en una
   medición intermedia — pulsar «Rotar» no abría su modal, el primer clic iba a la flecha.

No se arreglan aquí a propósito: son del componente compartido y merecen su propio cambio.

author: dvaerum
body:
Final PR of `admin_tools.py`'s 9-tool surface — and, with it, **Phase D5 in its entirety**.

## What
`PurgeAgentTool` — operator-only hard-delete cascade across every table referencing an agent_id.

## Design
- Tombstone-first: `AgentRepository::insert_tombstone` writes a synthetic `__tombstone_<agent_id>` row; every historical reference gets rewritten to point at `[deleted-<agent_id>]` rather than deleted alongside the agent — `message_repository::rename_participant`, a raw SQL UPDATE for `tasks.created_by`, a raw SQL UPDATE for `agent_actions.agent_id`.
- Task reassignment reuses the terminal-vs-active split `terminate_agent` (PR8) established: active tasks → reassigned to `"unassigned"` + wake broadcast via `ctx.waiter_registry.notify`; terminal tasks only get `assigned_to` cleared (FK-safety), status untouched (no resurrection).
- Audit row logged BEFORE the final DELETE (matches Python's own ordering/rationale), attributed to the real caller — verified by a dedicated test since the agent_actions rewrite runs first and only touches OLD rows.
- No Rust equivalent of Python's session-registry stream teardown (decision 2 from Phase D5's own research) — documented inline, not silently dropped.

## Testing
11 new tests. 968 total across the workspace, 3x clean, fmt/clippy(`--locked`)/audit all clean, no `Cargo.lock` drift.

**Live-verified** against the real compiled `conexus-backend` binary over a real UDS socket: seeded two workers + a cross-owned task + a message; worker denied; operator (real HMAC-signed forwarding header) purged successfully; confirmed on real on-disk SQLite state that the agent row is gone, the tombstone row exists, the task/message were rewritten to the tombstone (only where alice was the referenced party), and the durable audit row is attributed to the real operator.

author: thehumanworks
body:
## Summary

Native-loop hardening for "stream errors after a tool call, then the chat cannot recover" (OpenRouter, AIProxy, the ChatGPT `codex` backend). Root causes found by review and reproduced with the mock provider — each one is now fixed, tested on both wires, and recorded in **ADR 0069**:

- **No retry on the tool-result POST.** A gateway 5xx/429, a closed idle connection, an empty 200, or a relayed SSE `error` event ended the turn; the user had to type "continue". Now: bounded, non-blocking retry with backoff (1s/2s/4s, `Retry-After` honored, `TNY_PROVIDER_RETRIES` sets the budget), only while no answer text has been shown; each retry is a status line and a distinct `provider_request`/`provider_response` pair for extensions.
- **Misread failures.** `"error": null` in every chunk was treated as a failure (every stream "reported an error"); a JSON error document behind HTTP 200 or an empty 200 became a *successful empty answer*. Now framing is sniffed from the first bytes (SSE vs. one JSON document), errors are classified, non-streaming completions/Response objects work, and an empty stream is a retried error.
- **Transcripts strict providers reject forever.** Empty assistant messages were persisted; a runner killed mid-batch left `tool_calls` without results, so every later request 400'd with "no tool output found". Now both wires build from `session_provider_view()` (missing results synthesized, orphans dropped, empty assistant messages skipped; the stored transcript is untouched), and empty answers are not recorded.
- **Reasoning dropped.** Thinking models need the reasoning that produced a tool call sent back with it (OpenRouter `reasoning_details` with Anthropic signatures / Gemini thought signatures, DeepSeek/Kimi `reasoning_content`, OpenAI encrypted `reasoning` items with `store:false`). Now captured (fragments merged by index), stored on the assistant tool-call message, and echoed on the wire that produced it; `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` for OpenAI/ChatGPT hosts.
- **Opaque diagnostics.** "provider returned HTTP N" with the body unread (its bytes poisoned the kept-alive connection). Now: status + a bounded category token (`provider rejected the request (HTTP 400, invalid_request_error)`), never provider text (ADR 0028); `TNY_DEBUG_PROVIDER_ERRORS=1` opts in to the message; 403 is worded as a refusal rather than a bad key; error connections are dropped.

## Testing

- `make test-unit`: 442 tests pass (new: error token/retryability, reasoning-detail merge, provider view incl. 70-call batches, assistant extras, responses translation with reasoning items and summary form).
- `tests/integration/test_openai.py` (both wires): tool-result POST 502/429 once, empty stream once, JSON error body once, SSE error once, non-streaming JSON once, permanent 400 (no retry, category only, debug opt-in), retry budget/`TNY_PROVIDER_RETRIES=0`, `"error": null` chunks, reasoning passthrough (`details`/`content`/encrypted item, `include` for codex only), broken-session repair via `--resume`.
- Full `tests/integration/run.sh`, `test_extensions.py`, `test_codex_chatgpt.py` pass; `make valgrind` clean; clang-tidy (pinned 22.1.8) clean on changed files; `warn-strict` under gcc and clang; gcc `-fanalyzer`; ruff/JS lint; mutation targets added (`--focus stream-recovery`).
- Live check against a real provider: `tests/integration/live_provider_check.py --provider aiproxy --model grok-4.6` (tool call → follow-up → resume after a simulated runner death, both wires). **Not run from this session**: the sandbox egress policy denies `aiproxy.up.railway.app` (CONNECT 403), so please run it locally.

## Docs

- `docs/adr/0069-native-loop-stream-error-recovery.md` (+ index row)
- `docs/backends/openai-compatible.md`: stream errors/retries/diagnostics, transcript invariants, reasoning passthrough

author: rmahammad
body:
Implements the OpenSSF Scorecard checks this repo can satisfy through configuration, and adds a way to measure the criticality score instead of guessing at it.

## Scorecard checks now covered

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| Scorecard | weekly run, publishes results to the OpenSSF API |
| SAST | CodeQL, `javascript-typescript`, `security-extended` |
| Dependency-Update-Tool | Dependabot, npm + github-actions |
| Pinned-Dependencies | actions pinned to commit SHAs |
| Token-Permissions | explicit least-privilege `permissions:` per workflow |

**The pins are behaviour-neutral.** Each SHA is the commit the floating `v4` tag already resolves to today — `checkout` v4.4.0, `setup-node` v4.4.0, `pnpm/action-setup` **v4.3.0** (the `v4` tag has not moved to v4.4.0 yet). CI runs the same code it ran before. The `github-actions` Dependabot updater is there to keep those pins from rotting, since a SHA is unreviewable by eye.

## Criticality score

Separate metric, frequently confused with Scorecard, and **not implementable** — it is a weighted mean of ten observed signals measuring how much the ecosystem depends on this repo. No file moves it.

`scripts/openssf-criticality.mjs` reimplements the upstream algorithm (`config/scorer/original_pike.yml` + `internal/scorer/algorithm`) against the GitHub API:

```bash
pnpm openssf:criticality
```

Baseline **0.215**. Recency is maxed; the binding constraints are contributor count (1), contributor orgs (0), issue traffic (0/90d) and downstream mentions (20 vs a 500k threshold) — all adoption, none of it CI's to fix.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **Branch protection** — a repo setting, not a file. Worth doing *before* merge so the first published Scorecard number reflects it.
- **README badge** — `publish_results` must run on `main` once before the shields.io endpoint resolves. Check the real score at [scorecard.dev](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/RMahammad/motiq) after merge, then decide whether it earns a spot above the fold.
- **Signed-Releases / Packaging** — needs a publish workflow with npm provenance, and the changeset config still says `"access": "restricted"`. Open decision; requirement recorded in docs/17.

## Verification

`check-links`, `check-stale-dates`, `check-duplicate-titles`, `check-adr-index` and `pnpm lint` all pass locally. All four workflow YAMLs parse.

Note that Scorecard itself will **not** run on this PR — it only triggers on push to `main` and on schedule, because `publish_results` requires the default branch. CodeQL and the repinned `ci.yml` do run here.

author: andreasronge
body:
Closes #1627.

## What was wrong

Two numbers in `docs/reference/mcp.md`, both on the path someone follows when an
MCP provider times out during acquisition.

1. **`evaluation_timeout_ms` default.** The "lowest of" list said `1000`. The
   closed limit catalog says `30_000` (`lib/ptc_runner/kernel/limit_catalog.ex:57`).
   The value *was* `1_000` when the paragraph was written; `c19ebfdc` raised it
   and the prose did not follow. A reader diagnosing
   `provider_acquisition_timeout` therefore concluded a 1 s mission budget was
   binding, and tuned the value that was not biting.
2. **Node prerequisite.** The page required Node.js 22 for `ptc-fs-mcp@0.1.0`,
   while the published package declares `{ node: '>=20.19.0' }` and
   `ptc_runner_tutorial` says 20.19+ — so the two documents contradicted each
   other and sent readers on a supported Node to upgrade needlessly.

## What changed

Correcting the number alone would have left the section self-contradictory: with
the mission budget at `30000`, the existing example told the reader to *narrow*
it to `20000`, and the sentence "raising one while another stays at its default
changes nothing" no longer described the defaults it was written for. So the
surrounding guidance follows the number:

- on stock defaults the lowest of the three is the installed `ceilings.timeout_ms`
  at `5000`, and the examples say so instead of implying `evaluation_timeout_ms`
  is what to tune;
- the worked example is internally consistent — `20000` needs the ceiling alone,
  and anything past `30000` names matching values for both;
- the stdio transport's `start_timeout_ms` is also `5000`, so the spawn step —
  the one that usually expires on a cold `npx` launch — stays at `5000` ms if
  only one of the two is raised; and
- `limits.run_duration_ms` bounds the complete run, active preflight and
  acquisition included, and is `30000` too, so a budget past that needs headroom
  there as well.

The mirrored `site/reference/mcp/index.html` is regenerated by `mix ptc.gen_docs`.
Documentation only — no runtime behavior changes.

## Verification

- Defaults read from source: `LimitCatalog` (`evaluation_timeout_ms` and
  `run_duration_ms` both `30_000`), `HostConfig` (`ceilings.timeout_ms` `5_000`),
  `MCPStdioTransport` (`start_timeout_ms` `5_000`), and the run-clock bound at
  `ProviderCallbackBoundary`. `docs/guides/kernel-repl.md` and
  `docs/reference/repl.md` already said 30,000 ms, confirming the drift was
  isolated to this page.
- `npm view ptc-fs-mcp@0.1.0 engines` → `{ node: '>=20.19.0' }`.
- `mix ptc.gen_docs`, `mix precommit`, `MIX_ENV=dev mix docs --warnings-as-errors`,
  and the full pre-push suite (core tests, static analysis + Dialyzer, release
  verification, Viewer, launcher, ExDoc) all pass.

## Retrospective

The starting scope was two numbers. Both independent Codex review sessions found
that the *first* correction was incomplete in the same way the original drift
was: a number changed, its surrounding argument did not. Session 1 caught the
"changes nothing" claim and the mismatched `20000`/`40000` example pair; session
2 caught that a 40 s per-operation budget is unreachable anyway, because
`run_duration_ms` caps the whole run at 30 s by default. Neither was visible from
the issue — both needed the code read around the value, not just at it.

The lesson worth keeping: this paragraph derives a conclusion from several
defaults, so any one of them changing invalidates the conclusion, not just the
line quoting it. The generated site page has no such coupling and stayed correct
because it is projected; the prose drifted because nothing checks it. Worth
noting for the next default that moves.

author: agustin-perezz
body:
**Summary**
Completes the draft-emails-outreach PoC with the user-facing layer: a single page where a raw job post is pasted, an LLM draft is generated and presented for human editing, and nothing is dispatched until the Approve & Send button is clicked. The workflow state machine (idle, drafting, reviewing, sending, done, error) lives in a dedicated hook with a transition table so invalid states are impossible, and the E2E suite proves the human-in-the-loop invariant with stubbed APIs — no real LLM or Resend calls run in tests.

**Key changes**
- Add `useDraftReviewWorkflowState` hook with an allowed-transition table; invalid transitions are ignored and errors clear on retry
- Add `Textarea` shared primitive to the UI kit
- Add `/draft-review` page: composition-only server shell rendering `DraftReviewContainer`, which owns the workflow state, the draft payload and the approval token; `DraftReviewJobPostInput` for pasting, `DraftReviewForm` with react-hook-form + zod for editable To/Subject/Body and read-only attachments
- Add E2E suite (4 scenarios) with Playwright route interception: happy path, byte-for-byte edit round-trip to /api/send, 403 error banner without success, 422 draft failure without review form; Develogia Spanish post as canonical fixture
